searchDocs.title: ActivePerksGuiController
searchDocs.content: ActivePerksGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Binds the Studio-authored StarterGui.ActivePerksGui: a read-only view of the perks buffing the player right now. Each tab lists the active permanent perks first (PerkClient), then the run's shop perks: Personal = your ActiveRun.Personal minus ended clocks; Party = every party shop perk live in the run (PartyPerkBuffs.<Id>HolderId ~= 0). A Personal perk is active at the player's own level > 0; a Party perk at the server-wide max, and PerkOwner names the player holding it. Opens from a TopbarPlus icon (toggle key O). It is the Game Instance's only perk GUI: perk changes are Lobby-only (PerkMenuGuiController).

searchDocs.title: AmmoHudController
searchDocs.content: AmmoHudController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives the authored AmmoGui HUD (bottom-right). The ammo count is split across two labels either side of a divider, laid out horizontally: MainContainer (UIListLayout, Horizontal) ├── AmmoCount (TextLabel) <-- loaded magazine / carried count ├── Divider (Frame) └── ReserveAmmoCount (TextLabel) <-- reserve pool For a Gun that reads "mag | pool"; for a Throwable the carried count goes inAmmoCount and ReserveAmmoCount shows an em-dash, so the widget keeps its shape across weapon swaps. Hidden when nothing relevant is equipped. The GUI has no weapon-name label — the name is not displayed. These instance names are load-bearing: renaming any of them in Studio breaks the controller at load. Reads through AmmoApi and reacts to weapon/ammo Signals — it never talks to the server. AmmoController runs AmmoApi.Init(); this only renders.

searchDocs.content: ArmorController This item only works when running on the client. Client Bootstrap for the armor read model. searchDocs.title: ArmorConfig
searchDocs.content: ArmorConfig Single tuning surface for crafted player armor. Armor comes in two types that differ only in what happens when their pool empties: a Ballistic kind's pool is durability and the set is destroyed at zero; an Energy kind's pool is a reserve that can be recharged at the workbench and simply stops protecting while empty. Both drain by the damage the armor actually absorbed. Energy kinds always reduce less than the ballistic kind of the same tier, trading raw mitigation for a refillable pool. Kind id is the persisted unit (see ArmorManager), alongside the pool remaining. Reduction, maximum pool, type and tier are always derived from this table, so retuning a kind retroactively updates every player holding it. Per project convention, tune armor here, not in code.

searchDocs.title: ArmorResultCodes
searchDocs.content: ArmorResultCodes Frozen reason-code enum returned by ReqEquipArmor and ReqRechargeArmor. Shared by client and server so string literals never appear in business logic; the client maps codes to notification messages.

searchDocs.title: OwnsAtFullPool​
searchDocs.content: </> ArmorManager.OwnsAtFullPool( player: Player , kindId: string ) → boolean True when the player owns kindId and its pool is already at the kind's maximum. Crafting is refused in that case, so a redundant craft never costs materials.

searchDocs.title: Absorb​
searchDocs.content: </> ArmorManager.Absorb( player: Player , amount: number, efficiency: number ) → number Apply the worn armor to one incoming damage amount and drain its pool by what was absorbed. Returns the damage that survives to reach health. efficiency is the player's ArmorEfficiency perk bonus, read by the caller. It multiplies the kind's base reduction for both armor types, and the result is hard-clamped to ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap so stacking cannot reach immunity. A hit never absorbs more than the pool has left, so the overflow of the hit that breaks a ballistic set still reaches health.

searchDocs.title: Grant​
searchDocs.content: </> ArmorManager.Grant( player: Player , kindId: string ) → boolean Award kindId at full pool, or refill it if already owned — recrafting a damaged set is how it is repaired. Auto-equips when nothing is worn, so a player's first craft is immediately useful. Returns false (no-op) when the profile is missing, the kind is unknown, or it is already at full pool.

searchDocs.title: Equip​
searchDocs.content: </> ArmorManager.Equip( player: Player , kindId: string ) → ( boolean, number ) Wear an owned kind. Returns (ok, code) where code is an ArmorResultCodes member. Equipping an Energy kind at zero reserve is allowed — it is worn and worthless until recharged, which is the intended failure mode.

searchDocs.title: Recharge​
searchDocs.content: </> ArmorManager.Recharge( player: Player , kindId: string ) → ( boolean, number, number ) Refill an owned Energy kind's reserve from the shared MaterialPool Energy. Returns (ok, energyAdded, code). Spends only the points needed to fill (MaterialPool.SpendUpTo), like TrainFuelManager.handleRefuel.

searchDocs.title: ArmorService
searchDocs.content: ArmorService This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative handler for ReqEquipArmor and ReqRechargeArmor, and the bootstrap that initialises ArmorManager. Owns request validation only — the target is a tagged Workbench station and the player is near it — and delegates every state change to ArmorManager, which is the authority on ownership, pools and persistence. Client input is never trusted: the bench and proximity are re-checked from server-owned state on every request.

searchDocs.title: CannonConfig
searchDocs.content: CannonConfig Tuning for the manned cannon (Perk Spec 5). The CannonDamage perk MULTIPLIESDamage at the server damage line — never edit it for the perk. All sound keys resolve through SoundManager/SoundConfig (no ad-hoc Sound instances).

searchDocs.title: CannonController
searchDocs.content: CannonController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives the manned-cannon experience for the local player: a ProximityPrompt on each placed cannon to mount; while mounted, locks movement, shows a ballistic arc preview, and fires on input via ReqFireCannon (server is authoritative). Renders CannonFired (muzzle flash + barrel snap + fire sound) and the cannon explosion sound for all clients. No authoritative state lives here.

searchDocs.title: CannonGuiController
searchDocs.content: CannonGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Programmatic heat-bar HUD shown only while the local player mans a cannon. Driven by Signals.OnCannonMounted (which cannon, or nil) and reads the live Heat (0..1) and Overheated attributes the server writes on the cannon Model. Plays the overheat stinger once on the transition into overheat.

searchDocs.title: CannonServer
searchDocs.content: CannonServer This item only works when running on the server. Server Authority for the manned cannon (Perk Spec 5). Discovers placed cannons in workspace.PlacedObjects (by the PlaceableName attribute), validates mount/fire requests, and simulates an authoritative explosive arc shell via a FastCast2 cast with a gravity Acceleration (the rocket pattern from WeaponServer). Damage is scaled by the CannonDamage party perk and applied through CombatService.ApplyAOE. Heat is tracked per cannon and published as Heat/Overheated attributes on the placed Model (no extra packet). Client aim is never trusted for damage. Smart Cannon (party shop perk): a cannon with no live occupant forAutoLoaderIdleTime fires at the nearest visible enemy at AutoLoaderRate × the manned rate, credited to the perk holder.

searchDocs.title: CharacterCollisionService
searchDocs.content: CharacterCollisionService This item only works when running on the server. Server Places every BasePart of every player character into the Character collision group (see CollisionGroups). This is what lets physics projectiles (WeaponProjectile) and dropped materials (DroppedMaterial) pass through players while still colliding with world geometry — all three previously shared the Default group, so they could not be told apart by the physics solver. Parts that stream in after spawn (R15 limbs, accessories) are caught viaDescendantAdded; the connection is owned by a per-character Janitor torn down when the character is destroyed.

searchDocs.title: EnemyRenderTime​
searchDocs.content: </> Chrono.EnemyRenderTime() → number Client only. The render time (server os.clock() domain) this client is currently drawing ENEMY entities at. Sent with hit requests so the server can rewind enemies. Returns 0 until the clock has received a snapshot.

searchDocs.title: ChronoConfig
searchDocs.content: ChronoConfig Chrono (parihsz/chrono@2.2.0) configuration. Required by Chrono's Start (via SharedModules/Chrono) before its config locks — do not require it directly. Players use Chrono's built-in AUTOMATIC PLAYER type; spawned NPCs use ENEMY (see EnemyChrono).

searchDocs.title: ClientReadyController
searchDocs.content: ClientReadyController This item only works when running on the client. Client Announces this client's readiness to receive join-time snapshots, exactly once, by firing Packets.ClientReady. Timing matters. The vendored Packet library dispatches incoming payloads into signals with no backlog, so a snapshot that arrives before a consuming script has connected its handler is dropped. Waiting for game.Loaded and then deferring gives every StarterPlayerScript the chance to run its top-level code and connect. This is a best-effort gate, not a proof — TrainStateCache is what makes a late subscriber recoverable, and the two mechanisms are intended to be used together.

searchDocs.title: CollisionGroups
searchDocs.content: CollisionGroups This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative registrar for every physics CollisionGroup in the game and the single place their collidability matrix is defined. Requiring this module (cached, so it runs exactly once) registers the groups and applies the relationships below; consumers then assign part.CollisionGroup using the exported name constants. Groups (besides the built-in Default): Character — every BasePart of a player character (see CharacterCollisionService) or of a faction-tagged model ("EnemyNPC" / "FriendlyNPC", see NpcCollisionService). WeaponProjectile — thrown charges / physics projectiles (see ServerProjectile). DroppedMaterial / DroppableSurface — the proximity/drop item system. Relationships (only non-default entries; new groups collide with everything by default, so we only turn the wrong pairs OFF): A B Collidable Why DroppedMaterial Default ✗ drops pass through characters/walls/untagged world DroppedMaterial DroppableSurface ✓ …and only land on tagged surfaces DroppedMaterial Character ✗ preserve pass-through now that characters left Default WeaponProjectile Character ✗ charges pass through ALL players (AOE handles damage) WeaponProjectile WeaponProjectile ✗ charges don't knock each other around WeaponProjectile DroppedMaterial ✗ loose junk doesn't stop a charge mid-flight Everything else stays default-true: WeaponProjectile collides with Default DroppableSurface (so it bounces/sticks on arbitrary world geometry), and Character collides with Default/DroppableSurface/Character (players collide with world, platforms, and each other exactly as before).

searchDocs.title: DevCommandsService
searchDocs.content: DevCommandsService This item only works when running on the server. Server Server side of the dev-only chat commands registered in NovaChat'sCommands.client.luau. Chat commands execute on the client, so anything touching authoritative state has to come back through a packet — this is the handler for those. Every command here is gated on isAuthorised, which mirrors the check NovaChat's own ChatHandler.server.luau uses for moderation actions: the place owner, or rank 250+ in the owning group. Unauthorised callers are ignored (with a warn, so an attempt is visible in the server log) rather than answered, since a reply would only tell an exploiter where the gate is. Commands are deliberately self-only: none of them takes a target player. That keeps the worst case of a missed gate to "a player can inconvenience themselves".

searchDocs.title: DisruptionSystemLoader

searchDocs.title: EnemyBrain
searchDocs.content: EnemyBrain This item only works when running on the server. Server Centralized enemy AI director. Ticks every armed enemy at TICK_HZ through two independent concerns: MOVEMENT (pathfind toward the nearest player to a comfort distance) and FIRING (burst/cooldown, run-and-gun — added in later tasks). One Janitor per enemy record. PathfindingService:ComputeAsync is budgeted across enemies so 40 enemies stay affordable. Deliberately simple: no cover, no coordination, no target leading.

searchDocs.title: Dropdown
searchDocs.content: Dropdown This item only works when running on the client. Client A reusable dropdown/select widget. Re-implemented from the GuiLib reference pattern — it does NOT require GuiLib. Drives a caller-authored button that has an Option (TextLabel) and Arrow (ImageLabel) child, building a selectable option list directly beneath it. Fully decoupled from any specific GUI, config, or signal bus: callers connect .Changed and wire it themselves. local Dropdown = require(SharedModules.Gui.Dropdown) local dropdown = Dropdown.new(button, { { Value = "all", Label = "All" }, { Value = "weapons", Label = "Weapon" }, }, { StartValue = "all" }) dropdown.Changed:Connect(function(value) print("selected", value) end)

searchDocs.title: EnemyChrono
searchDocs.content: EnemyChrono This item only works when running on the server. Server Registers each spawned NPC as a Chrono ENEMY entity (NATIVE mode) so clients interpolate it with Chrono's buffer and the server keeps snapshot history for LagCompensation. One Janitor per NPC. Lifecycle: Humanoid.Died pauses replication (clients stop forcing the CFrame, so the body falls with normal physics). The entity is destroyed only after the model leaves the DataModel — server Entity.Destroy destroys the model, so it must never run on a model still in the world.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawner
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawner This item only works when running on the server. Server Generic, server-authoritative combatant spawner. Places enemy/friendly NPC Models at attachment-authored spawn points (tag EnemySpawnGroup / point tag EnemySpawnPoint), with radial jitter, SpawnVerification, cumulative-inverse weighted point selection, drip-feed waves, and a tracked WaveHandle. Spawned Models are tagged EnemyNPC/FriendlyNPC so CombatService/NpcCollisionService pick them up automatically. Owns spawning only — orchestrators decide when.

searchDocs.title: EnemyCombatConfig
searchDocs.content: EnemyCombatConfig Per-archetype enemy combat profiles. Keyed by the archetype name used in EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes. An archetype with NO entry here stays passive (EnemyBrain only arms archetypes it finds a profile for). Enemies have NO ammo/reload: ranged cadence is a burst-then-cooldown rhythm. Ranged fire is PROJECTILE (dodgeable), never hitscan. All combat tuning lives here. All enemies are ranged (melee was removed).

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnerConfig
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawnerConfig Tuning + archetype registry for the EnemySpawner service. Mirrors the JunkConfig pattern: archetype Model names are resolved against ServerStorage.EnemyAssets at load (warn on missing). All spawner tuning lives here — no magic numbers in spawner code.

searchDocs.title: EnemyWave
searchDocs.content: EnemyWave This item only works when running on the server. Server Factory for a WaveHandle: a Janitor-backed tracker over a set of spawned enemy Models. Watches each enemy's Humanoid.Died and removal; when the live count reaches 0 AND the wave has been marked complete (all drip-feed spawns attempted), fires OnCleared exactly once. Returned by EnemySpawner.SpawnWave.

searchDocs.title: EnemyWeapon
searchDocs.content: EnemyWeapon This item only works when running on the server. Server The enemy attack action. Reuses the player damage layer: FastCast2 projectiles, ServerProjectile lobs, and CombatService routing with attacker = enemyModel (Factions already allows Enemy -> Player). Enemy ranged fire is a TRAVELLING projectile (damage on FastCast2 Hit), never hitscan, so a moving player can dodge. Timing/ammo is owned by EnemyBrain, not here.

searchDocs.title: SetJumpPaused​
searchDocs.content: </> EventOrchestrator.SetJumpPaused(paused: boolean) → () Suspends event scheduling for the duration of a jump. Pausing force-finishes any Active channel through its existing activeFinish, the same path the MaxActiveDistance watchdog and Reset use. Because PirateAttackEvent registers its wave as ctx.janitor:Add(wave, "Destroy"), that despawns any surviving attackers — jumping mid-raid leaves them behind, which is what makes "players are safe inside the wormhole" actually true. The odometer is suspended, not reset, so encounter pacing resumes unchanged. Caveat: EventConfig.Enabled is currently false, so Init returns before ever subscribing to OnJumpPhaseChanged and this whole path is dormant. It is still wired correctly so it isn't the thing that breaks when the master switch is flipped on.

searchDocs.title: EventConfig
searchDocs.content: EventConfig Tuning + channel registry for the EventOrchestrator. Every scheduling knob lives here — virtual cruise speed, per-channel roll cadence, post-event delay, pity, and per-event parameters. No magic numbers in orchestrator or handler code.

searchDocs.title: Factions
searchDocs.content: Factions Combat faction policy shared by client and server. Resolves a Player or a Humanoid-bearing Model to a Faction, and decides whether one faction may damage another via a default-deny hostility table. Faction comes from: a Player (or a Model that is a player's character) → "Player"; a Model tagged EnemyTag → "Enemy"; a Model tagged FriendlyTag → "Friendly". These two tags REPLACE the former single "NPC" tag — being either tag marks a Model as a combatant (damageable + collision pass-through; see NpcCollisionService). Only Player<->Enemy damage is allowed. Every other ordered pair is denied, so there is no player-vs-player or enemy-vs-enemy damage, and friendly NPCs (e.g. the trader) cannot be damaged by anyone. The actual block is enforced server-side in CombatService; this module is shared so the client can reuse resolve for UI (e.g. hitmarker suppression).

searchDocs.title: GrabHook
searchDocs.content: GrabHook This item only works when running on the client. Client Tool script for the Grabhook item. On activation it spherecasts from the handle attachment toward the mouse cursor to find aimed junk, firesSignals.TryClaimJunk (handled by JunkController), then plays the outgoing beam and retraction animation via GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile before firing Signals.TryFinalizeJunk on retract completion. The looping sound is scheduled around the animation timeline. A per-frame force-field highlight tracks the currently aimed junk with a short grace period to prevent flicker. Equip and unequip toggle aim-mode camera via Signals.RequestShootingCamera.

searchDocs.title: GunHandler
searchDocs.content: GunHandler This item only works when running on the client. Client Category handler for hitscan guns. Predicts fire-rate and ammo for snappy feel, draws the shooter's tracer/muzzle FX, and sends ReqFireWeapon for the server to apply authoritative damage. Supports semi and automatic fire (held via OnActivate/OnDeactivate) and reload (OnReload). Local ammo is predicted via AmmoApi and reconciled by the server's WeaponMagSync/AmmoPoolSync.

searchDocs.title: CreateBeam​
searchDocs.content: </> GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam( att0: Attachment ,-- Origin attachment (typically on the tool handle). att1: Attachment ,-- Target attachment (typically on the junk part). parent: Instance -- Where to parent the created Beam. ) → Beam -- The newly created beam. Creates a Beam between att0 and att1, applies all visual properties from GrabHookConfig.Visuals, and parents it to parent.

searchDocs.title: AnimateProjectile​
searchDocs.content: </> GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile( beam: Beam ,-- The beam created by CreateBeam. startAtt: Attachment ,-- The origin attachment (handle side). targetPart: BasePart ,-- The junk part being reeled in. hitPos: Vector3 ,-- The world position where the hook latched. onCleanup: (() → ())?,-- Optional callback invoked when the animation ends. retractSpeed: number?-- Reel speed in studs/s (perks applied); defaults to GrabHookConfig.Physics.RetractSpeed. ) → RBXScriptConnection -- The RenderStepped connection driving the animation. Drives the three-phase grabhook animation for the tool user onRunService.RenderStepped: FLIGHT — the hook attachment lerps toward hitPos over a duration derived from distance and GrabHookConfig.Physics.Speed, with a sinusoidal rope wave that decays as the hook approaches. LATCH — a single transition frame that flattens the curve and records the retract distance. RETRACT — targetPart.Position is lerped back to the handle each frame. When retraction completes (or if targetPart leaves workspace), the beam and junk attachment are destroyed and onCleanup is called. Returns the RBXScriptConnection so the caller can disconnect early if needed.

searchDocs.title: AnimateObserver​
searchDocs.content: </> GrabHookVisuals.AnimateObserver( beam: Beam ,-- The beam to animate. startAtt: Attachment -- The origin attachment to clean up when done. ) → RBXScriptConnection -- The RenderStepped connection driving the animation. Drives a simplified rope-wave animation for spectating clients. Since the observer receives the event after server confirmation the hook is already assumed latched; the wave simply decays over time using a standard 1 / (1 + elapsed * decay) envelope. Automatically disconnects and destroys startAtt when the Beam is destroyed by the owning controller.

searchDocs.content: HealthStaminaGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives the authored HealthStaminaGui HUD's health and stamina bars from Signals.OnHealthValueChanged / Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged. Both bars are horizontal and are driven by the X scale of the bar Frame itself — the parent of the three layered fill frames, not one of the layers and not the enclosing CanvasGroup: MainContainer ├── CanvasHealth (CanvasGroup, ClipsDescendants) -- composites + clips │ ├── Health (Frame) <-- resize THIS │ │ ├── healthDarker / healthLighter / healthWhite -- art layers │ └── Shield (Frame) <-- resize THIS too (blue overlay, shieldFill inside) └── CanvasStamina (CanvasGroup, ClipsDescendants) └── Stamina (Frame) <-- resize THIS └── stamDarker / stamLighter / stamWhite Resizing a layer distorts that layer only; resizing the CanvasGroup moves the whole widget including its backing art. Keep these names in sync with the Studio asset — they are load-bearing.

searchDocs.title: JumpDriveConfig
searchDocs.content: JumpDriveConfig Single tuning surface for the Jump Drive: bench interaction, charge values, phase durations, the biome registry, and arrival rewards. Edit gameplay here, never in manager or controller code. Studio setup required: The bench is the PowerCore Model (also the TrainEngine), tagged JumpDriveBench with its PrimaryPart set. Give it a BasePart JumpPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt (key F, opens the GUI). No DepositPromptPart: charging happens in the panel (hold the JumpButton). Tag one BasePart WormholeAnchor marking where the black hole appears. Create ReplicatedStorage/JumpDriveVfx holding Models Wormhole and Lightspeed. ReplicatedStorage/GuiAssets/JumpDriveGui and .../PartyVoteGui (built by plan 2026-10-09-jump-drive-gui Task 3).

searchDocs.title: JumpDriveGuiController
searchDocs.content: JumpDriveGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives the jump drive panel (GuiAssets.JumpDriveGui, opened by the bench's JumpPromptPart prompt) and feeds the party vote banner (PartyVoteGui) from the single JumpStateSync payload, so the two can never disagree. Panel: charge card with one JumpButton (hold to charge while Idle, click to start the vote while Ready), the UNKNOWN SIGNAL threat card, the destination card (Biome Selector picker, or the ERROR state), the status line, an in-panel vote row and the named roster. Banner: pushed while Voting to everyone except the vote opener and anyone with the panel open, so nobody sees two sets of vote buttons. Non-modal: abstaining is neutral, so a vote nobody sees always passes. Y/N vote keys belong to the banner: they work only while it shows. Countdowns extrapolate from server deadlines (phaseEndsAt, ThreatStateSync), so every player sees the same number.

searchDocs.title: JumpTransitionController
searchDocs.content: JumpTransitionController This item only works when running on the client. Client Renders the jump transition: the wormhole growing ahead of the train, the lightspeed rig, and a post-processing wash — plus the one-shot and looped SFX. This is not a cutscene. Nothing here takes camera or movement control; the player keeps playing while the world changes around them. Lighting is captured before anything is applied and restored through the jump Janitor, so a disconnect, an error, or a phase packet arriving out of order can never leave a player's Lighting permanently altered. That restoration is the one part of this controller where failure is not merely cosmetic.

searchDocs.title: JunkController
searchDocs.content: JunkController This item only works when running on the client. Client Manages all client-side visuals for floating junk. Pooled model instances are spawned and moved each PreSimulation step at a shared speed that ramps smoothly via smoothstep whenever the server sends a SetJunkSpeed packet. When a claim succeeds the junk is removed from simulation and tracked as retracting — other players see it slide toward the collector, while the collecting player's animation is driven by GrabHook's AnimateProjectile. JunkCollected returns the model to its pool. All junk-related network calls (ReqJunkClaim, ReqJunkFinalize) are owned here and triggered via Signals.TryClaimJunk / TryFinalizeJunk.

searchDocs.title: JunkService
searchDocs.content: JunkService This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative server script that drives the junk economy for Endless Journey. Runs a timed spawn loop that performs two-stage weighted selection — first a tier roll (multiplied by live GlobalModifiers.TierMultipliers), then a type roll within that tier — with an energy-pity counter that guarantees an Energy item after ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD consecutive non-energy spawns. All active junk is tracked by a global distance odometer; a piece despawns automatically once it has travelled past DESPAWN_DISTANCE, keeping memory and network traffic bounded without a per-frame scan of every client. Claim/finalize follows a two-step reservation protocol: ReqJunkClaim checks server-side proximity (reconstructed from the shared odometer) and sets a timed reservation, while ReqJunkFinalize validates the reservation and hands the junk Tool to the player's Backpack via JunkToolManager.

searchDocs.title: ClampRewind​
searchDocs.content: </> LagCompensation.ClampRewind( now: number, renderTime: number, ping: number ) → number Pure. Clamp a client-claimed render time into a safe rewind time. Non-finite / non-positive input means "no rewind" (returns now).

searchDocs.title: LobbySharedPackets
searchDocs.content: LobbySharedPackets The packets both places use: join sync, XP, coins, permanent perks and shop perks. Packets re-exports every one of them, so callers always require SharedModules.Packets. They live in this child module so the Lobby can map them WITHOUT the gameplay packets in Packets/init (that module creates the placement ghost UnreliableRemoteEvents on require). The Lobby's own SharedModules.Packets (places/Lobby/SharedModules/Packets.luau) returns only this module. Add a packet here only when Lobby code uses it.

searchDocs.title: LoadingScreen
searchDocs.content: LoadingScreen This item only works when running on the client. Client Replaces the default Roblox loading screen and covers the view untilPreloadLib has loaded every sound, animation, and texture/material the client can see. Assets come from two sources: Instances of PRELOAD_CLASSES under the replicated services (MeshParts give only their TextureID, so their meshes still stream in during play). Every rbxassetid:// string inside the Configs modules (ids that only exist in code, such as SoundConfig SFX or TrainConfig animations). The bar counts batches, not PreloadLib's per-asset completed: one instance can resolve several assets or none. It never stands still: it creeps toward JOIN_END while the place downloads (Roblox gives no progress for that), and a highlight sweeps across the fill the whole time.

searchDocs.title: MaterialHudController
searchDocs.content: MaterialHudController This item only works when running on the client. Client Top-right Materials HUD for the server-wide material pool (Wood, Metal, Energy). Builds its own ScreenGui in code (mockup art; swap for a Studio-authored GUI later). The panel stays hidden and slides down when the pool gains material (any player, shred or research refund), on MaterialHudConfig.TOGGLE_KEY, or on a tap of the touch-only pull tab; it slides back up after HIDE_DELAY quiet seconds. Gains whose origin is on screen (within MAX_EFFECT_DISTANCE) play a LEGO-stud style effect: local Handle clones arc out of the station, rest, then fly as 2D icons into their HUD row, ticking the counter up on arrival. Off-screen gains roll the counter up instead. Energy has no CraftingMaterials template, so its pieces skip the 3D arc and fly as 2D icons straight from the grab point. Displayed value = server total − value still in flight, so spends and overlapping gains always settle on the exact server total.

searchDocs.title: NpcCollisionService
searchDocs.content: NpcCollisionService This item only works when running on the server. Server Places every BasePart of every faction-tagged Model ("EnemyNPC" / "FriendlyNPC", see Factions) into the Character collision group (see CollisionGroups), so thrown charges (WeaponProjectile) and dropped materials (DroppedMaterial) pass through NPCs exactly as they pass through players. This is the non-player sibling of CharacterCollisionService: players are handled by Players events there, NPCs are handled by the faction tags here. Those same faction tags gate direct Humanoid damage and friendly-fire in CombatService (see Factions), so one tag makes a Model both projectile-pass-through and damageable. Parts that stream in after tagging (R15 limbs, accessories) are caught via a per-model DescendantAdded connection owned by a per-model Janitor. The Janitor is torn down when the tag is removed OR the model is destroyed — GetInstanceRemovedSignal fires in both cases, so no separate Destroying backstop is needed.

searchDocs.title: Packets
searchDocs.content: Packets Typed network packet registry. All client↔server traffic in the game goes through packets defined here — do not use raw RemoteEvent instances for new channels. The full networking map (direction, payload types, and which scripts send/receive each packet) lives in the Reference → Networking map inDocumentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md. searchDocs.title: PerkClient
searchDocs.content: PerkClient This item only works when running on the client. Client Client-side read model + command surface for permanent perks. Owns NO GUI. Caches the authoritative PerkStateSync snapshot, watches the replicated PartyPerkBuffs folder, exposes queries returning PerkView descriptors, commands (Allocate with optimistic prediction, Unlock, Respec) and a Changed signal. Hidden perks (PerkConfig Hidden = true) are never listed or commanded. Call Init() once from a bootstrap.

searchDocs.title: PerkConfig
searchDocs.content: PerkConfig Single tuning surface for permanent perks. Each perk declares its pool (Personal buffs the owner; Party buffs the whole server, and only the highest level held by any player is active), its cap, and one or more buff keys with a linear per-level value (published value = PerLevel * level). Unlock = player level gate + coins + points; each upgrade = 1 point + UpgradeCoinStep * level coins. Hidden perks are declared but cannot be used yet (Wreck Salvage waits for enemy ships). Per project convention, tune perks here, not in code.

searchDocs.title: PerkController
searchDocs.content: PerkController This item only works when running on the client. Client Thin bootstrap. Initializes the PerkClient and PerkInventoryClient read models once on join so the perk data layer is warm before any perk GUI opens. Owns no GUI — ActivePerksGuiController (Game Instance) and PerkMenuGuiController (Lobby) bind the perk GUIs. Also mapped into the Lobby by Lobby.project.json.

searchDocs.title: PerkEffectsDispatcher
searchDocs.content: PerkEffectsDispatcher This item only works when running on the server. Server The single writer of the perk buff folders. Every key = permanent layer + shop layer (Perk Rework part 3). Personal buffs go toReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>: the player's permanent perk values plus their live shop perks. Party buffs go to ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs: the per-perk MAX permanent level across players (the "only highest active" rule), plus each live party shop perk counted once, plus <PerkId>Level, <PerkId>HolderId and <ShopPerkId>HolderId (0 = none). Recomputes on allocate/respec (Signals.OnPerkStateChanged), run start (Signals.OnShopPerksChanged), player join, player leave, and the next shop perk expiry (one task.delay, re-armed after every recompute). Bridges Scavenger's Eye / Lucky Streak and Golden Lure onto ApplyTierMultiplier, and Energy Forecast onto ApplyTypeMultiplier (JunkService listens for both).

searchDocs.content: PerkInventoryClient This item only works when running on the client. Client Client read model + command surface for shop perks. Owns NO GUI. Rules for button states: PerkLoadoutState. Call Init() once from a bootstrap.

searchDocs.title: PlacementCameraController
searchDocs.content: PlacementCameraController This item only works when running on the client. Client Owns the camera while build mode is active: a straight-down (90°) view with its yaw locked at entry. The player is frozen (their HumanoidRootPart is anchored locally) and move input — WASD, gamepad stick, mobile thumbstick — pans the camera instead, plus scroll-wheel zoom and PC edge scroll. The focus stays within PlacementConfig.PanRadius of the player so the camera (the placement ray origin) stays inside PlacementServer's 55-stud origin limit. Entry swings the camera over the player to straight down at its third-person distance, then zooms out to the top-down height. Exit plays the CoolTransitions Checkerboard; the top-down view is held until the screen is covered, then the camera is handed back to CameraController (which resumes its pre-build yaw/pitch). Death/reset tears down instantly with no transition. On PC the cursor is freed (Signals.RequestMouseIcon) while build mode is active, because the placement raycast aims from the cursor position.

searchDocs.title: bind​
searchDocs.content: </> PlaceableActions.bind( model: Model ,-- The placed object whose actions are being bound. gui: Instance -- Root GUI instance containing MoveButton and/or StashButton. ) → Binding-- Binding handle; call :Unbind() to clean up. Wires MoveButton and StashButton inside gui to their respective server packets (ReqMovePlaceable / ReqStashPlaceable) for the given model. Button clicks are debounced: only one request may be in-flight at a time. When the server succeeds, the corresponding signal is fired: Move success → Signals.OnPlaceableMoved Stash success → Signals.OnPlaceableStashed The returned Binding has a single method: binding:Unbind() — disconnects all button listeners and suppresses any pending success signal. Call this when the GUI closes. Safe to call multiple times (subsequent calls are no-ops). Model destruction When model is destroyed by the server (which happens on success before the response arrives), button listeners are disconnected automatically. The in-flight success-signal path is preserved so callers still receive the OnPlaceableMoved / OnPlaceableStashed event.

The filter includes: every instance tagged PlacementObstruction (placed items and static world fixtures), the ghost-models folder, every faction-tagged NPC (EnemyNPC / FriendlyNPC, see Factions), and any extra models supplied by the caller. searchDocs.title: CalculatePlacement​
searchDocs.content: </> PlacementSystem:CalculatePlacement( rayOrigin: Vector3 ,-- World-space ray origin (typically the camera or mouse position). rayDirection: Vector3 -- World-space ray direction (magnitude determines max distance). ) → Vector3? -- Resolved surface position, or nil if no valid build area was hit. Raycasts against tagged build-area parts and returns the resolved surface position (grid-snapped or free, based on IsGridMode), or nil if no build-area part was hit or IsBuildMode is false. The raycast uses an include-filter limited to build-area parts, so placed objects are transparent to the ray. Overlap with placed items is handled separately by CheckValidity. Also caches the hit part as self.LastBuildAreaPart for callers that need the platform bounds afterward (e.g. push-out-of-the-way logic).

searchDocs.title: prepareAssembly​
searchDocs.content: </> ServerProjectile.prepareAssembly( clone: Instance , root: BasePart , physics: PhysicalProperties ) → () Prepare a cloned throwable to fly as one rigid, falling body and land predictably: un-anchor every part (an assembly with ANY anchored part is immovable); keep the root massed (so gravity arcs it) while making cosmetic descendants massless; apply the low-elasticity / high-friction physics (small bounce, no slide); and weld every descendant to the root so a multi-part model flies + lands as one piece. For a single-part asset (the current grenade + C4) there are no descendants, so the weld and massless-child steps are inert.

searchDocs.title: spawnThrowable​
searchDocs.content: </> ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable( templateName: string, origin: Vector3 , direction: Vector3 , speed: number, rest: "Stick"landsdeadwithnobounceandplantswhereitsettles(C4);, ignore: instanceswhosedescendantsnevercountasalandingsurface ) → Instance?  Spawn a physics-driven, replicated throwable. Returns the cloned instance (BasePart or Model) or nil if the template is missing/invalid. Every throwable shares one arc — prepareAssembly + launch — and one mover (installSettle): arc, then plant flat once it has contacted a world surface and come to rest. The rest mode only sets bounciness: "Bounce" keeps one small hop before settling (grenade). Both arc, plant only at rest (never mid-flight), and pass through every character via the WeaponProjectile collision group. (e.g. the thrower's character; characters are skipped regardless).

searchDocs.title: spawnRocket​
searchDocs.content: </> ServerProjectile.spawnRocket( templateName: string, cframe: CFrame ) → BasePart?  Spawn an anchored, replicated rocket cosmetic at cframe. The caller (WeaponServer) steps its CFrame along the authoritative FastCast cast and destroys it on hit. CanQuery=false so the authoritative ray never hits the cosmetic itself.

searchDocs.title: ShopPerkConfig
searchDocs.content: ShopPerkConfig The 72 shop perks (Perk Rework part 2): 40 Consumable (the run uses one copy when it starts; the effect lasts the whole run) and 32 Expiring (a real-time clock that starts on the first equip and never stops). Players buy them with coins and equip them in the Lobby only. Family = stat family label for the catalog and GUI; no rule reads it (same-family perks stack). ExclusiveGroup perks never share a pool's loadout (XP Booster I/II, Coin Booster I/II). Buffs are read by Perk Rework part 3. Hidden perks need part 5 code: not buyable, not equippable (a grant still lands in the inventory). Per project convention, tune shop perks here, not in code.

Linearly interpolates the required hold duration based on how many junk items the player is shredding. The duration scales from config.MIN_HOLD_DURATION (when junkCount = 1) to config.MAX_HOLD_DURATION (when junkCount >= config.MAX_JUNK_COUNT). junkCount is clamped to [1, MAX_JUNK_COUNT] before interpolation. searchDocs.title: ShredderClient
searchDocs.content: ShredderClient This item only works when running on the client. Client Client controller for workbench shredding interactions. Discovers placed workbenches via CollectionService tags, then wires each bench's ProximityPrompt to a nonce-guarded two-step handshake: PromptButtonHoldBegan fires ReqShredderStart to timestamp the session on the server, and the completed Triggered fires ReqShredderComplete only if the nonce is still valid. The prompt's HoldDuration is kept in sync with the player's current Wood/Metal junk count so the progress ring reflects the expected shred time. An info notification is shown (rate-limited) when the player attempts to shred with no eligible junk.

searchDocs.title: ShredderServer
searchDocs.content: ShredderServer This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative server script that owns the Workbench Shredder flow for Endless Journey. On ReqShredderStart the server validates workbench proximity, per-player cooldown, and junk availability, then returns a hold duration computed by ShredderMath. On ReqShredderComplete it re-validates proximity and timing (anti-exploit: elapsed ≥ duration − tolerance), consumes all Wood/Metal junk Tools from the player's Backpack and equipped slot, computes the Wood/Metal yield via JunkConfig.MaterialRules, and credits it to the server-wide MaterialPool. The pool broadcast carries the workbench's TrajectoryPoints arc endpoints; every client plays the arc + fly-to-HUD effect locally (see MaterialHudController). No material Tools or floor pickups exist.

searchDocs.title: ShredderResultCodes
searchDocs.content: ShredderResultCodes Frozen enum-style table of integer result codes shared by ShredderServer and any client code that interprets shredder outcomes. The table is table.freezed — treat it as read-only at all times. Codes Name Value Meaning NONE 0 No result / default unset state. INVALID_WORKBENCH 1 The target workbench does not exist or is not a valid shredder. TOO_FAR 2 The player is too far from the workbench. WORKBENCH_BUSY 3 Another session is already active on this workbench. COOLDOWN 4 The workbench is on cooldown from a previous shred. NO_JUNK 5 The player has no junk items to shred. NO_SESSION 6 No active shredding session exists (hold-complete arrived with no matching session). SESSION_MISMATCH 7 The session token sent by the client does not match the server session. HOLD_TOO_SHORT 8 The player released the hold before the required duration elapsed. NO_MATERIAL_OUTPUT 9 The shred succeeded but produced no material (e.g. empty loot table).

searchDocs.title: Signals
searchDocs.content: Signals In-process client-side event bus. Provides typed Signal objects that any controller or service can fire and connect to without direct module coupling. All signals are created at module load time and shared as a single table — require this module and index the signal you need. The full per-signal list (what fires each signal, who listens, and the payload types) lives in the Reference → Signals map inDocumentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md. Register new signals there whenever you add one here.

searchDocs.title: GetRandomPoint​
searchDocs.content: </> SpawnHelper.GetRandomPoint() → Vector3? -- A random world-space position, or nil. Returns a uniformly random Vector3 point inside one of the enabled spawn volumes. Volume selection is weighted by world-space volume so larger parts are proportionally more likely to be chosen. Volumes in disabled groups are excluded. Returns nil if Init has not been called or no enabled volumes remain (e.g. every group is disabled).

searchDocs.title: Init​
searchDocs.content: </> SpawnHelper:Init() → () Scans workspace.SpawnVolumes and rebuilds the internal weighted cache from all BasePart children, reading each part's optional SpawnGroup attribute. Must be called at least once before GetRandomPoint. Safe to call again if spawn volumes change at runtime — any disabled groups remain disabled.

searchDocs.title: Init​
searchDocs.content: </> SoundManager.Init() → () Initialises all audio subsystems and must be called exactly once, from the client bootstrap (SoundController.client.luau). Calling Init more than once is a no-op. On first call it: Ensures SoundGroups and the positional SFX pool exist in the DataModel. Connects the server-replication listener for positional sounds. Warms per-asset positional pools so the first PlaySFXAt is instant. Auto-starts any ambience beds listed in SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart.

The sound is looked up in SoundConfig.Sfx, played through the appropriate SoundGroup, then destroyed automatically when it ends. Subject to per-asset debounce if configured.

searchDocs.title: PlayLooped​
searchDocs.content: </> SoundManager.PlayLooped( name: string,-- Key in SoundConfig.Sfx. opts: PlayOptions?-- Optional overrides; FadeIn fades from 0 to target volume. ) → LoopHandle?-- Control handle, or nil if the asset is not configured. searchDocs.title: CanHumanoidSprint​
searchDocs.content: </> SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint( humanoid: Humanoid ,-- The humanoid to evaluate. rules: Rules-- Threshold values that define valid sprint conditions. ) → boolean-- true if all sprint conditions are satisfied. Returns true when humanoid is in a state that permits sprinting under the given rules. Checks applied (all must pass): humanoid.Health > 0 — character is alive. humanoid.MoveDirection.Magnitude > rules.MinMoveDirection — character is actually moving. The local-space move direction's Z component is not greater than rules.MaxBackwardComponent — character is not moving backwards. The horizontal speed of RootPart.AssemblyLinearVelocity is at least rules.MinHorizontalSpeed — character has reached the minimum speed (prevents sprint activation while standing still due to input lag).

searchDocs.title: TechTreeGuiController
searchDocs.content: TechTreeGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Binds the Studio-authored StarterGui.TechTreeGui to the Research backend. Unlike the controller it replaces, this one never builds GUI — every card, connector line, and panel is authored in Studio, and each node's ResearchConfig.GuiPath names the card it drives. Node names and durations are written from config so the authored labels can never drift from the real values. Card and line colours come from ResearchConfig.NodeStateColors.

searchDocs.title: SurvivorPayService
searchDocs.content: SurvivorPayService This item only works when running on the server. Server Survivor Pay (shop perk QuestHunter, key SurvivorPayCoins): each ShopPerkConfig.SURVIVOR_PAY_SECONDS a player stays alive while the perk is live pays that many coins (normal coin multipliers apply). A death or a respawn starts the count again; leaving the game drops it.

searchDocs.title: ThreatConfig
searchDocs.content: ThreatConfig Tuning for the threat timer (the countdown to the Leviathan) and the train hull. Read by ThreatTimerManager, TrainShieldManager, TrainClient, ThreatController and MusicDirector. Edit gameplay here, not in code.

searchDocs.title: Initialize​
searchDocs.content: </> ThreatTimerManager.Initialize() → () Resets to a full paused Counting, registers the JoinSync sender, and wires the train-start, fuel-state, jump and game-over signals. Call exactly once from the owning server script.

searchDocs.title: ThrowableHandler
searchDocs.content: ThrowableHandler This item only works when running on the client. Client Category handler for thrown weapons (grenade + C4). On activate it gates on the throw cooldown, plays the throw sound, and sends ReqThrowProjectile. The projectile instance is server-spawned and replicates to every client (no local cosmetic). Manual detonation (C4) is handled globally by ThrowableDetonateController, which sends ReqDetonate on G regardless of the equipped Tool. Damage + detonation are server-side.

searchDocs.title: TrainClient
searchDocs.content: TrainClient This item only works when running on the client. Client Client-side controller for train interaction. Discovers engine and brake lever instances via CollectionService tags and wires their ProximityPrompts: engine prompts send ReqRefuelTrain (with early-out notifications for an empty Energy pool or a full tank), and lever prompts send ReqToggleBrake while keeping their ActionText in sync with the current brake state. Lever models are also posed to match: the pivot swings between its authored pose and a TrainConfig.BRAKE_LEVER_SWING_DEG rotation via MotionMaster, purely client-side. Incoming TrainStateSync packets are bridged into Signals.OnTrainStateChanged so downstream controllers (e.g. MusicDirector) never touch the network layer directly. Each incoming snapshot is also written to TrainStateCache before that signal fires, so a controller that subscribes late (e.g. TrainFuelGuiController) can still recover it.

searchDocs.title: TrainFuelGuiController
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives the authored TrainFuelGui HUD without issuing any network packets. On every RenderStepped frame it asks TrainStateCache for the extrapolated fuel level and eases the displayed bar toward it with frame-rate-independent exponential smoothing, so refuel jumps animate smoothly. The bar colour reflects running, braked, or stalled state. This controller holds no fallback snapshot. It previously seeded one fromTrainConfig plus workspace:GetServerTimeNow() read at module load — before the client's clock estimate had converged — which extrapolated to a clamped 0% and disagreed with the diegetic monitor. While the server has not yet sent a snapshot the HUD shows a placeholder instead of a guess.

searchDocs.title: Initialize​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainFuelManager.Initialize() → () Initialises (or resets) all internal fuel state and wires up the server-side packet handlers for refuelling and brake toggling. Must be called exactly once by the owning server script before any client requests arrive. The function: Resets fuel to TrainConfig.INITIAL_FUEL and sets isBraked to TrainConfig.INITIAL_BRAKED. Binds Packets.ReqRefuelTrain.OnServerInvoke and Packets.ReqToggleBrake.OnServerInvoke. Wires each ENGINE_TAG prompt's hold events to the cosmetic REFUEL_ATTR engine attribute (see TrainRefuelFxController). Registers a JoinSync sender so each client receives the current snapshot once it announces readiness (see docs/reference/join-sync.md). Fires the initial TrainStateSync broadcast and schedules the first deterministic transition.

searchDocs.title: SetJumpFreeze​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainFuelManager.SetJumpFreeze(frozen: boolean) → () Suspends fuel drain and fuel damage for the duration of a jump. Both edges call commitEvent() so the algebraic model re-snapshots under the old rate before switching — without it, every client's extrapolated bar would keep draining straight through the transition. The not hasStarted or TrainGameOver.HasFired() guard applies ONLY to the freeze edge (frozen == true): it exists so a jump signal can't disturb the pre-game freeze or act after game over. It must NOT guard the unfreeze edge — do not "restore symmetry" by moving it above the if frozen check. If it did, isJumping could get set true by a freeze that then completes after game-over fires, and the corresponding unfreeze would be silently dropped, leaving isJumping stuck true forever. That's inert today (the round is dead and HasFired() independently blocks ApplyFuelDamage), but would silently zero fuel drain/damage after a future TrainGameOver.Reset()-based round restart. Unfreezing after game over is always safe: commitEvent() just recomputes the rate, which rateForState() still pins to 0 via isStalled.

searchDocs.title: ApplyFuelDamage​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage( amount: number, _source: any? ) → boolean Combat fuel-damage sink, called by TrainShieldManager once the shield is down. amount is fuel units already converted by TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR. Returns true when fuel absorbed the hit (or the call was a no-op), and false when fuel was already 0 — the caller then counts a hull hit. A hit that takes fuel to 0 stalls the train at once (no Emergency Generator coast); it does not end the round.

searchDocs.title: AddFuel​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainFuelManager.AddFuel(amount: number) → () Free fuel from a perk (Fuel Line), capped at max fuel. Like a refuel, any gain clears a stall or a coast. No-op after game over, for a bad amount, or on a full tank.

searchDocs.title: HasFired​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainGameOver.HasFired() → boolean Whether the game-over sequence has already fired this round.

searchDocs.title: GetReason​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainGameOver.GetReason() → number The TrainGameOverReason code recorded by the first Trigger this round, or NONE if the round is still live.

searchDocs.title: Trigger​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainGameOver.Trigger(reason: number?) → () Fires the game-over sequence once, recording reason (a TrainGameOverReason code, default NONE) and broadcasting it via Signals.OnTrainGameOver. Subsequent calls are no-ops, so the first recorded reason wins.

searchDocs.title: Reset​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainGameOver.Reset() → () Re-arms the game-over flag and clears the recorded reason for a new round.

searchDocs.title: TrainGameOverReason
searchDocs.content: TrainGameOverReason Frozen numeric enum identifying how a train round ended. Mirrors TrainResultCodes. Stored by TrainGameOver and broadcast through Signals.OnTrainGameOver so the events system can branch on cause of death.

searchDocs.title: TrainRefuelFxController
searchDocs.content: TrainRefuelFxController This item only works when running on the client. Client Cosmetic refuel animation on every TrainConfig.ENGINE_TAG model (the PowerCore). While the engine's TrainConfig.REFUEL_ATTR attribute holds a UserId (set by TrainFuelManager from the refuel prompt's hold events), Energy cells fly from that player into ChuteAttachment and the model squashes and stretches about its ground pivot. Every client animates off the same replicated attribute, so all players see a teammate refuel.

searchDocs.title: TrainShieldController
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldController This item only works when running on the client. Client Discovers shield-console instances via CollectionService tags and wires their ProximityPrompt to send ReqRechargeShield (mirroring TrainClient's refuel prompt, including the "hold with an empty Energy pool" early-out). On a successful recharge it plays a SoundManager SFX. Incoming TrainShieldSync packets are also bridged into Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged, which TrainShieldGuiController uses as the edge trigger for the monitor's capacity readout. Each incoming snapshot is written to TrainStateCache before that signal fires, so a late subscriber can still recover it. This controller owns only the Energy-recharge prompt (TrainConfig.SHIELD_PROMPT_PART_NAME). The console's second prompt, which opens the full-screen readout, belongs to TrainShieldGuiController.

searchDocs.title: TrainShieldGuiController
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives every copy of the train shield readout — the diegetic TrainShieldGui SurfaceGui cloned onto each tagged TrainShieldMonitor part, and the full-screen TrainShieldGui ScreenGui in PlayerGui that the monitor's second ProximityPrompt zooms into. Both assets share one element layout under MainContainer.SafeContainer, so one resolver and one render path serve both. Two readouts are live today: the shield fraction (eased, banded HEALTHY/WARNING/DANGER per TrainConfig.ShieldBands) and shield capacity (TrainStateCache.ShieldMax() over TrainConfig.BASE_SHIELD, which already carries Tech Tree and perk buffs). The other three — strength rating, efficiency, auto-regeneration — read ReplicatedStorage.ResearchBuffs attributes and fall back to stock values until the Tech Tree writes them. The zoom panel is modal: opening it reveals the cursor (viaSignals.RequestMouseIcon, so CameraController stays the sole owner of MouseBehavior) and hides the rest of the HUD — Roblox's topbar, Satchel's hotbar, and the TopbarPlus icons, each needing its own switch. This controller holds no fallback snapshot of its own; while the cache has none, the shield readouts show a placeholder instead of a guess. Stats update on shield sync and buff change rather than per frame — only the eased shield number needs RenderStepped. Each monitor owns a Janitor that destroys its clone when the tag is removed.

searchDocs.title: GetShield​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainShieldManager.GetShield() → ( number, number ) Returns (currentShield, maxShield).

searchDocs.title: SetJumpFreeze​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainShieldManager.SetJumpFreeze(frozen: boolean) → () Suspends shield damage for the duration of a jump. The shield has no continuous drain, so unlike the fuel freeze there is nothing to re-snapshot.

searchDocs.title: ApplyDamage​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage( amount: number, source: any? ) → () The single damage sink — future enemy AI / hazards call this. While the shield holds, it absorbs the hit and clamps at 0; the hit that empties the shield discards its excess (no fuel damage that hit). Once the shield is already at 0, further hits convert to fuel damage viaTrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR and route to TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage, which stalls the train at 0. If fuel is already 0, the hit lands on the hull: ThreatConfig.HULL_HITS regular hits end the round (HULL_BREACHED), and one ThreatConfig.BOSS_DAMAGE_SOURCE hit ends it at once (LEVIATHAN_STRIKE). No-op before the round is live or after game over.

searchDocs.title: Initialize​
searchDocs.content: </> TrainShieldManager.Initialize() → () Initialises shield state and wires the recharge packet, join sync, buff subscriptions, and pre-game freeze. Call exactly once from the owning server script.

searchDocs.content: </> TrajectoryPreview.show( config: WeaponTypes.ThrowableWeaponConfig, character: Model , tool: Tool ) → () Start showing the arc for an equipped throwable. Idempotent: a second call tears the previous session down first. Captures character/tool for the per-frame origin + raycast filtering.

searchDocs.content: </> TrajectoryPreview.hide() → () Stop showing the arc and destroy the whole pool. Safe to call when nothing is showing.

searchDocs.title: WeaponConfig
searchDocs.content: WeaponConfig Central tuning registry for every weapon, keyed by weapon name (which must equal the in-game Tool's Name). Edit stats here, never in handler/server code. Covers gun and throwable (grenade + C4) entries.

searchDocs.title: WeaponController
searchDocs.content: WeaponController This item only works when running on the client. Client Bootstrap that drives every equipped weapon. Watches the local character for Tool equip (Tool parented to character) / unequip (removed), looks up the Tool's WeaponConfig entry by name, and dispatches to the category handler. Connects Tool.Activated to the handler's OnActivate. One Janitor per equipped Tool; one per character. Fires Signals.WeaponEquipped/Unequipped for the HUD, and drives the aim/shooting camera via Signals.RequestShootingCamera on equip/unequip (same intent as GrabHook).

searchDocs.title: WeaponEffectsController
searchDocs.content: WeaponEffectsController This item only works when running on the client. Client Receives replicated combat-FX packets and renders them for the local player: tracers for OTHER players' shots (WeaponFired) and explosions (ExplosionAt). The shooter draws its own tracer locally in GunHandler, so WeaponFired is ignored for the local player to avoid doubles. Also renders the Weak Spot glow (EnemyMarked).

searchDocs.title: WeaponFx
searchDocs.content: WeaponFx Shared resolver mapping a weapon name to its client FX sound keys. Player weapons live in WeaponConfig; enemy weapons live in EnemyCombatConfig. The client FX controller uses this so a single packet path (WeaponFired / ExplosionAt) renders BOTH player and enemy weapon names. Returns a table with optional keys; callers nil-check before playing sound.

searchDocs.title: WeaponServer
searchDocs.content: WeaponServer This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative weapon server. Infers the weapon from the requester's equipped Tool and never trusts client-claimed hits. Plan 2 adds authoritative hitscan fire (ReqFireWeapon), authoritative reload (ReqReloadWeapon), and ammo initialisation on gun equip (WeaponMagSync pushed to the owning client immediately; the shared ammo pool is owned by AmmoManager and synced via AmmoPoolSync). Plan 3 adds server-side rocket (projectile) cast via FastCast2. Throwable weapons (grenade fuse + C4 manual) are handled via ReqThrowProjectile and ReqDetonate. Hitscan is lag-compensated: ReqFireWeapon carries the client's Chrono render time and NPC hit tests run through LagCompensation (rewound to that time, clamped server-side).

searchDocs.title: WeaponState
searchDocs.content: WeaponState This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative per-player weapon state. Plan 1 tracks last-fire timestamps per weapon name for server-side fire-rate gating. Later plans extend the record with ammo ({ mag }) and reload timing. Call WeaponState.Initialize() once from a server bootstrap to clear state on player leave.

searchDocs.title: WeaponTypes
searchDocs.content: WeaponTypes Shared type definitions for the weapon system. Runtime value is an empty table; consumers use the exported types. Throwables (grenade, C4) carryDetonation/Rest discriminators distinguishing fuse-timed bouncers from manually-detonated stickies.

searchDocs.title: WeaponValidation
searchDocs.content: WeaponValidation Pure-ish shared helpers run on BOTH client (prediction) and server (authority) so the two agree. Holds the fire-rate gate, spread, ammo math, AOE falloff/query, and part→Humanoid-model resolution. No networking; the only world access is queryAOEModels.

searchDocs.title: WorkbenchConfig
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchConfig Single tuning surface for the Workbench crafting station: interaction constants, output template folders, and the recipe table. Edit gameplay here, never in service/controller code. The GUI is fixed to two material rows (Wood/Metal), so recipe Cost is limited to those two materials. Studio setup required: Tag the ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/Workbench Model with CollectionService tag Workbench (shared with the Shredder, which lives on the same station); give it a BasePart named CraftPromptPart (anywhere under the Model) holding a ProximityPrompt, and set its PrimaryPart. Create ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates holding craftable weapon Tools (e.g. clones of Pistol, SMG) — separate from StarterPack. Each craftable placeable needs its ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> Tool. Wood/Metal reuse ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials.

searchDocs.title: WorkbenchGuiController
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchGuiController This item only works when running on the client. Client Drives the Studio-authored WorkbenchGui. Opens via a placed Workbench station's CraftPromptPart ProximityPrompt (CollectionService tag Workbench, shared with the Shredder on the same station Model). Two pages under a UIPageLayout, switched by the Personal (workbench) and Recharge (armory) tab buttons: Workbench — builds the recipe grid from WorkbenchConfig, fills the detail pane on selection, sends ReqCraft on Accept. Greys recipes the player can't afford or that are gated by a locked Tech node. The grid is filtered by category; the DropdownButton (driven by the reusable SharedModules/Gui/Dropdown widget) fires Signals.RequestWorkbenchCategory. Armory — lists owned armor from ArmorClient, shows the selected kind's stats, equips it, and recharges an Energy kind while the charge button is held for ArmorConfig.RECHARGE_HOLD_TIME (shorter with Armor Weave). Both pages repaint live on MaterialPool, armor and Tech-unlock changes. Each page repeats Stash/Move, wired via PlaceableActions. The CloseButton calls close(). ResponsiveScale shrinks text-size limits and scrollbar thickness on screens smaller than the 1080p the GUI was authored at.

searchDocs.title: WorkbenchResultCodes
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchResultCodes Frozen reason-code enum returned by ReqCraft and produced by WorkbenchValidation. Shared by client and server so string literals never appear in business logic; the client maps codes to notification messages.

searchDocs.title: WorkbenchService
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchService This item only works when running on the server. Server Authoritative handler for ReqCraft. Validates (recipe membership, target is a tagged Workbench station, proximity, per-player cooldown, Tech Tree gate, output feasibility, then materials), spends Wood/Metal from the global MaterialPool, and dispatches the recipe output via CraftOutputDispatcher. Any failure returns a reason code and consumes nothing. Client input is never trusted: proximity and gate are re-checked from server-owned state.

searchDocs.title: IsValidStation​
searchDocs.content: </> WorkbenchStation.IsValidStation(bench: any) → boolean True if bench is a Model in the workspace carrying the Workbench tag. Takes any because it comes straight off the wire.

searchDocs.content: </> WorkbenchStation.IsPlayerNear( player: Player , bench: Model ) → boolean True if the player's HumanoidRootPart is within the configured interaction distance (plus tolerance) of the bench.
