searchDocs.title: WreckSalvageService
searchDocs.content: WreckSalvageService This item only works when running on the server. Server Wreck Salvage (permanent party perk Plunder, key WreckSalvageChance; Hidden until enemy ships exist). Each PerkConfig.WRECK_SALVAGE_STEP share of an EnemyShip's MaxHealth that its Health attribute loses rolls the chance once. Each hit adds WRECK_SALVAGE_WOOD Wood + WRECK_SALVAGE_METAL Metal to the pool at the ship. The damage source does not matter (cannon, gun or a future weapon).

searchDocs.title: XPConfig
searchDocs.content: XPConfig Tuning constants for the XP & Level system. Per project convention, tune progression here rather than in code. The level cost curve isxpToNext(L) = round(CURVE_COEFF * L ^ CURVE_EXP) + CURVE_OFFSET.

searchDocs.title: XPController
searchDocs.content: XPController This item only works when running on the client. Client Bridges XP replication into the client. On XPStateSync it re-fires Signals.OnXPChanged (reserved for a future XP HUD bar). On XPLevelUp it raises a level-up toast via the existing NotificationManager (through Signals.RequestNotification). Runs in both the lobby and gameplay places.

searchDocs.title: XPCurve
searchDocs.content: XPCurve Pure functions deriving level and progress from a single cumulativetotalXP value. Cumulative thresholds are precomputed once at require time from XPConfig. Used server-side by XPManager; safe to require anywhere.

searchDocs.title: XPSystemLoader
searchDocs.content: XPSystemLoader This item only works when running on the server. Server Gameplay-place entry point for the XP system. Initializes XPManager (profile lifecycle + replication), then wires the two earning sources: Distance: while the train is in its "go" state (running — not braked, not stalled), award XPConfig.DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK to the whole party every XPConfig.DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS. Go-state is read from Signals.SetTrainState (the train starts braked, so no XP accrues pre-start). Kills: award XPConfig.KILL_XP and CoinConfig.KILL_COINS to every player whenever an EnemyNPC-tagged model's Humanoid dies (attribution-agnostic — shared rewards; kill perks scale them per player). Do NOT run this in the lobby place; the lobby runs XPManager.Initialize only (for display + session handoff), without earners.

searchDocs.title: AddXP​
searchDocs.content: </> XPManager.AddXP( player: Player , amount: number ) → () Award amount XP to a single player, × the XP perk multipliers (the fraction carries to the next award). No-op if amount <= 0 or the player's profile is not loaded. Fires XPLevelUp when the level increases, then replicates the new snapshot.

searchDocs.title: AddPartyXP​
searchDocs.content: </> XPManager.AddPartyXP(amount: number) → () Award amount XP to every player in the server with a loaded profile. XP is party-shared and one party occupies one server, so this is the primary award path for both kills and distance.

searchDocs.title: Initialize​
searchDocs.content: </> XPManager.Initialize() → () Wire up the profile lifecycle. Call exactly once per server (from a loader).

searchDocs.title: GetLevel​
searchDocs.content: </> XPManager.GetLevel(player: Player ) → number Current level for player, derived from stored TotalXP. Returns 1 if the profile is not loaded (safe default for point derivation).

searchDocs.title: IsLoaded​
searchDocs.content: </> XPManager.IsLoaded(player: Player ) → boolean Whether the player's XP profile is loaded (so GetLevel is the real level).

searchDocs.title: Client Predicts / Server Authoritative​
searchDocs.content: All gameplay systems in Endless Journey follow a single authority model: the client predicts the outcome of player actions to keep the experience responsive, while the server is the source of truth and rejects or corrects any result that fails validation.  The key structural tool is a shared validator module — a module in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ that runs the same logic on both sides. The client uses it during prediction so its local view stays consistent with what the server will accept. The server uses it during validation before committing any state change. When changing a rule, you must edit the shared module so both sides agree; changing only the client or only the server creates a mismatch.  When touching any system that follows this pattern, change the client controller, the server module, and the shared module together. Protocol changes go through Packets.

searchDocs.title: Placement​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityShared validator	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlacementSystem.luau	Grid snapping, free-placement math, collision helpers Client	PlacementClient.client.luau	Runs PlacementSystem locally to render the placement preview Server	src/ServerScriptService/PlacementServer.server.luau	Re-runs PlacementSystem + additional anti-exploit checks before finalizing  PlacementServer adds server-only anti-exploit layers on top of PlacementSystem: origin distance check, raycast re-validation, and a per-player cooldown. These thresholds are sensitive — see the caution below.

searchDocs.title: Stamina / Sprint​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityShared helpers	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SprintValidation.luau	Validation predicates shared by both sides Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SprintController.client.luau	Predicts drain/regen and drives FOV locally Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/StaminaManager.luau	Authoritative stamina value; syncs to all clients at 10 Hz via StaminaStateSync packet  The high sync rate (10 Hz) keeps the client HUD and sprint-gating responsive without giving the client write access to the stamina value. Sprint logic changes must be mirrored on both SprintController and StaminaManager.

searchDocs.title: Junk​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityClient	JunkController.client.luau	Renders junk movement, visuals, and rope effects using pooled instances Pooling	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/GenericPoolInstance.luau / GenericPoolObject.luau	Instance pooling for client-side rendering Server	JunkService	Spawns weighted junk items; validates all collection requests  The client never spawns junk — it only renders what the server tells it exists. Collection is validated server-side before any inventory change occurs.

searchDocs.title: Grabhook​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityClient	src/StarterPack/Grabhook/ tool script	Drives the raycast, rope visuals, and swing physics locally Server	Server script	Receives the collection request, validates proximity and legality, then awards the item  The client's visual result is speculative. The server is the only side that awards currency or items.

searchDocs.title: Shredder​
searchDocs.content: Role	Module	ResponsibilityShared math	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderMath.luau	Computes dynamic hold duration from junk inputs Shared result codes	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderResultCodes.luau	Enum of result codes used by both client and server Client	ShredderClient.client.luau	Attaches ProximityPrompts to workbenches; drives the two-step handshake (start → complete) Server	src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau	Validates proximity, timing, junk availability, and anti-exploit; consumes junk; credits the Wood/Metal yield to the server-wide MaterialPool (clients animate the gain)  Both ShredderClient and ShredderServer call ShredderMath with the same inputs, so the displayed hold-duration progress bar matches the server's acceptance window.    Anti-exploit thresholds are sensitive The server-side anti-exploit checks in PlacementServer (origin distance, place distance, cooldown) and ShredderServer (INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE, PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN) are tuned against real network latency. Tightening them without testing under realistic ping conditions will cause legitimate actions to be rejected. Loosening them creates exploitable windows. Always test against real latency before shipping threshold changes.

searchDocs.title: Signals​
searchDocs.content: What. An in-process event bus that decouples controllers and services from each other without direct require chains. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau.  Why. Direct module coupling creates a tangle of dependencies and makes load order fragile. Signals let a controller fire a named event (Signals.RequestShootingCamera) without knowing which other controllers are listening. This is the preferred pattern for gameplay events and UI intents.  How to use. require the module, then fire or connect named events. Signals are client-only and in-process — they do not cross the network. For cross-boundary traffic, use Packets.  See the full event catalogue in Signals Map.

searchDocs.title: Packets​
searchDocs.content: What. Typed network packet definitions. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau.  Why. Raw RemoteEvent / RemoteFunction usage scatters network contracts across the codebase, making it impossible to audit traffic or catch type errors. Packets centralises every channel in one place with defined types.  How to use. All client↔server traffic must go through Packets — never create ad-hoc RemoteEvent instances. When adding a new network channel, register it in Packets/init.luau and update the Networking Map in the Maintenance Guide.

searchDocs.title: Configs​
searchDocs.content: What. A directory of tuning tables at src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/. Modules cover: Placement, Junk, Stamina, GrabHook, ShiftLock, Health, Shredder, JunkTool, Sound, and Notification.  Why. Keeping tunable values in config modules separates design decisions from code logic, makes auditing changes straightforward, and avoids touching behaviour code for what are purely numerical adjustments.  How to use. Prefer config changes over code changes when tuning gameplay numbers. require the relevant config module; do not hard-code magic numbers in controllers or server scripts. See the Config Map for the full list of tunables per module.

searchDocs.title: SoundManager​
searchDocs.content: What. The single entry point for all client-side audio — SFX, BGM, ambience, and looped sound beds. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/init.luau.  Why. Ad-hoc Sound instance creation leads to untracked audio, duplicate playback, and no central volume control. SoundManager owns all audio state.  How to use. require the module and call PlaySFX, PlaySFXAt, PlayLooped, PlayMusic, SetAmbience, or SetVolume. Never create Sound instances directly. Asset IDs, volumes, pitch ranges, playlists, and ambience beds all live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau. The client bootstrap script (SoundController.client.luau) calls SoundManager.Init() once on startup.  For a full guide see Sound System.

searchDocs.title: NotificationManager​
searchDocs.content: What. A signal-driven toast notification system. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/NotificationManager/init.luau.  Why. Centralising toast creation prevents duplicated UI code in every system that needs to surface feedback to the player (e.g., refuel errors on the train, collection results, stamina warnings).  How to use. Fire the relevant Signal to request a notification; NotificationController.client.luau listens and delegates to NotificationManager for rendering. Do not construct toast UI frames directly in other controllers.  For a full guide see Notification System.

searchDocs.title: Janitor​
searchDocs.content: What. The project's cleanup primitive, provided by the howmanysmall/janitor Wally package at Packages/Janitor.  Why. Hand-rolled { RBXScriptConnection } arrays and manual disconnect loops are error-prone, easy to forget, and hard to audit. Janitor provides a single, consistent cleanup API for any scope that owns connections or instances.  How to use. Create one Janitor per lifecycle scope. Add connections, instances, and callbacks with :Add. Call :Cleanup to disconnect and destroy everything when the scope ends (e.g., on character removal or session teardown). For keyed collections, store one Janitor per entry under entry.cleaner. Call :Destroy only when the Janitor object itself will not be reused — :Cleanup preserves the Janitor for reuse.  See Janitor Patterns for Cleanup vs Destroy guidance and common lifecycle recipes.

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster​
searchDocs.content: What. The project's animation library. Defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/MotionMaster.luau.  Why. TweenService does not support springs, splines, or composable sequences, and scatters animation logic across controllers. MotionMaster provides a unified, expressive API for all client-side motion.  How to use. Do not use TweenService for client-side animations — use MotionMaster instead.  Key entry points:  -- Fire-and-forget tween MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, { Duration = 0.5, Model = "EaseOutQuad" }) -- Manual lifecycle control local tween = MotionMaster.Create(target, goals, { Duration = 0.3, Model = "Spring" }) tween:Play() -- Spring driven by a named preset MotionMaster.fromPreset("UIPanel", target, "Position") -- Chained sequence MotionMaster.Sequence({ tweenA, tweenB }) -- Catmull-Rom spline movement MotionMaster.SplineMove(target, controlPoints, { Duration = 2 }) -- Model pivot animation MotionMaster.PivotMove(model, targetCFrame, { Duration = 0.4, Model = "EaseInOutQuad" })   Key config fields: Duration, Model (easing name), TimeWarp, Delay, Repeat, RepeatDelay, From. Sixteen named spring presets are available under MotionMaster.Presets (e.g., "UIPanel", "CameraFollow", "DoorBouncy").  For the full API reference and preset list see MotionMaster Cheatsheet.

searchDocs.title: The train never moves​
searchDocs.content: The world scrolls, the train is static The train is fixed in place and never translates or rotates. The sense of travel is produced by moving everything else past it — junk scrolls by and despawns at the far edge, biomes and outposts swap around it. Two consequences run through the whole codebase: Distance is a virtual odometer, never a position delta. The Events Orchestrator accumulates EventConfig.CruiseSpeed * dt while the train is running; junk despawn distance is integrated the same way on both client and server. Nothing reads a train CFrame to work out how far the run has gone."Train speed" and "braking" mean the speed the world scrolls at. Every visible junk instance must share one speed, or the illusion breaks — that is the whole point of the consistent-junk-speed work. Props placed near the train (Workspace.Monitor, Workspace.Brake, the engine, the benches) therefore sit loose under Workspace with no welds or joints to a train model. That is correct and intentional, not an oversight — there is no train assembly to weld them to.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: Client code lives under src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ (controllers, *.client.luau) and src/StarterPack/Grabhook/ (tool scripts). Controllers own local prediction, UI, camera, and visual rendering. They never write game state directly — they send Packet requests and react to Packet syncs or Signal events.  Notable scripts:  Script	ResponsibilityBuildModeGuiController.client.luau	Build-mode HUD and input PlacementClient.client.luau	Placement preview and request dispatch HealthStaminaGuiController.client.luau	Health and stamina bar rendering SprintController.client.luau	Predictive stamina drain/regen and FOV CameraController.client.luau	Third-person, aim, and free-look camera modes; mouse-look sensitivity, scroll zoom, and occlusion SoundController.client.luau	Bootstraps SoundManager.Init() JunkController.client.luau	Pooled junk visual rendering and rope effects TeleportToSpawn.client.luau	Spawn teleportation ShredderClient.client.luau	ProximityPrompts and two-step shredder handshake HealthController.client.luau	Forwards HealthStateSync to HUD MobileGeneralGuiController.client.luau	Mobile-specific UI NotificationController.client.luau	Toast notification rendering StarterPack/Grabhook/	Grabhook tool — client raycast and visuals WeaponController.client.luau	Weapon equip/fire input and client-side prediction AmmoHudController.client.luau	Ammo HUD rendering XPController.client.luau / CoinController.client.luau	XP/level and coin balance HUD QuestController.client.luau / BattlePassController.client.luau / PerkController.client.luau	Read-models for quest, battle pass, and perk GUIs SettingsController.client.luau	User preference UI and apply SessionClient.client.luau	Party lock / mid-run rejoin client hooks

searchDocs.title: Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared code lives under src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ and is require-able from both the client and the server. This layer contains the cross-cutting backbone modules, typed packet definitions, config tables, pooling utilities, and shared validators used by both sides of the authority pattern.  Notable modules:  Signals/init.luau — in-process event busPackets/init.luau — typed network packet registryConfigs/ — all gameplay tuning tablesPlacementSystem.luau — shared placement validation logicSprintValidation.luau — shared sprint validation helpersCameraRig.luau — stateless camera CFrame compositionShredderMath.luau — shared hold-duration computationShredderResultCodes.luau — shared result-code enumSoundManager/init.luau — unified audio APINotificationManager/init.luau — signal-driven toast systemGui/SliceScaler.luau — rescales 9-slice SliceScale to screen height (reference)MotionMaster.luau — animation library (replaces TweenService)GenericPoolInstance.luau / GenericPoolObject.luau — instance poolingWeaponValidation.luau / WeaponTypes.luau — shared weapon fire validation and type definitionsFactions.luau — faction/team identity helpers used by combatQuestState.luau — shared quest period/bucket mathBattlePassState.luau — shared season/tier mathPerkState.luau — shared perk point/level mathXPCurve.luau — shared level curve derivation

searchDocs.title: Server​
searchDocs.content: Server authority modules live under src/ServerScriptService/ (entry-point scripts) and src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ (authority modules required by server scripts). The server validates every state-changing request, owns the source of truth, and syncs relevant state back to clients via Packets.  Notable scripts and modules:  Script / Module	ResponsibilityPlacementServer.server.luau	Placement validation, anti-exploit, finalization JunkService	Junk spawn authority and collection validation StaminaManager.luau	Stamina source of truth; syncs at 10 Hz StaminaBuffManager.luau	Stamina buff application ShredderServer.server.luau	Shredder validation, junk consumption, material ejection HealthManager.luau	Health regen and HealthStateSync ReplicatedSoundService	Sound replication relay WeaponServer.server.luau	Weapon fire validation and damage authority CombatService.luau	Shared damage routing (hitscan/projectile/AOE) EnemyCombatSystemLoader.server.luau / EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau	Enemy AI and spawner bootstrap XPSystemLoader.server.luau / CoinSystemLoader.server.luau	XP and coin authority bootstrap QuestSystemLoader.server.luau / BattlePassSystemLoader.server.luau	Quest and battle pass authority bootstrap PerkSystemLoader.server.luau / ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau	Perk and research authority bootstrap SessionSystemLoader.server.luau	Party lock + mid-run rejoin bootstrap (SessionCoordinator, SessionStore) SettingsSystemLoader.server.luau	User-preferences authority bootstrap (SettingsManager)

searchDocs.title: Communication Diagram​
searchDocs.content: flowchart TB subgraph Client["CLIENT"] Controllers["Controllers / UI"] -->|Signals| Controllers Controllers -->|fire Packet request| ClientPackets["Packets layer\n(typed; no raw Remotes)"] end ClientPackets -->|RemoteEvent / RemoteFunction| ServerPackets subgraph Server["SERVER"] ServerPackets["Packets layer"] -->|sync / response Packet| Authority["Authority Modules\n(StaminaManager, PlacementServer, WeaponServer, XPManager, …)"] end   Signals are client-only and in-process — they never cross the network. All cross-boundary traffic uses Packets.

searchDocs.title: Where Content Lives​
searchDocs.content: There are two sources of documentation:  Narrative pages (docs/) — the files you are reading now. Written by hand in Markdown and checked into this repository. Covers architecture, playbooks, getting-started guides, and everything that isn't a raw API reference.API reference — generated automatically by Moonwave from doc-comments (--[=[...]=] blocks) in the Luau source under src/. Moonwave extracts these at build time; no separate documentation file is needed for module APIs.

searchDocs.title: Local Preview​
searchDocs.content: Install Moonwave globally once:  npm i -g moonwave@latest   Then, from the repo root:  Command	Effectmoonwave dev	Starts a live-reload local server. Edit any docs/ page or source doc-comment and the browser updates instantly. moonwave build	Produces a static output in build/ for inspection. The CI pipeline runs this automatically — you rarely need it locally.

searchDocs.title: Publishing​
searchDocs.content: Pushing to main triggers a GitHub Action that:  Runs moonwave build.Pushes the static output to the separate endless-journey-docs repository.GitHub Pages serves the result from that repo.  You do not need to run the build or push to endless-journey-docs manually.

searchDocs.title: The Discipline Rule​
searchDocs.content: When a code change touches a system, the same commit must also update:  That system's narrative page under docs/.Any affected playbook in docs/playbooks/.The networking map or signals map if a new packet or signal was added.  This extends the project's existing "record any new signal/packet" rule (see old guide § Recommended Update Process) to cover the Moonwave site. Keeping documentation and code in the same commit makes it easy to find the change context later and prevents the docs from silently drifting out of date.  tip If the change is large (e.g. a new system), write the narrative page first as a draft, then implement the code, then finalize both in the closing commit. This forces you to articulate the design before you are buried in implementation details.

searchDocs.title: System page template​
searchDocs.content: Every page under docs/systems/ follows this H2 skeleton, in this order:  # <System Name> <1 short paragraph: what it does, why it exists, authority model.> ## At a glance | Layer | File | Role | |---|---|---| | Client | `src/...` | ... | | Server | `src/...` | ... | | Shared | `src/...` | ... | | Config | `src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/...` | ... | **Packets:** `PacketA`, `PacketB` — see [Networking Map](../reference/networking-map.md) **Signals:** `SignalA` — see [Signals Map](../reference/signals-map.md) ## How it works ### <one H3 per mechanism> <paragraphs ≤ 4 sentences; show code for any call/shape being described> ## Data flow <Mermaid sequenceDiagram> ## Tuning <Config module link + relevant playbook links, bullet list> ## API <Bullets linking Moonwave classes, e.g. [`QuestManager`](/api/QuestManager)>   Prose rules: paragraphs ≤ 4 sentences; enumerable facts in tables; anything invocable as code; bold sparingly; relative links between doc pages (../systems/foo.md style, matching existing pages); Mermaid over ASCII for any diagram.

searchDocs.title: Playbook template​
searchDocs.content: Every page under docs/playbooks/ follows this skeleton:  # <Task Name> **Goal:** <one sentence> ## Steps 1. <one action per step; exact file paths; code blocks for edits> ## Verify <How to confirm the change works in Studio.> ## Related - <system page link> - <API class links>

searchDocs.title: Adding a page or class (checklist)​
searchDocs.content: New doc page → add its id to .moonwave/sidebars.js in the right family (pages not listed there do not appear).New @class in source → add it to the fitting [[classOrder]] section in moonwave.toml in the same commit (unlisted classes sink to an unsorted lump; a typo fails the build).Adding a packet or signal → update docs/reference/networking-map.md / signals-map.md in the same commit.Run moonwave build before pushing docs changes.

searchDocs.title: Rules​
searchDocs.content: Every project file has servePlaceIds. The Rojo plugin then refuses to sync into a different place. A wrong-place sync can delete work.Every project file has its own servePort. Two places can then sync at the same time.Ownership comes from the path, not from game.PlaceId. Shared code never branches on game.PlaceId. Storing a target PlaceId for a teleport is fine (see PlaceIds in config).Set $ignoreUnknownInstances: true on every service node. With a $path, Rojo defaults it to false and deletes Studio-only instances (maps, GUI prefabs, terrain).Use { "optional": "<path>" } for folders that can be missing. Rojo then skips the node instead of failing. An empty place folder is not tracked by git, so this matters on a fresh clone.

searchDocs.title: What each place gets​
searchDocs.content: src/ is not shared by every place. It is the gameplay code, and it runs in Game Instance and Tutorial. The Lobby gets only the single modules it requires, listed one by one in Lobby.project.json.  Tree	Game Instance	Tutorial	Lobbysrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules	Yes	Yes	Listed modules only Packages	Yes	Yes	Janitor only src/ServerStorage + ServerPackages	Yes	Yes	Listed modules only (no ServerPackages) src/ServerScriptService	Yes	Yes	No src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts	Yes	Yes	Listed scripts only src/StarterPack	Yes	Yes	No places/<Place>/...	own only	own only	own only  Mapping the whole SharedModules tree into the Lobby would sync hundreds of gameplay modules it never uses. Some shared modules also start work on require (for example Chrono); keep those out of the Lobby.  Code that must run in Game Instance but not Tutorial goes in places/GameInstance/, or stays in src/ behind a PlaceConfig flag. Do not copy it.

searchDocs.title: Layout​
searchDocs.content: Game Instance/ # repo root src/ # gameplay + shared modules (see table above) places/ # create only when a place needs its own scripts Lobby/ ReplicatedStorage/ # lobby modules (Packets, PartySystem, Zone, Satchel, ...) ServerScriptService/ StarterGui/ # GUI scripts; see "Scripts inside Studio-only instances" StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ Tutorial/ ServerScriptService/ StarterPlayerScripts/ default.project.json # Game Instance Lobby.project.json Tutorial.project.json   default.project.json stays the Game Instance file. Then rojo serve with no argument and the sourcemap command keep working.

searchDocs.title: The Lobby project file​
searchDocs.content: See Lobby.project.json. What the Lobby code does is on the Lobby Place page. The pattern: a service points its $path at places/Lobby/<Service>. Each shared module the Lobby needs is added by hand at its normal path, so require paths match the Game Instance:  "ReplicatedStorage": { "$className": "ReplicatedStorage", "$ignoreUnknownInstances": true, "$path": "places/Lobby/ReplicatedStorage", "SharedModules": { "$className": "Folder", "$ignoreUnknownInstances": true, "Configs": { "$className": "Folder", "$ignoreUnknownInstances": true, "SessionConfig": { "$path": "src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SessionConfig.luau" } } } }   To share another module with the Lobby, add one $path node for it. Also add every module it requires, or its require fails in the Lobby. Check what the module creates on require, too: the Game Instance Packets creates placement UnreliableRemoteEvents, so the Lobby maps places/Lobby/SharedModules/Packets.luau (which returns only Packets/LobbyShared) at the same path. A new packet that Lobby code uses goes in LobbyShared. The Lobby maps only the Wally packages it uses, one by one (today: Janitor, for PerkClient and PerkInventoryClient). Never map the whole Packages folder: packages ship instances too (chrono has a Remotes folder of RemoteEvents). The Lobby Place page lists every mapped module.  The Lobby still has its own older copies of Packets, PartySystem, Zone and Satchel at the ReplicatedStorage root.

searchDocs.title: Scripts inside Studio-only instances​
searchDocs.content: Rojo makes a directory into a Folder and deletes children it does not know. A script that lives inside a GUI, a model, or next to Studio-only children therefore needs an init.meta.json in each directory above it:  { "className": "Frame", "ignoreUnknownInstances": true }   className must match the Studio class exactly (ScreenGui, Frame, ImageButton, ...). A wrong class replaces the Studio instance and loses its children.ignoreUnknownInstances: true keeps the Studio-only children (labels, layouts, UIStroke, runtime folders).A Script with RunContext = Client (for example SatchelLoader in ReplicatedStorage) is init.server.luau plus "properties": { "RunContext": "Client" }. A .client.luau file becomes a LocalScript, which does not run in ReplicatedStorage.

searchDocs.title: Recipe: import a place from Studio​
searchDocs.content: Azul (or any Studio-to-file sync) writes a script with children as X.luau beside a folder X/. Rojo wants X/init.luau (keep the .server/.client suffix: X/init.server.luau).  Sync the place to a temporary folder and move it to places/<Place>/.Move every X.luau that has a sibling X/ folder to X/init.luau.Read the class of every non-script ancestor from Studio. Add the init.meta.json files from the section above.Run rojo sourcemap <Place>.project.json and compare its classes with the Studio tree.Turn off Azul before you connect Rojo. Two sync tools on one place fight each other.

searchDocs.title: Recipe: Tutorial project file​
searchDocs.content: Copy default.project.json. Change name, servePort (34874) and servePlaceIds. Then merge the place folders under the shared services with a named child:  "ServerScriptService": { "$className": "ServerScriptService", "$ignoreUnknownInstances": true, "$path": "src/ServerScriptService", "PlaceScripts": { "$className": "Folder", "$ignoreUnknownInstances": true, "$path": { "optional": "places/Tutorial/ServerScriptService" } } }   Do the same under StarterPlayerScripts. The child name (PlaceScripts, PlaceConfig) must not collide with a folder in src/<Service>/.  Each file repeats the full tree. This is deliberate: three short files are easier to read than a nested-project setup.

searchDocs.title: Recipe: place-specific settings​
searchDocs.content: Shared code must not branch on the place. Each place that runs the shared code supplies a module at the same path instead:  -- places/Tutorial/ReplicatedStorage/PlaceConfig.luau return { EnemyWavesEnabled = false, }   -- shared code local PlaceConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.PlaceConfig)   Once shared code requires PlaceConfig, every place that runs that code must supply one (make the path required, not optional). A missing module fails loudly at require, which is correct. Do not add PlaceConfig before a flag needs it.

searchDocs.title: PlaceIds in config​
searchDocs.content: Teleport targets live in the existing configs, not in project files:  SessionConfig.GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID — Game Instance. The Lobby reserves a server here and teleports the party in. See Session Rejoin.DisruptionConfig.LOBBY_PLACE_ID — Lobby. Players return here after a disruption. See Disruption.  Add a TUTORIAL_PLACE_ID beside them when the tutorial teleport exists.

searchDocs.title: Recipe: add a place​
searchDocs.content: Create the place in the Creator Dashboard, inside the Endless Journey universe. Copy its PlaceId (Studio: print(game.PlaceId)).Create <Place>.project.json from the recipe above. Use the next free servePort.Create places/<Place>/ only when the place has its first script.Add the PlaceId to the table at the top of this page and to the teleport configs.Open the place in Studio and pick <Place>.project.json in the Rojo extension.Re-set the TweenPlus TweenPreallocations attribute in that place (see Toolchain). It is per place file.

searchDocs.title: Luau LSP​
searchDocs.content: The sourcemap covers one project file. To get autocomplete in places/<Place>/, regenerate it from that place's file:  rojo sourcemap Lobby.project.json -o sourcemap.json --include-non-scripts   Or set "luau-lsp.sourcemap.rojoProjectFile": "Lobby.project.json" in your local .vscode/settings.json (.vscode/ is not tracked).

searchDocs.title: Cross-place gotchas​
searchDocs.content: ProfileStore session lock. A profile that is still open in one place delays the session start in the next place. The Lobby ends every member's sessions with PersistenceRegistry.ReleaseForTeleport right before the teleport and reopens them if it fails (see Perk Inventory). A new profile manager must call PersistenceRegistry.RegisterHandoff.Studio-only content (maps, GUI prefabs, terrain) lives only in each place file. If a script waits for an instance that is not in the repo, look in that place. TODO.md in the repo root tracks the Game Instance gaps.Place files (.rbxl/.rbxlx) stay out of git. Publish from Studio.

searchDocs.title: Checklist before you finish a change​
searchDocs.content: Every *.project.json has servePlaceIds and a unique servePort. Every required $path exists (rojo sourcemap <file>.project.json fails if not). No shared code reads game.PlaceId to pick behaviour. New place-only code is under places/<Place>/, not src/. Lobby code does not require a module that starts gameplay systems.

searchDocs.title: Initial Setup​
searchDocs.content: After cloning the repo, run this once:  rokit install   This installs the pinned versions of Rojo, Wally, wally-package-types, and selene into your local toolchain.

searchDocs.title: Common Commands​
searchDocs.content: Command	Purposerojo serve	Start the live-sync server for Studio editing. rojo build -o "Game Instance.rbxlx"	Emit a static place file from src/. rojo sourcemap default.project.json -o sourcemap.json --include-non-scripts	Regenerate the sourcemap used by Luau LSP. Re-run after adding or moving files. wally install	Fetch Wally dependencies into Packages/ (shared) and ServerPackages/ (server). wally-package-types --sourcemap sourcemap.json Packages/	Regenerate type exports for Wally packages. Run after every wally install so Luau type-checking sees package types. selene src	Lint Luau source against the Roblox standard library (std = "roblox", config in selene.toml).

searchDocs.title: After wally install — Manual Studio Step Required​
searchDocs.content: TweenPlus TweenPreallocations After every wally install, you must manually re-set the TweenPreallocations attribute in Studio — or TweenPlus will crash on load. wally install deletes and regenerates the entire Packages/ directory. The TweenPlus package (Packages/_Index/alexanderlindholt_tweenplus@<ver>/tweenplus) reads a TweenPreallocations number attribute from its own script instance at require-time with no nil fallback (table.create(script.Parent:GetAttribute("TweenPreallocations"))). When the attribute is absent the package throws: invalid argument #1 to 'create' (number expected, got nil) This error cascades: TweenPlus → PlacementSystem → SprintController → every consumer fails to load. Steps to fix after wally install: Open Studio with rojo serve running.In the Explorer, navigate to:ReplicatedStorage → Packages → _Index → alexanderlindholt_tweenplus@<ver> → tweenplusIn the Properties panel, add an attribute: Name: TweenPreallocationsType: numberValue: 256 Save the place file. The attribute persists until the next wally install.  A default.project.json $properties override cannot be used here: in live Rojo sync, Rojo recreates the path-synced instance instead of patching it, so the attribute would be wiped on every sync cycle.

searchDocs.title: No Automated Tests​
searchDocs.content: note There is no automated test suite. All verification happens by playtesting in Studio. See the How-To Playbooks for the manual smoke-test steps specific to each system.

searchDocs.title: Core Loop​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesPlacement	Grid and free-placement of world objects; client previews, server validates. Placeable Actions	Stash returns a placed item to the Backpack, Move re-equips it; both server-validated. Junk	Server spawns weighted floating debris; client renders pooled visuals and simulates movement locally. Grabhook	Tool-driven traversal; client drives raycast and rope visuals, server validates the claim and awards it. Proximity Pickup	Dropped craft materials and shredder-ejected items auto-register for proximity claim or delayed auto-collect. Shredder	Two-step server handshake converting Wood/Metal junk into crafting materials at a Workbench. Material Pool	Server-wide Wood/Metal pool shared by all players, shown in a hide-by-default top-right HUD. Workbench Crafting	Server-authoritative, instant crafting of weapons/armor/placeables from config-defined recipes. Research Bench	Server-wide, session-only research: enqueue, advance, complete, refuel, and cancel jobs gated by shared fuel.

searchDocs.title: Train​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesTrain Fuel	Single global fuel value computed algebraically by the server; clients predict the bar locally. Train Shield	Global, event-driven shield pool depleted by damage and restored with pool Energy. Cannon	Grid-placeable, manned cannon firing server-authoritative explosive arc shells. Events Orchestrator	Server-authoritative scheduler deciding when and which in-game events fire per channel. Disruption / Maintenance	Notifies players, force-saves progress, and teleports to the lobby on shutdown or maintenance.

searchDocs.title: Combat​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesWeapons	Client-predicted / server-authoritative combat with a shared validator; all damage applies server-side. Enemy Combat	A centralized AI director ticks every armed enemy, reusing the player weapon and damage stack. Enemy Spawner	Generic server-authoritative spawner selecting weighted spawn points and validating placement. Health	The server is the single source of truth for health; it drives regen and syncs the client HUD. Damage Numbers	Client-only, render-only floating world-space damage numbers; never computes or applies damage.

searchDocs.title: Player​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesStamina & Sprint	Client-predicted, server-authoritative stamina simulation synced at up to 10 Hz. Camera	A fully script-owned third-person camera computing Camera.CFrame every frame. Settings	Generic server-authoritative user-preferences registry for audio volumes and sensitivity.

searchDocs.title: Progression & Economy​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesProgression (XP & Level)	Server-authoritative, party-shared XP & Level system persisted with ProfileStore. Economy (Coins)	Server-authoritative coin wallet persisted with ProfileStore, shared across lobby and gameplay places. Quests	Rotating ProfileStore-backed quest system with four buckets plus a Season scope feeding the Battle Pass. Battle Pass	Monthly ProfileStore-backed 60-tier track with Free and Premium reward rows. Perks	Level-driven permanent progression spending Personal/Party points on persistent buffs.

searchDocs.title: Audio & UI​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesSound	A layered client audio system; all game audio flows through the SoundManager facade. Notifications	A signal-driven client toast stack; NotificationManager is the sole subscriber.

searchDocs.title: Sessions & Lobby​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesParty Lock + Mid-Run Rejoin	Server-enforced party lock and mid-run rejoin guarantees for a live run. Lobby	The separate Lobby place: players pick a party size in a room, then teleport together into a reserved Game Instance server.

searchDocs.title: Design philosophy​
searchDocs.content: Every gameplay system follows a client predicts / server authoritative pattern with a shared validator. The client runs local prediction (placement preview, stamina drain, fuel bar interpolation) so interaction feels instant, while the server re-validates every request and broadcasts the authoritative result. Protocol changes must go through src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau; cross-module events go through src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau. When in doubt, the server wins.

searchDocs.title: How to read these docs​
searchDocs.content: Getting Started — install the toolchain, run a build, and understand the one manual step that trips everyone up (TweenPreallocations).Architecture — runtime layers, cross-cutting modules, and the authority pattern.Systems — one page per system, grouped by family (Core Loop, Train, Combat, Player, Progression & Economy, Audio & UI, Sessions & Lobby).How-To Playbooks — step-by-step safe-change guides, grouped the same way (plus a Backbone group for packets/signals).Reference — the networking / signals / config maps, Janitor and MotionMaster cheat-sheets, plus the Moonwave-generated API docs for every annotated module.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Choose a notification type. The canonical types are defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau: "success" | "info" | "warn" | "alert" | "default" Each type has a pre-configured background color (NotificationConfig.Colors), icon image (NotificationConfig.ImageIds), and stinger SFX (NotificationConfig.SfxNames). If an existing type fits, skip to step 3. (Optional) Add a new type. If none of the five built-in types fit, extend NotificationConfig (file: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau) by adding the new lowercase key to every relevant table: -- 1. Register the type name NotificationConfig.Types = { "success", "info", "warn", "alert", "default", "mytype" } -- 2. Background color NotificationConfig.Colors.mytype = Color3.fromRGB(80, 40, 120) -- 3. Background transparency (0 = opaque, 1 = invisible) NotificationConfig.BaseTransparency.mytype = 0.5 -- 4. Icon asset ID NotificationConfig.ImageIds.mytype = "rbxassetid://XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" -- 5. SFX stinger — must match a key in SoundConfig.Sfx NotificationConfig.SfxNames.mytype = "NotifDefault" If you add a custom stinger, first register it in SoundConfig.Sfx (see Add a Sound). Fire the signal from any client controller. local Signals = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) -- Basic timed toast (disappears after the default duration): Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("success", "Item placed!") -- Custom duration (seconds): Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("warn", "Low fuel!", 5) -- Executed-function toast (stays until the function returns, then closes): Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("info", "Loading...", nil, function() -- async work here; toast closes when this returns task.wait(2) end) -- Dismiss all active toasts: Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() Signal signature (from src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau): RequestNotification : Signal<string, string, number?, (() -> ())?> arg1 notificationType (lowercase, must be in NotificationConfig.Types) arg2 message (display text, wraps automatically) arg3 duration? (seconds; nil = config default per device) arg4 executedFunction? (if provided, toast stays until function returns) The stack allows up to NotificationConfig.MaxConcurrent (default 5) concurrent toasts. When the cap is exceeded the oldest non-executed toast is automatically closed.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Play-test in Studio (client context).Trigger the code path that fires Signals.RequestNotification.Confirm the toast appears at the top of the screen, plays its stinger, and auto-dismisses after the expected duration.If the toast does not appear: confirm the type string is lowercase and present in NotificationConfig.Types; confirm NotificationController.client.luau has run NotificationManager.Init().

searchDocs.title: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
Steps​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: Open Packets/init.luau. File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau. Browse the existing definitions to understand the declaration style before adding yours. Declare the packet. Add it in the appropriate section (or create a new labelled section). Match the style of existing entries: a local variable, a direction comment, and field-level type annotations. Simple payload (no response): -- Client → Server: description of what this carries local MyPacket = Packet( "MyPacket", Packet.String, -- fieldOne Packet.NumberF32, -- fieldTwo Packet.Boolean8 -- fieldThree ) Request/response pattern: -- Client → Server: description local ReqMyAction = Packet( "ReqMyAction", Packet.Instance -- target ):Response( Packet.Boolean8, -- success Packet.NumberU8 -- reason code ) Server → Client broadcast: -- Server → All Clients: description local BroadcastMyEvent = Packet( "BroadcastMyEvent", Packet.Instance :: Player, -- the relevant player Packet.Vector3F32 -- position ) Available type tokens: Packet.String, Packet.Boolean8, Packet.NumberF32, Packet.NumberF64, Packet.NumberU8, Packet.NumberU16, Packet.NumberF16, Packet.Instance, Packet.Vector3F32, Packet.CFrameF32U16, Packet.Any. For high-frequency unreliable streams (e.g., per-frame position updates) use the makeUnreliable helper already present in the file. Export the packet. Add it to the return table at the bottom of init.luau: return { -- ... existing entries ... MyPacket = MyPacket, ReqMyAction = ReqMyAction, BroadcastMyEvent = BroadcastMyEvent, } Wire the sender. On the client (fires to server): local Packets = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Packets) -- Fire and forget: Packets.MyPacket:Fire(valueOne, valueTwo, valueThree) -- Request/response: local success, reasonCode = Packets.ReqMyAction:Fire(targetInstance) On the server (fires to clients): local Packets = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Packets) -- Broadcast to all: Packets.BroadcastMyEvent:Fire(player, position) -- Fire to one client: Packets.BroadcastMyEvent:FireClient(targetPlayer, player, position) Wire the receiver. On the server (listening for client sends): Packets.MyPacket.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(sender: Player, valueOne, valueTwo, valueThree) -- validate and handle end) On the client (listening for server sends): Packets.BroadcastMyEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(player, position) -- handle end) Update the networking map. Open docs/reference/networking-map.md and add a row for your new packet in the same commit. Include: packet name, direction (C→S / S→C / S→All), payload summary, and which scripts send/receive it.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: Play-test with at least one client and the server running.Trigger the send path and confirm the receiver fires.Check the Output window — Packet will warn if a type mismatch or serialization error occurs.For request/response packets, confirm the response values arrive correctly on the caller side.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Author the model in Studio.Open Studio and build or import the item as a Model. Give it a clear, unique name (e.g. WoodenCrate). This name is the canonical identifier shared between the storage folder and the PlaceableName attribute. Place the model in the placeable-items storage folder.Move (or keep) the model inside the storage location that PlacementServer scans at startup. Verify src/ServerScriptService/PlacementServer.server.luau for the exact FindFirstChild / WaitForChild call that resolves the folder name, and make sure your model lands there. Add a CollisionBox part.Inside the model, create a BasePart named CollisionBox. Size and position it to represent the footprint used for overlap/validity checks. Set Anchored = true, CanCollide = false, and make it invisible (Transparency = 1). PlacementSystem reads this part to decide valid placement. Set the PlaceableName attribute on the Tool.On the Tool instance that players use to enter placement mode, open Properties → Attributes and add a string attribute named PlaceableName with the value matching the model name from step 1 (e.g. WoodenCrate). PlacementServer reads this attribute at line 205 and PlacementClient at line 253. Configure ghost appearance (optional).Ghost transparency and color cues come from src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau: VisualGhostTransparency -- opacity of the main model parts during preview CollisionBoxGhostTransparency -- opacity of CollisionBox while ghosting ColorValid / ColorInvalid -- tint applied to the ghost ShowCollisionBox -- set true temporarily to debug footprint alignment Test grid mode and free mode.In a live Studio session (Rojo serving), equip the tool, open build mode, and place the item in both grid-snapped and free-rotation modes. Confirm the ghost tracks the cursor correctly and snaps as expected. Validate multiplayer ghost behavior.Run a local server with at least two clients. Confirm that observers see the ghost rendered correctly (via the replication path in PlacementClient) and that the server accepts the final placement without a distance/raycast rejection from PlacementServer. If you also need Stash / Move support, see Enable Stash & Move for the additional attribute and server wiring.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Equip the new Tool, enter build mode, and place the item. Check the Output window for any PlacementServer rejection messages. Then have a second client observe: the placed item should appear at the confirmed position with no ghost artifact remaining.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open Signals/init.luau. File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau. Browse existing entries to understand the declaration style and grouping before adding yours. Add your signal. Add it under the relevant comment group (or add a new group). Follow the existing pattern exactly — type-annotate the generic parameter so Luau can check call sites: -- My System (Client Side) -- Fired by <ProducerScript> when <event>. Consumed by <ConsumerScript>. -- (<argOne>: type, <argTwo>: type) MySignal = Signal() :: Signal.Signal<string, number>, For signals with no payload (fire/connect only): MySignal = Signal(), Fire from the producer. local Signals = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) Signals.MySignal:Fire("hello", 42) Only one script should act as the authoritative producer. Document it in the signal's comment. Connect in the consumer(s). local Signals = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) Signals.MySignal:Connect(function(argOne: string, argTwo: number) -- handle the event end) When the consumer has a scoped lifecycle (e.g., a GUI controller), track the connection with a Janitor so it is disconnected on cleanup: cleaner:Add(Signals.MySignal:Connect(function(argOne, argTwo) -- handle end), "Disconnect") Update the signals map. Open docs/reference/signals-map.md and add a row for your new signal in the same commit. Include: signal name, producer script, consumer script(s), and a one-line purpose summary.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Play-test in Studio.Trigger the code path that fires the signal.Confirm the consumer callback runs with the expected arguments.If the consumer never fires: confirm both scripts require the same Signals module instance (both via ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) and that the consumer connects before the first fire.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the junk config.All tunable constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau. Tune spawn rate. Field	Default	EffectDEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE	0.5	Seconds between spawns while the train is running STOPPED_SPAWN_RATE	1.5	Seconds between spawns while the train is braked/stalled Lower values = more frequent spawns. Both JunkService (server) and the spawn scheduler read these. Tune junk movement speed. Field	Default	EffectDEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED	10	Studs per second while train is running STOPPED_JUNK_SPEED	5	Studs per second while train is braked/stalled SPEED_RAMP_DURATION	1.5	Seconds to smoothly transition between speed states SPEED_RAMP_DURATION also controls how smoothly junk decelerates when the train brakes. The first SetTrainState or SetJunkSpeed packet after a client joins snaps to target speed immediately; subsequent ones smoothstep over this duration. Tune despawn distance. JunkConfig.DESPAWN_DISTANCE = 700 -- studs Both the server odometer (JunkService) and client odometer (JunkController) compare accumulated currentSpeed * dt against this value. Increase it to let junk travel farther before disappearing; decrease it to clean up junk sooner. Adjust tier weights.Each tier entry has a Weight field. Selection is weighted-random across tiers. Higher weight = more frequent. Default distribution: Tier 1: 2000 (common) Tier 2: 1000 Tier 3: 10 Tier 4: 5 Tier 5: 0 (currently disabled) To enable Tier 5, set its Weight above 0. To make high-tier junk rarer, reduce Tier 3/4 weights. Adjust type weights and spawn chances within a tier.Inside each tier, Types maps type names (Metal, Wood, Energy) to a rule: Metal = { SpawnChance = 80, Yield = 3 } SpawnChance — probability (0–100) that this type is chosen once its tier is selected.Yield — for Wood/Metal, the material units this junk gives when shredded; for Energy, the material pool points credited on grab (T1–T5: 10/20/40/60/100). To make Energy junk rarer within a tier, lower its SpawnChance relative to Metal/Wood. Tune the pity threshold. JunkConfig.ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD = 8 After this many consecutive non-Energy spawns, the next spawn is forced to be Energy. Raise the value to allow longer dry streaks; lower it to guarantee Energy more frequently. Adjust BaseModifiers for live multipliers (if used).BaseModifiers contains runtime-adjustable multipliers that scale spawn rates and per-tier/per-type frequency without rewriting the static tables: BaseModifiers = { GlobalSpawnRateMult = 1.0, TierMultipliers = { [1]=1.0, [2]=1.0, [3]=1.0, [4]=1.0, [5]=1.0 }, TypeMultipliers = { Metal=1.0, Wood=1.0, Energy=1.0 }, } These are applied by JunkService at spawn time. Modifying them at runtime (e.g. from an event/buff system) is safe; they are not cached. Validate spawn volume layout and motion path.After config changes, confirm that spawned junk appears within the intended volume and travels in the direction set by MOVE_DIRECTION (Vector3.new(1, 0, 0) by default). Open the Output window and watch for the JunkConfig: No models found warning — this fires if a JunkAssets tier folder is missing models. Verify the collection loop feels fair.Run a local session, collect junk at the new rate, and confirm the stamina/grabhook gameplay loop still has enough breathing room. If spawn rate is very high, increase MAX_SERVER_JUNKS (200) or MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS (250) to avoid the spawn cap cutting off the flow.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Run a solo playtest for 2–3 minutes with the Output window open. Confirm the observed spawn frequency roughly matches DEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE, that junk despawns before leaving the visible play area, and that no JunkConfig: warnings appear.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open SoundConfig. File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau. It exports three tables: SoundConfig.Sfx, SoundConfig.Music.Playlists, and SoundConfig.Ambience.Beds. Add your definition. One-shot / looped SFX — add an entry to SoundConfig.Sfx: MyNewSfx = { Id = "rbxassetid://XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", Volume = 0.5, -- optional; default engine volume if omitted Pitch = 1.0, -- optional PitchRange = { 0.9, 1.1 }, -- optional; overrides Pitch; random per play Group = "SFX", -- "SFX" | "BGM" | "Ambience"; default "SFX" Replicate = true, -- set true only for positional sounds other clients should hear Debounce = 0.1, -- optional; min seconds between plays (anti-spam) PoolInitial = 2, -- optional; for PlaySFXAt only — pre-warms the pool at Init PoolMax = 8, -- optional; hard cap for the positional pool }, The SoundDef type (exported from SoundConfig) documents every field. Music track — add asset IDs to one of the three context playlists in SoundConfig.Music.Playlists (see BGM contexts below): Normal = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://AAA", "rbxassetid://BBB" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 1.5, FadeOut = 1.5, GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300, Volume = 0.6, }, Ambience bed — add to SoundConfig.Ambience.Beds and, if it should start automatically, add its name to SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart: Beds = { MyAmbience = { Id = "rbxassetid://XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", Volume = 0.4 }, }, Autostart = { "MyAmbience" }, -- fade in on SoundManager.Init() Play the sound from a client script. Require SoundManager (never instantiate a Sound directly): local SoundManager = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.SoundManager) -- One-shot 2D: SoundManager.PlaySFX("MyNewSfx") -- Positional (requires PoolInitial / PoolMax in the def for pre-warm): SoundManager.PlaySFXAt("MyNewSfx", somePosition) -- Looped SFX (returns a LoopHandle — call :Stop() to end it): local handle = SoundManager.PlayLooped("MyNewSfx") -- ...later: handle:Stop() -- Music playlist (normally driven by MusicDirector via context, not called directly): SoundManager.PlayMusic("Normal") -- Ambience (replaces current beds; use AddAmbience to layer): SoundManager.SetAmbience({ "MyAmbience" }) SoundManager.AddAmbience("MyAmbience") SoundManager.RemoveAmbience("MyAmbience") SoundManager.StopAmbience() -- Volume bus (0..1): SoundManager.SetVolume("SFX", 0.8) SoundManager.Init() is called once by SoundController.client.luau — do not call it from feature code. Wire replication if needed. If other clients need to hear the sound when it plays at a world position, set Replicate = true in the SoundConfig.Sfx entry. The server relay uses SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() to build its allowlist. The loading screen (ReplicatedFirst/LoadingScreen.client.luau) preloads every rbxassetid:// id in SoundConfig automatically.

searchDocs.title: BGM contexts​
searchDocs.content: Background music is context-driven, not played by name from feature code. MusicDirector.client.luau owns the active context and calls SoundManager.PlayMusic for you — you only ever add tracks to a playlist and (for combat) call the server API.  SoundConfig.Music.Playlists has exactly three entries, one per context:  Context	Trigger	Gap behaviorNormal	Default; nothing else active	Gapped — random silence between tracks Combat	Server calls MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat")	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence LowFuel	Automatic, client-derived (see below)	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence  Priority when more than one condition is true: Combat > LowFuel > Normal.  Add asset IDs to Tracks on the relevant playlist — do not add new playlist names, the engine and director both assume exactly these three:  Playlists = { Normal = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://AAA", "rbxassetid://BBB" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 1.5, FadeOut = 1.5, GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300, Volume = 0.6 }, Combat = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://CCC" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 1.0, FadeOut = 1.0, GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0, Volume = 0.7 }, LowFuel = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://DDD" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 2.0, FadeOut = 2.0, GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0, Volume = 0.55 }, }   Field	MeaningFadeIn	Seconds to fade the new track up from 0 at start FadeOut	Seconds to fade a track down to 0 at its end (or the crossfade overlap window when continuous) GapMin / GapMax	Random silence range (seconds) between tracks. GapMax <= 0 means continuous — the next track starts FadeOut seconds before the current one ends, producing an overlapping crossfade instead of silence Volume	Target playback volume for tracks in this playlist (pre-bus-volume)  Normal uses GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300 (a real silent gap between tracks). Combat and LowFuel use GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0 so they loop continuously with no silence.  Low fuel is automatic — never set it manually. Combat is the only context gameplay code drives, via the server-authoritative MusicService:  local MusicService = require(game.ServerStorage.SharedModules.MusicService) MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") -- on event/outpost enter MusicService.SetContext(player, "Normal") -- on event/outpost leave   SetContext fires the Packets.SetMusicContext packet to that one player; MusicDirector.client.luau receives it and resolves the active context by priority. Passing "Normal" clears the combat override — the client then falls back to LowFuel or Normal based on its own fuel state; it does not force Normal if fuel is still low.  Low fuel itself needs no code: MusicDirector watches Signals.OnTrainStateChanged and activates the LowFuel context whenever fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL drops below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct (default 0.25).

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Play-test in Studio (client context).Trigger the code path that calls PlaySFX / PlaySFXAt / etc.Confirm the sound plays. If silent: check the asset ID is correct, that Volume is not 0, and that the Group bus volume (SoundManager.GetVolume) is non-zero.For positional sounds with Replicate = true, check the Output window for server-relay errors.For BGM: confirm the track plays in Normal by default, that calling MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") from a server script switches it with a crossfade (no silence), and that draining fuel below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct switches to LowFuel when not in combat.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the stamina/sprint config.Sprint constants share the file src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau with stamina values. Both SprintController (client) and StaminaManager (server) read from this single config module. Update sprint speed. WalkSpeed = 16 -- base walk speed (studs/s) SprintSpeed = 24 -- speed while sprinting Change SprintSpeed to the desired value. SprintController sets Humanoid.WalkSpeed directly and predicts locally; the server does not validate movement speed today (see Stamina & Sprint — Gotchas), so a speed change is purely a client-side/config edit. Update FOV. DefaultFOV = 70 -- camera FOV while walking SprintFOV = 85 -- camera FOV while sprinting SprintController animates the transition. Changing these values alters the start and end points of the FOV tween — no animation code changes are needed. Update keybinds. SprintBinds = { Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB } Add, remove, or replace entries. Both gamepad and keyboard inputs are accepted in the same array. SprintController reads this array to register UserInputService listeners. If state machine behavior changes, mirror both sides.If you add a new sprint-blocking condition (e.g. a new "dash" state): Edit src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SprintController.client.luau for client-side prediction and visual feedback.Edit src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/StaminaManager.luau for server-side authority and packet emission.Update src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SprintValidation.luau if the validation predicates need to change (e.g. MinMoveDirection, MaxBackwardComponent, MinHorizontalSpeed) — this module is the single gate called identically by both sides.Register any new packet in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau and document it in the networking map. Verify shift-lock interaction.SmoothShiftLock (vendored in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SmoothShiftLock/) reacts to the sprint state. After changing sprint speed or keybinds, confirm that entering and exiting shift-lock while sprinting does not produce a stuck speed or FOV. Verify placement interaction.Build mode disables sprint while active. After changing sprint config, open build mode, attempt to sprint, and confirm it stays suppressed. Exit build mode and confirm sprint re-enables immediately. Test stamina drain under new speed.If SprintSpeed changed significantly, revisit StaminaDrain and StaminaRegen in the same config to ensure the economy still feels balanced. See Tune Stamina Economy for field details.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Sprint in a straight line, confirm the WalkSpeed and FOV match the new config values. Trigger shift-lock while sprinting, confirm no stuck state. Enter build mode, confirm sprint is suppressed; exit, confirm sprint resumes. Open the Output window and confirm no StaminaManager sync errors.

searchDocs.title: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
Steps​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Confirm the placement Model exists.ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> must already exist — this is required for placement itself and is the same model used by Stash/Move. Author the Tool template.Create (or confirm) a Tool in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name>. Create the PlaceableTools folder under ReplicatedStorage if it does not exist yet.Set the attribute PlaceableName = "<Name>" on the Tool root (string attribute, exact match).The Tool must have a Handle BasePart. Author its scripts and behaviour as you would any other placeable tool. If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing, both buttons fail silently server-side — no model is destroyed and no item is lost, but the buttons do nothing. Add the buttons to the GUI.Inside the GUI that the placeable's ProximityPrompt opens, add two ImageButton instances: one named exactly MoveButton, one named exactly StashButton. They can be placed at any depth in the GUI's descendant hierarchy. To make them invisible but still clickable, set both ImageTransparency = 1 and BackgroundTransparency = 1 on each button. If either button is missing, PlaceableActions.bind will log a warning at runtime. Bind and unbind in the controller.In the controller script that opens and closes the placeable GUI, call PlaceableActions.bind when the GUI opens and binding:Unbind() when it closes: local PlaceableActions = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.PlaceableActions) -- When the GUI opens for a specific placed Model: local binding = PlaceableActions.bind(placedModel, guiRoot) -- When the GUI closes (or the controller cleans up): binding:Unbind() placedModel is the Model instance in workspace.PlacedObjects. guiRoot is the root GUI instance opened by the ProximityPrompt (the ancestor that contains MoveButton and StashButton). If you use a Janitor for the GUI lifecycle, track the binding with it: cleaner:Add(binding, "Unbind") (Optional) Configure sound IDs.In src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau (or the equivalent config for your placeable system), set PlacementConfig.Sounds.Stash and PlacementConfig.Sounds.Move to the desired rbxassetid:// strings. Leave as "" to disable sound playback for that action. See Add a Sound if the asset ID does not yet exist in SoundConfig. (Optional) Tune cooldown and poof duration.In PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions: Cooldown — minimum seconds between successive Stash/Move requests per player (default 0.4).PoofDuration — how long the shrink-and-disappear visual plays (seconds).

searchDocs.title: Server-side guarantees​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Per-player cooldown gates spam.The target must be a direct child of workspace.PlacedObjects and carry a non-empty PlaceableName attribute (set automatically by PlacementServer at place-time).An atomic claim ensures two players cannot double-grant the same Tool simultaneously.No distance check — the ProximityPrompt enforces proximity at GUI-open time.  On success, every client receives a BroadcastPlaceablePoof packet and renders a transient shrinking clone at the model's position, parented to workspace.PlaceablePoofs and destroyed when the animation completes.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Place the item in Studio via the normal placement flow.Walk up to it so the ProximityPrompt activates and the GUI opens.Click StashButton — confirm the model disappears with the poof effect and the Tool appears in your Backpack.Place it again, open the GUI, click MoveButton — confirm the model disappears and the Tool is immediately equipped.Check the Output window for any PlaceableActions warnings about missing buttons or a missing Tool template.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Choose a starter perk. A perk with UnlockCost, UnlockLevel, and UnlockPointCost all 0 is a free "starter" — PerkManager.seedStarters auto-unlocks it for every player on load and after every respec of its pool. Today the two starters are IronConstitution (Personal) and ScavengersEye (Party) — one per pool, so a brand-new player always has a perk to upgrade in each pool. Starters still pay upgrade coins. IronConstitution = { Category = "Personal", DisplayName = "Iron Constitution", Order = 1, Description = "+{1} max health", MaxLevel = 10, Buffs = { { Key = "HPBonus", PerLevel = 0.04 } }, UnlockCost = 0, UnlockLevel = 0, UnlockPointCost = 0, UpgradeCoinStep = 100 }, -- starter To make a different perk a starter, set its UnlockCost, UnlockLevel, and UnlockPointCost to 0. Make sure at least one perk per pool stays a 0/0/0 starter. A starter cannot be Hidden (a boot self-check asserts this). Set a perk's level gate and costs. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau and edit the entry: MarathonLungs = { Category = "Personal", DisplayName = "Marathon Lungs", Order = 2, Description = "+{1} max stamina, −{2} sprint drain", MaxLevel = 6, Buffs = { { Key = "MaxStaminaBonus", PerLevel = 0.05 }, { Key = "SprintDrainReduction", PerLevel = 0.03 } }, UnlockCost = 250, UnlockLevel = 2, UnlockPointCost = 1, UpgradeCoinStep = 100 }, UnlockLevel — minimum player XP level (LEVEL_REQUIRED below this).Upgrade gates follow from UnlockLevel: the max level needs UnlockLevel + PerkConfig.UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN (35), see Perks — Upgrade gates.UnlockCost — coins deducted once via CoinManager.DeductCoins at unlock, and recorded in the CoinsSpent ledger.UnlockPointCost — points from the perk's own pool, spent once at unlock (NO_POINTS when the pool can't pay).UpgradeCoinStep — each later level n costs UpgradeCoinStep × n coins plus 1 point. All checks are enforced server-side by PerkState.canUnlock (order: unknown → hidden → already unlocked → level → points → coins). Unlock is one-time; upgrades are paid per level. UnlockCost buys access. Each level after that costs 1 point plus rising coins (see Perks — Point and coin economy). UnlockPointCost competes with upgrades for the same pool, so a high point cost delays a player's first levels in other perks. Respec refunds come from the ledger. PerkManager.Respec (a pool) and RespecPerk (one perk) refund exactly CoinsSpent[perkId] — every coin the player paid on that perk — via CoinManager.RefundCoins (not scaled by Pocket Change). A coin-price re-tune therefore never changes what an existing player gets back. A starter refunds its upgrade coins, loses its levels, and stays unlocked. Unlock points always come back in full, because points are derived.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Open the Perk menu (P). Confirm both starters (Iron Constitution, Scavenger's Eye) show unlocked, locked perks show their coin + point price, and the six hidden perks never appear.Unlock Marathon Lungs (250 coins + 1 point), then upgrade it to level 1 (100 coins) and level 2 (200 coins; needs player Lv 9, the upgrade gate). The button reads UPGRADE · 300 before level 3 and NEED COINS when short.Try to unlock a perk while under-leveled, out of points, or under-funded and confirm the request is rejected with no coin deduction.Reset the perk and confirm: the level clears, the perk re-locks, exactly 550 coins (250 + 100 + 200) come back, and the points return. Changing UpgradeCoinStep in Studio before the reset does not change the 550.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing UnlockPointCost re-prices perks players already own Points are derived: spent reads the current UnlockPointCost of every unlocked perk. Raising a perk's point cost from 1 to 3 takes 2 more points from every player who already unlocked it — their available points can drop to 0. Lowering it gives points back. Coins do not have this problem (the ledger records what was paid); points do. Tune point costs before launch, or pair a raise with a Respec announcement.  Changing STORE_NAME wipes all saved perk + unlock data PerkConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerPerks") is the ProfileStore key for PerkLevels, Unlocked and CoinsSpent. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile — equivalent to wiping all perk progress, unlocks and the refund ledger. Only do this intentionally.  Schema migrations run once per profile migrateAndSeed has two version-guarded steps: schema 1 (one-time wipe) and schema 2 (Perk Rework: bank the v1 unlock coins in PendingLegacyRefund, wipe, pay the refund once the coin profile loads). PerkManager only bumps PerkSchemaVersion forward; editing it back down does not replay cleanly. A future perk-id change that strands old ids needs a new guarded step (schema 3) with its own frozen refund table.
