searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Set up the premium subscription. BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID gates the entire Premium row. While it's "" (the pre-launch default), premium is never granted and the subscription APIs (GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync, PromptSubscriptionPurchase) are skipped entirely — safe to ship pre-launch without spamming errors. In the Creator Dashboard, go to Monetization → Subscriptions and create the subscription first (price, billing period, display copy).Paste its id (format EXP-XXXXXXXXXX) into BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID.Keep the value identical in every place of the universe — BattlePassManager runs place-agnostic (lobby and gameplay both resolve premium status live), so a mismatch would make premium appear/disappear across a teleport. Edit the tier track. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/BattlePassConfig.luau. The base Tiers[level] table (level = 1..MAX_LEVEL) is generated in a loop; edit an individual tier after generation, or edit the loop itself for a track-wide change: -- Bump a single regular tier's Free reward after the fact: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[7].Free = { Type = "Coins", Amount = 300 } -- Or add a one-off Item reward on a non-milestone tier: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[20].Premium = { Type = "Item", ItemId = "SomeAccessoryId" } A Reward is { Type = "Coins", Amount: number } or { Type = "Item", ItemId: string }. An empty ItemId = "" is a placeholder milestone slot — see Gotchas. Milestone tiers (15, 30, 45, 60 in the shipped default) pay a chunkier Free coin bonus plus a Premium Item slot; regular tiers pay Coins on both rows. Add a SeasonOverrides entry for one month (optional). To swap in a different reward for one specific season only (e.g. a themed accessory for this month's milestone) without touching the evergreen base Tiers, add an entry to BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides, keyed by season index (year*12 + month-1, i.e. BattlePassState.seasonIndex), then by tier level: -- Override tier 30's Premium reward for a specific season (e.g. July 2026 = 2026*12+6 = 24318). BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides[24318] = { [30] = { Premium = { Type = "Item", ItemId = "JulyAccessory" } }, } Any row present in SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level] shadows the base Tiers[level] entry for that row, for that one season only — an override that only sets Premium leaves Free on the base table for that tier. BattlePassState.tierReward resolves the override before falling back to Tiers, and both the server (grant) and client (display) call the same function, so they can never disagree. Fill milestone ItemIds. Every milestone tier ships with an empty Premium Item slot (ItemId = "") as a placeholder. Before launch, replace each with a real asset id: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[15].Premium = { Type = "Item", ItemId = "AccessoryAssetId15" } See Gotchas — an unfilled slot silently grants nothing and still marks itself claimed. Tune ExpPerLevel against quest BPExp. BattlePassConfig.ExpPerLevel (a flat number, or a { [level]: number } table for a curve) sets the cumulative EXP cost per tier. The only EXP source is Reward.BPExp on quests (fed via Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted — see Battle Pass — EXP earning), so a full clear's reachability is entirely a function of how much BPExp the quest pool pays out over a month: Flat default: ExpPerLevel = 1000, MAX_LEVEL = 60 → 60,000 total EXP for a full clear.The shipped Scope = "Season" quests alone pay 3000 BPExp each (SeasonJunk/SeasonKills/SeasonDistance = 9,000 for the month) — Daily/Weekly BPExp amounts (e.g. 200–1200 per quest, repeating every rotation) make up the rest.To make a full clear reachable in a month: estimate the average daily/weekly BPExp a reasonably active player earns per day, multiply by ~30, add the Season total, and set ExpPerLevel (or the per-level table) so the running total lands near or under that number. Raise per-quest BPExp values instead of lowering ExpPerLevel if you want the quests to feel more rewarding rather than the track to feel shorter.A { [level]: number } table lets early tiers cost less (fast early momentum) and late tiers cost more (a grind at the top) — BattlePassState.levelFromExp/progress handle either shape transparently. Add Scope = "Season" quests (optional). Season quests are the dedicated battle pass EXP feed — the whole set is active for the entire month (no rotation/shuffle, unlike Daily/Weekly). Add an entry to QuestConfig.Quests in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/QuestConfig.luau: SeasonCrafting = { Scope = "Season", Category = "Personal", Metric = QuestConfig.Metrics.JunkCollected, Target = 2000, DisplayName = "Season Scrapper", Description = "Collect 2,000 junk this season", Reward = { Coins = 0, Exp = 0, BPExp = 3000 } }, Metric must be one of QuestConfig.Metrics, same as any other quest — see Tune Quests — Add a quest for wiring a brand-new metric. The shipped Season quests pay Coins = 0, Exp = 0 and only BPExp — Season quests exist purely to move the battle pass track, not the coin/XP economy — but this isn't enforced; a Season quest can also pay coins/exp if you want it to. No Counts entry applies to Scope = "Season" — every Season quest in the pool is always active, so add exactly as many as you want visible this month.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Confirm BattlePassClient.GetProgress() returns level 0, Exp 0 on a fresh profile, and BattlePassClient.GetTiers() reflects your edited Tiers/SeasonOverrides.Complete a quest carrying BPExp and confirm BattlePassClient.Changed fires with the level/progress advancing accordingly.Call BattlePassClient.Claim(); confirm BattlePassClient.GetClaimableSummary() returns (0, 0, 0) immediately after (idempotent — a second claim finds nothing outstanding).If testing Premium: set a real SUBSCRIPTION_ID, subscribe as a test account, and confirm BattlePassClient.IsPremium() flips to true and a retroactive sweep grants every reached Premium tier for the season.If you changed SeasonOverrides, confirm the override actually landed on the current season index (BattlePassState.seasonIndex(os.time())) — an override keyed to the wrong season silently never applies.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved data BattlePassConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerBattlePass") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets session-locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile: all season progress and claimed flags become unreachable. Only do this intentionally, and change it in both places together.  An empty ItemId slot grants nothing — and is still marked claimed A milestone Item reward left at ItemId = "" is a placeholder. Granting it fires no Signals.OnBattlePassItemGranted (there's nothing to hand off to an inventory system) but the claimed flag is still set, so the player never sees that tier offered again — even after you later fill in a real ItemId. Fill every milestone slot before launch, not after.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Change a perk's numeric values. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau and adjust the entry: IronConstitution = { Category = "Personal", DisplayName = "Iron Constitution", Order = 1, Description = "+{1} max health", MaxLevel = 10, -- ← cap Buffs = { { Key = "HPBonus", PerLevel = 0.04 } }, -- ← buff per level (0.04 = 4%) UnlockCost = 0, UnlockLevel = 0, UnlockPointCost = 0, UpgradeCoinStep = 100 }, -- ← level n costs 100 × n coins PerLevel is a fraction (not percent) unless the buff's Format says otherwise. The buff folder attribute is PerLevel * level, so a change here propagates automatically — no code change needed. Format only changes the GUI text: "percent" (default), "count", "total" (1 + value, used by Wide Net), "seconds". Change upgrade prices. UpgradeCoinStep sets the coin price of each level: level n costs UpgradeCoinStep × n coins plus 1 point. The catalog uses 100 for perks unlocked at level 0–9, 200 for 10–19, and 350 for 20+. A price change never changes refunds: respec returns exactly what each player paid, read from the CoinsSpent ledger (see Coin ledger). Add a new perk — declare it in PerkConfig.Perks. Pick a unique id, a Category ("Personal" or "Party"), Order (display order within the tab), DisplayName, Description with {1}, {2} … placeholders (one per buff), MaxLevel, one or more Buffs entries with unique keys, the unlock fields, and UpgradeCoinStep. Set Hidden = true if its consumer does not exist yet: the perk is then not listed and cannot be unlocked (PERK_UNAVAILABLE). Wire a consumer. Read the value through PerkBuffRead — never with a new inline folder lookup: Personal: PerkBuffRead.Personal(player, "MyKey")Party: PerkBuffRead.Party("MyKey") Apply it with the shared math: bonuses value * (1 + b), reductions PerkBuffRead.Reduce(value, b) (never below 10% of base), material costs PerkBuffRead.ReduceCost(cost, b) (rounded up), duration speed-ups duration / (1 + b). Read it fresh each time it is needed so a mid-run change applies live. Server checks read the server's own copy; a client read is for prediction and visuals only. Understand the point economy before tuning it. Each XP level grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point — no separate point storage.Available points = playerLevel - spent, where spent = perk levels + UnlockPointCost of unlocked perks in that pool.You cannot tune the point grant rate without changing PerkState.available and PerkManager.replicate in tandem. There is intentionally no config for it. Know what respec does. Players can respec a pool or one perk from the GUI. The server clears the levels, re-locks non-starter perks, and refunds every coin in CoinsSpent for them via CoinManager.RefundCoins (exact, not scaled by Pocket Change's CoinGainBonus). Points return automatically. Change a shop perk's numbers. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShopPerkConfig.luau. A shop perk has a fixed Value per buff (no levels). Its Description is hand-written, so change the number in the text too. Example: Gold Rush pays the JunkCoinsT4 / JunkCoinsT5 Buff values, and its Description repeats them. Timers and counters (SALVAGE_DRONE_SECONDS, OVERCLOCK_EVERY, …) are constants at the top of the file; their Descriptions repeat them as well.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled. The Output shows no assert failure from PerkState or PerkBuffRead (Studio-only self-checks).Open the perk panel (P).Upgrade a perk and confirm: The level counter increments and the coins drop by UpgradeCoinStep × level.In Explorer, ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId> shows the updated attribute(s).The downstream consumer reflects the change (e.g. Humanoid MaxHealth for Iron Constitution). Reset the perk and confirm levels reset, points return, and the refund equals everything paid on it.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Add a quest. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/QuestConfig.luau and add an entry to QuestConfig.Quests: JunkDailyC = { Scope = "Daily", Category = "Personal", Metric = QuestConfig.Metrics.JunkCollected, Target = 60, DisplayName = "Junk Fanatic", Description = "Collect 60 junk", Reward = { Coins = 350, Exp = 160 } }, Metric must be one of QuestConfig.Metrics (EnemyKills, DistanceTravelled, JunkCollected). Reusing an already-wired metric needs no code change — QuestManager and QuestSourcesLoader pick it up automatically the next time QuestState.selectQuests includes it in the rotation.To track a new kind of progress, wire it in src/ServerScriptService/QuestSourcesLoader.server.luau first: add a new key to QuestConfig.Metrics, then call QuestManager.ReportProgress(actor, metricKey, amount) (has an actor — credits Personal + fans out to Party) or QuestManager.ReportPartyProgress(metricKey, amount) (ownerless world event — Party only) from wherever the underlying game event fires. See Quests — Sources for the three existing examples.Category ("Personal" or "Party") and Scope ("Daily" or "Weekly") determine which sub-pool the quest rotates into — see Quests — Buckets. Choose Target and Reward. Target is the raw progress amount required (same units the source reports — e.g. junk count, enemy kills, distance units). Compare against similar existing quests of the same Scope/Metric to keep difficulty consistent (e.g. JunkDailyA = 25 vs JunkWeeklyA = 250, a 10x jump from daily to weekly).Reward.Coins / Reward.Exp are paid once per claim via CoinManager.AddCoins(player, coins, "Quest:"..questId) (scaled by the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus, like any other earned coins — see Economy) and XPManager.AddXP(player, exp). Scale both together with Target so effort-to-reward stays proportionate; weekly quests in the shipped pool pay roughly 8x their daily counterparts.DisplayName/Description are shown by a future GUI via QuestClient's QuestView; Description should read as an activity sentence (e.g. "Collect 25 junk") since there's no separate progress-text field. Icon is optional (nil = none). Adjust Counts per period. QuestConfig.Counts controls how many quests of each category rotate in per scope: QuestConfig.Counts = { Daily = { Personal = 1, Party = 2 }, Weekly = { Personal = 1, Party = 1 }, } Raising a count (e.g. Daily.Party = 3) requires at least that many quests of that Scope+Category to exist in QuestConfig.Quests — QuestState.selectQuests clamps to math.min(count, #pool), so an under-populated pool silently rotates in fewer quests than configured rather than erroring. Add enough quest entries before raising a count. Shift reset boundaries. Resets happen at local midnight, where "local" is set by QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset — a fixed offset in seconds from UTC (pre-launch default -5 * 3600 = US Eastern, the largest single Roblox player timezone). This is the one knob to change to re-timezone the whole system; set it to 0 for pure UTC. It's a fixed offset, so it does not follow daylight saving — during summer (EDT) resets land one wall-clock hour later. QuestConfig.DailyResetOffset (= -ResetTimezoneOffset, day rolls at 00:00 local) and QuestConfig.WeeklyResetOffset (= 345600 - ResetTimezoneOffset; the 4-day base aligns week starts to Monday since the Unix epoch was a Thursday) are derived from it — change ResetTimezoneOffset, not these two directly, unless you want the daily and weekly boundaries in different timezones. Changing any of them takes effect immediately for every player on their next ensureCurrent check (the periodic rollover tick, or their next join/progress/claim) — there's no migration needed, but changing a boundary mid-period can make the live rollover fire earlier or later than players expect for whichever period is in flight. Prefer changing these during a maintenance window (see Disruption) rather than live. Keep the value identical in the lobby and gameplay places (it's the same shared file) or the two places will disagree on which period is active.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Confirm QuestClient.GetQuests() (or a print in a test script) returns the expected active ids for the current period, matching what QuestState.selectQuests would compute server-side.Trigger the relevant source (collect junk, defeat a tagged enemy, or wait through a train-running distance tick) and confirm the matching quest's Progress advances and QuestClient.Changed fires.Complete a quest and call QuestClient.Claim(questId); confirm coins and exp are granted exactly once, and a second claim attempt fails with ALREADY_CLAIMED (result code 5).If you changed Counts, confirm the newly-added quest pool member actually appears in rotation (rotation is seeded by period index, so you may need to wait for a period boundary or temporarily lower ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS to observe it sooner).

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved quest data QuestConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerQuests") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets QuestManager's session-locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile: all prior progress, claimed flags, and the never-reset Lifetime table (the perk seam) become unreachable. Only do this intentionally, and change it in both places together.  Removing a quest id that's currently active can strand progress QuestState.selectQuests only picks from ids present in QuestConfig.Quests at call time. Deleting an id mid-period means any player with progress toward it simply loses visibility into that entry (the stored Progress[questId] value lingers harmlessly in the profile until the bucket resets, but nothing can claim it). Prefer retiring a quest by leaving it in the pool with an unreachable Target change only at a period boundary, or accept the stranded-progress edge case for a rarely-hit quest.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the shredder config.All shredder constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShredderConfig.luau. Tune hold duration.The required hold scales linearly between one junk item and MAX_JUNK_COUNT items: Field	Default	EffectMIN_HOLD_DURATION	0.3 s	Hold time required for exactly 1 junk item MAX_HOLD_DURATION	3.5 s	Hold time required when carrying MAX_JUNK_COUNT or more items MAX_JUNK_COUNT	10	Junk count at which duration is fully capped at MAX_HOLD_DURATION Increase MAX_HOLD_DURATION to make large batches feel weightier. Keep MIN_HOLD_DURATION above the sum of normal round-trip latency to avoid the server rejecting fast single-item shreds. Tune arc animation (client-side cosmetic). Field	Default	EffectARC_HEIGHT_BOOST	5 studs	Extra Y added to the arc midpoint — controls arc peak height ARC_DURATION	0.55 s	Travel time per cosmetic piece from spawn to landing LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS	1.5 studs	Random spread around LandingPoint Piece count, stagger, rest time, and the fly-to-HUD leg live in MaterialHudConfig — see Material Pool. Handle anti-exploit tolerances with care.These fields directly affect server-side rejection rates. Tighten them only after validating against real network conditions: Field	Default	Risk of over-tighteningINTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE	5 studs	Added on top of INTERACT_DISTANCE (10 studs) server-side to cover positional desync. Reducing below 3 will cause false rejections on high-latency clients. HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE	0.5 s	Subtracted from required hold when server validates timing. Setting below 0.3 will reject legitimate completions on 150ms+ RTT connections. PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN	1.0 s	Minimum gap between consecutive successful shreds per player. Do not set below 0.5 s. Adjust material yield.Material types produced by a shred are determined by JunkConfig.MaterialRules in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau: MaterialRules = { Metal = {"Metal"}, Wood = {"Wood"}, Energy = {"Energy"}, } The shredder credits only Wood and Metal: ShredderServer.computeYield counts those two. MaterialPool also holds Energy, but Energy is credited on grab, never shredded. A new shreddable material needs computeYield and the MaterialPool whitelist extended, plus a HUD row (MaterialPoolClient.Materials); a CraftingMaterials template is optional (without one its fly effect skips straight to 2D). Verify Studio asset setup before testing.The shredder system requires the following to be in place in the live place: Each workbench Model in Workspace must be tagged Workbench (CollectionService).Each workbench Model must have its PrimaryPart set.Each workbench should contain a child Model named TrajectoryPoints (field: TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: SpawnPoint (field: SPAWN_POINT_NAME) and LandingPoint (field: LANDING_POINT_NAME). Tag this model with PlacementIgnore. If missing, the pool is still credited and the effect starts at the workbench pivot.ReplicatedStorage should contain a Folder named CraftingMaterials (field: MATERIALS_FOLDER) with Tool templates Wood and Metal, each with a BasePart child named Handle. Clients clone the Handle for the cosmetic arc; without it the effect skips straight to the 2D fly.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Run a solo session, carry a mix of junk counts (1 item, 5 items, 10 items), and hold the shredder interaction. Confirm hold durations roughly match the linear interpolation between MIN_HOLD_DURATION and MAX_HOLD_DURATION. Watch the arc land near LandingPoint, then the pieces fly into the Materials HUD, and confirm the HUD total rises by the yield.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Change a node's cost or duration.Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ResearchConfig.luau and edit the Levels table on the node: Shield_Alpha = { DisplayName = "Shield α", Description = "+50 maximum shield energy.", GuiPath = "TrainShield.TrainShield1", Prereqs = nil, MaxLevel = 1, Effects = { { Type = "StatBuff", Key = "MaxHP", PerLevel = 50 } }, Levels = { [1] = { Cost = { Metal = 25 }, Duration = 30 } }, -- ← cost / time }, Cost is a { [material]: number } map spent from the server-wide Material Pool — only Wood and Metal are valid (any other key makes MaterialPool.Spend refuse the enqueue), matching the authored WoodCostContainer/MetalCostContainer. Duration is in seconds and is the wall-clock time the node takes to complete while fuel is available — see step 2 below. Both values take effect immediately for any job enqueued after the change; jobs already queued or active keep the cost/duration they were enqueued with (no live re-pricing). Every node ships at MaxLevel = 1 today, so in practice only Levels[1] exists. Changing an Effects entry's PerLevel (for StatBuff) or DrainPerLevel (for FuelEfficiency) changes the buff granted — see step 5 for the effect shapes. No code change is needed; ResearchEffectsDispatcher recomputes buffs from every node's Effects list on every level-up. Review the fuel and pause behavior before retuning it. FUEL_CAP (default 100) — the fuel reserve ceiling.FUEL_BURN_RATE (default 1.0/sec) — how fast fuel burns while a job is active. Raising this makes fuel run out faster relative to node Duration, so jobs pause more often; consider raising FUEL_PER_POINT in tandem if you raise this.FUEL_PER_POINT (default 2) — bench fuel per pool Energy point; a refuel fills to FUEL_CAP and spends only the points needed. Tune this against FUEL_BURN_RATE * <typical node Duration> so a single refuel roughly covers the jobs you want it to. A job's elapsed only advances while fuel is available (ResearchState.advance clamps effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel / burnRate)), so at FUEL_BURN_RATE = 1.0 and FUEL_CAP = 100, a fully-fueled bench can sustain 100 seconds of active research before needing a refuel. Change the queue depth.QUEUE_MAX (default 3) caps how many jobs can wait behind the active one (ResearchState.validateEnqueue rejects with QUEUE_FULL beyond this). It matches the three authored QueueButton1..3 slots in StarterGui.TechTreeGui — raising it beyond 3 needs matching Studio work (more queue slot Frames) or the extra queued jobs will have nowhere to render; lowering it forces more frequent bench visits. Change the cancel refund fraction.ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION (default 0.5) is the fraction of the active job's cost refunded when it is cancelled — queued jobs always refund at 1.0 (full), since they haven't started consuming fuel/time yet. Set this to 1.0 to make cancelling an in-progress job free, or 0 to make active progress non-refundable. This does not affect the cascade behavior itself (see Research Bench — Cascade-cancel) — only the fraction applied to the active job's refund. Add a new node.Unlike the old code-generated GUI, a new node needs both a config entry and a Studio card — TechTreeGuiController only binds cards that already exist under StarterGui.TechTreeGui...TechScrollingFrame; it does not create them. Author the card in Studio first: duplicate an existing card Frame (keeps TechText/StatusContainer/UIStroke/UICorner/UIPadding) under the right branch frame, rename it, and wire its ConnectionLines attribute (outgoing — the comma-separated Line* frames running out of it, if any) plus the new/incoming line(s) on whichever card(s) should point into it. Declare it in ResearchConfig.Nodes. Pick a unique key (the nodeId, <Branch>_<Name> by convention), DisplayName and Description (both shown — DisplayName/timer on the card, both plus Description in the detail panel), GuiPath ("<BranchFrame>.<CardFrame>", matching the card you just authored), an optional Prereqs list (other nodes' ids — all must reach level ≥ 1 before this node accepts enqueues; nil means available from the start), MaxLevel (1 for every shipped node — leave it at 1 unless you deliberately want a multi-level node, which also needs a QueueButton/queue-slot rethink since the GUI assumes one job per node), an optional Gamepass id (0/nil = no gate), and Levels (one {Cost, Duration} entry per level from 1 to MaxLevel). Example — a new single-level "Reinforced Hull" node gated behind both Shield_Gamma and Shield_EfficiencyPlus: TrainShield_ReinforcedHull = { DisplayName = "Reinforced Hull", Description = "+75 maximum shield energy.", GuiPath = "TrainShield.TrainShield5", Prereqs = { "Shield_Gamma", "Shield_EfficiencyPlus" }, MaxLevel = 1, Effects = { { Type = "StatBuff", Key = "MaxHP", PerLevel = 75 } }, Levels = { [1] = { Cost = { Metal = 260, Wood = 40 }, Duration = 90 } }, }, Choose an Effects list shape (omit entirely — Effects = nil — for an unlock-flag node with no buff; a node can list more than one effect, see Shield_Efficiency/Shield_Delta in ResearchConfig for two-entry examples): { Type = "StatBuff", Key = <attributeName>, PerLevel = <number> } — the effect handler in ResearchEffectsDispatcher sums PerLevel * level across every node sharing the same Key into that attribute on ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs. Reuse an existing Key (e.g. "MaxHP") to stack with existing nodes, or introduce a new Key — publishing a key with no consumer is safe (it just sits in the folder, as ShieldStrength/ShieldEfficiency/ShieldAutoRegen do today) but be deliberate about it, not accidental; wire a real consumer if you want the buff to do something.{ Type = "FuelEfficiency", DrainPerLevel = <number, 0 < n < 1> } — multiplies into ResearchBuffs.FuelEfficiency as DrainPerLevel ^ level (values below 1 reduce drain; e.g. 0.85 per level means 3 levels compound to 0.85^3 ≈ 0.614). TrainFuelManager already reads this attribute — no new consumer needed if you're adding a fuel-efficiency node.Any other Type string logs a warn and no-ops in ResearchEffectsDispatcher — safe to author a node ahead of its gameplay wiring, but the buff will not apply until a handler exists.nil — an unlock-flag node. Once it reaches level 1, ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> is written; wire a Workbench recipe's RequiresNode to that same id (see Workbench Crafting), or read the folder from any other gate you want to add. Reload in Studio: ResearchConfig.validate() warns on any unknown Prereqs id, a Prereqs cycle, a missing GuiPath, or an Effects entry with no dispatcher handler. TechTreeGuiController's bind pass separately warns if GuiPath doesn't resolve to a card, or if the card you authored isn't claimed by any node — fix both classes of warning before testing. Test in Studio: join at the bench, open the tree, confirm the new card is locked/greyed until its Prereqs are met, select it and enqueue, and confirm materials are deducted immediately. Let it complete (or refuel to speed through fuel pauses) and confirm the effect applies — check the ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs attribute in Explorer for a StatBuff/FuelEfficiency node, or ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> for an unlock-flag node.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled, walk to the placed bench under workspace.PlacedObjects.Open the tree (TechPromptPart prompt) and select/enqueue a cheap node.Confirm materials are deducted immediately (before the job completes) and the in-progress panel shows the job advancing, with the card's stroke pulsing (InProgress state).Let fuel run to 0 (or start with an empty bench) and confirm the progress bar stops advancing; click Refuel in the queue panel with Energy in the pool and confirm progress resumes.Cancel the active job from the in-progress panel — confirm it refunds at ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION and the card returns to Available. Queue a job, then cancel it from its QueueButton slot — confirm a full refund and that ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked/ResearchBuffs do not update for a job that never completed.Let a StatBuff node complete and confirm the target attribute in ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs updates and the card turns Unlocked (cyan), or let an unlock-flag node complete and confirm ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> appears and the corresponding Workbench recipe ungreys.If testing a Gamepass-gated node, confirm enqueue is rejected with GAMEPASS_REQUIRED while ungated, and succeeds after granting the pass in Studio (or setting BIOME_SELECTOR_GAMEPASS_ID to a pass you own).

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the stamina config.All tunable constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau. This file is shared between client and server, so one edit propagates to both sides. Adjust core stamina values. Field	Default	EffectMaxStamina	100	Pool ceiling StaminaDrain	10	Units drained per second while sprinting StaminaRegen	15	Units regenerated per second when not sprinting RegenDelay	1.4	Seconds after sprint ends before regen starts Adjust sprint feel. Field	Default	EffectWalkSpeed	16	Base walk speed (studs/s) SprintSpeed	24	Speed while sprinting DefaultFOV	70	Camera FOV at walk SprintFOV	85	Camera FOV during sprint FOV transitions are animated by SprintController; changing the values here is enough — no animation code changes needed. See Change Sprint Behavior for keybind and state-machine edits. Adjust sprint keybinds (if needed).The SprintBinds array accepts any mix of Enum.KeyCode and Enum.UserInputType values: SprintBinds = { Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB }, Add or replace entries. Both SprintController and StaminaManager read from the same config array. Tune buff parameters.Three buff types are defined; each has a Duration (seconds) and, where applicable, a Strength multiplier: StaminaRegenBuff = { Strength = 1.75, Duration = 18 } -- multiplies StaminaRegen StaminaUsageBuff = { Strength = 0.5, Duration = 15 } -- multiplies StaminaDrain InfiniteStaminaBuff = { Duration = 10 } -- disables drain entirely Strength is a multiplier applied to the base drain or regen rate. A Strength below 1.0 on StaminaUsageBuff means less drain (easier). Update buff icons (if adding a new icon).Icon asset IDs are in BuffIcons: BuffIcons = { InfiniteStamina = "rbxassetid://136295729783969", RegenMultiplier = "rbxassetid://126110497899525", UsageMultiplier = "rbxassetid://116908939168654", } Replace the rbxassetid://... string with a new uploaded asset ID. Validate client feel and server authority.SprintController (client) predicts drain and regen locally. StaminaManager (server) is the source of truth and corrects the client via packets. After saving, test in a live Studio session: sprint until exhausted, confirm drain/regen rates match the new values, and confirm the server correction does not cause jarring snaps. Test buff interactions.Trigger each buff type (via a test script or the existing pickup pathway) while sprinting. Confirm: StaminaRegenBuff accelerates refill during and after sprint.StaminaUsageBuff visibly slows drain while active.InfiniteStaminaBuff allows indefinite sprinting with no drain.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Sprint until stamina is depleted, release sprint, and confirm the regen delay then regen rate match the new config values. Trigger a buff and confirm it overrides base rates correctly. Check the Output window for any StaminaManager sync errors.

searchDocs.content: Open the placement config.Visual and icon settings live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau. Replace icon asset IDs.The Icons table holds one entry per toolbar button: Icons = { GridOn = "rbxassetid://118749020984103", GridOff = "rbxassetid://132920215751528", GhostUnlocked = "rbxassetid://132512888685903", GhostLocked = "rbxassetid://128344634676430", } Replace the rbxassetid://... value for any icon you want to update. Upload the new image in Studio's Asset Manager first to get a valid asset ID. The key names (GridOn, GridOff, GhostUnlocked, GhostLocked) must remain unchanged — BuildModeGuiController looks them up by key. Adjust ghost appearance. Field	Default	EffectVisualGhostTransparency	0.45	Opacity of main model parts during ghost preview CollisionBoxGhostTransparency	0.65	Opacity of the CollisionBox part during preview OtherGhostVisualTransparency	0.60	Opacity of other parts in other players' ghosts ShowCollisionBox	false	Set true to make CollisionBox visible during preview (debug aid) ColorValid	Color3.fromRGB(100, 210, 255)	Tint when placement is valid ColorInvalid	Color3.fromRGB(255, 80, 80)	Tint when placement is blocked ColorTweenTime	0.12 s	Duration of color transition between valid/invalid states Adjust ghost movement responsiveness. Field	Default	EffectFreeModeLerpSpeed	20	How quickly the ghost follows the cursor in free mode RotationLerpSpeed	15	How quickly the ghost rotates when the player rotates the item GhostUpdateHz	20	Raycast update rate (Hz) — lower values reduce CPU cost but feel less smooth Adjust the grid overlay. Field	Default	EffectGridTextureId	"rbxassetid://6372755229"	Decal texture applied to build area surfaces during grid mode GridTransparency	0.35	Opacity of the grid overlay (0 = opaque, 1 = invisible) Keep the button-to-signal mapping consistent.src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/BuildModeGuiController.client.luau wires each toolbar button to a Signals event. If you add a new button (e.g. a new toggle), you must: Add the new icon key to PlacementConfig.Icons.Create a corresponding Signals entry in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau if the button drives new behavior.Wire the button in BuildModeGuiController to fire/subscribe to that signal.Update the signals map (and the networking map if the signal crosses the client/server boundary). Do not add raw RemoteEvent calls from BuildModeGuiController — all cross-boundary communication must go through Packets. Test mobile input parity.Build mode must be fully operable without a keyboard. In a Studio mobile emulation session (or on device): Confirm all toolbar buttons are reachable and tap targets are large enough.Confirm grid/free toggle and rotation controls work via touch.Confirm the ghost follows touch drag correctly. Test desktop input parity.In a standard Studio session: Confirm keyboard shortcuts for grid toggle and rotation still fire correctly after any icon or signal changes.Confirm the cursor-following ghost is smooth at the configured GhostUpdateHz.

Else rows are styled from the button. MaxVisible: number?, -- cap visible rows; scroll beyond RowHeight: number?, -- pixel height per row (default 28) ArrowUp: string?, ArrowDown: string?, -- arrow image overrides } local dropdown = Dropdown.new(button, options, config?) searchDocs.title: Notes​
searchDocs.content: The host ScreenGui should use Global ZIndexBehavior so the open list (high ZIndex) draws over sibling content.All connections are owned by a Janitor and released on :Destroy().When no OptionTemplate is given, each row's Label is a clone of the button's Option label, so rows inherit its text styling (alignment,TextScaled, font, RichText, child UIPadding) and stay in sync if the button is restyled. searchDocs.title: Core rule: one Janitor per lifecycle scope​
searchDocs.content: Each distinct lifecycle gets exactly one Janitor. When that lifecycle ends, call:Cleanup or :Destroy on it (see below for which to use).  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Janitor = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Janitor) local janitor = Janitor.new() -- Track a signal connection (cleaned up by calling :Disconnect) janitor:Add(inst.Event:Connect(fn), "Disconnect") -- Track an Instance (cleaned up by calling :Destroy) janitor:Add(part, "Destroy") -- Tear down and reuse (leaves the Janitor alive for the next cycle) janitor:Cleanup() -- Tear down and discard (the Janitor itself is gone afterward) janitor:Destroy()

searchDocs.title: Cleanup vs Destroy​
searchDocs.content: Method	When to use	Typical example:Cleanup()	The Janitor is module-level and reused across respawns or re-equips.	characterJanitor, backpackJanitor — cleaned on every CharacterAdded, then refilled. :Destroy()	The Janitor is created per-entry and discarded when the entry is removed.	WorkbenchEntry.Cleaner, engine/lever entry janitors.  Using :Destroy on a reused janitor silently breaks the next cycle because the object becomes unusable. Using :Cleanup on a per-entry janitor leaks the janitor table itself. Match the method to the ownership model.

searchDocs.title: Keyed-collection pattern​
searchDocs.content: When managing a dynamic set of entries (workbenches, junk pickups, registered engines, etc.), give each entry its own Janitor stored under a predictable key:  -- Type annotation (Luau) type Entry = { model: Model, cleaner: Janitor.Janitor, } local registry: { [string]: Entry } = {} local function register(id: string, model: Model) local entry: Entry = { model = model, cleaner = Janitor.new(), } entry.cleaner:Add(model, "Destroy") entry.cleaner:Add(model.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child) -- ... end), "Disconnect") registry[id] = entry end local function unregister(id: string) local entry = registry[id] if entry then entry.cleaner:Destroy() -- per-entry → Destroy registry[id] = nil end end   The pattern guarantees that removing an entry also disconnects every signal and destroys every instance that entry owns, with no possibility of leaking a handle.

searchDocs.title: Singleton exception​
searchDocs.content: Top-level controller connections that live for the full session do not need a Janitor. If the connection is created once at script root and never torn down (for example, Players.LocalPlayer.CharacterAdded at the top of a client controller), wrapping it in a Janitor adds overhead with no benefit.  Only use a Janitor when the scope can end before the script does.

searchDocs.title: Why a PlayerAdded push is unreliable​
searchDocs.content: Packet (the vendored networking library) connects the underlyingRemoteEvent at module-require time and dispatches every incoming payload into a plain Signal with no backlog. That connection is almost always live well before the script that actually cares has connected its own handler — every client script that requires Packets at the top of the file opens the door before anything downstream is listening. Anything the server sends in that window is dispatched into a signal with no subscribers and is gone. There is no retry, and no way for a late subscriber to ask for the current value.  Players.PlayerAdded compounds this: it is not guaranteed to fire for the first player in a server, who may already be in Players when the server script runs. A manager that only connects the event — never also iteratingPlayers:GetPlayers() — can miss that player's join entirely.  Put together: a one-shot PlayerAdded → FireClient push can be dropped by either the player already being present, or the client not yet listening, and the sender has no idea it happened.

searchDocs.title: The mechanism​
searchDocs.content: JoinSync inverts the direction. The client, not the server, decides when it is ready:  ClientReadyController.client.luau fires Packets.ClientReady (client → server, zero payload) exactly once, after game.Loaded plus a task.defer— giving every other StarterPlayerScript a chance to finish connecting.JoinSync.Initialize() (called once, from JoinSyncLoader.server.luau) handles that packet by running every registered sender for that player, each isolated in its own task.spawn + xpcall so one erroring sender can't starve the rest.JoinSync.Register(name, sender) also serves any player who is alreadyready at the moment of registration. This is what makes registration order and script-load timing irrelevant — a manager whose Initialize() runs late still reaches everyone.A per-player ready flag (cleared on PlayerRemoving) means a repeatedClientReady is a no-op, so a client can't make the server replay every system's snapshot in a loop.  name must be unique per system — it exists only to label the warning if that sender's send errors, or to catch a double-registration (skipped, with a warning, rather than double-sending).

searchDocs.title: The rules​
searchDocs.content: Follow these when adding any new server-authoritative readout that a client needs on join:  Register a JoinSync sender; never connect PlayerAdded to push a snapshot. PlayerAdded fires too early relative to the client's own readiness, and can miss the first player outright. JoinSync fires exactly when the client says it's listening.Read state at send time, inside the sender; never capture it at registration. Register is called once, at server startup, long before any player exists. A sender is a closure that reads live state (an upvalue, a table lookup) each time it runs — it must never close over a value snapshotted at registration, or every player will be served whatever the state happened to be at boot.Server-side record creation stays on PlayerAdded; only the send moves. If a manager's PlayerAdded handler both creates a per-player record and pushes it, keep the record creation where it is — gameplay code may read that record before the client is ready — and move only theFireClient call into a JoinSync.Register sender. That handler still needs the usual Players:GetPlayers() bootstrap loop alongside itsPlayerAdded connection, so a player already present when the server script runs still gets a record.Never invent a client-side default for a server-authoritative value.Render a placeholder ("—", a neutral colour, a zero-width bar — whatever fits the widget) until the real snapshot arrives, and snap directly to the first real value instead of easing from a guess. A guessed default is worse than no data: it looks like an answer.Never seed an extrapolation baseline from a client-read clock.workspace:GetServerTimeNow() is the client's own converging estimate of server time; read early in the client's life (module load, script start) it has not converged yet. Extrapolate only from a serverTime the server itself stamped onto the snapshot it sent.  Rule 4 and rule 5 are what actually fixed the reported bug — JoinSync alone makes the send reliable, but the old fallback snapshots (seeded from config defaults, timestamped from an unconverged client clock) were what turned an occasional dropped packet into a HUD that always swept 100% → 0% on join. SeeTrainFuelGuiController and TrainShieldGuiController for the placeholder pattern, and TrainStateCache for the shared extrapolation helper that returns nil until a real snapshot lands.

searchDocs.title: Worked example​
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelManager.Initialize() registers its join-time sender instead of connecting Players.PlayerAdded:  -- The client send waits until the client is listening; see JoinSync. JoinSync.Register("TrainFuel", function(player: Player) Packets.TrainStateSync:FireClient(player, fuelAtLastEvent, currentRate, isBraked, isStalled, lastEventTime) end)   fuelAtLastEvent, currentRate, isBraked, isStalled, and lastEventTimeare all upvalues read fresh every time the closure runs (rule 2) — a player who joins mid-round gets the fuel level as of their join, not whatever it was when the server booted.  MaterialPool follows the same pattern: it registers "MaterialPool" at module load and sends MaterialPoolUpdate with the live Wood/Metal totals and zero gain, so the joining client's HUD snaps to the real totals with no fly-to-HUD effect. It deliberately broadcasts (:Fire) instead of:FireClient: the Packet library flushes the broadcast buffer before per-player buffers each frame, so a FireClient snapshot could arrive aftera same-frame Add broadcast and leave the joiner on stale totals. For the other clients a zero-gain update is a harmless re-render. SeeMaterial Pool.

searchDocs.title: The two deliberate exclusions​
searchDocs.content: Not every server-authoritative system needs a JoinSync sender. Two managers were deliberately left out of this conversion:  AmmoManager pushes nothing at join. Ammo pools start empty, and an empty pool is the correct initial state — there is nothing to snapshot.AmmoPoolSync only fires on award, consume, or equip, none of which need a join-time replay.ArmorManager replicates through an attribute folder, not a packet.Attributes are ordinary replicated Instance state — readable by the client at any time, including before it has connected anything. There is no connect-after-the-fact race to guard against, so JoinSync would add nothing.  If a future system's join state is provably always correct with no send at all (like AmmoManager), or replicates through Instance/attribute state rather than a packet (like ArmorManager), it does not need a JoinSyncsender either. Everything else that pushes a one-shot snapshot to a joining player does.

searchDocs.title: Quick TweenService equivalence​
searchDocs.content: -- TweenService (do NOT use this in client code) TweenService:Create(target, TweenInfo.new(0.5, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), goals):Play() -- MotionMaster equivalent MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, { Duration = 0.5, Model = "EaseOutQuad" })

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Fire-and-forget shorthand. Creates a TweenObject, calls :Play(), and returns it.  MotionMaster.Play(frame, { BackgroundTransparency = 0 }, { Duration = 0.3, Model = "EaseOutQuad" })

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Create(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Returns a TweenObject for manual lifecycle control. Does not start playback.  local tween = MotionMaster.Create(label, { TextTransparency = 1 }, { Duration = 0.5 }) tween:Play()   TweenObject methods​  Method	Description:Play()	Start or restart from current elapsed position. :Pause()	Pause; preserves elapsed time. :Resume()	Resume a paused tween. :Cancel()	Pause and reset to the start value. :Reverse()	Flip direction mid-playback; elapsed time mirrors continuously. :Scrub(alpha)	Jump to a normalized position [0, 1] without playback. :Destroy()	Disconnect all connections and release memory. :OnStep(cb)	Register cb(alpha, dt) — fires every frame. Chainable. :OnComplete(cb)	Register cb() — fires when the tween finishes. Chainable. :OnDestroy(cb)	Register cb() — fires on :Destroy(). Chainable.

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Spring(target, prop, config)​
searchDocs.content: Creates and starts a SpringDriver that follows a dynamically updated endpoint. Supports number and Vector3 properties only.  local driver = MotionMaster.Spring(frame, "Position", { Omega = 18, Zeta = 1.0 }) driver:SetTarget(newPosition) -- update the goal at any time   SpringDriver config fields: Omega (natural frequency), Zeta (damping ratio),MaxSubsteps, FixedDt.  SpringDriver methods: :SetTarget(v), :OnStep(cb), :IsSettled(eps?), :Stop(), :Destroy().

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.fromPreset(presetName, target, prop)​
searchDocs.content: Instantiate a SpringDriver from one of the 16 named presets.  local driver = MotionMaster.fromPreset("UIPanel", frame, "Position")   Named spring presets​  Category	PresetsUI / Interface	UIPanel, UIFade, UIBounce, UISnap Camera	CameraFollow, CameraLag, CameraShake Gameplay objects	RecoilCritical, RecoilSnappy, DoorBouncy, DoorStiff, WeaponSway, JiggleBone Environment	HoverStabilizer, SpringPlatform, HeavyGate

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Sequence(config)​
searchDocs.content: Chain or parallelize TweenObjects. Returns a Sequence.  local seq = MotionMaster.Sequence() -- serial (default) seq:Add(tweenA) seq:Add(tweenB, 0.1) -- 0.1 s gap before tweenB seq:Play() local par = MotionMaster.Sequence({ Parallel = true }) -- all at once par:Add(tweenC) par:Add(tweenD) par:OnComplete(function() print("all done") end) par:Play()   Sequence methods: :Add(tweenObj, delay?), :Play(), :OnComplete(cb), :Destroy().

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.SplineMove(target, controlPoints, config)​
searchDocs.content: Moves target (a BasePart) along an arc-length-reparameterized Catmull-Rom spline.controlPoints is an array of BasePart instances or Vector3 values (minimum 2).  local tween = MotionMaster.SplineMove(cart, { p0, p1, p2, p3 }, { Duration = 4, Model = "EaseInOutCubic", ConstantSpeed = true, -- default true for SplineMove }) tween:Play()   Returns a TweenObject (same lifecycle methods as above).

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.PivotMove(model, targetCFrame, config)​
searchDocs.content: Animates a Model via :PivotTo(), preserving relative part offsets. Accepts a CFrame as the goal.  local tween = MotionMaster.PivotMove(door, openCFrame, { Duration = 0.8, Model = "DoorBouncy", -- preset name accepted for Model field }) tween:Play()

searchDocs.title: Signals Map
searchDocs.content: Signals Map Update this table in the same commit when you add a signal — see also the Add a Signal playbook. Signals are the in-process event bus (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau). Prefer signals over direct module coupling for gameplay events and UI intents. All signals defined here are created at module require time and are singletons for the lifetime of the script. Signal	Producer	Consumers	PurposeSetTrainState	TrainFuelManager (on running-state flip)	JunkService	Slows junk spawn/speed when braked or stalled. Reused by the fuel system. Signal<boolean> SetTrainStarted	TrainFuelManager (false at init, true on first un-brake)	JunkService	Gates whether junk spawns at all; game is frozen until first un-brake. Signal<boolean> ApplyTierMultiplier	PerkEffectsDispatcher (on every party-buff publish, tiers 3–5)	JunkService	Dynamic per-tier spawn-rate multiplier (tier: number, multiplier: number). Fired with 1 + JunkTierRarityBonus for rare tiers on every perk state change. ApplyTypeMultiplier	(no producer yet — planned spawn-modifier hook)	JunkService	Dynamic per-type spawn-rate multiplier (typeName: string, multiplier: number). TryClaimJunk	GrabHook	JunkController	Fire claim request (id: number, hitPos: Vector3); JunkController invokes ReqJunkClaim. TryClaimJunkBatch	GrabHook (Wide Net perk, capacity ≥ 2)	JunkController	Fire batch claim request ({number}) (junk ids); JunkController invokes Packets.ReqJunkClaimBatch. TryFinalizeJunk	GrabHook	JunkController	Fire finalize request (id: number) after retraction completes; JunkController invokes ReqJunkFinalize. OnStaminaValueChanged	StaminaManager (server sync via StaminaStateSync)	HealthStaminaGuiController	Stamina bar update Signal<number>. OnStaminaBuffsChanged	StaminaManager	SprintController	Buff state update Signal<boolean, number, number>. OnSprintToggled	SprintController	HealthStaminaGuiController	Sprint state change Signal<boolean>. searchDocs.title: Formula​
searchDocs.content: From the SliceScale formula devforum thread(post 5: SliceScale = ViewportSize.Y / 2700, i.e. 0.4 at 1080p), generalised to any designed value:  live SliceScale = designed SliceScale * (ViewportSize.Y / 1080)

searchDocs.title: Authoring rule​
searchDocs.content: Set SliceScale in Studio while the viewport is 1080 px tall (e.g. the 1920×1080 device emulator). That value is captured as the designed value the first time the image appears in PlayerGui.

searchDocs.title: Behaviour​
searchDocs.content: Covers every ImageLabel / ImageButton with ScaleType = Slice under the local PlayerGui, including respawned ScreenGuis and runtime-built UI (e.g. Satchel's slot selector). Set ScaleType before parenting so the image is picked up.Rescales on Camera.ViewportSize changes (debounced to one pass per frame) and rebinds when Workspace.CurrentCamera changes.Scales by height only; width is ignored.Do not write SliceScale from other scripts at runtime — the scaler will overwrite it with the captured designed value on the next resize.

searchDocs.title: Season math​
searchDocs.content: The season index is a calendar-month index, not a rolling 30-day window: BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now) = year*12 + (month-1), computed in the timezone defined by BattlePassConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset (a fixed seconds-from-UTC offset, pre-launch default US Eastern -5*3600, mirroring QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset). Being a fixed offset, month boundaries do not track daylight saving.  BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now: number): number BattlePassState.seasonExpiresAt(now: number): number -- unix ts of the 1st of next month   The underlying day math (daysFromCivil) is a pure-integer proleptic-Gregorian calculation (Howard Hinnant's algorithm), so client and server always agree without relying on os.date's host timezone handling. seasonExpiresAt is sent to the client so it can drive a countdown without any client-side date math. The server re-checks online players for a rollover — and refreshes cached premium status — every BattlePassConfig.ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS (default 60s).  The quest system's Season scope (see Quests — Season quests) uses this exact same seasonIndex as its period key, so a battle pass season and its season-long quests always start and end together.

searchDocs.title: EXP earning​
searchDocs.content: There is no gameplay source that awards battle pass EXP directly. Instead, BattlePassManager subscribes to Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted — fired by QuestManager.grantReward on every quest reward grant, manual claim or rollover auto-sweep alike — and reads the optional Reward.BPExp field off the quest's reward table:  Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Connect(function(player, reward) if reward and reward.BPExp then BattlePassManager.AddExp(player, reward.BPExp, "Quest") end end)   Any quest can feed the pass just by adding a BPExp number to its Reward table — no new signal or wiring per quest. The shipped pool leans on this for its dedicated Scope = "Season" quests: three quests (SeasonJunk, SeasonKills, SeasonDistance), the whole set active for the entire month, each paying 0 coins/exp but 3000 BPExp. Regular Daily/Weekly quests also carry smaller BPExp amounts (e.g. JunkDailyA pays 200), so ordinary questing keeps the pass moving too.

searchDocs.title: Tier track and bulk claim​
searchDocs.content: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[level] (level = 1..MAX_LEVEL, MAX_LEVEL = 60) is a { Free: Reward?, Premium: Reward? } pair. A Reward is either { Type = "Coins", Amount } or { Type = "Item", ItemId } (an empty ItemId = "" marks a milestone slot not filled in yet).  Tier kind	Free row	Premium rowRegular	Coins = 100 + (level-1)*10	Coins = 150 + (level-1)*15 Milestone (15/30/45/60)	Chunkier 500-coin bonus	Empty accessory Item slot (to be filled)  BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level] sparsely shadows the base Tiers entry for one specific season only (e.g. swap in a different accessory for one month while keeping the rest of the track the same):  BattlePassState.tierReward(level: number, row: "Free" | "Premium", seasonIndex: number): BattlePassConfig.Reward?   tierReward resolves the override first, falling back to the base table, and is used identically by the server (grant) and client (display) so the two can never disagree.  Level is derived, never stored:  BattlePassState.levelFromExp(exp: number): number BattlePassState.progress(exp: number): (level: number, expIntoLevel: number, expForNextLevel: number)   levelFromExp walks MAX_LEVEL down to 1 and returns the highest level whose cumulative EXP threshold (BattlePassConfig.ExpPerLevel — a flat per-level number or a { [level]: number } table) is met; progress additionally returns the two extra values for a progress bar (both 0 once level >= MAX_LEVEL).  There is only one claim entry point:  function BattlePassManager.ClaimBattlePass(player: Player): (boolean, number, number, number, number)   Packets.ReqClaimBattlePass (no payload) invokes it, and it bulk-banks every unlocked-but-unclaimed reward across both rows in one call — there's no per-tier claim. Premium-row rewards are only granted while the player is currently premium. Claimed flags (ClaimedFree[level] / ClaimedPremium[level]) are set before the grant executes (the same idempotent-guard pattern as QuestManager.ClaimQuest), so a re-entrant call finds nothing outstanding and returns NOTHING_TO_CLAIM rather than double-paying. Returns (ok, reasonCode, freeCount, premiumCount, coinsGranted); counts/coins are 0 on any failure. Result codes (BattlePassResultCodes): OK = 0, NO_PROFILE = 1, NOTHING_TO_CLAIM = 2.

searchDocs.title: Premium (subscriptions)​
searchDocs.content: Premium is never persisted — it's live-resolved from MarketplaceService:GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync(player, SUBSCRIPTION_ID) and cached in-memory per session (premiumCache, keyed by Player). The cache is (re)populated at three points:  Trigger	WhyJoin	Before the first sweep/replicate MarketplaceService.PromptSubscriptionPurchaseFinished	The prompt closing doesn't guarantee a successful purchase, so status is always re-resolved rather than assumed Periodic rollover tick	Bounds staleness to ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS  resolvePremium yields (a web call), so it only ever runs from spawned contexts — never from the synchronous AddExp/ClaimBattlePass paths, which read the cache. On a false→true transition (a fresh subscribe), onPurchaseFinished retroactively runs a sweep granting the Premium row for every tier already reached this season, so buying mid-season immediately feels rewarding instead of only affecting future tiers. Packets.ReqPromptPremium (no payload, server-initiated) calls MarketplaceService:PromptSubscriptionPurchase — the prompt must originate server-side.  While BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID = "" (the pre-launch default), premium is never granted and the subscription APIs are skipped entirely — resolvePremium short-circuits to false and ReqPromptPremium returns false without calling MarketplaceService, so pre-launch never spams errors for a subscription that doesn't exist yet.

searchDocs.title: Rollover and auto-grant sweep​
searchDocs.content: ensureCurrent (called at the top of AddExp and ClaimBattlePass, on join, and on the rollover tick) compares the profile's stored SeasonIndex against BattlePassState.seasonIndex(os.time()). On a mismatch it first auto-grants every reached-but-unclaimed tier from the old season (Free always; Premium only if the player is currently premium) via the same sweep helper the manual claim uses — nothing earned is lost just because a player never opened a claim UI before the month rolled. It then resets Exp = 0, ClaimedFree = {}, ClaimedPremium = {}, and advances SeasonIndex to the current value. Coins and items already granted by the sweep persist wherever they live (the coin wallet, a future inventory) — only the pass's own tier/EXP bookkeeping resets.

searchDocs.title: Item seam​
searchDocs.content: Item-type rewards fire Signals.OnBattlePassItemGranted(player, itemId) — a seam with no consumer this cycle, reserved for a future inventory/accessory system. Milestone tiers ship with an empty Premium Item slot (ItemId = ""); granting one is a no-op (no signal fires) and logs a one-time warning (warnedEmptyItem, a module-level flag) reminding a developer to fill BattlePassConfig with a real asset before launch. The claimed flag is still set even for an empty slot, so it's marked claimed and never re-offered.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: BattlePassClient is a GUI-agnostic read-model, same shape as QuestClient/PerkClient. It caches the authoritative BattlePassStateSync snapshot and derives per-tier views using the same BattlePassState.tierReward the server grants from:  export type TierView = { Level: number, FreeReward: BattlePassConfig.Reward?, PremiumReward: BattlePassConfig.Reward?, IsUnlocked: boolean, IsFreeClaimed: boolean, IsPremiumClaimed: boolean, }   Exposes GetProgress (level, expIntoLevel, expForNextLevel), GetLevel, IsPremium, GetSeasonExpiresAt, GetTiers (all 60, in order), GetClaimableSummary (a preview of what a Claim() would bank right now — counts + coin total, without actually claiming), and fire-and-forget Claim() / PromptPremium() commands. A Changed signal fires on every snapshot update. No GUI ships this cycle — a future screen requires BattlePassClient and subscribes to Changed.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved battle pass data BattlePassConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerBattlePass") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets session-locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile: all season progress and claimed flags become unreachable.  An empty ItemId slot grants nothing — and is still marked claimed A milestone Item reward with ItemId = "" is a placeholder. Granting it fires no OnBattlePassItemGranted signal (nothing to grant) but still flips the claimed flag, so the player never sees it offered again even after you fill in a real ItemId later — fill milestone slots before launch.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Season Surge (BPExpBonus): BattlePassManager.AddExp scales BP EXP × (1 + bonus), rounded down, at least 1.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant QM as QuestManager (server) participant BPM as BattlePassManager (server) participant Client as BattlePassClient (owning client) Note over QM: quest CLAIM or auto-sweep QM->>QM: grantReward() — CoinManager.AddCoins, XPManager.AddXP QM->>BPM: Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Fire(player, quest.Reward) alt reward.BPExp present BPM->>BPM: AddExp(player, reward.BPExp) — ensureCurrent() first BPM->>BPM: profile.Data.Exp += amount alt derived level rose BPM->>BPM: Signals.OnBattlePassLevelUp:Fire(player, newLevel) end BPM->>Client: BattlePassStateSync (season, exp, level, progress, claimed, premium, expiresAt) end Note over Client,BPM: bulk CLAIM Client->>BPM: ReqClaimBattlePass() BPM->>BPM: ensureCurrent(); sweep(1..level) — Free always, Premium if isPremium BPM->>BPM: claimed flags set BEFORE grant (idempotent guard) BPM-->>Client: (ok, reasonCode, freeCount, premiumCount, coinsGranted) BPM->>Client: BattlePassStateSync (reconciled snapshot)

searchDocs.content: Config module: BattlePassConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/BattlePassConfig.luauPlaybook: Tune Battle PassQuestConfig.Quests[id].Reward.BPExp (optional) is how a quest feeds the pass; Scope = "Season" quests are the dedicated monthly source — see Tune Quests.  Field	EffectSTORE_NAME	ProfileStore key — change this only if you intentionally want to wipe all saved battle pass progress. SUBSCRIPTION_ID	The Roblox subscription id whose active status unlocks Premium. Empty ("") disables premium entirely and skips the subscription APIs. ResetTimezoneOffset	Fixed seconds-from-UTC offset the calendar-month boundary is measured in (mirrors QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset). No DST tracking. MAX_LEVEL	Top tier of the track (60). ExpPerLevel	BP EXP required per level — a flat number or a { [level]: number } table. ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS	How often the live server tick re-checks online players for a season rollover and refreshes cached premium status. Tiers[level].Free / .Premium	Base reward per tier per row. SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level]	Sparse per-season tier reward shadowing, keyed by BattlePassState.seasonIndex.

searchDocs.title: The two types​
searchDocs.content: Every armor kind — Ballistic or Energy — is defined entirely by ArmorConfig.Kinds[kindId] (Type, Tier, BaseReduction, Pool, RequiresNode) plus one persisted number: pool remaining. ArmorManager.Absorb drains that number by whatever damage the hit actually absorbed, identically for both types. The only branch is what happens when the pool reaches zero:  Ballistic — the set is destroyed: owned[kindId] is cleared and, if it was worn, Equipped is cleared too. The player is unarmored until they craft another.Energy — the kind stays in Owned and stays Equipped. Absorb returns the full incoming amount unmitigated (pool <= 0 short-circuits before any reduction), so a drained Energy set simply does nothing until ArmorManager.Recharge refills it.

searchDocs.title: The catalog​
searchDocs.content: ArmorConfig.Kinds is the entire catalog — five kinds, no separate tier ladder (Tiers no longer exists; Tier on a kind is a display badge only):  Kind id	Type	Tier	Reduction	Pool	Research nodeLight	Ballistic	1	0.10	250	Armor_Light MedBallistic	Ballistic	2	0.20	500	Armor_MedBallistic MedEnergy	Energy	2	0.14	700	Armor_MedEnergy HeavyBallistic	Ballistic	3	0.30	900	Armor_HeavyBallistic HeavyEnergy	Energy	3	0.22	1200	Armor_HeavyEnergy  By design, the Energy kind at a given tier always reduces less than its Ballistic counterpart (0.14 vs 0.20 at tier 2; 0.22 vs 0.30 at tier 3) — a refillable reserve trades raw mitigation for never being permanently destroyed. Light has no tier-1 Energy counterpart. Reduction, pool size, type and tier are all derived from this table at read time, so retuning a kind here applies retroactively to every player already holding it.

searchDocs.title: Crafting​
searchDocs.content: Each kind has a matching recipe in WorkbenchConfig.Recipes (CraftArmorLight, CraftArmorMedBallistic, CraftArmorMedEnergy, CraftArmorHeavyBallistic, CraftArmorHeavyEnergy), each with Output = { Kind = "Armor", ArmorKind = "<id>" } and its own RequiresNode gate matching the table above. WorkbenchService's craft handler checks CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(player, output) before consuming materials; for an Armor output that calls ArmorManager.OwnsAtFullPool, so crafting a kind already at full pool is refused up front and costs nothing. Crafting a kind that is owned but damaged (or destroyed, for a Ballistic kind) instead calls ArmorManager.Grant, which refills it to full — recrafting is how a set is repaired. Grant also auto-equips the kind if the player has nothing worn, so a player's first craft is immediately useful without a separate equip step.

searchDocs.title: Mitigation​
searchDocs.content: HealthManager.ApplyDamage is the single damage sink for every attack category (Bullet/AOE/environment/NPC). Its internal applyDamageInternal reads the player's ArmorEfficiency perk bonus and calls ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency) on every hit — no caching, so crafting, equipping or recharging armor takes effect on the very next hit. Absorb computes reduction = clamp(kind.BaseReduction * (1 + efficiency), 0, ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap) for whichever kind is equipped, exactly as the armor-efficiency perk (now Plated) already worked before this system existed (see Perks — Armor damage mitigation), then drains the pool by min(amount * reduction, pool). A hit never absorbs more than the pool has left, so the overflow of the hit that breaks a Ballistic set still reaches health in the same call. With nothing equipped, or an Energy kind at zero pool, Absorb returns the full amount and health takes it all.

searchDocs.title: Equipping and recharging​
searchDocs.content: Both Equip and Recharge are workbench actions — ReqEquipArmor and ReqRechargeArmor — handled by ArmorService, which validates the target with WorkbenchStation.IsValidStation and WorkbenchStation.IsPlayerNear (the same checks WorkbenchService uses for crafting) before delegating to ArmorManager. Client input is never trusted: both the bench and the distance are re-derived from server-owned state on every request.  ArmorManager.Recharge refills an owned Energy kind's reserve by spending shared pool Energy via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", Pool − reserve, ArmorConfig.RESERVE_PER_POINT) — only the points needed, stopping at the Pool cap. It draws on the same material pool Energy the train burns for fuel (mirroring TrainFuelManager.handleRefuel), and needs no serialization: the path is synchronous with no yield point, so two in-flight requests can't interleave.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: ArmorClient is a GUI-free read model, structured like PerkClient/QuestClient: it caches the ArmorStateSync snapshot, exposes IsReady/GetArmors/GetEquipped queries returning ArmorView descriptors, carries the Equip/Recharge request/response calls — both are declared with Packet:Response(...), so calling them on the client yields until the server answers and returns (ok, code) and (ok, energyAdded, code) respectively (no optimistic prediction — the server owns ownership and pools) — and fires Changed on every snapshot update. ArmorController.client.luau is the one-line bootstrap that calls ArmorClient.Init() once on join.  The player-facing surface is the Workbench GUI's armory page (ArmoryContainer, reached by the Recharge tab), driven by WorkbenchGuiController. The page is gated on owning at least one armor: with none, the tab, a swipe, gamepad or scroll wheel all bounce back to the workbench page with a "You must wear or craft an armor to access Recharge." toast. The gate checks owned, not worn, because this page is the only place to equip — an unworn owned set (e.g. after a worn Ballistic set broke) must stay reachable. If the last armor breaks while the page is showing, or a reopen lands on it, it silently returns to the workbench page.  Inventory (RightContainer…InventoryContainer.ScrollingFrame) — one item per owned kind, cloned from ExampleItem, in ArmorClient.GetArmors() order. Tapping one selects it; the selected item's UIStroke is opaque, the rest 0.7. With nothing selected (or the selected Ballistic set broke) the selection falls back to the worn kind, then the first owned.Detail — name, EquipButton (worn kind: EQUIPPED, Interactable = false, bg #130f18; any other kind: EQUIP, interactable with AutoButtonColor, bg #383753, sends ReqEquipArmor), base reduction and RECHARGEABLE (TRUE for Energy kinds). Icons borrow the kind's CraftArmor* recipe icon, since ArmorConfig carries no art.Recharge (LeftContainer.ArmorRechargeContainer) — FillBar and percent show the selected kind's PoolFraction; ENERGY RESERVE shows pool Energy. Holding ChargeButton for ArmorConfig.RECHARGE_HOLD_TIME eases the fill toward the level the pool Energy can reach, then sends one ReqRechargeArmor; releasing early (anywhere on screen) snaps it back. HintText always reads HOLD TO RECHARGE, except for a Ballistic kind: there the fill still shows durability, ChargeButton.Interactable is false, and the hint reads CANNOT RECHARGE THIS ARMOR in warning red (230,150,150, readable on the #1f1927 backing). A full Energy reserve also sets Interactable false. With no pool Energy the button stays enabled, and a press toasts "No energy to spare." (ArmorClient.CodeMessages[NO_ENERGY]) instead of starting the hold.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Equipping a depleted Energy kind is allowed ArmorManager.Equip does not check the pool — wearing an Energy kind at zero reserve succeeds and returns Codes.NONE. It is worn and worthless until recharged; this is the intended failure mode, not a bug.  A catalog rename or removal drops the profile's copy, not just the display If a kind id is renamed or deleted from ArmorConfig.Kinds, ArmorManager drops it from Owned (and clears Equipped if it was worn) the next time that player's profile loads — silently, with no refund. Renaming a shipped kind id is effectively deleting it for every player who owns it.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Armor Weave (ArmorRechargeBonus): ArmorManager.Recharge refills RESERVE_PER_POINT / Reduce(1, bonus) per Energy point; WorkbenchGuiController shortens the hold to Reduce(RECHARGE_HOLD_TIME, bonus) and previews the same reach.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant H as HealthManager (Server) participant A as ArmorManager (Server) participant S as ArmorService (Server) participant C as ArmorClient (Client) Note over H: HealthManager.ApplyDamage(amount, type, ...) H->>A: ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency) A->>A: reduction = clamp(kind.BaseReduction * (1+efficiency), 0, MaxReductionCap) A->>A: absorbed = min(amount * reduction, pool); pool -= absorbed alt Ballistic pool reaches 0 A->>A: owned[kindId] = nil; Equipped cleared if worn else Energy pool reaches 0 A->>A: kind stays owned + equipped, protects nothing end A->>C: ArmorStateSync:FireClient(owned, equipped) A-->>H: return amount - absorbed H->>H: record.Health -= (amount - absorbed) Note over C,S: EQUIP / RECHARGE (at a Workbench) C->>S: ReqEquipArmor(bench, kindId) / ReqRechargeArmor(bench, kindId) S->>S: WorkbenchStation.IsValidStation + IsPlayerNear S->>A: ArmorManager.Equip / ArmorManager.Recharge A->>C: ArmorStateSync:FireClient(owned, equipped) A-->>S: (ok, code) / (ok, energyAdded, code) S-->>C: (ok, code) / (ok, energyAdded, code)

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CannonController.client.luau	Mount prompt, movement lock, ballistic arc preview, fire input, CannonFired/ExplosionAt FX Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CannonGuiController.client.luau	Programmatic heat-bar HUD, shown only while manning a cannon Server	src/ServerScriptService/CannonServer.server.luau	Placed-cannon discovery, mount/fire validation, authoritative shell simulation, damage application, heat/overheat Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/CannonConfig.luau	Ballistics, mount range, overheat params, part/sound keys, EnemyShip tag  Packets: ReqMountCannon, ReqFireCannon, CannonFired (impact reuses ExplosionAt) — see Networking MapSignals: OnCannonMounted — local-client-only bridge from mount state to CannonGuiController

searchDocs.title: Placement → mount → fire​
searchDocs.content: Place — the cannon is a placeable (PlaceableItems/Cannon + PlaceableTools/Cannon). Placement, stash, and move are inherited from Placement; the placed clone lands in workspace/PlacedObjects with a PlaceableName = "Cannon" attribute (an attribute, not a CollectionService tag — a tag would also match client build-mode ghosts).Mount — CannonController attaches a ProximityPrompt to each placed cannon's MountPromptPart. Triggering it sends ReqMountCannon(model); the server validates proximity (MountRange) and single-occupancy and records the gunner. Mounting locks the gunner's WalkSpeed/JumpPower and shows a ballistic arc preview raycast client-side every RenderStepped.Fire — input sends ReqFireCannon(muzzle, aimDir). The server re-derives occupancy, cooldown, and overheat, then simulates the shell from its own muzzle CFrame with a gravity Acceleration via FastCast2 (the same pattern WeaponServer uses for rockets). On impact it applies Damage * (1 + CannonDamageBonus) via CombatService.ApplyAOE and broadcasts CannonFired (muzzle flash + barrel snap + sound) and ExplosionAt (boom + explosion sound).

searchDocs.title: Occupancy​
searchDocs.content: A live occupant (character alive) blocks takeover by another player; a dead occupant's seat can be taken over. CannonController releases the player's previous cannon when mounting a new one and dismounts on death, on the cannon being stashed/destroyed (model.AncestryChanged), or on pressing X. Signals.OnCannonMounted fires the model (or nil on dismount) so CannonGuiController can show/hide its heat bar without touching the network layer.

searchDocs.title: Overheat​
searchDocs.content: Each shot adds CannonConfig.HeatPerShot; heat decays at HeatDecayPerSec on a server Heartbeat. Reaching MaxHeat locks the cannon for OverheatLockTime. Heat (0–1) and Overheated are attributes on the placed Model (no packet) — CannonGuiController reads them directly every RenderStepped, eases the displayed percentage, and plays the overheat sound once on the transition into overheat.

searchDocs.title: Server authority & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Occupancy, cooldown, overheat-lock, and shell origin are all re-validated server-side; the server fires from its own muzzle, so a forged client-side origin or aim direction cannot help. CannonDamageBonus is read server-side from the server-written PartyPerkBuffs folder on every shot — unforgeable. Faction routing is inherited from CombatService.ApplyAOE, so EnemyNPC rigs must be in a hostile faction to take player damage. Direction is sanity-checked (rejects NaN/near-zero magnitude) before the cast fires.

searchDocs.title: EnemyShip forward seam​
searchDocs.content: CannonServer.applyCannonAOE damages Humanoids via CombatService.ApplyAOE and, in the same call, decrements a numeric Health attribute (the ship also needs a numeric MaxHealth, which WreckSalvageService reads) on in-radius models tagged CannonConfig.ENEMY_SHIP_TAG ("EnemyShip") with linear falloff to the blast edge, destroying the model at Health <= 0. This is inert until a future enemy-ship spec tags ships; it requires no change to the perk hook.

searchDocs.title: Smart Cannon (party shop perk)​
searchDocs.content: While any player holds Smart Cannon (PartyPerkBuffs.AutoLoaderRate > 0), the Heartbeat tick fires each cannon that has had no live occupant for AutoLoaderIdleTime (3 s). Every AUTO_SCAN_INTERVAL (0.5 s) it looks for the nearest live EnemyNPC or EnemyShip model within AutoLoaderRange (150 studs) that the muzzle can see in a straight line, solves the low ballistic arc to it (CombatPerkMath.lowArcDirection; out of reach → no shot), and fires through the same fireShell path as a manned shot. The cooldown is FireCooldown / AutoLoaderRate (≈ 6.7 s); overheat and heat apply. The shot is credited to the perk holder (PartyPerkBuffs.AutoLoaderHolderId), who is the CannonFired gunner and the AOE attacker; when the holder leaves, the HolderId becomes 0 and cannons stop firing by themselves.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: OnCannonMounted is not in the shared signals map The signal is real (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau) and fires from CannonController on mount/dismount, consumed only by CannonGuiController — it is a pre-existing gap in Signals Map, not a code issue.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Cl as CannonController participant Sv as CannonServer participant Gui as CannonGuiController Cl->>Sv: ReqMountCannon(model) Sv->>Sv: validate not-occupied-by-live-player, proximity <= MountRange Sv-->>Cl: accepted: boolean Cl->>Cl: lock WalkSpeed/JumpPower, start arc-preview raycast loop Cl->>Gui: Signals.OnCannonMounted(model) loop while mounted, on fire input Cl->>Sv: ReqFireCannon(muzzle, aimDir) Sv->>Sv: validate occupant, cooldown, overheat; sanity-check direction Sv->>Sv: FastCast2 shell from own muzzle CFrame + Gravity Acceleration Sv->>Sv: heat += HeatPerShot; lock if heat >= MaxHeat Sv-->>Cl: (accepted, remainingCooldown) Sv->>Cl: CannonFired(gunner, muzzlePos, velocity) - all clients Note over Sv: on shell impact Sv->>Sv: applyCannonAOE - CombatService.ApplyAOE + EnemyShip Health falloff Sv->>Cl: ExplosionAt(center, radius, "Cannon") - all clients end Sv->>Sv: Heartbeat: heat -= HeatDecayPerSec*dt; release overheat lock when elapsed Cl->>Sv: ReqMountCannon(nil) - dismount (death, X key, or cannon destroyed) Cl->>Gui: Signals.OnCannonMounted(nil)

See Perks.
