searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CameraController.client.luau	State machine, mouse-look, zoom, occlusion, offset spring, render step, signal wiring Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/PlacementCameraController.client.luau	Owns the camera during build mode; see Placement camera Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/CameraRig.luau	Pure, stateless CFrame composition (Compose, ClampPitch) Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/CameraConfig.luau	Offsets, look angles, spring tuning, reticle, zoom range, occlusion buffer  Packets: none — camera state is entirely client-localSignals: consumes RequestShootingCamera, RequestMouseIcon, RequestCameraLookLock, RequestReticleScale, OnBuildModeChanged, OnSettingChanged; produces OnShootingCameraToggled — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: State machine​
searchDocs.content: Two orthogonal booleans select the mode (aim wins over free-look):  aimMode — set exclusively via Signals.RequestShootingCamera. No player keybind activates aim directly; only tools (GrabHook on equip), weapons (WeaponController on weapon equip/unequip), and systems (PlacementClient on build-mode entry) fire this signal.freeLookMode — toggled by LeftAlt via ContextActionService:BindAction("ToggleCameraMode", ...); inert while aimMode is true (the action sinks the input but silently no-ops).  Two more flags participate in lookActive()/applyState() without being a "mode" of their own:  guiRequestsMouse — true while any requester holds Signals.RequestMouseIcon(true, requester) (a keyed set, so one GUI closing can't re-lock the cursor another still needs; unkeyed producers share "default"); frees and shows the cursor and suspends mouse-look, independent of freeLookMode.buildModeActive — set by Signals.OnBuildModeChanged; see Placement camera.lookLocked — set by Signals.RequestCameraLookLock; lookActive() returns false while it is set.  On every CharacterAdded a new MotionMaster.Spring (offsetSpring) is created bound to a plain { Value, Parent = true } holder (offsetHolder), not directly to humanoid.CameraOffset — the spring drives offsetHolder.Value, which the render step then feeds into CameraRig.Compose as the screen-relative offset. The spring's Omega/Zeta come from CameraConfig; it is destroyed on CharacterRemoving. The render step runs at Camera priority via RunService:BindToRenderStep("Camera", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value, ...).  CameraRig.luau is pure, stateless camera math shared by nothing else today but kept separate so it's independently testable/reviewable: CameraRig.ClampPitch(pitch, minPitch, maxPitch) is a math.clamp wrapper, and CameraRig.Compose(focusPosition, offset, yaw, pitch, distance, lookOffset) rotates offset into the yaw/pitch look frame, adds it to focusPosition, then backs the camera off distance studs along the look vector, returning (cameraCFrame, adjustedFocusPosition).  lookOffset is an optional Vector2 (radians, X=pitch, Y=yaw) that rotates the look direction about the fixed camera position — the camera position and the occlusion raycast (which fires before Compose runs) are untouched. CameraConfig.ShootingLookAngle and CameraConfig.ThirdPersonLookAngle supply this in degrees; CameraController blends the active mode's angle with a second MotionMaster.Spring, mirroring offsetSpring/offsetHolder exactly (retargeted on the same applyState() calls, created/destroyed alongside it).

searchDocs.title: Modes​
searchDocs.content: Locked third-person (default) — mouse always drives yaw/pitch (lookActive() returns true); MouseBehavior = LockCenter, cursor hidden; the HRP lerps to face humanoid.MoveDirection while moving.  Aim — entered only via Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true). Shoulder offset (CameraConfig.ShootingOffset) via the offset spring, reticle visible, mouse locked+hidden, HRP lerps to face the camera's yaw (not movement direction) so aiming and strafing look correct together. Exiting fires Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled(false).  Free-look — toggled by LeftAlt when not aiming. Cursor is freed and shown (MouseBehavior = Default), but lookActive() only returns true while the right mouse button is held — a faithful port of the old default-camera free-look behavior. HRP still lerps to face movement direction, same as locked third-person.  Signals.RequestMouseIcon is orthogonal to all three modes: while guiRequestsMouse is true (and aimMode is false), the cursor is freed/shown and lookActive() returns false regardless of freeLookMode, for GUIs that need a clickable cursor — the workbench and the train shield zoom panel today.

searchDocs.title: Sensitivity​
searchDocs.content: sensitivity is read once at startup from SettingsClient.Get("CameraSensitivity") and kept live-updated by subscribing to Signals.OnSettingChanged (filtering on key == "CameraSensitivity"). Every frame that lookActive() is true, raw pixel delta from UserInputService:GetMouseDelta() is scaled by CameraConfig.MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity before being applied to yaw/pitch. See Settings for how CameraSensitivity is defined, synced, and persisted.

searchDocs.title: Zoom​
searchDocs.content: Scroll wheel input adjusts targetDistance by CameraConfig.ScrollZoomStep per notch, clamped to [CameraConfig.CameraMinZoomDistance, maxDistanceForMode()]. maxDistanceForMode() returns ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance in aim mode or ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance otherwise.

searchDocs.title: Occlusion​
searchDocs.content: Each frame, a raycast runs from the offset focus point toward the desired camera position, excluding the local character. If it hits, occludedDistance is clamped to hitDistance - CameraConfig.BoomBuffer (floored at CameraMinZoomDistance); otherwise it's just targetDistance. A separate renderDistance is lerped toward occludedDistance at BoomSmoothingSpeed * dt per frame and is what actually gets passed to CameraRig.Compose — targetDistance (the zoom-wheel target) is never touched by occlusion, so releasing from behind a wall smoothly zooms back out to the player's chosen distance.

searchDocs.title: Placement camera​
searchDocs.content: While build mode is active, PlacementCameraController.client.luau — a separate script, not part of CameraController — takes exclusive ownership of the camera:  Sets Camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable and looks straight down from PlacementConfig.TopDownHeight, with screen-up locked to the yaw the camera had when build mode started.Freezes the player by anchoring their HumanoidRootPart locally (not WalkSpeed, which SprintController/CannonController also write). Move input from the default PlayerModule (GetControls():GetMoveVector() — WASD, gamepad stick, mobile thumbstick) pans the camera at PanSpeed; on PC the cursor at the screen edge (EdgeScrollMargin px) pans too, and the wheel zooms between ZoomMin and ZoomMax. The focus stays within PanRadius of the player: the camera is the placement ray origin, so sqrt(PanRadius² + ZoomMax²) must stay under PlacementServer's 55-stud origin limit. CameraController ignores the wheel and SprintController drops sprint intent while build mode is active.Entry (Arknights Endfield style) orbits the camera over the frozen player to straight down at its third-person distance (EnterSwingDuration, EaseInOutCubic), then zooms straight up to TopDownHeight (EnterZoomDuration, an accelerating curve with a short soft stop), plus the BuildCamEnter SFX. MotionMaster tweens a plain { Pitch, Distance, Blend, Parent = true } pose table; the Camera + 1 render step composes the orbit CFrame from it and blends in from the exact starting camera pose so there is no jump. Exit plays the CoolTransitions Checkerboard (ExitTransitionDuration). The top-down view is held until the screen is covered; then CameraController takes over again. Mouse look (Signals.RequestCameraLookLock) and the freeze stay on until the checkerboard ends, so input under the transition does not read as camera jitter. Death/reset unfreezes instantly with no transition; the camera stays put until CameraController resumes on respawn. A re-equip during the checkerboard waits for it to finish.Fades any PlacementConfig.OccluderTag-tagged parts (e.g. roofs) to OccluderTransparency for the duration and fires Signals.RequestMouseIcon(true) on PC so the cursor is free to aim mouse.UnitRay.  CameraController and PlacementCameraController both own the Scriptable camera at different times, and coordinate via Signals.OnBuildModeChanged. CameraController subscribes to this signal and sets buildModeActive accordingly; its render step's first statement is if buildModeActive then return end, a full no-op for the duration of build mode. On resume it reasserts camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable (guarded — only writes if not already Scriptable) and continues from the yaw/pitch it had before build mode. Because it resumes the moment the signal fires, PlacementCameraController binds its render step one priority later (Camera + 1) and overwrites camera.CFrame with the held top-down view until the checkerboard midpoint.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Aim mode is signal-only There is no keybind that activates aimMode directly. Only external systems fire Signals.RequestShootingCamera. If a new tool or system needs to enter aim mode it must fire this signal — do not read or write the aimMode local directly.  Never set CameraType = Custom The camera is always Scriptable. Setting Custom, even for one frame, wakes Roblox's default CameraModule. If the camera is looking straight down at that moment (the build camera), BaseCamera:CalculateNewLookCFrameFromArg takes math.asin(LookVector.Y) with Y a hair under −1, gets NaN, and throws invalid argument #3 to 'clamp' (max must be greater than or equal to min). Hand the camera back by letting CameraController resume, not by switching type.  Do not use TweenService to animate the camera offset. offsetSpring is a MotionMaster.Spring driver bound to offsetHolder.Value; bypassing it will produce conflicting states and the spring will override any TweenService tween on the next frame.CameraController and PlacementCameraController both write Camera.CameraType/Camera.CFrame and must never run their write paths in the same frame — that's what buildModeActive exists to prevent. Do not add a third script that writes Camera.CFrame without wiring it into this same coordination.The offset spring is re-created on every CharacterAdded and destroyed on CharacterRemoving. Holding a reference to an old spring past the character death will produce a dangling driver pointing at a destroyed Humanoid.freeLookMode frees and shows the mouse cursor, but does not re-enable humanoid.AutoRotate; CameraController always drives HRP facing itself and sets humanoid.AutoRotate = false unconditionally (skipped entirely while humanoid.Sit is true).A GUI that needs a clickable cursor fires Signals.RequestMouseIcon:Fire(true); while set (and not aiming) the camera holds MouseBehavior = Default and shows the cursor, restoring LockCenter on Fire(false).CameraSensitivity changes take effect on the very next frame via Signals.OnSettingChanged — there is no need to re-fetch SettingsClient.Get manually or restart the character.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant U as UserInputService participant C as CameraController participant Cam as Camera participant Ext as External systems U->>C: GetMouseDelta() (every RenderStep, when lookActive()) C->>C: yaw/pitch -= delta * MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity C->>C: CameraRig.ClampPitch(pitch, MinPitch, MaxPitch) U->>C: MouseWheel scroll C->>C: targetDistance = clamp(targetDistance + step, MinZoom, maxDistanceForMode()) loop RunService RenderStep "Camera" (Priority = Camera) C->>C: if buildModeActive then return end C->>C: reassert CameraType = Scriptable C->>C: occlusion raycast -> renderDistance lerped toward occludedDistance C->>Cam: CameraRig.Compose(subject, offset, yaw, pitch, renderDistance, lookOffset) C->>C: lerp HRP facing toward camera yaw (aim) or move direction end Ext->>C: Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true/false) C->>C: aimMode = value; applyState() C->>C: offsetSpring/angleSpring retarget; MouseBehavior; reticle visible C-->>Ext: Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled(aimMode) U->>C: LeftAlt (non-aim only) C->>C: freeLookMode toggles; applyState() Ext->>C: Signals.RequestMouseIcon(visible) C->>C: guiRequestsMouse = visible; applyState() Ext->>C: Signals.OnBuildModeChanged(isActive) C->>C: buildModeActive = isActive (render step becomes no-op while true)

Lag compensation adds renderTime to ReqFireWeapon (see Networking Map).Signals: none.

searchDocs.title: Start order​
searchDocs.content: Every consumer requires SharedModules/Chrono, never Packages.chrono directly. The wrapper calls chrono.Start(Configs.ChronoConfig) at require-time, so Chrono is always started (and its config locked) before any entity is created. ChronoConfig must only be required by Start — its SetConfig/RegisterEntityType calls assert if the config is already locked.

searchDocs.title: Players​
searchDocs.content: PLAYER_REPLICATION = "AUTOMATIC" (Chrono default). Chrono registers each character as a PLAYER entity (NATIVE mode, dynamic buffer, always replicated), owned by its player. No project code touches this.

searchDocs.title: Enemies (EnemyChrono)​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawner.placeAt calls EnemyChrono.Track(model) right after parenting the model (before EnemyBrain.Register). Every spawned NPC — enemy or friendly — becomes an ENEMY entity in NATIVE mode: Roblox still replicates the model (animations, health, client raycasts and FX keep working), and Chrono overrides the client CFrame with its interpolated value. NATIVE was chosen over NATIVE_WITH_LOCK (server physics would act anchored, breaking Humanoid:MoveTo) and CUSTOM (hides the server model from clients).  Event	Action	WhyHumanoid.Died	Entity.PauseReplication	Clients stop forcing the CFrame; the body falls with normal physics. Model leaves the DataModel	Entity.Destroy, drop from tracked map	Server Entity.Destroy destroys the model, so it only runs once the model is already gone.  EnemyChrono.Tracked() returns the live { [Model]: Entity } map that LagCompensation reads. Server history: MAX_SNAPSHOT_COUNT (30) at 30 Hz = 1 s.

searchDocs.title: Lag compensation (LagCompensation)​
searchDocs.content: Server module used by WeaponServer for hitscan. See Weapons — Lag compensation for the flow. Key facts:  ENEMY.STORE_SNAPSHOTS = true is what makes rewind work — without it the server keeps only the latest CFrame.Client render time is in the server os.clock() domain (Chrono sends server os.clock() quantized to 0.1 ms). ClampRewind snaps whole u32 wraps (~4.97 days of uptime).Exploit ceiling: a cheater may choose any time inside their own window (≤ 1 s).Limits: rigid rewind (current animation pose); half-ticked NPCs (> 150 studs) use the NORMAL clock as an approximation.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: wally install wipes TweenPlus's TweenPreallocations attribute — re-set it to 256 in Studio (see Toolchain).wally install also deletes the empty ServerPackages/ folder (there are no server dependencies). default.project.json maps it as an optional path, so Rojo skips it when missing.Chrono's source uses the Luau const keyword. If Luau LSP flags it inside Packages/, that is an LSP version issue only.Server-side character teleports (e.g. PlacementServer's push-out PivotTo) are caught by Chrono's default REPLICATE_CFRAME_SETTERS = "PLAYER_ENTITIES": the HRP CFrame change becomes an Entity.SetCFrame teleport, so other clients snap (no slide) and the server ignores the owner's normal updates until a teleport-flagged packet arrives (≤ 0.5 s + ping).Remote players are only interpolated if their PrimaryPart (HRP) is the assembly root — the built-in PLAYER type has ASSEMBLY_ROOT_PART_CHECK = true and silently skips otherwise (Warn.low). Verify with SingleCollider (CollisionPart) avatars.Chrono sets every tracked NPC root's network owner to the server (nil).StreamingEnabled interaction is unverified.

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/DamageNumbers.luau	Pooled BillboardGui spawner, style application, pop/rise/fade animation Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/DamageNumbersController.client.luau	Bootstrap: pre-warms the pool once via DamageNumbers.Init() Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/DamageNumberConfig.luau	Styles, timing, jitter, pool sizing, billboard size/distance  Packets: none — a damage source (client-predicted hit or a server broadcast handler) calls Show directlySignals: none — no combat wiring; the settings menu calls SetEnabled directly

searchDocs.title: API surface​
searchDocs.content: Function	DescriptionDamageNumbers.Show(worldPosition, amount, styleName?)	Spawn a number. No-op if disabled or amount <= 0. styleName defaults to Config.DefaultStyle; unknown names fall back to it. DamageNumbers.SetEnabled(value)	Toggle spawning of new numbers (for a settings menu). In-flight numbers finish. DamageNumbers.IsEnabled()	Returns the current toggle state. DamageNumbers.Init()	Build + pre-warm the pool. Idempotent; lazy-runs on first Show otherwise. Called once by DamageNumbersController.

searchDocs.title: Spawn and animate​
searchDocs.content: Each number is a pooled BillboardGui (GenericPoolInstance). On Show it acquires an entry, applies a named style (color/font/size/stroke from DamageNumberConfig.Styles), offsets the spawn by a random jitter so rapid hits fan out, then animates with MotionMaster:  Pop — UIScale.Scale from Pop.StartScale to 1 with a back-out overshoot curve (a custom backOut alpha function, since MotionMaster's built-in easing has no overshoot).Rise — BillboardGui.StudsOffsetWorldSpace.Y drifts up by Rise.Height over Lifetime.Fade — text/stroke transparency animates to 1 during the final Fade.Duration seconds of Lifetime.  One Janitor per live number owns the pop/rise/fade tweens and a delayed fade thread. When the rise tween completes, the Janitor is destroyed and the part returns to the pool (resetEntry hides it for reuse). The billboard uses world-space (Scale) sizing, so numbers shrink with camera distance and cull past Billboard.MaxDistance.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant D as Damage source (predicted hit / server broadcast handler) participant N as DamageNumbers participant P as GenericPoolInstance D->>N: Show(worldPosition, amount, styleName?) N->>N: enabled? amount > 0? else no-op N->>P: RetrieveObject(jittered CFrame) N->>N: apply style (color/font/size/stroke) N->>N: MotionMaster.Play (Pop, Rise, Fade via delayed thread) Note over N: Rise:OnComplete N->>N: Janitor:Destroy() (cancel tweens/fade thread) N->>P: InsertObject(part) - resetEntry hides it for reuse

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/DisruptionController.client.luau	Shows the non-blocking countdown notice; no input is blocked Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/DisruptionCoordinator.luau	Trigger funnel (automatic + manual) and the full drain sequence Server	src/ServerScriptService/DisruptionSystemLoader.server.luau	Bootstrap — calls DisruptionCoordinator.Initialize(), runs in both the lobby and gameplay places Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/PersistenceRegistry.luau	Force-save registry; gameplay managers register a flush callback in their Initialize Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/DisruptionConfig.luau	Lobby place id, timing budgets, admin command, player-facing copy  Packets: DisruptionBegan — see Networking MapSignals: none — DisruptionController reuses Signals.RequestNotification for the countdown toast, but the disruption system itself defines no signals

searchDocs.title: Trigger​
searchDocs.content: Two paths funnel into the same drain sequence, guarded by an isDisrupting flag so it only ever runs once:  Automatic — game:BindToClose fires beginDisruption("shutdown") when Roblox shuts the server down.Manual — DisruptionCoordinator.BeginMaintenance(reason) (an admin chat command, DisruptionConfig.ADMIN_COMMAND, default "!maintenance") publishes to every server in the universe via MessagingService, so a fleet-wide maintenance drain doesn't require restarting each server individually. If the publish fails, it falls back to draining just the local server.

searchDocs.title: Drain sequence​
searchDocs.content: beginDisruption(reason) runs in order, all timed from a single drainStart:  Notify — broadcasts the DisruptionBegan packet (reason, NOTICE_SECONDS); each client shows a non-blocking countdown via Signals.RequestNotification.Wait — task.wait(NOTICE_SECONDS) so players can read the notice.Flush — PersistenceRegistry.FlushAll(FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) force-saves every registered profile. profile:Save() is used, not EndSession(), so players stay connected until the teleport.Teleport — TeleportService:TeleportAsync(LOBBY_PLACE_ID, …) per player, retried up to TELEPORT_RETRIES times. Skipped entirely in Studio or when LOBBY_PLACE_ID <= 0 — players then disconnect with data already saved.Drain-wait — yields until the server empties or MAX_DRAIN_SECONDS (measured from drainStart, so steps 1–4 eat into the same budget rather than adding to it) elapses; leftover players disconnect with data already saved. Skipped in Studio, where no real teleport occurs and waiting would hang every Studio "Stop" for the full budget.  A player joining mid-drain is caught by Players.PlayerAdded, which starts a teleport attempt immediately — this cannot wait on the client, or the drain would never finish emptying the server. The DisruptionBegan notice, being a client render rather than drain bookkeeping, is instead registered with JoinSync and sent once that player's client announces readiness (or not at all, if the drain has already ended by then).

searchDocs.title: Correctness​
searchDocs.content: ProfileStore session-locking is the backstop: even if a save is in flight when a player reaches the lobby server, that server's StartSessionAsync waits for the old lock to release, so no data is lost. The explicit flush in step 3 just tightens the window and gives a "saved before we move you" ordering — it is not the only thing preventing data loss.

searchDocs.title: Force-save registrants​
searchDocs.content: PersistenceRegistry.Register(flush) is called from each manager's Initialize; FlushAll invokes every registered callback with a shared timeout. Current registrants: CoinManager, ArmorManager, PerkManager, PerkInventoryManager, QuestManager, SettingsManager, XPManager, BattlePassManager.  PersistenceRegistry also holds the Lobby's teleport hand-off: RegisterHandoff(release, reopen) (called by CoinManager, XPManager, PerkManager, PerkInventoryManager), ReleaseForTeleport(players) and Reopen(players). A release ends the session without the manager's kick; it is separate from the drain flush above. See Perk Inventory — Teleport hand-off.

searchDocs.title: Known limitation​
searchDocs.content: Direct teleport to the lobby can bounce if the lobby place is also restarting during a universe-wide Roblox update. The reliable path is the manual maintenance command, which drains the gameplay place while the lobby stays up.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: MAX_DRAIN_SECONDS bounds the whole sequence, not just the final wait Notice + flush + drain-wait together must fit under Roblox's ~30s BindToClose budget. Tuning NOTICE_SECONDS or FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS eats into the same budget rather than adding to it.  LOBBY_PLACE_ID = 0 skips the teleport, not the flush While unset, the coordinator still runs the full notify/flush sequence — players just disconnect afterward instead of being teleported. Data is not lost, but there's no lobby to land in.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Trig as Trigger (BindToClose / admin command) participant Co as DisruptionCoordinator participant Pers as PersistenceRegistry participant Cl as DisruptionController Trig->>Co: beginDisruption(reason) Co->>Co: isDisrupting guard (idempotent) Co->>Cl: DisruptionBegan(reason, NOTICE_SECONDS) - all clients Cl->>Cl: Signals.RequestNotification countdown Co->>Co: task.wait(NOTICE_SECONDS) Co->>Pers: FlushAll(FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) Pers->>Pers: profile:Save() per registered manager alt LOBBY_PLACE_ID > 0 and not Studio Co->>Co: TeleportAsync(LOBBY_PLACE_ID, player) per player, retry TELEPORT_RETRIES else Studio or unset Co->>Co: warn - players disconnect, data already flushed end Co->>Co: wait until server empties or MAX_DRAIN_SECONDS (from drainStart)

NOTICE_SECONDS	4	Seconds between showing the notice and starting the drain FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS	6	Max seconds to wait for PersistenceRegistry.FlushAll() before proceeding anyway MAX_DRAIN_SECONDS	25	Hard cap on the whole sequence; must stay under Roblox's ~30s BindToClose budget TELEPORT_RETRIES	3	Retries per player on TeleportInitFailed MESSAGING_TOPIC	"EndlessJourney_Disruption"	MessagingService topic for fleet-wide manual maintenance fan-out ADMIN_USER_IDS	{}	UserIds allowed to invoke the manual maintenance chat command ADMIN_COMMAND	"!maintenance"	Chat command (case-insensitive, first word) that starts manual maintenance NOTIF_TYPE	"warn"	Notification type passed to Signals.RequestNotification DEFAULT_MESSAGE / REASON_MESSAGES	—	Player-facing copy, keyed by trigger reason (shutdown / maintenance)

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CoinController.client.luau	Bridges CoinStateSync to Signals.OnCoinsChanged Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/CoinManager.luau	Sole wallet authority: profile lifecycle, earn/spend/read API, replication Server	src/ServerScriptService/CoinSystemLoader.server.luau	Calls CoinManager.Initialize() once per server (place-agnostic) Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/CoinConfig.luau	STORE_NAME, STARTING_BALANCE, MAX_BALANCE  Packets: CoinStateSync — see Networking MapSignals: OnCoinsChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Data model​
searchDocs.content: The PlayerCoins profile stores a single value, Coins. STORE_NAME ("PlayerCoins") and the UserId key are identical in every place of the universe, so the lobby and gameplay share one DataStore record. The Lobby boots CoinManager from PerkLoadoutService. Right before a party teleport it ends the coin session without a kick (PersistenceRegistry.ReleaseForTeleport), so the Game Instance opens it without waiting on the session lock; a failed teleport reopens it. See Perk Inventory — Teleport hand-off. Wallet bounds (STARTING_BALANCE, MAX_BALANCE) live in CoinConfig.

searchDocs.title: Wallet API (server-authoritative)​
searchDocs.content: CoinManager is the sole authority — every mutation goes through one of these four functions:  function CoinManager.GetCoins(player: Player): number function CoinManager.AddCoins(player: Player, amount: number, reason: string?) function CoinManager.DeductCoins(player: Player, amount: number): boolean function CoinManager.RefundCoins(player: Player, amount: number)   AddCoins scales the amount by the personal CoinGainBonus (Pocket Change, Coin Booster, Coin Booster II) plus the party PartyCoinBonus (Party Advisor): math.max(1, math.floor(amount * (1 + CoinGainBonus + PartyCoinBonus))), a 1-coin floor, and clamps to MAX_BALANCE; reason is an optional source tag logged server-side only. DeductCoins is atomic — it returns false with no mutation on amount <= 0, a missing profile, or insufficient funds. RefundCoins returns an exact amount and is not scaled by CoinGainBonus, so unlock→respec cycling can't mint coins. IsLoaded(player) reports whether the coin profile is loaded (the perk legacy refund waits on it).

searchDocs.title: Sources​
searchDocs.content: Source	Call	NotesEnemy kills	CoinManager.AddCoins(player, coins)	XPSystemLoader: every player gets CoinConfig.KILL_COINS (5) per enemy death, × (1 + KillCoinBonus + PartyKillRewardBonus) (Bounty Contract, Pirate Bounty Board), rounded down, then the normal coin multipliers. No log line. Gold Rush	CoinManager.AddCoins(player, JunkCoinsT4/T5, "GoldRush")	JunkService finalize: tier 4 / tier 5 junk pays coins while the Gold Rush shop perk is live. Scrap Pay	CoinManager.AddCoins(player, ScrapPayCoins, "ScrapPay")	JunkService finalize: each junk a player grabs pays 1 coin while the shop perk is live. Survivor Pay	CoinManager.AddCoins(player, SurvivorPayCoins, "SurvivorPay")	SurvivorPayService: every SURVIVOR_PAY_SECONDS (600) alive pays 100 coins; a death resets the count. Quest rewards	CoinManager.AddCoins(player, quest.Reward.Coins, "Quest:"..questId)	Paid by QuestManager's shared grantReward path (manual claim or rollover auto-grant). Scaled by CoinGainBonus. Battle Pass tiers	CoinManager.AddCoins(player, reward.Amount, "BattlePassFree:"..level) / "BattlePassPremium:"..level	Paid by the bulk-claim sweep for Coins-type tier rewards. Scaled by CoinGainBonus. Premium row is gated by a Roblox subscription (BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID), not a one-time purchase — that gates the reward row, it does not grant coins directly.  Quests also pay an EXP reward via XPManager.AddXP — a separate system with its own profile. See Quests and Battle Pass.

searchDocs.content: Sink	Call	NotesPerk unlock	CoinManager.DeductCoins(player, perk.UnlockCost)	PerkManager.UnlockPerk pays a perk's one-time unlock cost. See Perks — Unlock gate. Respec refund	CoinManager.RefundCoins(player, CoinsSpent[perkId])	PerkManager.Respec / RespecPerk return every coin paid on the perk (unlock + upgrades) exactly, not scaled by CoinGainBonus. See Perk Inventory.  Perk unlocking is the first implemented sink; quest/battle-pass rewards are the first implemented sources.

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: Every successful mutation fires CoinStateSync(balance: U32) to the owning client. CoinController re-fires it as Signals.OnCoinsChanged(balance); nothing consumes it yet. There is no client→server packet — earning and spending are fully server-driven.

searchDocs.title: Not yet built​
searchDocs.content: Additional earning sources (gameplay-session completion), additional sinks (a shop + purchase packet), and the coin HUD are separate systems that would call the CoinManager API — they are not part of the wallet module.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleServer	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemyBrain.luau	Centralized AI director: 10 Hz tick, targeting, path-budgeted movement, ranged firing state machine, registration + Janitor lifecycle Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemyWeapon.luau	Enemy attack actions: MuzzleOrigin, FireProjectile (FastCast2 bullet caster), Lob (arcing AOE throwable) — all routed through CombatService Server	src/ServerScriptService/EnemyCombatSystemLoader.server.luau	Thin bootstrap: calls EnemyBrain.Init() once per server Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/WeaponFx.luau	WeaponFx.resolve(weaponName) — checks WeaponConfig then EnemyCombatConfig.FindByWeapon for FX sound keys Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/WeaponEffectsController.client.luau	Renders tracers/sparks/explosions for both player and enemy shooters via WeaponFx.resolve Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemyCombatConfig.luau	Per-archetype Profile registry (Profiles table), GetProfile/FindByWeapon lookups  Packets: WeaponFired (widened shooter: Instance), ExplosionAt — see Networking MapSignals: none new — enemy fire reuses the player combat packets/signals documented in WeaponsReplication: every spawned NPC is a Chrono ENEMY entity (NATIVE mode) — see Chrono Replication. Player hitscan against enemies is lag-compensated (see Weapons); enemy fire at players is not.

searchDocs.title: The EnemyBrain director​
searchDocs.content: EnemyBrain is a single module-level loop, not one script per enemy. EnemyBrain.Init() connects one RunService.Heartbeat listener and accumulates dt until TICK_INTERVAL (1 / TICK_HZ, TICK_HZ = 10) has elapsed, then calls tick() once. Every registered enemy is iterated in that single tick — there are no per-enemy RunService connections, task.spawn loops, or while true do task.wait() end patterns. This keeps the cost of N enemies roughly linear and avoids N independent scheduler entries.  Each registered enemy is a Record (an in-memory table, not an Instance) keyed by its Model in a module-level records dictionary:  type Record = { model: Model, humanoid: Humanoid, root: BasePart, profile: Profile, -- EnemyCombatConfig.Profile cleaner: Janitor.Janitor, target: Player?, -- movement waypoints: { PathWaypoint }, waypointIndex: number, pathGoal: Vector3?, nextRepathAt: number, -- firing fireState: "Idle" | "Bursting" | "Cooldown", shotsLeft: number, nextShotAt: number, nextBurstAt: number, telegraphUntil: number?, }   Every tick, for every record that is still alive and rooted, EnemyBrain:  Reacquires a target if the current one is missing or dead — nearestPlayer scans Players:GetPlayers() for the closest player with a living Humanoid and a HumanoidRootPart. Targeting is pure distance; there is no aggro persistence, threat table, or line-of-sight requirement to pick a target (LOS only gates firing, see below).Steps movement (stepMovement) — independent of firing.Steps firing (stepFiringRanged) — independent of movement.  This is the two-concern (move ‖ fire) model: an enemy can be walking toward the player and shooting at the same time (run-and-gun), because neither step blocks or depends on the other completing first within the tick.  Movement and path-compute budgeting​  stepMovement holds the enemy still (Humanoid:MoveTo(currentPosition)) once it is within profile.CloseDistance (default 30) of the target — this "comfort band" makes ranged enemies stop closing once they're inside a distance they consider safe to shoot from, rather than walking into point-blank range. Outside that band, it paths toward the target's HumanoidRootPart position.  Paths are computed via PathfindingService:CreatePath/ComputeAsync, but not on every tick for every enemy. A shared pathBudget of PATH_BUDGET_PER_TICK (1) ComputeAsync calls is allocated per tick and decremented as enemies consume it — with a 10 Hz tick this caps fresh pathfinding compute at ~10 calls/sec total across all enemies, naturally staggering large waves instead of bursting 40 simultaneous ComputeAsync calls in one frame. An enemy only requests a new path when it has none yet, REPATH_INTERVAL (1.0s) has elapsed since its last compute, or the target has drifted more than REPATH_THRESHOLD (8 studs) from the path's original goal — most ticks for most enemies do no path computation at all, they just step along existing waypoints (WAYPOINT_REACHED = 3 studs advances to the next one). If ComputeAsync fails or the budget is exhausted, the enemy falls back to beelining straight at the goal with Humanoid:MoveTo — pathfinding failure is non-fatal, it just degrades to dumb-walk.  Ranged firing: the burst/cooldown state machine​  stepFiringRanged drives a three-state machine per enemy: "Idle" → "Bursting" → "Cooldown" → back to "Idle".  No target, out of range, or no line of sight: firing is suspended and movement keeps closing/repositioning. Critically, if the enemy was mid-burst ("Bursting") when any of these interruptions occurs, its state is reset to "Idle" rather than left to resume later: if rec.fireState == "Bursting" then rec.fireState = "Idle" end This reset exists specifically so that re-engagement always rolls a brand-new burst (startBurst) instead of resuming a stale partial burst whose nextShotAt/shotsLeft may be long expired or, for a sniper, whose Telegraph window has already elapsed. Without the reset, a player could duck behind cover for a moment to skip past a sniper's aim-telegraph and pop back out already inside the weapon's nextShotAt window — defeating the reaction-window fairness the telegraph exists to provide. The fix applies identically to the out-of-range case (LOS-break and range-break share the same reasoning) so the dodge counter-play stays consistent regardless of why the enemy lost its shot. "Cooldown": holds fire until now >= nextBurstAt, then transitions to "Idle". "Idle": immediately calls startBurst, which rolls shotsLeft between BurstMin/BurstMax, sets fireState = "Bursting", and sets nextShotAt = now + Telegraph (0 for non-snipers). For a sniper (Telegraph > 0), this delay before the first shot is the player's reaction window — telegraphUntil is exposed on the record so a future client-side "enemy is aiming at you" cue could read it, though nothing currently renders it. "Bursting": once now >= nextShotAt and shotsLeft > 0, fires one shot (fireOneShot — routes to EnemyWeapon.Lob or EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile depending on profile.FireMode), decrements shotsLeft, and schedules the next shot at now + ShotInterval. When shotsLeft reaches 0, transitions to "Cooldown" and rolls the next burst's start time.  Line of sight is checked every tick a ranged enemy considers firing (hasLineOfSight): a raycast from the muzzle origin to the target's root, excluding the shooter's own model, treats a hit against the target's own character as clear (not blocked) and anything else solid as blocked. This stops enemies shooting through walls; it is a fairness check, not a cover-seeking AI — enemies make no attempt to flank around an obstruction, they simply hold fire and let stepMovement keep closing the distance.  Fairness rationale​  No ammo, ever. Enemies have no magazine or reload — the only throttle on rate of fire is the burst/cooldown rhythm in EnemyCombatConfig. This is a deliberate simplification versus the player's ammo system (Weapons); the challenge lever is burst size and cooldown length, not resource starvation.No hitscan. EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile always launches a travelling FastCast2 projectile at a finite ProjectileSpeed; damage applies on Hit after real flight time elapses, so a player who strafes out of the bullet's path after it's fired takes no damage, exactly like dodging a player-fired bullet.No target leading. Both FireProjectile and Lob aim at the target's current position (targetPos) at the moment of firing, never a predicted future position. Combined with finite projectile speed and Spread (an aim-error cone in degrees, via WeaponValidation.applySpread), this makes every ranged archetype dodgeable by lateral movement, not just by breaking LOS.Sniper telegraph as a reaction window. PirateSniper's Telegraph = 0.6 inserts a fixed delay between entering "Bursting" and the first (and only) shot, giving the player six-tenths of a second of visible aim-up before the highest single-hit damage in the game (Damage = 40) fires. The reset-on-interrupt fix above ensures this window cannot be bypassed by ducking LOS or range right before the shot and popping back — the telegraph always re-applies on re-engagement.

searchDocs.title: EnemyWeapon​
searchDocs.content: EnemyWeapon is the enemy attack action — it owns no timing or ammo state (that's EnemyBrain's job) and instead reuses the exact same player damage layer end to end:  EnemyWeapon.MuzzleOrigin(model, profile) — returns the world position fire should originate from. If the rig has a descendant Attachment named "Muzzle" (an authored weapon model), its WorldPosition is used. Otherwise it falls back to the root part's CFrame offset by profile.MuzzleOffset (default (0, 1.5, -1)) — an art-less first pass that still produces a sensible shoulder-height, slightly forward origin.EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile(model, profile, origin, targetPos) — fires one travelling bullet through a dedicated module-level FastCast2.new() caster (bulletCaster, separate from the player gun caster in WeaponServer, but wired the same way: LengthChanged steps an optional cosmetic part, Hit resolves the struck model via WeaponValidation.resolveHumanoidModel and applies damage via CombatService.ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, damage, "Bullet", enemyModel)). Fires Packets.WeaponFired on both a real hit and a miss-timeout backstop (task.delay guarded by a data.fired flag so a real hit and the timeout can never both resolve), so the tracer always renders even when nothing is struck. The optional cosmetic bullet comes from ServerProjectile.spawnRocket(profile.Weapon, ...) — nil-safe; if no WeaponAssets/<Weapon> template exists, fire still works, just without a visible bullet model.EnemyWeapon.Lob(model, profile, origin, targetPos) — reuses the player grenade path: ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable(weapon, origin, unit, speed, "Bounce", { model }) for a server-replicated physics throw, biased upward (+ Vector3.yAxis * 0.5) so it arcs rather than fires flat. After profile.FuseTime, detonates via CombatService.ApplyAOE and fires Packets.ExplosionAt, then destroys the charge instance. In every case the attacker argument passed to CombatService is the enemy Model, not a Player — CombatService/Factions already supports a non-Player attacker (the Faction of a Model is resolved by its EnemyNPC/FriendlyNPC CollectionService tag), so no changes were needed to the damage router itself to support enemies attacking players. Factions.canDamage("Enemy", "Player") is true by default; the reverse and same-faction pairs are not, which is what prevents enemies from ever damaging each other or friendly NPCs by the same mechanism that prevents player-on-player damage. See Weapons → CombatService and Architecture → Backbone for the faction model itself.

searchDocs.title: EnemyCombatConfig profiles​
searchDocs.content: EnemyCombatConfig holds one Profile per archetype name, keyed identically to the archetype names used in EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes. An archetype with no entry here stays passive — EnemyBrain.Register looks up EnemyCombatConfig.GetProfile(archetypeName) and simply returns without arming the enemy if it's nil. This is the only "is this archetype armed" check in the system — see Studio setup below for the common mistake this invites.  export type FireMode = "Projectile" | "Lob" export type Profile = { Weapon: string, -- FX/sound key (WeaponFx) + WeaponAssets cosmetic name Damage: number, -- Ranged FireMode: FireMode?, -- "Projectile" | "Lob" ProjectileSpeed: number?, -- studs/s; finite + dodgeable Spread: number?, -- aim-error cone (degrees) Range: number?, -- max distance the enemy will fire from CloseDistance: number?, -- pathfind until generously inside Range, then hold MuzzleOffset: Vector3?, -- HRP-relative origin until a "Muzzle" attachment exists -- Burst rhythm (no ammo) ShotInterval: number?, BurstMin: number?, BurstMax: number?, BurstCooldownMin: number?, BurstCooldownMax: number?, Telegraph: number?, -- sniper: seconds aiming before the shot -- Lob-only AOERadius: number?, FuseTime: number?, -- Optional animation asset ids (server rig) FireAnimId: string?, }   EnemyCombatConfig.FindByWeapon(weaponName) linear-scans Profiles for a matching Weapon key — used by WeaponFx to resolve enemy weapon FX by name, the mirror of how it resolves player weapons via WeaponConfig.  Shipped archetypes​  Archetype	Weapon (FX key)	Damage	Fire mode	Projectile speed	Spread	Range / Close	Burst (shots)	Shot interval	Cooldown	TelegraphPirateGruntSMG	EnemySMG	6	Projectile	140	5°	80 / 35	2–5	0.10s	1.2–2.5s	— PiratePistoleer	EnemyPistol	8	Projectile	150	3°	60 / 30	3–5	0.18s	1.5–3.0s	— PirateSniper	EnemySniper	40	Projectile	320	1°	200 / 120	1–1	0s	3.0–4.5s	0.6s PirateGrenadier	EnemyGrenade	50 (AOE r16)	Lob	60	—	90 / 50	1–1	—	3.5–5.0s	—  PirateGrenadier's FuseTime is 2.0s; MuzzleOffset for all archetypes is (0, 1.5, -1) except PirateGrenadier's (0, 2, -1). These archetype names are combat profiles only — they still need a corresponding entry in EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes to ever be spawned in the first place (see Studio setup).

searchDocs.title: WeaponFx bridge and the widened WeaponFired packet​
searchDocs.content: Player weapon FX (impact/explosion sounds) are looked up by weapon name in WeaponConfig. Enemy weapons are a different name (EnemySMG, not SMG) living in a different config module, so a single client FX controller needs a single resolver that checks both. WeaponFx.resolve(weaponName) checks WeaponConfig[weaponName] first, then falls back to EnemyCombatConfig.FindByWeapon(weaponName), returning { ImpactSound?, ExplodeSound? } either way (or an empty table if neither matches). WeaponEffectsController.client.luau calls this for WeaponFired/ExplosionAt instead of indexing WeaponConfig directly — this is the only client-side change needed to render enemy weapon FX through the existing tracer/spark/explosion rendering code.  This works because the WeaponFired packet's shooter field was widened from Player to Instance so it can carry either a Player (player guns) or an enemy Model (EnemyWeapon fire):  local WeaponFired = Packet( "WeaponFired", Packet.Instance :: Instance, -- shooter (Player or enemy Model) Packet.String, -- weaponName Packet.Vector3F32, -- origin (muzzle) Packet.Vector3F32, -- endpoint (hit position or max-range point) Packet.Boolean8 -- isHit )   WeaponEffectsController ignores WeaponFired only when shooter == player (the local player's own gun already drew its own tracer client-side); an enemy Model shooter is never equal to a Player instance, so enemy shots always render for every client, including the player they're aimed at. See the WeaponFired row in the Networking Map for the full packet contract.

searchDocs.title: Lifecycle and cleanup​
searchDocs.content: EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) is idempotent (returns immediately if the model is already registered) and requires the model to have both a Humanoid (via FindFirstChildOfClass) and a root part (PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart) — if either is missing, registration silently no-ops and the enemy stays unarmed. On success, one Janitor is created per record (cleaner) and two connections are added to it, both tagged "Disconnect":  humanoid.Died → EnemyBrain.Unregister(model)model.AncestryChanged (fires when parent becomes nil) → EnemyBrain.Unregister(model)  EnemyBrain.Unregister(model) removes the record from the module-level records table and calls cleaner:Destroy(). This covers both lifecycle exits an enemy can take: dying (Humanoid.Died) and being despawned without dying (wave Despawn/Destroy, or any other code that removes the model from the DataModel — see EnemySpawner → WaveHandle lifecycle). There is no Destroy/Cleanup distinction here (unlike some other Janitor-owning modules in this codebase) because an unregistered enemy record has no further use — the Janitor is always fully torn down.  Within tick() itself, a record whose root.Parent is falsy or whose humanoid.Health <= 0 is skipped for that tick (continue) rather than acted on — the actual removal from records happens asynchronously via the Died/AncestryChanged connections above, so there's a brief window (within the same frame) where a dead enemy's record can still exist but is simply not ticked.

searchDocs.title: Edge cases​
searchDocs.content: Case	BehaviorNo target found (no living, rooted player)	stepMovement halts the enemy in place (MoveTo(currentPosition)); stepFiringRanged resets fireState to "Idle" so the next valid target starts a fresh burst. Target dies or leaves mid-burst	Next tick's targetRoot lookup fails, rec.target is re-acquired via nearestPlayer (or left nil if no one is left), and a stale "Bursting" state is abandoned the same way as the out-of-range/LOS-blocked cases. Target goes out of Range mid-burst	Firing is suspended; a "Bursting" state resets to "Idle" (see the telegraph-reset fix); movement keeps closing. Line of sight blocked mid-burst	Same reset-to-"Idle" behavior as out-of-range; the enemy holds fire and lets movement reposition rather than trying to flank. Friendly fire (enemy vs. enemy, enemy vs. friendly NPC)	Physically impossible by design — CombatService.ApplyToModel gates every hit through Factions.canDamage, and Enemy -> Enemy / Enemy -> Friendly are not in the allow table. Wave despawn while enemies are armed	EnemyWave's Despawn/Destroy removes the enemy Model from the DataModel, which fires model.AncestryChanged with a nil parent, which calls EnemyBrain.Unregister — the brain record and its Janitor are torn down in the same tick the model is destroyed, with no dangling references. Archetype has no EnemyCombatConfig profile	EnemyBrain.Register returns early; the enemy spawns and is fully visible/collidable but never moves toward or fires at players. Enemy model missing Humanoid or root part	EnemyBrain.Register returns early without warning (mirrors EnemySpawner's existing tolerance for placeholder/incomplete rigs during early development).

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: EnemyAssets rig requirements​  An enemy Model in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/ needs the same minimum viable rig that EnemySpawner already requires for spawning at all: a Humanoid and a PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart. EnemyBrain.Register re-checks both of these independently and silently skips arming the enemy if either is missing — so a rig that spawns fine but never moves or fires is almost always missing one of these two parts.  Optional Muzzle attachment​  For a visually accurate origin, add an Attachment named exactly Muzzle anywhere in the rig's descendant hierarchy (typically welded to a held weapon model's barrel tip). EnemyWeapon.MuzzleOrigin finds it via model:FindFirstChild("Muzzle", true) (a recursive search) and fires from its WorldPosition. Without one, fire still works — it falls back to the root part's CFrame offset by the profile's MuzzleOffset, a perfectly playable art-less placeholder. Add the attachment (and a welded weapon model, and optional FireAnimId) whenever art is ready; no code changes are needed either way.  Arming an archetype: the two-registry relationship​  This is the most common setup mistake, so it's worth stating explicitly: an archetype needs entries in BOTH registries to be a functioning armed enemy.  EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes[name] — required for the archetype to spawn at all (Model name, Health, WalkSpeed, DefaultRadius, optional Faction). See Enemy Spawner → Tuning.EnemyCombatConfig.Profiles[name] — required for the spawned enemy to be armed (move toward and fire at players). Keyed by the same archetype name as above.  An archetype with only #1 spawns, walks nowhere on its own, and never fires — useful for cosmetic/decorative NPCs or placeholder testing before combat tuning is ready. An archetype with only #2 (a profile with no matching spawner entry) is simply dead config — EnemySpawner.placeAt is the only call site for EnemyBrain.Register, so a profile with no way to spawn the archetype never gets used. There is no validation or warning today if these two registries drift out of sync (e.g. renaming an archetype in one but not the other) — check both tables by hand when adding or renaming an archetype.  Verifying combat in Studio​  No additional Studio-side wiring is required beyond the two config entries above and the rig requirements — EnemyBrain.Init() is called once automatically by EnemyCombatSystemLoader.server.luau at server start, the same pattern as EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau calling EnemySpawner.Init(). Spawn a wave with an archetype that has both registry entries and the enemy should path toward the nearest player and open fire once in range.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Telegraph and burst values are tuned by feel, not measured ProjectileSpeed, Spread, Telegraph, and the burst/cooldown ranges directly control how dodgeable and how punishing each archetype is. There is no automated test for "is this fair" — these are Studio-playtest-and-adjust knobs, the same as PATH_BUDGET_PER_TICK/REPATH_INTERVAL/REPATH_THRESHOLD/TICK_HZ at the top of EnemyBrain.luau. Adjust archetype values in EnemyCombatConfig directly; avoid touching EnemyBrain's tick/path constants unless movement itself feels laggy or pathfinding spikes with large waves.  Cosmetic bullet/throwable templates are optional, not required EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile's cosmetic bullet (ServerProjectile.spawnRocket) and EnemyWeapon.Lob's throwable charge (ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable) both look up a template by profile.Weapon in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets. If the named template doesn't exist yet, both functions are nil-safe — the shot/lob still fires, damages, and broadcasts its FX packet; it just has no visible travelling model. Add WeaponAssets/EnemySMG (etc.) whenever art is ready; this is a drop-in, no code change.  Re-engagement always restarts the burst from scratch By design (see the telegraph-reset fix), an enemy that loses LOS or range mid-burst does not "remember" how many shots it had left — it goes back to "Idle" and rolls an entirely new BurstMin–BurstMax count next time it can see and reach the target. This is intentional fairness behavior, not a bug: do not "fix" it by trying to persist shotsLeft/nextShotAt across an interruption, as that would let a player skip past a sniper's telegraph window by breaking LOS for a single frame.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Fuzzy Hologram (PartyPerkBuffs.EnemyAccuracyPenalty): EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile widens the spread cone × (1 + penalty).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant B as EnemyBrain (10 Hz tick) participant W as EnemyWeapon participant FC as FastCast2 (bulletCaster) participant CS as CombatService participant Fx as WeaponEffectsController (all clients) Note over B: tick(): reacquire target -> stepMovement -> stepFiringRanged B->>B: stepFiringRanged: fireState machine (Idle -> Bursting -> Cooldown) B->>B: hasLineOfSight? in Range? else reset "Bursting" -> "Idle" B->>W: fireOneShot -> EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile(model, profile, origin, targetPos) W->>FC: cast bullet at ProjectileSpeed (+ Spread) FC-->>W: LengthChanged (steps optional cosmetic part) FC-->>W: Hit(target) OR miss-timeout backstop W->>CS: CombatService.ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, Damage, "Bullet", enemyModel) CS->>CS: Factions.canDamage("Enemy","Player") gate CS->>CS: HealthManager.ApplyDamage (armor mitigation) W->>Fx: Packets.WeaponFired(shooter=enemyModel, weaponName, origin, endpoint, isHit) Fx->>Fx: WeaponFx.resolve(weaponName) -> WeaponConfig or EnemyCombatConfig.FindByWeapon Fx->>Fx: render tracer + impact FX (shooter is never == local Player, so always renders)

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: EnemyCombatConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemyCombatConfig.luau. Tune per-archetype values here directly; see the Shipped archetypes table above.  EnemyBrain.luau constant	Default	EffectTICK_HZ	10	AI director tick rate (Hz); all movement/firing decisions happen on this cadence. PATH_BUDGET_PER_TICK	1	Max ComputeAsync calls allocated per tick across all enemies combined. REPATH_INTERVAL	1.0s	Minimum time between an enemy's path recomputes. REPATH_THRESHOLD	8 studs	Target drift from the path's original goal that forces an early repath. WAYPOINT_REACHED	3 studs	Distance to a waypoint that advances to the next one.  These tick/path constants are Studio-playtest-and-adjust knobs, not automated-test-verified — avoid touching them unless movement itself feels laggy or pathfinding spikes with large waves.

searchDocs.title: API​
searchDocs.content: EnemyBrainEnemyWeaponWeaponFxEnemyCombatConfigEnemy Spawner — owns spawning/placement; EnemyBrain.Register is called from its placeAt function and is the only bridge between the two systems.Weapons — the player-facing combat system whose damage layer (CombatService, WeaponValidation, ServerProjectile, FastCast2) is reused here.Architecture → Backbone — the Factions faction model that gates all damage, enemy or player.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleServer	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemySpawner.luau	Group registry, point selection, jitter, placement, SpawnWave/SpawnAt/ResetGroup, drip-feed scheduling, global cap Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemyWave.luau	WaveHandle factory: Janitor-backed enemy tracker, OnCleared signal, Despawn/Destroy Server	src/ServerScriptService/EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau	Thin bootstrap: calls EnemySpawner.Init() once per server Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnVerification.luau	Stateless ground/wall/spacing validator; returns a ground-snapped position on success Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau	OnEnemySpawned signal registration Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemySpawnerConfig.luau	Archetype registry, global tuning constants, Verification.* knobs; validates model names against ServerStorage.EnemyAssets at load  Packets: none — spawned Models replicate to clients via native Roblox replicationSignals: OnEnemySpawned — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Authoring contract​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawnGroup. A spawn group is a Model in the DataModel tagged with the CollectionService tag EnemySpawnGroup. The group's identity is its GroupName string attribute; if the attribute is absent the model's .Name is used. The tag is all that is required — any Model (a pirate ship, an outpost building, a plain Part wrapped in a Model) becomes a valid group. Because spawn-point attachments are descendants of the group Model, their .WorldPosition moves automatically with the model's CFrame — placing the group on a moving ship and calling SpawnWave places enemies relative to the ship's current pose at spawn time, with no code changes.  EnemySpawnPoint. Each spawn point is an Attachment tagged EnemySpawnPoint, parented anywhere beneath the group model. Two optional per-point attributes control selection and jitter:  Attribute	Type	Default	PurposeRadius	number	archetype DefaultRadius → DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS	Radial jitter disc radius in studs Weight	number	1	Base selection weight before the cumulative-inverse falloff  Points are visually editable in Studio — add, remove, or move an attachment and the spawner picks it up immediately (the cache is rebuilt on first use per group, and a CollectionService.GetInstanceRemovedSignal listener invalidates the group if the root model is untagged or removed).  EnemyAssets folder. Enemy Model assets live in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/. Each child Model must have a Humanoid (authoritative stats are applied at spawn time from the archetype config, but the Humanoid must exist for health/death tracking) and a PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart (used for pivot placement and SpawnVerification spacing tests). At module load, EnemySpawnerConfig validates every archetype's Model name against EnemyAssets children and emits a warn for any missing model. Building before art is ready is fully supported: register a placeholder dummy (any Model with a Humanoid) under the expected name.

searchDocs.title: Public API​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawner is a server-only module. Call EnemySpawner.Init() once from the system loader before using the rest of the API.  EnemySpawner.Init()   Called once by EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau at server start. Creates workspace.ActiveEnemies if absent and wires the group-cache invalidation listener.  EnemySpawner.SpawnWave(groupName: string, request: SpawnRequest): WaveHandle   Spawns request.count enemies across the named group's points using the selection algorithm below. composition is either a single archetype name ("PirateGrunt") or a weighted table ({ PirateGrunt = 3, PirateScout = 1 }) — rolled per enemy. If request.interval > 0, spawns are staggered in a task.spawn loop (drip-feed); the WaveHandle is returned immediately and OnCleared waits for both all spawns to be attempted and all registered enemies to die. If request.seed is set, the internal Random is re-seeded for deterministic reproduction.  export type SpawnRequest = { count: number, composition: string | { [string]: number }, interval: number?, -- seconds between spawns; nil/0 = all at once seed: number?, -- optional deterministic RNG seed }   EnemySpawner.SpawnAt(groupName: string, pointName: string, archetypeName: string): Model?   Direct escape hatch: place exactly one archetype at the named attachment (matched by Attachment.Name), still subject to verification. Returns the placed Model or nil if verification fails after MaxRetries or the point/archetype is not found.  EnemySpawner.ResetGroup(groupName: string)   Clears the group's cumulative per-point spawn counts. Call this at the start of each new encounter so point weighting begins fresh. Deaths do not reduce a point's count; only ResetGroup does.

searchDocs.title: Per-enemy spawn algorithm​
searchDocs.content: For each enemy in a wave the spawner runs:  Select a point — weighted random over the group's EnemySpawnPoint attachments. Effective weight is point.Weight / (cumulativeCount + 1) ^ WeightFalloff, where cumulativeCount is the number of enemies spawned from that point this encounter. A point with count 0 carries its full base weight; counts are per-encounter (ResetGroup resets them, enemy deaths do not).Jitter — candidate position = point world position + a uniform random offset within a disc of the point's Radius on the XZ plane. The disc uses sqrt(NextNumber()) * radius so the distribution is uniform over the area rather than biased toward the centre.Verify — the candidate is passed to SpawnVerification with the archetype's body size, an ignore list containing the group model and the ActiveEnemies folder, and the current list of living enemies.Retry-then-skip — steps 2–3 repeat up to Verification.MaxRetries times. If no valid position is found, the enemy is skipped (a warn is emitted) and the wave continues. The wave never hard-fails; it never places a broken enemy.Place — if the global cap (GLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES) is already met, the enemy is skipped with a warn. Otherwise the archetype Model is cloned from ServerStorage.EnemyAssets, archetype stats are applied (Humanoid.MaxHealth/Health/WalkSpeed), the model is tagged EnemyNPC (or FriendlyNPC if archetype.Faction == "Friendly"), pivoted to the verified ground-snapped CFrame, parented to workspace.ActiveEnemies, and the point's cumulative count is incremented. The spawned model is registered with the wave handle, EnemyChrono.Track(model) registers it as a Chrono entity (see Chrono Replication), EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) is called (see Enemy Combat), and Signals.OnEnemySpawned fires with the placed position and archetype name.  SpawnVerification​  SpawnVerification (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnVerification.luau) is a stateless pure-geometry validator with no server-only dependencies. It lives in SharedModules so it is independently testable and reusable from a future client-side preview; all v1 callers are server-side.  SpawnVerification.Verify( candidate: Vector3, bodySize: Vector3, ignoreList: { Instance }, livingEnemies: { Model } ): VerifyResult -- { ok: boolean, position: Vector3?, reason: string? }   Checks run cheapest-first with short-circuit on failure:  Ground below — workspace:Raycast straight down from candidate + (0, 2, 0) up to MaxGroundDrop studs, excluding ignoreList. No hit returns { ok = false, reason = "void" }. On hit, the Y position snaps to the floor: snapped.Y = hit.Position.Y + bodySize.Y / 2.Clear of walls / headroom — workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox of HeadroomSize centred on the snapped position, excluding ignoreList. Any solid collidable part returns { ok = false, reason = "blocked" } — this catches both embedded-in-wall and under-floor cases.Spacing — if any model in livingEnemies has its pivot within MinEnemySpacing studs of the snapped position, returns { ok = false, reason = "crowded" }.  A successful check returns { ok = true, position = snapped }.

searchDocs.title: WaveHandle lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: SpawnWave returns a WaveHandle backed by a Janitor. The handle tracks every spawned enemy's death and removal.  export type WaveHandle = { OnCleared: Signal<()>, -- fires once: all enemies dead AND wave complete GetAlive: (self) -> number, -- count of enemies still alive GetEnemies: (self) -> { Model }, -- list of enemies still alive Despawn: (self) -> (), -- destroy remaining enemies + remove from tracking Destroy: (self) -> (), -- Despawn + Janitor teardown }   Each spawned enemy's Humanoid.Died and AncestryChanged (for despawn-without-death) are connected via the handle's Janitor. OnCleared fires once when the alive count reaches zero and the wave has been marked complete (all drip-feed spawns attempted) — killing enemies before the last drip-feed slot fires will not trigger OnCleared prematurely.  local wave = EnemySpawner.SpawnWave("PirateShip", { count = 6, composition = { PirateGrunt = 3, PirateScout = 1 }, -- hypothetical second archetype interval = 0.5, }) wave.OnCleared:Connect(function() resumeEncounter() end)   Despawn lets an orchestrator abort a wave early (encounter cancelled, train resumes) and cleanly destroy remaining enemies; calling it when all enemies are already dead is a safe no-op. Destroy implies Despawn and additionally tears down the Janitor.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawnGroup model: select any Model in the workspace (pirate ship, outpost, or a plain wrapped Part), tag it EnemySpawnGroup via the Studio Tag Editor, and optionally set a GroupName string attribute (defaults to model.Name).  EnemySpawnPoint attachments: under the group model, insert one or more Attachment instances, tag each EnemySpawnPoint, and optionally add Radius/Weight number attributes. The attachment's Studio position is the spawn point's world-space origin at runtime; move attachments freely, the spawner reads .WorldPosition live at spawn time.  EnemyAssets folder: create a folder named EnemyAssets inside ServerStorage; each child Model needs a Humanoid and a PrimaryPart/HumanoidRootPart, and its name must match the Model field in the corresponding EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes entry. Minimum viable setup for testing before art is ready: insert a default Roblox Dummy into ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/ and rename it to match an archetype (e.g. PirateGrunt) — the archetype validation warning clears and SpawnWave clones the dummy.  Collision and combat wiring​  No additional Studio wiring is required for collision passthrough or combat. Spawned enemies are tagged EnemyNPC (or FriendlyNPC), and both services detect the tag automatically via CollectionService.GetInstanceAddedSignal:  NpcCollisionService places their parts in the Character collision group (registered and matrixed by CollisionGroups) so players and thrown charges (WeaponProjectile) pass through them — the non-player sibling of CharacterCollisionService, which does the same for player characters.CombatService.ApplyToModel resolves them via Factions so weapon hits deal damage.  placeAt also calls EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) immediately after placement, arming any archetype that has a matching EnemyCombatConfig profile so it paths toward and fires at players. Archetypes with no profile entry are unaffected — Register no-ops and they remain passive. See Enemy Combat for the full director, weapon, and config breakdown.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: WaveHandle OnCleared requires both conditions OnCleared fires only when the alive count is zero AND all drip-feed spawns have been attempted (MarkComplete called internally). In an instant wave (interval = 0) this means OnCleared can fire during SpawnWave itself, before it returns, if every enemy was skipped. Always set up OnCleared connections before calling SpawnWave; do not assume it is deferred.  Cumulative counts survive across waves; ResetGroup does not run automatically. If SpawnWave is called a second time without resetting, previously-used points start at a cumulative disadvantage. For repeating encounter patterns (waves 1, 2, 3…), decide explicitly whether to reset between waves or let cumulative weighting carry across the full encounter.  GLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES counts workspace.ActiveEnemies children. If enemies are not parented there (e.g. manually cloned models outside the spawner), they do not count toward the cap, which may allow over-cap situations. Always spawn enemies through EnemySpawner.  SpawnVerification is in SharedModules but is server-only in v1. It has no server-only dependencies so it can be reused from a future client-side preview (e.g. displaying valid spawn zones in a director tool), but in v1 all calls happen server-side via EnemySpawner. Do not call it on the client in production without auditing the ignoreList/livingEnemies arguments for client-visible data.  Archetype validation warns but does not error. If a model is missing from EnemyAssets at load time, EnemySpawnerConfig emits a warn but does not error; the spawner also warns (and skips the enemy) at spawn time if the model is still absent. Register placeholder models early to keep the Output clean during development.

searchDocs.title: Future directions​
searchDocs.content: Off-screen spawn preference — an additional weighting term in the point-selection step that demotes EnemySpawnPoints currently inside any player's camera frustum, so enemies appear from behind cover or the edge of vision.Reachability pre-check — PathfindingService:CreatePath from the verified candidate to the nearest player, rejecting candidates in sealed-off areas. This is the deferred line-of-sight check in SpawnVerification, done properly.Encounter director — a layer above the spawner that scales count/composition/interval by wave number, player count, or Tech Tree progress. The spawner stays a dumb placement service; the director owns escalation and pacing.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant O as Orchestrator participant ES as EnemySpawner participant SV as SpawnVerification participant EB as EnemyBrain participant W as WaveHandle O->>ES: SpawnWave(groupName, { count, composition, interval, seed? }) ES->>W: create WaveHandle (Janitor-backed) ES-->>O: return WaveHandle (immediately) loop per enemy (drip-fed if interval > 0) ES->>ES: select point (cumulative-inverse weight) ES->>ES: jitter position within point Radius ES->>SV: Verify(candidate, bodySize, ignoreList, livingEnemies) SV-->>ES: { ok, position, reason } alt verification failed after MaxRetries ES->>ES: skip enemy (warn) else global cap reached ES->>ES: skip enemy (warn) else success ES->>ES: clone from EnemyAssets, apply stats, tag EnemyNPC/FriendlyNPC ES->>W: register spawned Model (tracks Died/AncestryChanged) ES->>ES: EnemyChrono.Track(model) ES->>EB: EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) ES->>ES: Signals.OnEnemySpawned:Fire(position, archetypeName) end end ES->>W: MarkComplete (all drip-feed spawns attempted) Note over W: OnCleared fires once alive count = 0 AND MarkComplete W-->>O: OnCleared

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: EnemySpawnerConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemySpawnerConfig.luau  All tuning lives in this module. It is accessible from both client and server; the archetype validation block is guarded by RunService:IsServer() since ServerStorage is inaccessible on the client.  Field	Default	EffectGLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES	40	Hard cap on total active enemies across all groups. Exceeding the cap skips spawns with a warn. Lower temporarily to verify the cap in Studio. DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS	6	Fallback jitter disc radius (studs) when neither the point Radius attribute nor the archetype DefaultRadius is set. WeightFalloff	1.0	Exponent k in effectiveWeight = baseWeight / (count + 1) ^ k. At 1.0 weight halves each time a point is used. Raise to flatten selection (less adaptive); lower toward 0 to disable cumulative penalisation. Verification.MaxGroundDrop	25	Maximum downward raycast distance (studs) to find a floor below the candidate. Verification.HeadroomSize	Vector3.new(3, 6, 3)	Box dimensions used for the wall/headroom overlap check. Should match or slightly exceed the tallest enemy body. Verification.MinEnemySpacing	4	Minimum distance (studs) between a new candidate and any already-living enemy pivot. Verification.MaxRetries	8	Number of jitter re-rolls before an enemy is skipped with a warn. Archetypes	(see below)	Per-archetype table: Model (child name in EnemyAssets), Health, WalkSpeed, DefaultRadius, optional Faction ("Enemy" / "Friendly"; defaults to "Enemy").  EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes = { PirateGrunt = { Model = "PirateGrunt", Health = 100, WalkSpeed = 14, DefaultRadius = 6 }, }   Adding a new archetype: add an entry here, create the corresponding Model in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/, and the spawner picks it up at next load — no code changes elsewhere are needed. Note that an archetype also needs a matching entry in EnemyCombatConfig.Profiles to be armed; see Enemy Combat → Studio setup.
