searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleServer	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EventOrchestrator.luau	Odometer loop, per-channel state machines, weighted roll + pity, handler registry Server	src/ServerScriptService/EventSystemLoader.server.luau	Bootstrap — registers handlers, calls EventOrchestrator.Init() Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/Events/PirateAttackEvent.luau	Handler stub; wires to EnemySpawner.SpawnWave Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/Events/OutpostEvent.luau	Handler stub; side-attribute marker for a fixed window Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EventConfig.luau	Cruise speed, tick interval, per-channel roll tables/cadence, per-event parameters, master enable switch  Packets: none — the orchestrator never touches networking; each handler owns its own client communicationSignals: OnGameEventStarted, OnGameEventEnded — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Master switch​
searchDocs.content: EventConfig.Enabled gates the entire system — while false, EventOrchestrator.Init() registers nothing, builds no channels, and never starts the odometer loop; the orchestrator stays fully dormant. It defaults to false pending the Studio wiring tracked in TODO.md.

searchDocs.title: The virtual odometer​
searchDocs.content: The train has no physical speed/odometer of its own — TrainFuelManager only tracks Running/Braked/Stalled state. EventOrchestrator owns its own distance counter: a task.spawn loop ticks every EventConfig.TickInterval seconds (0.25s by default — ample precision for event cadence and cheaper than a per-frame Heartbeat). While running is true it accumulates EventConfig.CruiseSpeed * dt into the odometer, then ticks every channel. running is driven by Signals.SetTrainState (fired by TrainFuelManager on every brake/stall flip) — accumulation pauses on brake, stall, and the pre-game freeze. Signals.SetTrainStarted(true) (first un-brake of a round) calls EventOrchestrator.Reset(), zeroing the odometer and returning every channel to Idle, including force-finishing any handler that's currently Active via its finish().

searchDocs.title: Channel model​
searchDocs.content: Channels run fully independently, each with its own roll table, cadence, and state:  Encounter — PirateAttack and Outpost share this channel and are mutually exclusive (only one can be active at a time).  Each channel is a state machine: Idle → Active → Cooldown → Idle.  Phase	BehaviorIdle	Every RollInterval boundary crossed since the last tick rolls the weighted table once (a long pause/lag spike doesn't skip rolls). A real pick moves the channel to Active. Active	The chosen handler's Start(ctx, finish) is running. A MaxActiveDistance watchdog (if > 0) force-finishes a handler that never calls finish(). Other channels keep rolling independently. Cooldown	After finish(), the channel stays quiet until PostEventDelay odometer studs have passed, then returns to Idle with lastRollAt reset to the current odometer (the next roll is a full RollInterval away, not immediate).

searchDocs.title: Weighted roll + pity​
searchDocs.content: Each channel's Table is a list of RollEntrys — either a real event ({ Event = "PirateAttack", Weight = 50 }) or the no-op entry ({ Nothing = true, Weight = 20 }). On each roll:  Build the eligible candidate set: real entries are excluded if their handler's optional CanTrigger(ctx) returns false (or no handler is registered for that Id); the Nothing entry is excluded outright when pity is forcing a real event.Pick one candidate by weight (Random:NextNumber(0, total) against cumulative weight).If the pick is Nothing (or nothing was eligible), emptyRollStreak increments and the channel stays Idle.If the pick is a real event, emptyRollStreak resets to 0 and the channel activates that event's handler.  Pity: once emptyRollStreak >= PityRolls, the next roll excludes the Nothing entry, forcing a real event. This bounds the maximum distance a channel can go without a real event to roughly (PityRolls + 1) * RollInterval studs.

searchDocs.title: EventHandler interface​
searchDocs.content: export type EventContext = { odometer: number, -- current odometer value at roll/activation time rng: Random, -- orchestrator-owned Random instance channel: string, -- the channel name this activation belongs to janitor: Janitor.Janitor, -- per-activation Janitor; destroyed automatically on finish() } export type EventHandler = { Id: string, -- unique; must match an EventConfig table entry Channel: string, -- which channel this handler is registered under CanTrigger: ((ctx: EventContext) -> boolean)?, -- optional eligibility guard, checked at roll time Start: (ctx: EventContext, finish: () -> ()) -> (), -- begin the event; call finish() exactly once when done }   Handlers register via EventOrchestrator.RegisterHandler(handler) (call before Init(), from the system loader). A duplicate Id is ignored with a warn. Start runs inside a pcall; a throwing handler is logged and the channel is force-finished into Cooldown so one bad event can't wedge the channel. finish is guarded by a per-activation nonce — late or duplicate calls (e.g. a watchdog firing after the handler already finished normally) are no-ops. ctx.janitor is destroyed automatically the moment finish() resolves, so handlers should hang connections/instances/cleanup off it rather than tearing down manually. A load-time validation pass (validate() in Init) warns if a config table references an Id with no registered handler, or a handler's Channel doesn't match the channel it's listed under (or targets an unknown channel) — these are warnings, not hard errors, matching the EnemySpawnerConfig missing-model convention.

searchDocs.title: Public API​
searchDocs.content: EventOrchestrator.RegisterHandler(handler: EventHandler)   Registers a handler module. Call before Init() (from the system loader).  EventOrchestrator.Init()   Builds channel state from EventConfig.Channels, runs the validation pass, subscribes to Signals.SetTrainState / Signals.SetTrainStarted, and starts the odometer loop. No-ops entirely while EventConfig.Enabled is false. Idempotent otherwise — a second call warns and is ignored.  EventOrchestrator.Reset()   Zeroes the odometer, force-finishes any Active channel (via its handler's finish), and returns every channel to Idle with lastRollAt reseeded from StartGrace. Called automatically on Signals.SetTrainStarted(true).  EventOrchestrator.GetState()   Returns a snapshot (odometer, running, per-channel phase/lastRollAt/emptyRollStreak/activeId/cooldownUntil) for debugging/inspection.

searchDocs.title: The two event handlers (stubs)​
searchDocs.content: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/Events/ holds one module per event, each implementing EventHandler. Both are intentionally thin — full behavior is deferred to later, per-event specs:  PirateAttackEvent (Channel = "Encounter") — calls EnemySpawner.SpawnWave with the group/wave composition from EventConfig.Events.PirateAttack, hangs the returned WaveHandle off ctx.janitor (so a force-finish despawns survivors), and calls finish when WaveHandle.OnCleared fires. It also sets the replicated workspace attribute PirateAttackActive = true on start; its janitor sets it back to false on every end path (wave cleared, watchdog, reset, jump pause) — Free Runner reads it. This is the one handler with "real" wiring; wave difficulty/rewards are a later spec.OutpostEvent (Channel = "Encounter") — picks a side via ctx.rng, sets a workspace attribute (ActiveOutpostSide), and calls finish after a fixed distance window approximated as time at CruiseSpeed (a handler has no direct access to the live odometer tick). Approach telegraph, stop-by prompt, and outpost contents are a later spec.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Master switch defaults off EventConfig.Enabled = false. Until flipped, Init() returns immediately and the orchestrator never rolls, subscribes to signals, or starts its loop — check this first if events "aren't firing" in a playtest.  Reset force-finishes Active handlers, not Cooldown EventOrchestrator.Reset() only calls activeFinish() for a channel currently in the Active phase. A channel in Cooldown is simply snapped back to Idle — there's no handler running to finish. A round reset mid-cooldown discards the cooldown window rather than honoring it.  OutpostEvent's window is time-based, not distance-based Because a handler doesn't have direct access to the live odometer tick, OutpostEvent approximates its Window (studs) as Window / EventConfig.CruiseSpeed seconds and uses task.delay. If the train brakes or stalls during the window, the outpost still ends on the original wall-clock timer rather than pausing with the odometer. Called out as a stub limitation in the handler's own doc comment.  Channels are independent; "Encounter" exclusivity is per-channel, not global PirateAttack and Outpost cannot overlap because they share the Encounter channel. A future event on its own channel could roll and activate while an Encounter event is Active; one needing true global exclusivity would need an explicit cross-channel guard (e.g. a CanTrigger that inspects another channel's state).  Biome change is now a player-initiated Jump Drive action, not a random orchestrator event — see Jump Drive.

searchDocs.title: Future directions​
searchDocs.content: See the design spec's "Out of scope" section: full Pirate-attack behavior (wave composition/difficulty/rewards), full Outpost behavior (approach telegraph, stop-by prompt, contents, departure), any client HUD/banner, and persistence of event history across sessions.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Fuel as TrainFuelManager participant Orc as EventOrchestrator participant H as EventHandler (e.g. PirateAttackEvent) Fuel->>Orc: Signals.SetTrainStarted(true) Orc->>Orc: Reset() - zero odometer, all channels Idle Fuel->>Orc: Signals.SetTrainState(isRunning) Orc->>Orc: running = isRunning loop every TickInterval while running Orc->>Orc: odometer += CruiseSpeed * dt Orc->>Orc: tickChannel() per channel alt Idle, RollInterval boundary crossed Orc->>Orc: weightedPick() - CanTrigger filter, pity check alt real event picked Orc->>Orc: activate() - phase=Active Orc->>H: Signals.OnGameEventStarted(eventId); Start(ctx, finish) else Nothing / no eligible candidate Orc->>Orc: emptyRollStreak += 1 end else Active, MaxActiveDistance exceeded Orc->>H: force-call finish() (watchdog), warn end end H->>Orc: finish() Orc->>Orc: ctx.janitor:Destroy(); phase=Cooldown; cooldownUntil = odometer + PostEventDelay Orc->>Orc: Signals.OnGameEventEnded(eventId)

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: EventConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EventConfig.luau  Field	Scope	EffectEnabled	global	Master on/off switch. false disables the orchestrator entirely (no registration, no loop). CruiseSpeed	global	Virtual odometer rate in studs/sec, accumulated only while the train is running. TickInterval	global	Seconds between odometer-loop ticks (task.wait cadence). Weight	per roll-table entry	Relative chance this entry (event or Nothing) is picked on a roll. RollInterval	per channel	Odometer studs between roll attempts on this channel. PostEventDelay	per channel	Quiet studs after an event's finish() before the channel resumes rolling. PityRolls	per channel	Consecutive empty rolls before the Nothing entry is excluded, forcing a real event. StartGrace	per channel	Odometer offset before the channel's first roll (keeps players from being ambushed the instant the train starts moving). MaxActiveDistance	per channel	Watchdog: if an Active handler hasn't called finish() within this many odometer studs, the orchestrator force-finishes it with a warn. 0 disables the watchdog.  Current channel values for Encounter and the per-event parameter tables (EventConfig.Events.PirateAttack / .Outpost) live directly in the config module — see it for exact numbers, since those are expected to be tuned independently of this page.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPack/Grabhook/GrabHook.client.luau	Tool activation, spherecast aim, force-field highlight, grapple animation orchestration, sound scheduling Server	src/ServerScriptService/JunkService.server.luau	Validates claim/finalize requests (see Junk) Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/GrabHookVisuals.luau	Beam creation and projectile / observer animation loops Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/GrabHookConfig.luau	All physics, visuals, and sound timing constants  Packets: none directly — claims/finalizes flow through Packets.ReqJunkClaim / ReqJunkClaimBatch / ReqJunkFinalize, fired by JunkController on behalf of the GrabHook (see Junk and Networking Map)Signals: TryClaimJunk, TryClaimJunkBatch, TryFinalizeJunk, RequestShootingCamera, RequestReticleScale — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Aiming​
searchDocs.content: GrabHook.client.luau runs entirely as a LocalScript inside the Grabhook Tool under StarterPack. On equip, mouse.TargetFilter is set to the PlacedObjects folder so placed items don't occlude aim, and Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true) puts CameraController into aim mode. Every RenderStepped frame while equipped, GetAimedJunk(rootPart) performs a Spherecast from the handle's Attachment.WorldPosition toward mouse.Hit.Position — radius Physics.HitboxRadius (2 studs), max distance Physics.MaxDistance (150 studs), gated to within 90° of the character's forward vector. The junk ID is resolved by invoking GetJunkIdFromPart via BindableCore (registered by JunkController).  A force-field highlight (ReplicatedStorage/ForceField template cloned to workspace) tracks the currently aimed junk part on every RenderStepped tick; if aim is found it calls ShowForceField(junkPart, junkId), and a 0.08-second grace window prevents flickering (HideForceField) when the spherecast briefly misses.

searchDocs.title: Firing​
searchDocs.content: On tool.Activated, if no earlier cast is still reeling in (canShoot), the client fires Signals.TryClaimJunk(id, hitPoint) (handled by JunkController), increments fireToken to version all pending callbacks, then calls FireGrappleAndAttach(targetPart, hitPoint, junkId, token):  Creates an Attachment on the junk part ("HookAttachment").Calls GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam(handleAtt, junkAtt, targetPart).Calls GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile, a three-phase animation: Flight (junkAtt.WorldPosition lerps toward the junk at Physics.Speed = 200 studs/s, beam curves oscillate with Amplitude=12, Frequency=40, Decay=4), Latch (a single transition frame, curves flattened to 0), Retract (targetPart.Position lerps back to the handle at Physics.RetractSpeed = 50 studs/s).On retract complete, fires Signals.TryFinalizeJunk(id) (handled by JunkController).  SoundManager.PlaySFXAt("GrabHookFire") plays a shot replicated to all clients; SoundManager.PlayLooped("GrabHookLoop") schedules a fade-in/out loop. When retraction completes, the collector hears the 2D MaterialCollect cue (the same cue the Materials HUD plays), so Wood/Metal pickups are as audible as Energy. The loop sound is scheduled with a LoopStartDelay (0.15 s) fade-in and a timed fade-out matched to the total hook animation duration.

searchDocs.title: Unequipping​
searchDocs.content: On unequip, fireToken is incremented (invalidating all pending task.delay callbacks), loopHandle:Destroy() runs, and Signals.RequestShootingCamera(false) returns CameraController to its normal mode.

searchDocs.title: Wide Net perk (multi-catch)​
searchDocs.content: The WideNet perk (see Perks) raises hook capacity beyond 1. netCapacity() reads NetCapacityBonus client-side through PerkBuffRead.Personal: capacity = 1 + NetCapacityBonus. At capacity 1 (no perk levels) the tool is byte-for-byte identical to the base single-hook path (GetAimedJunk + Signals.TryClaimJunk). At capacity ≥ 2:  Aim — GetAimedJunks(rootPart, capacity) replaces the single spherecast with workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox at GrabHookConfig.Physics.NetHitboxRadius (4 studs) along the aim line, returning up to capacity NetTargets ({ id, part, hitPos }) sorted by distance.Fire — one tool.Activated still means one cast (the next cast waits for the last beam), one GrabHookFire sound, and one loop sound, but drives a beam per target. Claim ids are batched through Signals.TryClaimJunkBatch:Fire(ids) (consumed by JunkController, which invokes Packets.ReqJunkClaimBatch) instead of the per-junk TryClaimJunk. Finalize remains per-junk (Signals.TryFinalizeJunk / ReqJunkFinalize) once each beam's retraction completes.Server clamp — JunkService.ClaimJunkBatchForPlayer never trusts the client's capacity or positions: it re-reads NetCapacityBonus from the published buff folder, clamps to GrabHookConfig.Physics.NetMaxTargets (5, hard cap), and reconstructs each junk's position from the junk odometer (SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer)) before reserving it.Reticle — on equip, if netCapacity() >= 2, fires Signals.RequestReticleScale(CameraConfig.NetReticleScale) (1.6×) so CameraController enlarges the aim reticle; otherwise fires RequestReticleScale(1). Unequip always fires RequestReticleScale(1) unconditionally, so the reticle never gets stuck enlarged.Highlighting — the force-field highlight loop shows one force field per currently-aimed NetTarget instead of a single one when capacity ≥ 2.Reel slowdown — a fuller net reels slower: the reel speed is multiplied by PerkBuffRead.NetReelFactor(caught) = max(0.1, 1 − 0.10 × (caught − 1)). The client uses the aimed count; the server uses the count it accepted when it times BeginJunkRetract.

searchDocs.title: Shared visuals​
searchDocs.content: GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam(att0, att1, parent) instantiates a Beam and copies all properties from GrabHookConfig.Visuals onto it. AnimateProjectile(beam, startAtt, targetPart, hitPos, onCleanup, retractSpeed?) (reel speed with perks applied; defaults to Physics.RetractSpeed) runs the three-phase RenderStepped loop (Flight / Latch / Retract), aborts if targetPart leaves workspace (e.g. pool reclaim), and calls onCleanup when retraction completes or on abort. AnimateObserver(beam, startAtt) is a simpler decay loop for other players watching the retraction animation, started by JunkController on BeginJunkRetract.

searchDocs.title: Server-side validation​
searchDocs.content: ReqJunkClaim reconstructs junk world position from SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer), checks player distance against MaxDistance × (1 + HookRangeBonus) + 15 studs, rejects the claim while the player still has a pull in flight (reserved, not collected, before its reel-in end), and reserves the junk. There is no time cooldown: the next cast is allowed as soon as the pulled junk lands. ReqJunkFinalize checks reservation ownership and the reservation deadline (reel-in time + 5 s), marks the junk collected, broadcasts JunkCollected, and gives the corresponding tool to player.Backpack. See Junk for the full server-side claim/finalize detail.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Server proximity check uses a latency slack of 15 studs The claim check compares the player's position against the reconstructed junk position with GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15. The extra 15 studs compensates for network latency. Increasing MaxDistance without adjusting the slack (or vice versa) can allow or block claims unexpectedly.  Shift-lock / aim camera interplay. Equipping the GrabHook fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true) to enter aim mode. Unequipping fires (false) to exit. If you add another system that also drives RequestShootingCamera, ensure the signals do not conflict (last writer wins).mouse.TargetFilter = PlacedObjects prevents placed items from blocking the aim raycast. If new workspace folders are added for collidable world geometry that should also be ignored, add them to the filter.fireToken versioning. Incrementing fireToken on unequip cancels all pending task.delay callbacks (sound fade-out, finalize). Never skip the token check inside scheduled callbacks or sounds will play on the next hook cycle.Force-field template must exist. GrabHook.client uses ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForceField") at startup. If the template is missing, the script will yield indefinitely.Beam and attachment cleanup. AnimateProjectile destroys both the Beam and the HookAttachment on cleanup. If you add more attachments or constraints to the junk part during a hook cycle, extend the CleanupJunkModel function in JunkController to remove them on pool return.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Wide Net (permanent, HookAimBonus 0.05/level): GrabHook.client scales HitboxRadius and NetHitboxRadius × (1 + HookAimBonus). Client only: the server checks reach distance, and REACH_SLACK covers the wider cast.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant G as GrabHook (client) participant Cam as CameraController participant JC as JunkController participant S as JunkService (server) P->>G: Equip GrabHook tool G->>Cam: RequestShootingCamera(true) loop RenderStepped while equipped G->>G: GetAimedJunk - Spherecast toward mouse.Hit alt junk found G->>G: ShowForceField(junkPart, junkId) else aim lost > 0.08s G->>G: HideForceField end end P->>G: tool.Activated (no cast in flight) G->>JC: Signals.TryClaimJunk(id, hitPoint) JC->>S: ReqJunkClaim S->>JC: BeginJunkRetract (broadcast) G->>G: FireGrappleAndAttach: Flight -> Latch -> Retract G->>JC: Signals.TryFinalizeJunk(id) JC->>S: ReqJunkFinalize S->>JC: JunkCollected (broadcast) P->>G: Unequip tool G->>Cam: RequestShootingCamera(false)

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: GrabHookConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/GrabHookConfig.luauSee also Junk — Adjust Junk Flow for the claim/collection side of the loop.Perks: ReelSpeedBonus (reel speed ×(1+b), Wide Net ×NetReelFactor), HookRangeBonus (reach ×(1+b)), NetCapacityBonus (net size). The client (GrabHook.client) and the server (JunkService) apply the same PerkBuffRead math. The reel bonus now also drives GrabHookVisuals and the server BeginJunkRetract time (before the Perk Rework it changed only the loop-sound timing). searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/HealthController.client.luau	Minimal bridge: HealthStateSync → Signals.OnHealthValueChanged Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/HealthManager.luau	Authoritative health record, regen heartbeat, ApplyDamage, HealPlayer Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ArmorManager.luau	Owns crafted armor; Absorb is the mitigation seam HealthManager calls at the damage sink Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/HealthConfig.luau	HPMultiplier (scales every HP amount), MaxHealth, regen rate/delay, regen kill-switch Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ArmorConfig.luau	The five-kind armor catalog, reduction cap — see Armor  Packets: HealthStateSync — see Networking MapSignals: OnHealthValueChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Server: authoritative record and regen heartbeat​
searchDocs.content: HealthManager is bootstrapped by HealthSystemLoader.server.luau via HealthManager.Initialize(). It maintains a HealthRecord per player (Health, LastDamageTime, LastSyncTime, LastSyncedHealth), created on PlayerAdded and deleted on PlayerRemoving — no stale data persists across sessions. CharacterAdded unconditionally resets record.Health to MaxHealth and mirrors it to humanoid.MaxHealth/humanoid.Health.  The regen heartbeat runs on RunService.Heartbeat, capped at MAX_HEALTH_STEP_DT = 0.1 seconds per step to prevent delta-time spikes from applying burst healing. While eligible (alive, not full, past RegenDelay since last damage), it adds HealthRegen * HPMultiplier * dt to the record each step. Syncs are batched: regen fires HealthStateSync at most every HEALTH_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 seconds, or immediately when health reaches full.

searchDocs.title: Damage and armor mitigation​
searchDocs.content: HealthManager.ApplyDamage validates AttackType/AOEVariant, clamps the amount to [0, MaxHealth / HPMultiplier] (amounts arrive at 100-HP scale), then applies armor mitigation, then scales what is left by HPMultiplier before subtracting from the record:  amount = ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency) amount *= HPMultiplier -- armor works at 100-HP scale, so its pools keep their meaning record.Health -= amount record.LastDamageTime = os.clock() humanoid.Health = record.Health -- HealthStateSync:FireClient(player, record.Health)   applyDamageInternal reads PerkBuffs/<UserId>.ArmorEfficiency (the Plated perk) and calls ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency) on every hit — Absorb is the mitigation seam: it looks up the player's equipped kind, computes clamp(kind.BaseReduction * (1 + efficiency), 0, ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap), drains the kind's pool by the amount absorbed, and returns what's left to subtract from health. Crafting, equipping, recharging or respeccing the perk all take effect on the next hit; with nothing equipped, or an Energy kind at zero pool, Absorb returns the full amount unmitigated. The old ReplicatedStorage/ArmorState folder and its ArmorBaseReduction attribute no longer exist — mitigation is a direct function call, not a published attribute. See Armor for the two armor types and Perks for the cap rationale and the attacker-bonus-then-armor multiplication order. HealthManager.HealPlayer is the mirror path: record.Health = min(MaxHealth, record.Health + amount * HPMultiplier), mirrored and synced the same way. It ignores a dead player, so a heal never revives.

searchDocs.title: Temporary shields​
searchDocs.content: Each health record holds Shields: source name → list of entries { amount, expiresAt }, at 100-HP scale (pure math in ShieldMath). HealthManager.AddShield(player, source, amount, seconds, maxStacks) adds an entry (the one ending first drops past maxStacks). In ApplyDamage the order is: Shock Absorber → shields (Plating, then Scrap, then Spawn; inside a source the entry that expires first drains first; expired entries take nothing) → armor → × HPMultiplier → health. A hit a shield takes in full still sets LastDamageTime (regen delay, Recharge Plating) and still syncs. The Heartbeat prunes ended entries for every live player, even with RegenEnabled = false, and re-syncs when the total changes. A respawn clears all shields.  HealthStateSync(health, shield) carries the live shield total × HPMultiplier. HealthStaminaGuiController draws it as CanvasHealth.Shield (with shieldFill inside): a light-blue overlay from the left edge, width = shield ÷ max health.  CombatService is the only caller of ApplyDamage for weapon and NPC-collision damage — see Weapons → CombatService for the routing logic.

searchDocs.title: Client bridge​
searchDocs.content: HealthController.client.luau listens to Packets.HealthStateSync.OnClientEvent and re-fires Signals.OnHealthValueChanged with the received health value. It owns no state. HealthStaminaGuiController (not part of this system) consumes OnHealthValueChanged to animate the HUD bar.

searchDocs.title: Dev command​
searchDocs.content: /hurt (aliases /damage, /dmg) in the chat command bar damages the caller for 10% of their own max health, for exercising the HUD and the damage pipeline. It is registered client-side in NovaChat's Commands.client.luau and handled by DevCommandsService.server.luau, which gates it on place owner / group rank 250+ and ignores unauthorised callers. It routes through HealthManager.ApplyDamage, so armour reduction applies — the health actually lost is less than 10% whenever the player has armour.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: The HUD bar is the parent Frame, not a layer or the CanvasGroup HealthStaminaGui authors each bar as three stacked art layers (healthDarker / healthLighter / healthWhite) inside a parent Health Frame, which in turn sits inside a clipping CanvasHealth CanvasGroup. The parent Frame is what carries the fill: HealthStaminaGuiController drives Health.Size = UDim2.fromScale(ratio, 1). Resizing one of the art layers distorts only that layer, and resizing the CanvasGroup moves the whole widget including its backing art. The stamina bar mirrors this exactly (CanvasStamina → Stamina → stamDarker / stamLighter / stamWhite). These names are load-bearing — renaming any of them in Studio breaks the controller at load.  Non-CombatService damage bypasses HealthManager Any damage source that writes directly to Humanoid.Health — such as default Roblox fall damage or unrouted hazards — bypasses HealthManager's internal record, causing the HUD to show a stale value and skipping armor mitigation. Before shipping such a source, either disable it or listen to Humanoid.HealthChanged and reconcile the record.  One-way mirror: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write to humanoid.Health is invisible to the manager until a HealthStateSync event corrects the client. Keep all health mutations going through HealthManager.ApplyDamage or HealthManager.HealPlayer.  HP scale: every HP amount passed to ApplyDamage / HealPlayer and every HP number in configs (enemy damage, healing, the lifesteal cap) is at 100-HP scale. To raise player health, change HealthConfig.HPMultiplier, never each damage source. SetHealth / GetHealth / GetMaxHealth are absolute (/hurt divides the multiplier back out).  Roblox default regen is off: an empty Script StarterCharacterScripts.Health (from src/StarterPlayer/StarterCharacterScripts/Health.server.luau) replaces Roblox's built-in regen script, which raised Humanoid.Health behind the record.  Character respawn resets health: CharacterAdded unconditionally resets record.Health to MaxHealth. If a partial-health respawn mechanic is ever needed, this reset must be conditional.  Sync rate: HealthStateSync is sent at most every 0.1 seconds during regen, but every ApplyDamage call forces an immediate sync — avoid calling it in tight per-frame loops.  Coverage is bounded by the chokepoint: damage that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage also bypasses armor mitigation.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Shock Absorber (AOEResist): AOE hits are reduced (PerkBuffRead.Reduce) before armor.Quick Recovery (RegenDelayReductionPct): cuts a percent of the regen delay left after Field Medic's seconds; the delay stays at least 1 s.Vampire Rounds (Lifesteal 0.03): CombatService heals the attacker by 3% of the NPC health a player's hit actually removed (any weapon), at most ShopPerkConfig.LIFESTEAL_MAX_PER_SECOND (2) per second, through HealthManager.HealPlayer.Rally Banner (RallyRegenBonus 0.20, party): regen rate ×(1 + RegenBonus + rally) while another live player is within ShopPerkConfig.RALLY_RADIUS (20 studs) — PerkBuffRead.Rally.Recharge Plating (PlatingShieldHP 15): after ShopPerkConfig.PLATING_RECHARGE_DELAY (8 s) without a hit, the Heartbeat refills the Plating shield to 15 (no timeout). It drains before Scrap Shield. A respawn refills it at once.Fresh Start (SpawnShieldPct 0.30): on CharacterAdded, after the shield reset, HealthManager adds one Spawn shield worth 30% of max health (MaxHealth ÷ HPMultiplier at 100-HP scale, so it follows HPMultiplier) for ShopPerkConfig.FRESH_START_SECONDS (90 s). It drains last, after Plating and Scrap. The first spawn of a run can come before the perk buffs publish, so that spawn can miss the shield.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant S as HealthManager (Server) participant H as Humanoid participant C as HealthController (Client) Note over S: PlayerAdded -> create HealthRecord{Health=MaxHealth} Note over S: CharacterAdded -> reset Health to MaxHealth S->>H: humanoid.MaxHealth / humanoid.Health = record.Health S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient(player, health) C->>C: Signals.OnHealthValueChanged:Fire(health) loop RunService.Heartbeat (server) alt regen eligible (alive, not full, past RegenDelay) S->>S: record.Health += HealthRegen * dt S->>H: humanoid.Health = record.Health opt periodic sync (0.1s) or full S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient end end end Note over S: HealthManager.ApplyDamage(amount, type, ...) S->>S: record.LastDamageTime = os.clock() S->>S: amount = ShieldMath.absorb(Shields, amount) (Plating, Scrap, Spawn) opt shields took the whole hit S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient (return early) end S->>S: amount = ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, ArmorEfficiency) S->>S: record.Health -= amount S->>H: humanoid.Health = record.Health S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient Note over S: HealthManager.HealPlayer(amount) S->>S: record.Health = min(MaxHealth, record.Health + amount) S->>H: humanoid.Health = record.Health S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleServer	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/JumpDriveManager.luau	Authority: charge gauge, deposit handling, vote, phase state machine, biome seam, arrival rewards Server	src/ServerScriptService/JumpDriveSystemLoader.server.luau	Bootstrap — calls JumpDriveManager.Initialize() Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/JumpDriveGuiController.client.luau	Bench panel JumpDriveGui (hold-to-charge JumpButton, UNKNOWN SIGNAL threat card, destination picker or ERROR card, vote row, named roster); feeds the generic PartyVoteGui banner (SharedModules/Gui/PartyVoteGui.luau) Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/JumpTransitionController.client.luau	Wormhole/lightspeed VFX, post-processing wash, SFX — owns one Janitor per jump Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JumpDriveConfig.luau	Bench tags/prompt names, charge values, phase durations, biome registry, arrival rewards, VFX tuning Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/JumpDriveResultCodes.luau	Deposit/vote/jump rejection codes  Packets: JumpStateSync, ReqDepositJumpCharge, ReqStartJumpVote, ReqCastJumpVote, ReqPickJumpDestination — see Networking MapSignals: OnJumpPhaseChanged — see Signals MapJoin-time delivery: via JoinSync on ClientReady, not Players.PlayerAdded — see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake  The bench is the PowerCore model, which is also the train engine (it carries both JumpDriveBench and TrainEngine; see Train Fuel). It has two prompts: Refuel (ProxPromptPart, key E, hold) and Jump Drive (JumpPromptPart, key F). The keys differ because Exclusivity = OnePerButton shows only one prompt per key. It has no DepositPromptPart: players charge the drive by holding the JumpButton in the panel.

searchDocs.title: The charge gauge​
searchDocs.content: A single scalar 0..JumpDriveConfig.MAX_CHARGE, server-authoritative and global (one drive for the whole train, not per player). It does not decay. Players hold the panel's JumpButton; the client fires ReqDepositJumpCharge(bench)every HOLD_TICK (0.1 s). Each call spends at most DEPOSIT_PER_TICK (2) pool Energy points via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo, only what is needed to fill, so a full drive takes 5 s of holding. JumpDriveConfig.CHARGE_PER_POINT (1) is charge per Energy point, so a full drive costs 100 points. Range is checked against JumpPromptPart. The server refuses one player's calls closer thanMIN_DEPOSIT_INTERVAL (TOO_FAST). An isDepositing guard still serializes deposits.

searchDocs.title: Phase machine​
searchDocs.content: JumpDriveManager owns a single server-side phase. Every advance is guarded by a generation nonce, so a scheduled callback left over from a previous jump can never advance a later one (the same pattern TrainFuelManager.reschedule()uses).  stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Idle Idle --> Ready: gauge reaches MAX_CHARGE Ready --> Voting: a player starts a jump vote Voting --> Ready: vetoed, or expires with no > yes Voting --> Engulf: vote passes (charge consumed) Engulf --> InWormhole: EngulfDuration elapsed InWormhole --> Exit: biome ready AND MinWormholeHold elapsed InWormhole --> Exit: MaxWormholeHold watchdog fires Exit --> Idle: ExitDuration elapsed, rewards granted   Phase	MeaningIdle	Gauge not full; deposits accepted Ready	Gauge full; a vote can be opened Voting	Vote open, countdown running (VoteDuration) Engulf	Black hole grows ahead of the train and swallows it (EngulfDuration) InWormhole	Held while the destination biome prepares (MinWormholeHold..MaxWormholeHold) Exit	Lightspeed burst out into the new biome (ExitDuration)  The whole state — phase, gauge, and ballots — travels in one JumpStateSyncbroadcast rather than three, so a client can never render a phase and a gauge from two different moments. phaseEndsAt is a workspace:GetServerTimeNow()deadline; clients extrapolate their own countdown against it (the same prediction pattern TrainStateSync uses for the fuel bar), so there's no per-frame server traffic. InWormhole broadcasts phaseEndsAt = 0, meaningindefinite — hold the current visual state until the next broadcast; clients must treat 0 as "no known end," never as "already expired." Joining players get the current snapshot via a JoinSync sender ("JumpDrive"), run once the client announces readiness with ClientReady — not from Players.PlayerAdded, which is unreliable (seeJoin-Sync Snapshot Handshake). JumpDriveGuiControllerneeds no client-side cache for this: phaseEndsAt is always a server-supplied absolute timestamp, and countdownText() already renders "--" when it is unset, so a dropped or delayed snapshot just leaves the countdown honestly blank rather than wrong.

searchDocs.title: The vote​
searchDocs.content: Opening a vote (ReqStartJumpVote) requires standing at the bench and phaseReady; the opener is recorded as an automatic yes. Casting a ballot (ReqCastJumpVote) has no proximity check — see "Why the vote banner is pushed, not bench-gated" below — and may be changed freely while the countdown runs. Players.PlayerRemoving drops a leaver's ballot so they can't hold a decision hostage.  The opener's userId travels in JumpStateSync as initiator (0 outsideVoting), so the client can hide the pushed banner from the player who started the vote.  Every accepted ballot change and destination pick broadcasts JumpStateSync to all players, so the server refuses one player's picks and ballot changes closer than REQUEST_COOLDOWN (0.25 s) apart with TOO_FAST (silent on the client). A looping client can then cause at most four broadcasts a second.  Resolution is a pure function so it can be exercised in isolation (JumpDriveManager._resolveVoteForTest exposes it for a Studio command-bar check):  resolveVote(yes, no) -> yes > 0 and no <= yes   It passes if at least one player approved and the objectors do not outnumber them; abstaining (AFK, loading, never walked to the bench) is neutral and can never deadlock a jump. The countdown also resolves early — as soon as every present player has voted, or as soon as no remaining ballot could change the outcome — so a decided vote doesn't sit on screen for the rest of the 60 seconds.  Why the vote banner is pushed, not bench-gated​  Abstaining is neutral in resolveVote. If casting a ballot required standing at the bench, everyone who never walked over would abstain — over a 60-second window mid-combat, that's most of the party. The vote would then resolve on the initiator's lone yes every time: no > yes is nearly impossible to reach with a single voter, so the veto would exist in the resolution rule and never fire in practice. Pushing a non-modal banner to every player the momentVoting starts (JumpDriveGuiController) is what makes the vote a vote — opening it still requires the bench; casting a ballot in response to the pushed banner does not. The banner must not capture input (no ModalEnabled, nothing over the crosshair) so a player under attack can keep fighting and vote with one click when they choose to.

searchDocs.title: Destination​
searchDocs.content: CurrentBiome starts at START_BIOME. With the Biome Selector researched (BIOME_SELECTOR_NODE, gamepass-gated in ResearchConfig), a player at the bench picks the next biome with ReqPickJumpDestination while Idle orReady. The pick is stored as picked and sent in the destination field until a vote opens; chooseDestination (pure, _chooseDestinationForTest) then locks it in, or rolls at random when there is no valid pick or no research. A failed vote keeps the pick; arrival clears it.

searchDocs.title: Cross-system state during a jump​
searchDocs.content: Signals.OnJumpPhaseChanged(phase: string) is the single broadcast point for suspending world activity. JumpDriveConfig.IsJumpActive(phase) is true forEngulf/InWormhole/Exit (not Voting — the train runs normally while players decide). Six consumers:  Consumer	Behavior while IsJumpActiveJunkService	CurrentState.IsSpawning = false; restored on return to Idle EventOrchestrator	SetJumpPaused(true) — odometer and channel ticking suspended, and any Active handler is force-finished TrainFuelManager	SetJumpFreeze(true) — drain rate pins to 0; ApplyFuelDamage early-returns TrainShieldManager	SetJumpFreeze(true) — ApplyDamage early-returns QuestSourcesLoader	Reports QuestConfig.Metrics.BiomeJumps progress once, on the IsJumpActive -> false edge (arrival, not vote-pass) ThreatTimerManager	Countdown paused; reset to a full Counting on the IsJumpActive -> false edge (arrival) — see Threat Timer  Why SetTrainStarted is not reused to halt junk spawning​  JunkService already gates spawning on Signals.SetTrainStarted, which looks like the obvious signal to reuse for a jump. It is not: EventOrchestrator.Initwires SetTrainStarted(true) to EventOrchestrator.Reset(). Re-firing it after a jump would silently zero the event odometer and desynchronize encounter pacing. OnJumpPhaseChanged is a dedicated signal precisely so the jump doesn't carry that invisible side effect.  Why jumping despawns an active encounter wave​  EventOrchestrator.SetJumpPaused(true) calls each channel's existingactiveFinish() — the same path the MaxActiveDistance watchdog and Reset()already use. PirateAttackEvent registers its spawned wave asctx.janitor:Add(wave, "Destroy"), so force-finishing it despawns any surviving pirates. This is deliberate, not a side effect: it's what makes "players are safe inside the wormhole" actually true — without it, a live wave would keep shooting people through the transition — and it doubles as a panic button, a balance lever the later chase-timer/pressure-loop spec should be aware of.

searchDocs.title: The biome seam​
searchDocs.content: -- inside JumpDriveManager local function prepareBiome(biomeId: string, done: () -> ()) workspace:SetAttribute(JumpDriveConfig.BIOME_ATTRIBUTE, biomeId) done() end   This local function — not a separate module — is the entire seam the future biome-content overhaul replaces. Today it writes the CurrentBiome attribute and calls done() immediately. The InWormhole hold already waits ondone() (floored by MinWormholeHold, capped by the MaxWormholeHoldwatchdog), so real scenery/weather/hazard load time is absorbed with no other change to this module — the overhaul only needs to replace prepareBiome's body.

searchDocs.title: Rewards on arrival​
searchDocs.content: Two separate call sites fire on arrival, not one:  JumpDriveManager.finishJump, on the Exit -> Idle transition, grantsCoinManager.AddCoins, XPManager.AddXP, and BattlePassManager.AddExp to every player in Players:GetPlayers() (each pcall-wrapped so one player's DataStore hiccup can't rob the rest of the party). Values live inJumpDriveConfig.ArrivalReward. JumpDriveManager never requiresQuestManager.  Rift Harvest (permanent party perk, id JumpBounty): finishJump pays ArrivalReward.Coins × (1 + JumpBountyBonus) coins and ArrivalReward.Xp × (1 + JumpBountyXP) XP, both floored. Battle Pass EXP is not changed.  Quest progress is a different module entirely: QuestSourcesLoader listens toSignals.OnJumpPhaseChanged itself and reportsQuestManager.ReportPartyProgress(QuestConfig.Metrics.BiomeJumps, 1) once, on the same IsJumpActive -> false arrival edge (see the cross-system table above). It lives there, not in JumpDriveManager, because of the convention documented on QuestConfig.Metrics itself: every quest metric gets its source wired in QuestSourcesLoader, so all quest sources stay discoverable in one file instead of being scattered across each feature that can grant progress.

searchDocs.title: Client presentation​
searchDocs.content: JumpTransitionController owns one Janitor per jump and captures Lighting's pre-jump values before applying any post-processing, registering their restoration on that Janitor — a mid-jump disconnect, error, or out-of-order phase packet can never leave a player's Lighting permanently altered. Nothing in this system takes camera or movement control; the player keeps playing while the world changes around them.  JumpDriveGuiController drives the panel and feeds the banner from the singleJumpStateSync payload, so they can never disagree. Pure text/state rules live in JumpDriveGuiRules (Studio self-check in the plan). It setsResetOnSpawn = false on the cloned ScreenGui in code (PartyVoteGui does the same for the banner) — a clone with ResetOnSpawn = true would be destroyed on the first respawn.  JumpButton: while Idle, hold it (MouseButton1/Touch) to charge — oneReqDepositJumpCharge per HOLD_TICK, a single success toast on release. While Ready, click it to open the vote; the press must begin in Ready, so releasing a hold that just filled the drive never opens a vote.Threat card ("UNKNOWN SIGNAL", never names the boss): readsThreatStateSync, hidden until the first one. Omen line, 12-segment meter and mm:ss clock come from JumpDriveGuiRules.threatView; omen texts areThreatConfig.CardOmens. The dot blink and the last-20 % border pulse are step toggles in the 0.1 s tick.Destination card: with ReplicatedStorage.ResearchUnlocked.Special_BiomeSelectorpresent, three biome buttons (current biome left out) sendReqPickJumpDestination, locked once the vote opens; without it, "DESTINATION: ERROR" and "Biome Selector module broken". The card switches the moment the research finishes, even with the panel open.Vote: a VoteRow in the panel and the PartyVoteGui banner. The banner shows only while Voting, and not to the initiator or to anyone with the panel open, so nobody sees two sets. Y/N keys belong to the banner:PartyVoteGui binds them with ContextActionService only while the banner shows, so they do nothing for the vote opener or with the panel open (the panel's VoteRow shows no key hints). Key hints show only with a keyboard. The banner shows "n/m voted", not who agreed.

searchDocs.title: Config surface​
searchDocs.content: JumpDriveConfig — edit gameplay here, never in manager or controller code:  Section	FieldsStation / interaction	BENCH_TAG, JUMP_PROMPT_PART_NAME, PROXIMITY_TOLERANCE, WORMHOLE_ANCHOR_TAG Charge	MAX_CHARGE, CHARGE_PER_POINT (charge per pool Energy point), HOLD_TICK, DEPOSIT_PER_TICK, MIN_DEPOSIT_INTERVAL, REQUEST_COOLDOWN (per-player floor on picks and ballot changes) Phases	Phase (string enum), IsJumpActive(phase), VoteDuration, EngulfDuration, MinWormholeHold, MaxWormholeHold, ExitDuration Biomes	BIOME_ATTRIBUTE (workspace attribute name), Biomes (destination list; a jump never rolls the current biome), START_BIOME, BIOME_SELECTOR_NODE Rewards	ArrivalReward — Coins/Xp/BPExp per player, flat for now VFX	VFX_FOLDER, WORMHOLE_MODEL, LIGHTSPEED_MODEL, WormholeStartScale, PostFx (brightness/contrast/tint/blur)  Perks: JumpSparkPerMinute (Jump Spark, Party shop, 1) — a 1 Hz clock in JumpDriveManager.Initialize counts travel seconds while Signals.SetTrainState says the train moves and the phase is Idle; each full minute adds JumpSparkPerMinute% of MAX_CHARGE and calls refreshReadiness (which broadcasts, and enters Ready at full). The vote still runs. JumpChargeBonus (Jump Engineer, Party) — each deposit gains CHARGE_PER_POINT ×(1+b) charge per Energy point. See Perks.

searchDocs.title: Not in scope​
searchDocs.content: These are deliberately deferred to their own future specs; each has a named seam so an implementer doesn't need to touch anything documented above:  Chase timer / pressure loop — built: see Threat Timer. It resets on the Exit -> Idle arrival edge. The Leviathan boss itself is still deferred (seam: Signals.OnThreatArrived).Biome content overhaul — per-biome scenery, skybox, lighting, weather, ambience, spawn tables, hazards. The seam is prepareBiome(biomeId, done)(see above).Reward scaling by biome tier or jump count — flat values belong with the content overhaul, which is what introduces tiers.EnemySpawner is not an OnJumpPhaseChanged consumer: it has no ambient spawn loop of its own, only SpawnAt/SpawnWave called from event handlers, so gating at EventOrchestrator is sufficient.

searchDocs.title: What gets preloaded​
searchDocs.content: Instances under ReplicatedStorage, Workspace, Lighting, SoundService, StarterGui, StarterPack, and MaterialService whose class is in PRELOAD_CLASSES (Animation, Sound, Decal/Texture, MaterialVariant, SurfaceAppearance, ImageLabel, ImageButton, ParticleEmitter, Beam, Trail, Sky).MeshPart TextureIDs as plain content ids. The MeshPart itself is skipped, so its mesh still streams in during play.Every rbxassetid:// string in the Configs modules (except rbxassetid://0). This covers ids that exist only in code, such as SoundConfig SFX and TrainConfig.BRAKE_LEVER_ANIM_ID. ChronoConfig is skipped: it must only be required through the Chrono wrapper.  A new asset in a config module or a replicated folder is picked up with no extra wiring. An id hardcoded inside a controller is not picked up; move it into a config.

searchDocs.title: Progress bar​
searchDocs.content: The bar first creeps toward JOIN_END while the place downloads (Roblox gives no progress for that). The preload then fills the rest, one step per batch. ASSET_TIMEOUT caps how long one stuck batch can hold the screen. Failed assets are warned, not fatal.  SoundManager.Pool.Warm also uses PreloadLib, to keep its parked pool Sounds loaded.

searchDocs.title: Client rendering and pooling​
searchDocs.content: JunkController builds per-model GenericPoolInstance pools at startup, one per model name found in JunkAssets, with initial size 5, max 60, expand by 10. On SpawnJunk it checks the MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS = 250 cap, retrieves a model from the pool, sets Transparency = 0, parents it to workspace/JunksVisuals, and records it in activeJunks and junkMap. A PreSimulation loop advances the smoothstep speed ramp, moves each active junk by currentSpeed * dt along MOVE_DIRECTION, applies per-junk random rotation, and increments DistanceTraveled; junk despawns via RemoveJunkLocal when DistanceTraveled > DESPAWN_DISTANCE.  JunkController also bridges claim/finalize signals from GrabHook.client to Packets.ReqJunkClaim / Packets.ReqJunkFinalize via Signals.TryClaimJunk and Signals.TryFinalizeJunk, and exposes GetJunkIdFromPart(part) via BindableCore so GrabHook.client can resolve a junk ID from a raycast hit part.

searchDocs.title: Retraction and collection cleanup​
searchDocs.content: On BeginJunkRetract, the client removes the junk from simulation and moves it to retractingJunks. The local player's animation is driven by GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile; other players see an observer lerp on RenderStepped. An 8-second safety-net timeout returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives. On JunkCollected, the client cleans up rope attachments and beams on the model and returns it to the pool.

searchDocs.title: Server spawn loop​
searchDocs.content: JunkService performs weighted tier selection: each tier's weight is multiplied by GlobalModifiers.TierMultipliers[tier], and a random number selects the tier by accumulated weight. Type selection uses pity: if spawnsSinceLastEnergy >= ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD (8), an Energy-type junk is forced; otherwise a type is chosen weighted by SpawnChance * TypeMultiplier. The pity counter resets on every Energy spawn.

searchDocs.title: Special junk​
searchDocs.content: spawnSpecial(tier, count) and spawnCache(count) add junk outside the spawn roll: at SpawnHelper.GetRandomPoint(), ignoring MAX_SERVER_JUNKS and IsSpawning. The type is rolled by SpawnChance × TypeMultipliers without touching the pity counter. A Cache is a JunkConfig.Special entry (Tier = 0, Type = "Cache", model in JunkAssets.Special.Cache; the current one is a placeholder crate). Its grab credits the whole Yield table (50 Wood / 30 Metal / 20 Energy) to the pool at the player and gets no Lucky bonus. JunkToolManager skips the Special folder, so a Cache never becomes a Tool.  Perk travel clock. A 1 Hz loop counts travel seconds while the train has started, is running (SetTrainState) and is not in a jump (IsSpawning). Each perk keeps its own accumulator (SalvagePerkMath.tick) that only grows while the perk is live: Salvage Beacon (BeaconJackpots) spawns Tier 5 junk every SALVAGE_BEACON_SECONDS; Treasure Map (TreasureCaches) spawns a Cache every TREASURE_MAP_SECONDS. The EventOrchestrator odometer is not used: it does not run while EventConfig.Enabled = false. Beacon and Map spawns that fall due while the jump phase is Voting or JumpDriveConfig.IsJumpActive are held in pendingSpecial and spawn when the phase leaves that set (arrival, or a failed vote), because the jump removes junk spawned during the vote. Salvage Drone is not held: its grab goes straight to the player.  Salvage Drone (party, DroneGrabs): every SALVAGE_DRONE_SECONDS of travel, droneGrab picks the nearest tier junk within SALVAGE_DRONE_RANGE of the first TrainEngine-tagged instance that is not collected and not under a live reservation. It marks the junk Collected at once (a player claim of it then fails), fires DroneGrab(id, bench) to all clients with the nearest placed Workbench, and after DRONE_FLIGHT_SECONDS fires Signals.DroneJunkDelivered(bench, type, tier); ShredderServer turns it into pool materials and animates the bench. Fuel Line counts drone Energy grabs. No engine, junk or placed workbench: that grab is skipped. Clients fly the junk visual to the bench (MotionMaster.PivotMove) and return it to the pool; no JunkCollected follows.

searchDocs.title: Odometer and despawn​
searchDocs.content: The server records SpawnOdometer (the value of junkOdometer at spawn time) and SpawnPos for each active junk; the junk's current world position is reconstructed on claim as SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer). A distance-based despawn on Heartbeat removes any junk where (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer) > DESPAWN_DISTANCE, mirroring the client-side DistanceTraveled check. The junk counter wraps at 65535 (NumberU16 boundary) to keep IDs compact in the SpawnJunk packet.

searchDocs.title: Claim and finalize validation​
searchDocs.content: ReqJunkClaim reconstructs the junk's world position, checks distance against MaxDistance × (1 + HookRangeBonus) + 15 studs (latency slack), enforces a per-player cooldown, computes retract time, reserves the junk until fly-out + retract + RESERVATION_TIMEOUT (5 s slack), and fires BeginJunkRetract to all clients. ReqJunkFinalize checks reservation ownership and that the reservation has not expired, marks the junk collected, fires JunkCollected to all clients, then awards it: Energy junk credits its Yield as points to MaterialPool (origin = the player's character pivot); Wood/Metal junk gives the tool to the player's Backpack. SetTrainState(isMoving) and SetTrainStarted(started) are wired to Signals.SetTrainState and Signals.SetTrainStarted for external control.

searchDocs.title: Spawn volumes​
searchDocs.content: SpawnHelper:Init() caches all BasePart children of workspace/SpawnVolumes weighted by volume; SpawnHelper.GetRandomPoint() picks a random world position inside one of the spawn volumes using volume-weighted selection. SpawnHelper:Init() must be called before the spawn loop — JunkService calls it at startup; if no SpawnVolumes parts exist in workspace, GetRandomPoint always returns nil and no junk spawns.

searchDocs.title: Disabling spawn volumes​
searchDocs.content: Spawn volumes can be grouped and toggled at runtime without touching the workspace. Author an optional SpawnGroup string attribute on a BasePart under workspace/SpawnVolumes; every part sharing the same value forms a togglable group. Parts with no SpawnGroup attribute are ungrouped and always active — never affected by a toggle. SpawnHelper exposes three methods on top of Init / GetRandomPoint:  SpawnHelper:SetGroupEnabled(groupName: string, enabled: boolean) — enables or disables every volume in groupName. warns on an unrecognized group name (typo guard) but still records the state.SpawnHelper:IsGroupEnabled(groupName: string): boolean — true unless the group is currently disabled; unknown or ungrouped names always read true.SpawnHelper:GetGroups(): { string } — the distinct SpawnGroup values authored across the spawn volumes, for validation/debug.  The pirate-ship event uses this to disable the ship-facing group during the at-range cannon phase: junk stops spawning toward the ship, and any junk already floating there clears out via the normal distance-despawn instead of being force-removed, so the area is clean by the time players board. If every group with volumes ends up disabled, GetRandomPoint() returns nil and the spawn loop simply idles until a group is re-enabled — no junk spawns, but nothing errors.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Both sides integrate the same ramp — keep them in sync The server (junkOdometer) and client (DistanceTraveled) both use the identical smoothstep ramp over SPEED_RAMP_DURATION. If you change the ramp formula in one place, change it in the other. Drift causes the server's proximity check to reject valid claims.  Reservation timeout is 5 seconds If a client claims junk but never finalizes (e.g. disconnects mid-retract), the reservation expires 5 seconds (RESERVATION_TIMEOUT) after the expected reel-in ends (fly-out + retract, so Long Line and Wide Net pulls never expire mid-reel). Another player can then claim the same junk. The client has a safety net (RETRACT_RECLAIM_TIMEOUT = 8 s, added to the retract time) that returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives — it must exceed RESERVATION_TIMEOUT plus fly-out plus round-trip time.  Pool cleanup is mandatory. Every path that removes a junk from activeJunks or retractingJunks must call CleanupJunkModel then pool:InsertObject. Skipping cleanup leaks HookAttachment or Beam instances on the model, which will appear on the next retrieval.workspace/JunksVisuals folder must exist. JunkController uses WaitForChild to find it; the folder should be created in the place file or by a server startup script.Junk ID wraps at 65535. This is intentional for the NumberU16 wire type in SpawnJunk. Long-running servers are safe because entries are removed before the counter can collide.Tier 5 weight is 0. Items in Tier 5 will never spawn under default config. Set the weight above 0 to enable them.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Salvage Instinct (permanent, SalvageTierUpChance 0.04/level): FinalizeJunkForPlayer rolls first. On a hit, the grab uses tier + 1 (max Tier 5) and a random model of that tier, if that tier has the type (a Cache never tiers up). Gold Rush, Junk Collector and Lucky Charm then use the final tier. A tier-up fires the same JunkBonus toast as the bonus perks. Drone grabs do not roll.Scrap Pay (ScrapPayCoins 1): each finalized grab pays CoinManager.AddCoins(player, value, "ScrapPay"). A net pays per junk; a Cache grab pays too.Energy Tap (EnergyTapBonus 1): a player's Energy grab passes the bonus to creditEnergy, which adds it after the Energy Siphon rounding (a flat +1).Gold Rush (JunkCoinsT4, JunkCoinsT5): FinalizeJunkForPlayer pays that many coins for a tier 4 / tier 5 grab (the final tier, after Salvage Instinct; any type) through CoinManager.AddCoins.Golden Lure / Energy Forecast: PerkEffectsDispatcher sends the combined tier multipliers and the Energy type multiplier; ApplyTierMultiplier / ApplyTypeMultiplier overwrite, never multiply. See Perks — Shop perk layer.Scrap Shield (permanent, ScrapShieldHP 2/level): each finalized grab calls HealthManager.AddShield(player, "Scrap", value, PerkConfig.SCRAP_SHIELD_SECONDS, PerkConfig.SCRAP_SHIELD_MAX_STACKS) (20 s, at most 5 stacks). Wide Net finalizes per junk, so each junk in the net counts as one grab.Junk Collector (LuckyCoinCopies) / Lucky Charm (BonusJunkChance): after a Wood/Metal/Energy grab, grantLuckyBonuses gives extra junk through giveJunk (the same path as a grab: a Tool, or Energy points to the pool). Junk Collector counts grabs per player (session-only, only while live) and copies every LUCKY_COIN_EVERYth grab (same type and final tier; same model unless Salvage Instinct raised the tier). Lucky Charm rolls BonusJunkChance per grab; the bonus has the grabbed type and a tier from LUCKY_CHARM_TIER_WEIGHTS (SalvagePerkMath.rollTier). Each bonus fires JunkBonus(perkName, type, tier) to the player; JunkController shows a toast. A bonus is not a grab: no counter, quest, Fuel Line, Scrap Shield, Gold Rush, Scrap Pay or Energy Tap.Fuel Line (party, FuelPerEnergyJunk): each Energy grab calls TrainFuelManager.AddFuel(value).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant S as JunkService (server) participant C as JunkController (client) participant G as GrabHook (client) S->>S: selectRandomJunk() - weighted tier + pity type S->>S: assign id (U16), record SpawnOdometer + SpawnPos S->>C: SpawnJunk(id, modelName, startPos) C->>C: pool:RetrieveObject(startPos), add to activeJunks/junkMap S->>C: SetJunkSpeed(targetSpeed) Note over S,C: first receipt snaps currentSpeed; later receipts smoothstep-ramp Note over S,C: Shared speed ramp (identical smoothstep both sides)<br/>Server: junkOdometer += currentSpeed * dt<br/>Client: DistanceTraveled advances in PreSimulation<br/>Despawn when delta > DESPAWN_DISTANCE (both sides) G->>G: Player fires GrabHook -> Signals.TryClaimJunk(id, hitPos) G->>C: Signals.TryClaimJunk C->>S: ReqJunkClaim(id, hitPos) S->>S: proximity check vs junkOdometer, in-flight check, reserve junk S->>C: BeginJunkRetract(id, hitPos, retractTime, player) Note over C: local player -> GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile<br/>other players -> observer lerp on RenderStepped G->>C: Signals.TryFinalizeJunk(id) C->>S: ReqJunkFinalize(id) S->>S: verify reservation + timeout, mark Collected, award (Energy → MaterialPool, else Tool) S->>C: JunkCollected(id, player) C->>C: pool:InsertObject (returns model)

searchDocs.content: Config module: JunkConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luauPerks: JunkSpawnRateBonus (spawn interval ÷(1+b) — Dense Debris), EnergyYieldBonus (Energy credit ×(1+b), rounded — Energy Siphon), JunkTierRarityBonus (via ApplyTierMultiplier), plus the GrabHook claim keys (HookRangeBonus, ReelSpeedBonus, NetCapacityBonus — see GrabHook). See Perks.Playbook: Adjust Junk Flow  Field	Default	EffectMAX_SERVER_JUNKS	200	Hard cap on server-side active junk entries MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS	250	Client silently drops SpawnJunk events beyond this count MOVE_DIRECTION	Vector3.new(1,0,0)	World direction all junk travels DESPAWN_DISTANCE	700 studs	Odometer delta at which junk is removed (both sides) DEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE	0.5 s	Seconds between junk spawns when train is moving STOPPED_SPAWN_RATE	1.5 s	Seconds between spawns when train is stopped DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED	10 studs/s	Junk movement speed when train is moving STOPPED_JUNK_SPEED	5 studs/s	Junk movement speed when train is stopped SPEED_RAMP_DURATION	1.5 s	Smoothstep ramp time on speed change ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD	8	Non-energy spawns before Energy is guaranteed BaseModifiers.GlobalSpawnRateMult	1.0	Global spawn rate multiplier (runtime-adjustable) Tiers[n].Weight	varies	Relative spawn weight for each tier (Tier 5 is 0 = disabled) Tiers[n].Types[t].SpawnChance	varies	Relative spawn chance for each type within a tier Tiers[n].Types[t].Yield	varies	Item count awarded on collection  Model lists (Tiers[n].Types[t].Models) are auto-populated from ReplicatedStorage/JunkAssets/TierN/TypeName folder contents at require time.

searchDocs.title: Room states​
searchDocs.content: Each Studio part tagged trigger becomes a Zone. A clone of ServerStorage.RoomTexts sits under it and shows the room state.  State	Entered when	Billboard showsEmpty	Server start, or 1 s after the room clears	0 / 5 Selecting	A player with no party enters an empty room. A party is created with that player as leader.	"choosing party size" Countdown	The leader picks a size in the GUI (SetRoomSize)	members / size, countdown, optional "friends only" Teleporting	The countdown reaches 0	"teleporting"

searchDocs.title: Flow​
searchDocs.content: Leader enters an empty room. The server creates a party, sets the room to Selecting, opens the GUI (ToggleRoomSizeGui) and locks the leader's controls (SetPlayerControl false). Leader picks a size (1–5) and friends-only. SetRoomSize sets MaxMembers, moves the room to Countdown and starts a 30 s countdown. The leader's controls unlock. The server ignores the packet unless the sender is the leader, the size is 1–5 and the room is still Selecting. Other players enter during the countdown. They join if the party has space. When friends-only is on, the leader must be their friend. Otherwise the server sends EjectPlayer and the client steps them 12 studs back. A player leaves the room. A member leaves the party. If the leader leaves, leadership moves to another member. If the leader is alone, the party disbands, the countdown stops and the room resets. 2 s before the end, every member's controls lock. At 0, TeleportParty fulfils the Session Rejoin contract: TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync(GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID) returns an access code and the PrivateServerId.SessionStore.WriteRoster writes the party's user ids under that PrivateServerId. If this fails, the party does not teleport.SessionStore.SeedPointer writes one session pointer per member. A failure here only disables mid-run rejoin.PersistenceRegistry.ReleaseForTeleport(members) saves and ends each member's coin, XP, perk and inventory sessions without a kick, so the Game Instance opens them without waiting on the session lock.party:TeleportMembers(GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID, { ReservedServerCode = accessCode }) teleports the party. The room resets 5 s later. If any step fails (always in Studio, where teleports do not work), the server clears what it wrote, unlocks and ejects every member, disbands the party and resets the room. If the failure comes after the release (TeleportMembers errors, or TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed fires for one member), PersistenceRegistry.Reopen also gives those members their sessions back. In Studio ReserveServerAsync fails first, so no session is released and nothing reopens.  Cancel: the GUI's cancel button sends CancelRoom. The server ejects the player. The playerExited handler then disbands the party.

searchDocs.title: How it works​
searchDocs.content: Sources: shredder completion (ShredderServer) and research cancel refunds (ResearchService) call MaterialPool.Add(counts, MaterialPool.ArcPoints(station)). Energy junk grabs add at the player (Energy Tap adds a flat bonus to a player's own grab); Wreck Salvage (WreckSalvageService, hidden until enemy ships exist) adds Wood + Metal at a damaged EnemyShip.Sinks: workbench crafts (WorkbenchService) and research enqueues (ResearchService) call MaterialPool.Spend(cost); false means nothing was consumed.SpendUpTo(mat, missing, perPoint): the Energy spend path. Spends ceil(missing ÷ perPoint) points (at least 1), capped by the pool, and returns (pointsSpent, unitsAdded). Every Energy consumer calls it with its own *_PER_POINT rate, so a top-up never wastes points.Replication: every change fires MaterialPoolUpdate(wood, metal, energy, gainedWood, gainedMetal, gainedEnergy, origin, landing) to all clients. Spends and the join snapshot carry zero gain. The join snapshot is a broadcast, not FireClient, because the Packet library flushes broadcasts first each frame — a per-player snapshot could land after a same-frame gain and leave the joiner stale.Effect backstop: each fly effect destroys its Janitor after its time budget even if a piece thread errors, so undelivered value is always handed back to the counter.HUD: hidden by default. Slides down on any gain, on LeftControl, or on the touch-only pull tab; tapping the open panel or pressing the key again closes it; auto-hides after HIDE_DELAY.Rows: Wood, Metal, Energy (Energy colour 13FAFD). Panel sized for three rows: PANEL_HEIGHT_SCALE 0.165, PANEL_MIN_HEIGHT_PX 96, PANEL_ASPECT 1.6.Effect: if the gain's origin is on screen and within MAX_EFFECT_DISTANCE, up to MAX_FLY_PIECES local Handle clones arc out, rest for LAND_HOLD, then fly as 2D icons into their row; each carries a share of the gain. Pieces are split across materials in proportion to the gain; every material with a gain gets at least one. Energy has no CraftingMaterials template, so its pieces skip the 3D arc and fly as 2D icons from the grab point. Otherwise the counter rolls up over ROLL_DURATION.Counter rule: displayed = server total − value still in flight (clamped ≥ 0), so overlapping gains and mid-flight spends always settle on the exact total.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/NotificationManager/init.luau	Full toast manager: layout, animation, audio, cleanup. Do not require this directly from feature code Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/NotificationController.client.luau	One-line bootstrap: calls NotificationManager.Init() Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau	Types, colors, images, SFX names, device sizing, animation timing, MaxConcurrent, ExecutedFunctionTimeout  Packets: none — notifications are client-onlySignals: RequestNotification, RequestClearNotifications (both consumed, fired by any controller) — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Firing a toast​
searchDocs.content: Any client script fires Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?). NotificationManager is the sole subscriber:  Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("success", "Item placed!") Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("warn", "Low fuel!", 5) Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("info", "Loading...", nil, function() task.wait(2) -- toast stays open until this returns end)   NotificationController.client.luau calls NotificationManager.Init() once; after that, NotificationManager subscribes to Signals.RequestNotification and Signals.RequestClearNotifications. No other setup is required. Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() closes every active toast immediately.

searchDocs.title: Toast lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: NotificationManager creates (lazily) a ScreenGui named NotificationGui with a UIListLayout container anchored top-center, offset by NotificationConfig.TopOffsetScale (a fraction of viewport height). New toasts insert at the top of the stack; LayoutOrder is a negated monotonic counter so newer toasts sort above older ones. Executed-function toasts sit above timed toasts in a reserved LayoutOrder band.  Font size and padding are viewport-responsive: scaled by math.min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) / BaseScreenMin, clamped to [0.7, 1.3]. Text width is measured via TextService:GetTextSize after accounting for icon width, time-bar width (timed toasts only), and padding gaps, so the label never clips.  Close animations run a MotionMaster tween that shrinks the frame to UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0); a per-entry Janitor destroys the frame when the tween completes. A debounced viewport resize handler (requestResize) re-measures and re-tweens all live toasts when the window size changes.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Use Signals — never require NotificationManager directly Feature controllers must fire Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?). Requiring NotificationManager directly and calling internal functions breaks the decoupled contract and will error if accidentally required server-side.  type must exactly match one of the five lowercase strings in NotificationConfig.Types. An unrecognized type is silently dropped (no toast, no error).duration overrides the device default (NotificationConfig.Device.Desktop.Duration or .Mobile.Duration). Pass nil to use the default.executedFunction makes the toast persist until the function returns (or ExecutedFunctionTimeout elapses). It runs in a pcall-protected task.spawn — errors are suppressed and the toast still closes. Keep the function short; it runs on the client main thread.When MaxConcurrent is reached, the oldest timed toast is force-closed. Executed-function toasts are never evicted by the cap — avoid queuing many long-running ones simultaneously.Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() closes all toasts regardless of type or remaining duration. Use it only for hard resets (e.g. character death, scene transitions).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Feature as Any client controller participant Manager as NotificationManager participant Sound as SoundManager Feature->>Manager: Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?) Manager->>Manager: validate type against NotificationConfig.Types Manager->>Manager: enforce MaxConcurrent (evict oldest non-executed toast if needed) Manager->>Manager: build toast Frame (icon, time-left bar, gradient-sweep text) Manager->>Sound: PlaySFX(NotificationConfig.SfxNames[type]) Manager->>Manager: intro animation (MotionMaster size expand + fade in) alt timed toast Manager->>Manager: task.delay(duration or device default, closeEntry) else executed-function toast Manager->>Manager: task.spawn(executedFunction) -> closeEntry on return end Feature->>Manager: Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() Manager->>Manager: closeEntry() on every active toast simultaneously
