searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleConfig	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShopPerkConfig.luau	72 entries: Kind, Category, UnlockLevel, Price / Variants, Family, Group, Buffs, Hidden; slot rules in Slots (per pool and kind) Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PerkLoadoutState.luau	Pure rules: slotCount(pool, kind, level), owns, canBuy, canEquip, add, equip, unequip, prune, beginRun (Studio self-check at boot) Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShopPerkResultCodes.luau	Frozen result-code enum Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PerkInventoryClient.luau	Client read model: Get() snapshot, Changed, Buy / Equip / Unequip Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/PerkInventoryManager.luau	Owns the PlayerPerkInventory profile; Buy, Equip, Unequip, Grant, BeginRun, GetActiveRun Server (Game Instance)	src/ServerScriptService/PerkSystemLoader.server.luau	PerkInventoryManager.Initialize(runId): each loaded profile starts the run Server (Lobby)	places/Lobby/ServerScriptService/PerkLoadoutService.server.luau	Boots JoinSync, coins, XP, perks and inventory; binds every perk request handler Server (Lobby)	places/Lobby/ServerScriptService/PartyCreation.server.luau	Releases sessions before the party teleport, reopens them on failure Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/PersistenceRegistry.luau	RegisterHandoff, ReleaseForTeleport, Reopen  Packets: ReqBuyShopPerk, ReqEquipShopPerk, ReqUnequipShopPerk (Lobby only), PerkInventorySync — defined in Packets/LobbyShared.luau (see Networking Map)Signals: OnShopPerksChanged (produced by BeginRun) — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Kinds​
searchDocs.content: Kind	Buy	Stock	ActiveConsumable	Price coins for one copy	Copies[id]	The whole run that used a copy, even at 0 copies left Expiring	One of Variants (Seconds, Price)	Banked[id] (clock stopped) or Expires[id] (clock running)	While Expires > now  Expiring clock. The first equip moves Banked into Expires = now + Banked. Time added while the clock runs (a purchase or a grant) extends Expires. Time added while it is stopped goes to Banked. Unequip never pauses the clock, and the clock also runs while the player is offline.

searchDocs.title: Loadout rules​
searchDocs.content: Slots: per pool and kind (ShopPerkConfig.Slots[pool][kind]). Personal: 3 consumable (+1 at Lv 10, 30, 60; max 6) and 1 expiring (+1 at Lv 25, 50; max 3). Party: 1 consumable (+1 at Lv 45; max 2) and 1 expiring (+1 at Lv 70; max 2). Saved data is one dense list per pool; canEquip counts the equipped entries of the perk's own kind. The Lobby has one Studio row per slot (<Pool><Kind>Slot<i>, up to Base + #ExtraAtLevels) and LoadoutPage waits for each one, so a new slot level also needs a new row in PerkMenuGui.Equip appends to the end of the pool. Unequip removes one slot and the later slots move up. The saved lists never have gaps.Equip checks, in this order: unknown → hidden → wrong pool → level → not owned → already equipped → exclusive → no slot of its kind.Same perk once: a pool holds each perk at most once. Perks of one Family stack: Overcharged Rounds (+10%) and Marksman Tonic (+20%) give +30% gun damage. Family is a label for the catalog and GUI.Exclusive groups: a pool holds at most one perk per ExclusiveGroup: XPBoost (XP Booster, XP Booster II) and CoinBoost (Coin Booster, Coin Booster II). Equip returns EXCLUSIVE and the Lobby card reads Can't use with <name>. Both clocks still run while equipped. Family stays a label only.Level gate applies to buy and equip, not to Grant. A granted perk above the player's level waits in the inventory.Hidden perks (Hidden = true in ShopPerkConfig, built batch by batch in Perk Rework part 5) cannot be bought or equipped.Prune runs on every profile load and before each buy, equip and grant. It deletes ended clocks and removes each loadout entry that is unknown, hidden, in the wrong pool or no longer owned, and each later entry of an exclusive group (old saves; the first in slot order stays), and each entry past the most slots of its kind (old saves; the first in list order stays — the level count is checked at equip, because the XP profile can load after the inventory). Unequip does not prune, so the slot index the client sent still points at the perk it shows.

searchDocs.title: Coin shop​
searchDocs.content: Buy(player, id, variantIndex) checks that both the inventory and coin profiles are loaded, then the level gate and price (PerkLoadoutState.canBuy), then calls CoinManager.DeductCoins. Only after a successful deduct does it add the stock. A failed deduct changes nothing.

searchDocs.title: Grant​
searchDocs.content: PerkInventoryManager.Grant(player, id, amount, reason) gives stock with no price and no level gate: amount is copies for a consumable and seconds for an expiring perk. Hidden perks can be granted. Drops and the Battle Pass (Perk Rework part 6) use it.

searchDocs.title: Run start​
searchDocs.content: The Game Instance passes a run id to PerkInventoryManager.Initialize: game.PrivateServerId (the reserved server), else game.JobId, else a fresh GUID (both are empty in Studio, so each Studio Play is a new run). On each profile load, the manager first asks SessionCoordinator.IsAuthorized(player) (it yields until the roster is read, and is always true under the Studio bypass). A player the party lock bounces back to the Lobby keeps every copy: no run starts for them. For an authorized player, BeginRun:  If ConsumedRun == runId, this is a rejoin: ActiveRun stays and nothing is used.Otherwise it prunes, copies Loadout into ActiveRun, uses one copy of each equipped consumable, sets ConsumedRun, and prunes again. The second prune unequips consumables that reached 0, so the next run's loadout is honest. An expiring perk whose clock ended is not in ActiveRun.Fires Signals.OnShopPerksChanged(player) and replicates.  The Game Instance binds no buy, equip or unequip handler, so ActiveRun cannot change during the run. GetActiveRun(player) is the list Perk Rework part 3 reads. It returns the saved ActiveRun only when ConsumedRun is this server's run id; otherwise (the Lobby, a bounced player, a profile whose last run was another server) it returns empty lists, so an old run's perks can never apply. PerkInventorySync sends the same filtered list, so a client never shows an old run's perks.  Effects: PerkEffectsDispatcher reads GetActiveRun and GetExpires (the expiring clock ends) and republishes on OnShopPerksChanged and at each expiry; see Perks — Shop perk layer.

searchDocs.title: Loadout GUI​
searchDocs.content: The Lobby PerkMenuGui (see Perks — Client) has two shop perk pages. Button states come from the pure PerkLoadoutState and PerkGuiRules; every command runs in task.spawn and ignores the reply (the next PerkInventorySync reconciles).  Loadout page. The slot column shows the rows of the pool the Personal / Party filter picks: <Pool>ConsumableHeader + <Pool>ConsumableSlot1–N, then <Pool>ExpiringHeader + <Pool>ExpiringSlot1–N (N = the most slots of that kind). PersonalHeader and PartyHeader stay visible with used/open counts; each kind header shows its own count. PerkGuiRules.slotRows maps row i of a kind to the i-th list entry of that kind, so UnequipButton sends that entry's dense-list index (PerkInventoryClient.Unequip(pool, index); packets unchanged). A row above the player's count reads Locked · reach Lv N; an open row reads Empty slot; a filled row shows the kind mark, the name, the foot text and UnequipButton — also when an old save fills a row above the count. The inventory lists every known, non-hidden id in Copies, Banked or Expires, filtered by pool and kind (All / Consumable / Expiring); an empty list shows EmptyLabel. Foot text: ×N copies, <h:mm:ss> left (live), Banked <duration> or Expired (red). Card verb: Unequip (equipped), Equip, or the canEquip block reason (Requires Lv N, No free slot, Expired); clicking equips or unequips.Shop page. Cards follow the visible list rule within the pool and kind (PerkGuiRules.shopIds: the next milestone is found inside the filtered list, so a kind filter never goes blank); status Lv N, Own ×N or Owned; price from 1,000 when there are several variants. The detail shows the kind, <Group> · <Pool> · Lv N, the description, You own (foot text) and the note (Works for one run. / A second copy adds time. The effect does not double., plus the "counts once" sentence for Party). BuyButton1–3 show one price each (BUY, BUY 30 MIN, or REQUIRES LV N / NEED COINS when canBuy blocks); unused buttons are hidden.  The client clock is Workspace:GetServerTimeNow(), the same clock as the server's os.time() Expires.

searchDocs.title: Teleport hand-off​
searchDocs.content: A profile that is still open in the Lobby delays the session start in the Game Instance. PartyCreation.TeleportParty therefore calls PersistenceRegistry.ReleaseForTeleport(members) right before party:TeleportMembers. Each manager's release marks the player released, saves and ends the session, and its OnSessionEnd handler skips the usual kick. If TeleportMembers errors, or TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed fires for one member, PersistenceRegistry.Reopen starts the sessions again and the client gets fresh snapshots. In Studio ReserveServerAsync fails first, so this path runs only in a published test.  sequenceDiagram participant C as Lobby client participant L as PerkInventoryManager (Lobby) participant S as PerkLoadoutState participant P as PartyCreation participant G as PerkInventoryManager (Game Instance) C->>L: ReqEquipShopPerk(id, pool) L->>S: prune, canEquip, equip L-->>C: (ok, code) + PerkInventorySync P->>L: ReleaseForTeleport(members) P->>P: TeleportMembers G->>G: StartSessionAsync (no lock wait) G->>S: beginRun(runId) G-->>G: Signals.OnShopPerksChanged G-->>C: PerkInventorySync

searchDocs.title: Saved data​
searchDocs.content: Store PlayerPerkInventory (key = UserId), separate from PlayerPerks:  { Copies = {}, -- { [shopPerkId]: number } Banked = {}, -- { [shopPerkId]: seconds }, clock not started Expires = {}, -- { [shopPerkId]: os.time() clock end } Loadout = { Personal = {}, Party = {} }, ConsumedRun = "", ActiveRun = { Personal = {}, Party = {} }, SchemaVersion = 1, }

searchDocs.title: Result codes​
searchDocs.content: Code	Name	Meaning0	OK	Done 1	NO_PROFILE	Inventory or coin profile not loaded 2	UNKNOWN	Unknown id, bad argument, or an empty slot 3	HIDDEN	Not built yet (part 5) 4	LEVEL_REQUIRED	Player level below UnlockLevel 5	NOT_ENOUGH_COINS	Balance below the price 6	NOT_OWNED	No copy or no time left 7	NO_SLOT	Every slot of the perk's kind in the pool is full 8	WRONG_POOL	Personal perk sent to Party, or the reverse 9	ALREADY_EQUIPPED	The pool already holds this perk 10	BAD_VARIANT	No duration at that variant index 11	EXCLUSIVE	The pool already holds a perk of the same ExclusiveGroup

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Equipping changes no stat until Perk Rework part 3 adds the shop layer to PerkEffectsDispatcher.The client commands yield until the server answers. In the Game Instance there is no handler, so they return nil after the Packet's 10 s timeout.The run start lives in PerkSystemLoader, a gameplay script, so a future Tutorial place would also use consumables. Decide that when the Tutorial exists.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleShared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlaceableActions.luau	Client bind/unbind helper + poof visual renderer; auto-connects poof broadcast on the client side Server	src/ServerScriptService/PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau	Server validation, atomic claim, Tool grant, BroadcastPlaceablePoof dispatch Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau	PlaceableActions sub-table with all tuning knobs  Packets: ReqStashPlaceable, ReqMovePlaceable, BroadcastPlaceablePoof — see Networking MapSignals: OnPlaceableStashed, OnPlaceableMoved — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Binding the GUI​
searchDocs.content: PlaceableActions.bind(model, gui) wires MoveButton and StashButton into the packet system and returns a Binding with a single Unbind() method. On success the module fires Signals.OnPlaceableMoved or Signals.OnPlaceableStashed so other systems can react without polling. Call binding:Unbind() when the GUI closes — failing to unbind leaves the Janitor alive and button listeners connected to a GUI that may already be gone.

searchDocs.title: Poof visual​
searchDocs.content: The poof handler is client-only and lives in PlaceableActions.luau. On receiving BroadcastPlaceablePoof it clones the matching model from ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems, strips scripts/collisions/shadows from the clone, parents it to workspace.PlaceablePoofs, then runs a parallel MotionMaster.Sequence that shrinks every BasePart to near-zero while fading it out. The clone self-destructs when the sequence completes.

searchDocs.title: Server validation and atomic claim​
searchDocs.content: PlaceableActionsServer owns the OnServerInvoke handlers for ReqStashPlaceable and ReqMovePlaceable. It runs, in order: a per-player cooldown check (os.clock), an ancestry check (model.Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects), an attribute check (PlaceableName attribute on the model), a tool template check (ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools/<Name>), and a proximity check (HRP distance <= MaxActionDistance). The atomic claim pattern (model.Parent = nil followed by a re-read) prevents two simultaneous requests from granting the same item twice. The handler returns boolean — false on any failed check, true on full success.

searchDocs.title: Move and the revert store​
searchDocs.content: On a successful Move, the handler also calls PlaceableRevertStore.Set(player, { cframe = cframe, placeableName = placeableName, tool = newTool }), recording the item's original CFrame under the granted tool instance. This lets the build-mode cancel (RequestPlacementRevert) revert the item to its original spot if the player presses X without re-placing. The entry is cleared when the player re-places via PlaceItem, when the revert fires and consumes it, or when the player leaves the server.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Three requirements must all be present A placeable supports Stash/Move only when all three of the following exist simultaneously: A Model in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> (already required for placement).A Tool template in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> with a PlaceableName attribute set to the same name string.ImageButton instances named exactly MoveButton and StashButton somewhere inside the GUI that PlaceableActions.bind is called with. Every match is wired, so a multi-page GUI (e.g. the Workbench) may repeat them per page. Either the Tool or a button may be omitted, but the missing one will log a warning and that action will be silently unavailable to the player. If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing, the server returns false and nothing is destroyed — no item is lost — but the player gets no feedback.  The server proximity check (MaxActionDistance) is a second guard independent of the ProximityPrompt range. Keep them in sync when tuning the in-world prompt.Stash/Move discards all per-instance state on the placed model. The granted Tool is always a fresh clone from the template. If per-instance state matters, snapshot attributes before the action reaches the server.Any nearby player can stash any placement — ownership is not tracked. Add per-instance owner attributes and an ownership check in handleAction if griefing becomes a concern.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as PlaceableActions (client) participant S as PlaceableActionsServer participant O as All clients P->>C: Press MoveButton / StashButton C->>S: ReqMovePlaceable / ReqStashPlaceable S->>S: Cooldown check (per-player, os.clock) S->>S: Ancestry check (model.Parent == PlacedObjects) S->>S: Attribute check (PlaceableName) S->>S: Tool template check (PlaceableTools/<Name>) S->>S: Proximity check (HRP distance <= MaxActionDistance) S->>S: Atomic claim (model.Parent = nil, race guard) S->>S: Clone Tool -> player.Backpack alt Move S->>S: humanoid:EquipTool(newTool) end S->>O: BroadcastPlaceablePoof(cframe, placeableName, isMove) S->>S: model:Destroy() + record cooldown timestamp O->>O: PlaceableActions plays shrink tween + SFX

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: PlacementConfig (PlaceableActions sub-table) — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luauPlaybook: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable  Field	Default	DescriptionCooldown	0.4 s	Per-player minimum gap between accepted stash/move requests PoofDuration	0.25 s	Duration of the shrink-to-nothing tween on poof MaxActionDistance	24 studs	Server-side re-check of player proximity to the placed model

searchDocs.title: API​
searchDocs.content: PlaceableActions

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/PlacementClient.client.luau	Build-mode controller: tool equip detection, ghost Heartbeat loop, input wiring, observer ghost rendering Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/PlacementCameraController.client.luau	Owns the camera during build mode (top-down view + occluder fade) Server	src/ServerScriptService/PlacementServer.server.luau	Server authority: ghost relay, anti-exploit validation, item finalization Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlacementSystem.luau	Ghost model lifecycle, placement calculation, and validity checking; used by both client and server Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau	All tuning constants for the placement system  Packets: ClientToggleGhost, ServerToggleGhost, ClientUpdateGhost, ServerUpdateGhost, PlaceItem, RequestPlacementRevert — see Networking MapSignals: OnBuildModeChanged, OnBuildValidityChanged, OnPlacementModeChanged, OnGhostLockChanged, RequestRotate, RequestPlacementConfirm, RequestPlacementCancel, RequestGridModeToggle, RequestGhostLockToggle, RequestShootingCamera — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Entering build mode​
searchDocs.content: On tool equip, PlacementClient creates one PlacementSystem instance (grid size 2, tag BuildArea), calls SetBuildMode(true) and SetGhostModel(template), and fires ClientToggleGhost. It also fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(false) to disable the aim camera. PlacementCameraController then takes over: it freezes the player, swings the camera over the player and zooms out into a straight-down CameraType.Scriptable view that move input pans, fades any PlacementOccluder-tagged geometry, and exits through a CoolTransitions checkerboard. See Camera.

searchDocs.title: Tracking the ghost​
searchDocs.content: A Heartbeat loop rate-limited to GhostUpdateHz (default 20 Hz) raycasts, calls UpdateGhostPosition, and fires ClientUpdateGhost with the resulting CFrame. Signals.OnBuildValidityChanged fires whenever validity changes so UI and audio can react. Grid/free toggle, rotation, confirm, cancel, and ghost-lock are all driven by signals wired to BuildModeGuiController. The client listens for ServerToggleGhost / ServerUpdateGhost and calls SetOtherGhost to render other players' ghost previews.

searchDocs.title: Server relay and validation​
searchDocs.content: PlacementServer relays ClientToggleGhost to other players after confirming the item name exists in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems, and relays ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame type-checked) to other players. On PlaceItem it enforces a per-player cooldown (PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 s), character/tool guards, ray-origin distance (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 55 studs), final-position distance (MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60 studs), and collision validity — all using an isolated PlacementSystem instance with a ServerStorage-parented ghost that is never replicated.

searchDocs.title: Finalizing a placement​
searchDocs.content: On success, the server clones the template, calls finalizeModel (makes CollisionBox invisible + non-collidable, visual parts opaque, and tags the CollisionBox with PlacementObstruction so future placements collide with it), parents it to workspace/PlacedObjects, destroys the player's tool, and broadcasts ghost-clear to all clients. Any player whose character overlaps the placed item — the placer or anyone else — is then teleported clear of it (see Players never block; safe push-out).

searchDocs.title: Shared PlacementSystem​
searchDocs.content: PlacementSystem handles ghost model lifecycle, grid-snap vs free-placement position calculation, collision-box derivation, obstruction validity check, and other-player ghost rendering. IS_CLIENT guards prevent Texture and TweenPlus calls from running on the server; SetBuildMode is client-only (it creates grid Texture instances on build area parts), while the server sets IsBuildMode = true directly. Each PlaceItem request creates an isolated PlacementSystem instance — this is intentional, so concurrent requests from different players cannot corrupt shared state. Never cache a server-side PlacementSystem across requests.

searchDocs.title: Cancelling build mode​
searchDocs.content: Pressing X (configurable via PlacementConfig.CancelKey) or the on-screen Cancel button (mobile) fires Signals.RequestPlacementCancel. Both paths reach the same cancelPlacement function in PlacementClient, which snaps build-mode visuals off and sends a RequestPlacementRevert RemoteFunction call to the server. Escape is intentionally not used — Roblox reserves it for the in-game menu.  The server checks PlaceableRevertStore to determine the outcome:  Session type	OutcomeFresh placement (item was never placed before)	Server returns false → client calls humanoid:UnequipTools() and the tool returns to the Backpack Move session, original spot is free	Server re-places the item at its original CFrame, destroys the tool, returns true → item reverts, no unequip needed Move session, original spot is occupied	Server returns false → client falls back to unequip  See Placeable Actions for how a Move session records the revert entry.

searchDocs.title: Players never block; safe push-out​
searchDocs.content: BuildObstructionFilter never includes player characters, so no player blocks the client ghost or the server check. NPCs, placed items, and PlacementObstruction fixtures still block. After the item is parented, pushPlayersClearOfBox in PlacementServer finds every character overlapping the item's collision box and teleports each one:  Nearest safe spot around the box (findSafeSpot): 8 directions, starting toward the player, each far enough out that a PUSH_CHARACTER_SIZE box clears the item along that direction (box half-extent + character half-extent + PUSH_ITEM_GAP). A spot is safe when it is inside the BuildArea footprint (shrunk by the clearance), a floor exists within PUSH_FLOOR_PROBE studs below, and a PUSH_CHARACTER_SIZE box there touches no PlacementObstruction part.Else beside the nearest living player who is not in the box (same search, zero-size box around them).Else spawn: player.RespawnLocation or the first SpawnLocation, 3 studs above it.Else the player stays and the server logs a warn.  The revert path uses the same function.  The platform it clamps into comes from PlacementSystem.LastBuildAreaPart, populated only by CalculatePlacement's raycast (the PlaceItem path). The revert path re-places at a stored CFrame and never calls CalculatePlacement, so LastBuildAreaPart is nil there; PlacementServer falls back to findBuildAreaBelow, a dedicated helper that raycasts straight down from the revert position (filtered to the BuildArea tag, the same idiom CalculatePlacement uses) to resolve the platform part.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit — do not relax the server thresholds MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 55 (sized to the top-down camera's reach, sqrt(PanRadius² + ZoomMax²)), MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60, and PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 in PlacementServer are the primary defences against remote placement exploits. Raising these values substantially would allow clients to place items anywhere in the world or spam unlimited items.  Model structure is required. Every entry in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems must have a CollisionBox (BasePart) child. Without it, PlacementSystem warns and falls back to bounding-box collision, which can cause floating or incorrect validity checks.Obstruction is tag-driven, not folder-driven. Build placement only avoids a volume if it is tagged PlacementObstruction. Placed items are tagged automatically on their CollisionBox by finalizeModel. Any static world model that placement must respect (e.g. TrainShieldGeneratorPlaceholder, ResearchBench) must have a CollisionBox BasePart tagged PlacementObstruction by hand. Tag the CollisionBox part only, never the whole model — sibling sub-models like TrajectoryPoints would otherwise become map-wide placement blockers.CollisionBox must not be named RootPart or tagged PlacementIgnore. Those names cause the part to be treated as invisible/non-collidable in the ghost.SetBuildMode must only be called on the client. Calling it on the server would create Texture instances in workspace and replicate them to all clients.Ghost relay is observer-only. The GhostModels folder and its contents exist only on the client; the server's validity check correctly skips that folder for this reason.Cutscene and combat gates (isInCutscene, isInCombat) in PlacementClient are not yet wired to any external system — they are TODO integration points.  Server-side security thresholds live in PlacementServer.server.luau as local constants (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE, MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE, PLACE_COOLDOWN) — treat them as sensitive anti-exploit values.

searchDocs.title: Point and coin economy​
searchDocs.content: Each level-up grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point.Available points = playerLevel - spent, computed by PerkState.available — points are never stored directly. spent = the pool's perk levels plus the UnlockPointCost of every unlocked perk in that pool.Points cannot go negative; the pool is floored at 0.Upgrade cost: level n of a perk costs 1 point + UpgradeCoinStep × n coins. PerkState.upgradeCost(perkId, n) is the single price source (server, PerkClient, GUI). UpgradeCoinStep is 100, 200 or 350 per perk (perk review part 5 moved unlock levels but kept the coin steps). Starters pay upgrade coins too.Respec costs nothing to start, returns all points in the chosen pool, re-locks non-starter perks, and refunds every coin paid on them (see Coin ledger).Points carry across places because PerkManager uses the same DataStore key (PlayerPerks) everywhere in the universe.  PerkConfig.Perks is the single tuning surface. Each perk has Category, DisplayName, Description, MaxLevel, display Order, a Buffs list, the unlock fields, UpgradeCoinStep, and an optional Hidden flag. Each BuffSpec is { Key, PerLevel, Format? }: the dispatcher publishes PerLevel * level under Key.  PerkState.effectText(perkId, level) builds the GUI text: every {i} in Description becomes the formatted value of Buffs[i]. Format picks the formatting: "percent" (default, 0.025 → 2.5%), "count" (whole number), "total" (1 + value — Wide Net shows the whole net size), "seconds" (1.5 s). Example: Field Medic at level 5 reads +50% regen, −1.5 s regen delay.

searchDocs.title: Unlock gate​
searchDocs.content: Every perk declares an UnlockLevel (player level) gate plus a one-time cost: UnlockCost (coins) and UnlockPointCost (points from the perk's own pool). A perk with all three at 0 is a free starter, auto-unlocked: Iron Constitution (Personal) and Scavenger's Eye (Party).  Unlock is permanent: it persists on the PlayerPerks profile as an Unlocked map ({ [perkId]: boolean }).  function PerkManager.UnlockPerk(player: Player, perkId: string): (boolean, number) function PerkManager.AllocatePoint(player: Player, perkId: string): (boolean, number)   UnlockPerk validates with PerkState.canUnlock (order: UNKNOWN_PERK → PERK_UNAVAILABLE → ALREADY_UNLOCKED → LEVEL_REQUIRED → NO_POINTS → NOT_ENOUGH_COINS), deducts UnlockCost via CoinManager.DeductCoins, records it in the ledger, marks the perk unlocked, and replicates. AllocatePoint validates with PerkState.canAllocate (order: UNKNOWN_PERK → PERK_UNAVAILABLE → PERK_LOCKED → AT_MAX_LEVEL → LEVEL_REQUIRED (upgrade gate) → NO_POINTS → NOT_ENOUGH_COINS), deducts the upgrade coins before it raises the level (a failed deduct changes nothing), records them in the ledger, fires OnPerkStateChanged, and replicates. The frozen enum (PerkResultCodes):  Code	Value	MeaningOK	0	Success NO_PROFILE	1	Profile not loaded UNKNOWN_PERK	2	Perk id not in PerkConfig AT_MAX_LEVEL	3	Already at MaxLevel NO_POINTS	4	Pool can't pay (upgrade: < 1; unlock: < UnlockPointCost) PERK_LOCKED	5	Perk not yet unlocked ALREADY_UNLOCKED	6	Unlock requested twice LEVEL_REQUIRED	7	Below UnlockLevel (unlock) or the upgrade gate (upgrade) NOT_ENOUGH_COINS	8	Below UnlockCost (unlock) or the upgrade price (upgrade) NOTHING_TO_RESET	9	Per-perk respec on a perk at level 0 that is locked or a starter PERK_UNAVAILABLE	10	Perk is Hidden (declared, mechanic not built yet)  Unlocking a perk changes no buffs (its level is still 0), so UnlockPerk does not fire Signals.OnPerkStateChanged.  Hidden perks. A perk whose mechanic is not built yet ships with Hidden = true. canUnlock/canAllocate return PERK_UNAVAILABLE, and PerkClient never lists or commands it. PerkState.spent still counts its levels, so un-hiding needs no migration. Wreck Salvage (Plunder) is hidden until enemy ships exist (perk review part 3). Levels carried over from Plunder stay and still use Party points; the Party pool "reset all" (PerkManager.Respec) refunds them, because a hidden perk has no card for the per-perk respec.

searchDocs.title: Upgrade gates​
searchDocs.content: Each perk level also needs a player level: PerkState.upgradeGate(perkId, n) = UnlockLevel + ceil((n − 1) × UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN / (MaxLevel − 1)), capped at XPConfig.MAX_LEVEL. Level 1 needs UnlockLevel; the max level needs UnlockLevel + 35 (PerkConfig.UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN). Example: Ricochet (unlock 65, max 5) → levels at player Lv 65 / 74 / 83 / 92 / 100. canAllocate refuses a level under its gate with LEVEL_REQUIRED. Levels a save already holds above the gate stay; only new levels are checked.  Unlock levels are spread over player levels 1–75 in power bands (Basic 1–20, Mid 20–45, Strong 45–75). Levels 76–100 open only upgrade gates (the last loadout slot opens at Lv 70). See Progression — what each level opens.

searchDocs.title: Coin ledger​
searchDocs.content: CoinsSpent: { [perkId]: number } on the profile records every coin paid per perk (unlock + each upgrade). Respec (PerkManager.Respec, a pool) and per-perk respec (PerkManager.RespecPerk) refund exactly CoinsSpent[perkId] through CoinManager.RefundCoins — un-inflated, not scaled by the Pocket Change CoinGainBonus — then clear the entry. Only the ledger decides a refund, never current prices, so a later re-tune of UnlockCost or UpgradeCoinStep never changes what a reset returns. If the coin profile is gone mid-respec, the perk is still reset and a warn names the lost amount.  Respec clears PerkLevels, re-locks non-starter perks, then re-seeds starters. Per-perk respec is validated by PerkState.canRespecPerk (UNKNOWN_PERK → NOTHING_TO_RESET). Both fire OnPerkStateChanged and replicate. The starter rule lives in one place, PerkState.isStarter.

searchDocs.title: Migration​
searchDocs.content: migrateAndSeed runs on every load; each step is version-guarded:  Schema 1 (PerkSchemaVersion < 1): one-time clean-slate wipe of PerkLevels/Unlocked.Schema 2 (PerkSchemaVersion < 2, the Perk Rework): the 12 old perks are gone. The v1 unlock prices of every old unlocked perk (frozen in LEGACY_V1_UNLOCK_COSTS inside PerkManager; starters add 0) are added to the persisted PendingLegacyRefund, then PerkLevels, Unlocked and CoinsSpent are wiped and the version is set to 2.Starters are re-seeded after the steps.  The wipe never waits. The payout waits for the coin profile: payLegacyRefund polls CoinManager.IsLoaded for up to 60 s, then refunds PendingLegacyRefund and sets it to 0. If the coin profile does not load in time (or the perk session ends first), the amount stays saved and is paid on a later join — never lost, never paid twice.

searchDocs.title: Where perk commands run​
searchDocs.content: PerkManager.Initialize() loads profiles, migrates, replicates and resends on level-up. The four request packets are bound only by PerkManager.WireCommandHandlers(), which only the Lobby's PerkLoadoutService calls: perk changes are Lobby-only. In the Game Instance the Perk menu's buttons get no answer (Studio logs OnServerInvoke not found) until Perk Rework part 4 makes that menu read-only.  PerkManager, CoinManager, XPManager and PerkInventoryManager each register a teleport hand-off with PersistenceRegistry: the Lobby ends their sessions without a kick right before a party teleport and reopens them if it fails. See Perk Inventory.  Shop perks (consumable and expiring, equipped in the Lobby) are a separate system: see Perk Inventory.

searchDocs.title: Party-max resolution​
searchDocs.content: Party perks apply to the entire server, but only the highest level held by any single player is active. If Player A has Fuel Saver 6 and Player B has Fuel Saver 3, the server resolves at 6. PerkEffectsDispatcher recomputes the max on every allocate, respec, player join, and player leave.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk layer​
searchDocs.content: Perk Rework part 3 adds shop perks on top of the permanent perks. PerkEffectsDispatcher stays the only writer; for every key:  Personal: permanent value + the sum of the player's live shop perks.Party: permanent party max + each live party shop perk, counted once. Two players with the same party perk do not stack; different perks of one family do. <ShopPerkId>HolderId names the first holder (0 = not active).  A shop perk is live when it is in this run's ActiveRun (read only through PerkInventoryManager.GetActiveRun), visible, and (expiring) its clock has not ended. Every shop key is written each publish (0 when nothing is live), so an ended perk clears its key. The math lives in the pure ShopPerkEffects module (Studio self-check at boot). A shop key with no reader logs one warn at boot.  Expiry: the clock is real time. The dispatcher keeps one task.delay to the earliest upcoming expiry among present players and republishes when it fires, so a perk can end mid-run.  Junk bridges: JunkService overwrites its multipliers, so the dispatcher sends one value per tier — tier 1 1 − TierOneShift, tier 2 1 + TierOneShift · w1 / w2 (Golden Lure keeps the tier 1+2 total), tiers 3–5 1 + JunkTierRarityBonus — and ApplyTypeMultiplier("Energy", 1 + EnergySpawnBonus) (Energy Forecast).

searchDocs.title: Buff contract​

It listens to Signals.OnPerkStateChanged, Signals.OnShopPerksChanged, PlayerAdded, PlayerRemoving and the next shop perk expiry, then calls publishPersonal and publishParty. Both write every BuffSpec.Key of every perk in the pool, and every shop key of the pool. It also bridges Scavenger's Eye / Lucky Streak / Golden Lure to Signals.ApplyTierMultiplier and Energy Forecast to Signals.ApplyTypeMultiplier, which JunkService consumes. searchDocs.title: Armor damage mitigation​
searchDocs.content: Crafted armor (see Armor / ArmorConfig / ArmorManager) is the base of this mitigation, not the perk. HealthManager's damage sink calls ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency), passing the player's ArmorEfficiency perk bonus read fresh on every hit. The Plated perk does not reduce damage on its own; it's an efficiency multiplier on the equipped kind's BaseReduction, applied identically whether the worn kind is Ballistic or Energy:  reduction = clamp(kind.BaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap)   Absorb scales amount by (1 - reduction) as the final step before it reaches health, and drains the worn kind's pool by whatever was absorbed — mitigation and pool drain happen in the same call, because the two cannot be split without the pool going stale (see Armor — Mitigation). With nothing equipped, or an Energy kind at zero pool, the perk contributes nothing. Because the attacker's DamageBonus is already applied upstream in WeaponServer, attacker bonus and defender mitigation multiply independently: base * (1 + DamageBonus) * (1 - reduction). Coverage is every path routed through CombatService/HealthManager (Bullet/AOE and NPC hits); damage written directly to Humanoid.Health bypasses the sink and is not mitigated (see Health).

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: PerkClient.luau is the GUI-agnostic data layer (owns no GUI). It caches the authoritative PerkStateSync snapshot (perkLevels, unlocked, personalAvailable, partyAvailable, playerLevel, coinsSpent) and watches the replicated PartyPerkBuffs folder. A snapshot without coinsSpent (an older server during a live update) reads as {}. Queries return PerkView descriptors via GetPerks/GetActivePerks/GetAvailablePoints/GetPerk/GetPlayerLevel; hidden perks are skipped. Commands: optimistic-prediction Allocate/Respec/CanRespec, plus Unlock(perkId) (no optimistic coin prediction — the server owns the balance), and a Changed signal fired on every snapshot update.  "Active" is category-aware: a Personal perk is active at the player's Level > 0; a Party perk is active at its server-wide ActivePartyLevel > 0 (read from <PerkId>Level). PerkView carries Group, Summary, EffectText, NextEffectText (nil at max), UpgradeCost (coins for the next level, 0 at max), UpgradeGate (player level for the next level, 0 at max), CoinsSpent (what a reset refunds), CanRespec, the unlock fields, and for Party perks ActiveEffectText and ActivePartyHolder: Player? (from <PerkId>HolderId). PerkController.client.luau is the one-line bootstrap that calls PerkClient.Init() once on join.  Active Perks menu. ActivePerksGuiController.client.luau binds the Studio-authored StarterGui.ActivePerksGui, a read-only view and the Game Instance's only perk GUI. It opens from a TopbarPlus "Active Perks" icon (toggle key O; CloseButton deselects it). Personal / Party tabs (TopSection.CategoryContainer) list PerkClient.GetActivePerks(tab) into BottomSection.PerkContainer (clones of ExampleItem), then the run's shop perks: Personal = ActiveRun.Personal minus ended clocks (PerkGuiRules.liveRunIds); Party = every party shop perk with PartyPerkBuffs.<Id>HolderId ~= 0, by Order. The detail panel (BottomSection.InfoContainer) shows the name, Level N (Party: the active server level), one effect line, PerkOwner (Personal: you; Party: ActivePartyHolder, hidden when nil), and PerkConfig.CategoryBlurb. For a shop perk it shows This<br/>run (consumable) or Time<br/>h:mm:ss (expiring, your own clock, ticking once a second while open), Time<br/>— for a Party perk only another player holds (the client knows only its own clocks), the Description as the effect line, and the holder as PerkOwner. It repaints on PerkClient.Changed (also PartyPerkBuffs changes) and PerkInventoryClient.Changed; an own clock that ends drops its row. A tab with nothing active hides the detail panel. It has no reset button: perk changes are Lobby-only.  Lobby Perk menu. PerkMenuGuiController/ (Lobby only) binds the Studio-authored StarterGui.PerkMenuGui: one window with three pages, a header and two TopbarPlus icons. "Perks" (key P) opens the Upgrade tab and "Loadout" (key L) the Loadout tab; pressing the icon of the open tab closes the menu, the other icon switches tab (both icons have autoDeselect(false); the window is the one source of truth). The Shop tab is reached from the tab bar. CloseButton closes; a part tagged PerkKiosk with a ProximityPrompt opens the Loadout tab. MainContainer.UIScale = min(W / 1920, H / 1022) of the ScreenGui area. The header shows the level (PerkClient.GetPlayerLevel), the pool points (Upgrade tab only) and the coins (— until the first Signals.OnCoinsChanged; the controller connects it before its first yield). Every page repaints on PerkClient.Changed, PerkInventoryClient.Changed and OnCoinsChanged while open; countdowns tick once a second without rebuilding the lists. All text and list rules live in the pure PerkGuiRules; selected / unselected looks are read from the authored instances (LoadoutTab / UpgradeTab, the Upgrade page's PartyButton / PersonalButton, Pip1 / Pip4).  Upgrade page. Cards follow the visible list rule (reachable perks plus the next milestone level, sorted by UnlockLevel then Order). Unlocked: n/max or MAX and pips. Locked: dimmed, Lv N / Unlock / Locked, and CostLabel (1 pt + 250 coins). The detail shows PERMANENT, <Group> · Lv n / max or <Group> · Unlock at Lv N, the Summary, Now / Next effects, and Show all levels (an unlock row plus one row per level, owned rows in 76A2F2). UpgradeButton follows PerkGuiRules.upgradeAction: Requires Lv N, Need points, Need coins, Unlock, Maxed, Needs Lv N (upgrade gate), Upgrade; only Unlock (PerkClient.Unlock) and Upgrade (PerkClient.Allocate) act. LeftContainer.FilterContainer's PersonalButton / PartyButton pick the pool (Personal at start).  RespecButton (gray) resets the selected perk → PerkClient.RespecPerk; enabled when view.CanRespec, and hidden while no perk is selected.RespecAllButton (red) resets the shown pool → PerkClient.Respec(pool); enabled when PerkClient.CanRespec(pool). Its Label reads HOLD TO RESET <POOL>.  Each SubLabel shows the refund: CoinsSpent and points (levels + unlock points). Switching the filter, the tab or closing the menu cancels both holds. The Loadout and Shop pages are described in Perk Inventory — Loadout GUI.  Hold-to-reset. HoldButton.luau drives every reset button. Each button holds a Studio-authored HoldFill (Frame; 5A2328 in the Lobby PerkMenuGui) with a UIGradient whose transparency has a hard edge at 0.5, and a Label. Pressing sweeps the gradient Offset from (-0.6, 0) to (0.5, 0) (start past -0.5 so no purple sliver shows at the left edge) over PerkConfig.RESPEC_PERK_HOLD_TIME (one perk) or PerkConfig.RESPEC_HOLD_TIME (a whole pool) (MotionMaster, linear). Releasing anywhere, closing the menu, or changing the selection / tab cancels and empties the fill. A disabled button dims its Label and ignores presses.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: New readers must use PerkBuffRead Read buff values through PerkBuffRead.Personal / PerkBuffRead.Party, and apply reductions with PerkBuffRead.Reduce / ReduceCost. Do not add new inline PerkBuffs folder lookups, and never let a reduction stack reach zero. PerkBuffRead and PerkState run Studio-only boot asserts on the shared math.  Points are derived, not stored Available points are never stored directly. Available points = level - spent. Never add a separate stored point counter — it will desync.  Refunds come from the ledger only A respec refunds CoinsSpent[perkId], never a price recomputed from the config. Any new coin charge on a perk must call recordPaid, or a reset will under-refund.  Party perk levels shown in the GUI are per-player, not the resolved active level A Party card's LV n/max and the detail panel's CURRENT LEVEL show how many levels this player bought. The Active Perks menu shows the server-resolved max.  PerkEffectsDispatcher must run before PerkManager on join PerkEffectsDispatcher seeds its folder at boot. PerkManager fires OnPerkStateChanged after profile load, which triggers a republish. The ordering is correct because both are ServerScriptService scripts and PerkManager.Initialize() is called from PerkSystemLoader, which yields on ProfileStore:StartSessionAsync before firing the signal.  HPBonus subscription attaches once at join HealthManager subscribes to the HPBonus attribute change in PlayerAdded, not CharacterAdded. If PerkBuffs/<UserId> does not exist at join time (the dispatcher hasn't seeded yet), the subscription is skipped for that session. In practice the dispatcher seeds synchronously at boot, so the folder exists before any player's PlayerAdded fires normally.

searchDocs.content: Config module: PerkConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luauPlaybooks: Tune Perks, Tune Perk Unlocks  Field	EffectPerks[id].Buffs	List of { Key, PerLevel, Format? }; each key publishes PerLevel * level. Perks[id].MaxLevel	Cap on levels in this perk. Perks[id].DisplayName	Shown in the perk panel header. Perks[id].Description	Effect text; {1}, {2} … become the formatted value of Buffs[1], Buffs[2] …. Perks[id].UnlockCost	One-time coin cost to unlock (0 = free starter). Perks[id].UnlockLevel	Minimum player XP level required to unlock (0 = none). Perks[id].UnlockPointCost	One-time point cost from the perk's own pool; counted as spent, returned by respec (0 = free). Perks[id].UpgradeCoinStep	Level n costs UpgradeCoinStep × n coins. Re-tuning never changes refunds (ledger). Perks[id].Hidden	true = declared but not listed or unlockable (part 5 flips it). UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN	Player levels from a perk's unlock to its max-level gate (35). MIN_REDUCTION_FACTOR	Lowest fraction of a base value any reduction can leave (default 0.1). NET_REEL_SLOWDOWN_PER_EXTRA	Wide Net: reel slows by this fraction per extra junk in one cast (default 0.10). RESPEC_HOLD_TIME	Seconds a reset-all (whole pool) button must be held before the respec fires (default 3). RESPEC_PERK_HOLD_TIME	Seconds a single-perk reset button must be held (default 0.75; shorter, as it undoes much less). CategoryBlurb	One-line pool explanation shown in both perk menus' detail panels. STORE_NAME	ProfileStore key — change this only if you intentionally want to wipe all saved perk + unlock data.

searchDocs.title: Data model and curve​
searchDocs.content: The profile stores a single value, TotalXP (lifetime cumulative). Level and progress are never stored — they're derived from it every time via XPCurve:  XPCurve.xpToNext(level: number): number -- round(CURVE_COEFF * level ^ CURVE_EXP) + CURVE_OFFSET, 0 at/above MAX_LEVEL XPCurve.levelFromTotal(totalXP: number): number XPCurve.progress(totalXP: number): (level: number, xpIntoLevel: number, xpForNextLevel: number)   Defaults: CURVE_COEFF = 5, CURVE_EXP = 1.5, CURVE_OFFSET = 45, MAX_LEVEL = 100. Total XP to reach level 100 is roughly 204,000. All constants live in XPConfig.

searchDocs.title: Earning (party-shared)​
searchDocs.content: XP is shared with the whole party; one party occupies one server, so every player in the server receives the full award via XPManager.AddPartyXP.  Source	Amount	TriggerDistance	DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK (1) every DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS (5s)	Train is in its "go" state (running, not braked/stalled) — driven off Signals.SetTrainState Kills	KILL_XP (10) × (1 + KillXPBonus + PartyKillRewardBonus) per player, via AddXP	Any EnemyNPC-tagged model's Humanoid.Died (attribution-agnostic). The same hook pays CoinConfig.KILL_COINS — see Economy  The train starts braked, so no distance XP accrues before the first un-brake.  Perk multiplier: AddXP scales every award by 1 + XPGainBonus + PartyXPBonus (XP Booster, XP Booster II, Veteran Voyager). TotalXP stays whole; the fraction carries to the player's next award (in memory only, dropped on leave).  function XPManager.AddXP(player: Player, amount: number) function XPManager.AddPartyXP(amount: number)   Both are no-ops if amount <= 0 or the profile isn't loaded. AddXP fires XPLevelUp and Signals.OnPlayerLevelUp when the level increases, then replicates XPStateSync.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place sharing (lobby ↔ gameplay)​
searchDocs.content: DataStores are universe-wide: both places use the same STORE_NAME and key (tostring(UserId)), so XP/Level are shared automatically. The Lobby runs XPManager.Initialize() from places/Lobby/ServerScriptService/PerkLoadoutService.server.luau (perk points and level gates need the level) but not XPSystemLoader — there are no earners in the Lobby.  Teleport hand-off. XPManager registers a PersistenceRegistry.RegisterHandoff pair: right before a party teleport the Lobby ends the session without the usual kick, so the Game Instance opens it without waiting on the session lock, and reopens it if the teleport fails. See Perk Inventory — Teleport hand-off.  XPManager.IsLoaded(player) reports whether the XP profile is loaded. GetLevel returns 1 until then, so PerkManager waits for IsLoaded (up to 30 s) before its first perk snapshot, or the snapshot would show level-1 points.

searchDocs.title: Not yet built​
searchDocs.content: An XP bar HUD (would consume OnXPChanged), level rewards (hook: XPLevelUp), per-killer attribution, and additional XP sources are all unbuilt.

searchDocs.title: What each level opens​
searchDocs.content: Perks and loadout slots unlock over player levels 1–75 (perk review part 5). Levels 76–100 open only permanent-perk upgrade gates (the last loadout slot opens at Lv 70).  Levels	Opens1–20	Basic perks (both pools, all kinds). Personal consumable slot 4 at Lv 10. 20–50	Mid perks; the full Basic and Mid sets by Lv 50. Personal expiring slot 2 at Lv 25, consumable slot 5 at Lv 30, Party consumable slot 2 at Lv 45, Personal expiring slot 3 at Lv 50. 50–75	Strong perks: Wide Net, Ricochet, Gun Crew, Emergency Generator, Gold Rush, XP / Coin Booster II, Smart Cannon, Energy Recycler, Cannon Drill, Golden Lure (Lv 75). Personal consumable slot 6 at Lv 60, Party expiring slot 2 at Lv 70. 76–100	Upgrade gates only: the max level of a perk needs UnlockLevel + 35.  Tuning lives in PerkConfig / ShopPerkConfig (UnlockLevel, UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN, Slots); see Perks and Perk Inventory.

searchDocs.title: Drop path​
searchDocs.content: Pressing Backspace drops the equipped Tool as a direct child of workspace. A workspace.DescendantAdded listener in DroppedToolService catches craft-material Tools parented directly to workspace (the Roblox default Backspace drop path). The handle's CollisionGroup is set to "DroppedMaterial", CanCollide = true, Anchored = false. DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding(handle) then polls every DROP_POLL_INTERVAL (0.1 s) for DroppableSurface contact and a velocity below SETTLED_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD (0.5 studs/s). On landing, the handle is re-anchored with rotation reset to identity, and ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(tool, metadata, callback, keepModel=true) is called.  DroppedToolService also bootstraps two PhysicsService collision groups: DroppedMaterial (Tools that leave the player's hand) and DroppableSurface (tagged geometry). DroppedMaterial is non-collidable with Default and collidable with DroppableSurface, so dropped items fall through characters and walls but land on tagged floors.

searchDocs.title: Registration and claim​
searchDocs.content: ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(part, metadata, callback, keepModel?) is the sole public registration entry. It generates a GUID itemId, sets PickupItemId on the part as an attribute, tags the part "PickupItem", spawns an invisible anchored sphere zone (DEFAULT_RADIUS = 6 studs) in workspace.PickupZones, and fires PickupItemReady to all clients. zone.Touched is the primary claim trigger — any player, shared-loot semantics. Claim(part, player) is the programmatic claim path (no current caller). Both paths call the same executeClaimAsync, which transitions the record to "Claimed", destroys the zone, broadcasts PickupItemClaimed, then after FLOAT_DURATION (0.25 s) calls the callback and cleans up.  _TryMerge runs MERGE_DELAY (1 s) after registration and absorbs a newly registered handle into a nearby same-type unclaimed survivor within MERGE_RADIUS (2 studs), accumulating Quantity on the survivor. It skips keepModel items — merging would destroy one of the actual inventory objects, so only non-keepModel handles are eligible.

searchDocs.title: Client hover and claim animation​
searchDocs.content: ProximityPickupController listens to two packets only; it creates no UI and does no proximity math. PickupItemReady applies a HoverEffect (bob + Y-spin) to the handle via a Janitor-managed cleanup handle, and wires AncestryChanged so the effect stops cleanly when the part is destroyed. PickupItemClaimed stops the hover effect, then for the local claimer plays a pickup SFX (via SoundManager.PlaySFXAt using CharacterAnchor to resolve the player's position) and tweens the handle toward the camera using MotionMaster.Play; for all other clients it destroys the handle immediately.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Shared loot — not owner-only Any player who steps into the pickup sphere claims the item, regardless of who dropped it. If owner-only pickup is ever needed, the RegisterItem signature must be extended with an owner: Player? parameter and the zone.Touched handler must gate on it (see audit comment PP6 in ProximityPickupServer).  DroppableSurface tagging — no code change needed. Any BasePart tagged "DroppableSurface" in CollectionService is automatically assigned the DroppableSurface collision group at runtime via GetInstanceAddedSignal. To make a new floor or shelf surface catchable, tag it in Studio only.Collision groups are registered in one place. CollisionGroups.luau (ServerStorage/SharedModules) is the sole registrar and owns the full collidability matrix. Besides DroppedMaterial/DroppableSurface, it defines Character (every character BasePart, assigned by CharacterCollisionService) and WeaponProjectile (thrown charges, assigned by ServerProjectile). Because characters now live in their own group rather than Default, dropped materials and projectiles both pass through players while still colliding with world geometry. Any system that needs a new group or a new pair rule should edit CollisionGroups.luau, not call PhysicsService directly.keepModel semantics. When keepModel = true (the DroppedToolService path), the registered part is the actual Tool that will go into the player's Backpack — RegisterItem will not destroy it, and the callback sets tool.Parent = player.Backpack. When keepModel = false, the caller registers a stand-in handle and the callback grants the real item; the floor handle is destroyed after claim.Zone placement. Pickup zones are parented to workspace.PickupZones (not to the item part). This prevents "trying to set locked parent!" physics warnings when the zone is destroyed at claim time while the item is still mid-float.Late-joining players. ProximityPickupServer registers a JoinSync sender ("ProximityPickups") that replays all currently "Unclaimed" PickupItemReady events once the joining client announces readiness, so items already on the floor will show their hover effect for late joiners. It no longer connects Players.PlayerAdded directly — see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake for why a PlayerAdded push is unreliable.

searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant DTS as DroppedToolService participant PPS as ProximityPickupServer participant C as ProximityPickupController (client) P->>DTS: Press Backspace (Tool -> workspace) DTS->>DTS: DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding (poll 0.1s) DTS->>PPS: RegisterItem(tool, metadata, callback, keepModel=true) PPS->>PPS: generate itemId, tag PickupItem, spawn sphere zone PPS->>C: PickupItemReady(part, itemId) C->>C: HoverEffect.Apply (bob + spin) P->>PPS: zone.Touched -> executeClaimAsync PPS->>PPS: record.State = Claimed, destroy Zone PPS->>C: PickupItemClaimed(itemId, claimer) C->>C: cleanup hover; if claimer == LocalPlayer, play SFX + float to hand; else destroy PPS->>PPS: after FLOAT_DURATION, callback(player, metadata) -> Backpack

searchDocs.title: Buckets​
searchDocs.content: Each period (Daily or Weekly) rotates a fixed count of quests per category, set by QuestConfig.Counts:  Scope	Personal	PartyDaily	1	2 Weekly	1	1  Personal quests credit only the player who performed the action (e.g. collecting junk). Party quests credit every player in the server for ownerless world events (enemy kills, train distance) — a shared team objective, but the reward is still claimed and paid out per player.

searchDocs.title: Global rotation​
searchDocs.content: The active quest ids for a scope are never stored — they're recomputed deterministically from the period index alone:  QuestState.selectQuests(scope: "Daily" | "Weekly" | "Season", periodIndex: number): { string }   A seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle (distinct large-prime seeds per category so Personal and Party picks don't correlate) runs over the sorted id pool for that scope+category, sliced to Counts, then re-sorted for stable display order. Given the same periodIndex, every machine — client or server, any server in the universe — produces the identical set. Only progress, claimed flags, period indices, and lifetime stats persist on the PlayerQuests profile; the set itself is derived, not saved.

searchDocs.title: Period math​
searchDocs.content: Period indices come from os.time() (UTC), never client input:  Function	FormulaQuestState.dayIndex(now)	floor((now - DailyResetOffset) / 86400) QuestState.weekIndex(now)	floor((now - WeeklyResetOffset) / 604800) QuestState.dailyExpiresAt(now)	Unix timestamp the current daily period ends QuestState.weeklyExpiresAt(now)	Unix timestamp the current weekly period ends  Daily rolls at 00:00 local (QuestConfig.DailyResetOffset); Weekly rolls Monday 00:00 local (QuestConfig.WeeklyResetOffset, a 4-day base offset — the Unix epoch was a Thursday, so shifting 4 days aligns week starts to Mondays). Both offsets are derived from QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset — a fixed seconds-from-UTC offset defining the timezone "midnight" is measured in (pre-launch default US Eastern, -5 * 3600). It's fixed, so it does not track daylight saving; set it to 0 for pure UTC resets (DailyResetOffset = -ResetTimezoneOffset; WeeklyResetOffset = 345600 - ResetTimezoneOffset). The expiry functions are sent to the client so it can drive a live countdown with no client-side period math.

searchDocs.title: Season quests​
searchDocs.content: A fifth Scope = "Season" exists alongside Daily/Weekly, dedicated to feeding the Battle Pass. It doesn't rotate — selectQuests("Season", periodIndex) returns the entire curated set (Personal ids then Party ids, each sorted), not a Counts-limited shuffle-and-slice, so every Season quest is active for the whole month. Its period index is BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now) (a calendar-month index, not a quest-owned index), so a season's quests reset in lockstep with the battle pass itself — the profile's SeasonPeriod/SeasonProgress/SeasonClaimed fields follow the exact same rollover/auto-grant pattern as Daily/Weekly.  The shipped pool (SeasonJunk, SeasonKills, SeasonDistance) pays Coins = 0, Exp = 0 and a large BPExp (3000 each) — Season quests exist purely to move the battle pass track, not the coin/XP economy. Any quest, of any scope, can additionally carry an optional Reward.BPExp: number?; the shipped Daily/Weekly pool also pays smaller BPExp amounts alongside normal coins/exp, so ordinary questing keeps the pass moving too.

searchDocs.title: Attribution​
searchDocs.content: Two entry points on QuestManager mirror XPManager.AddXP/AddPartyXP:  function QuestManager.ReportProgress(actor: Player, metricKey: string, amount: number) function QuestManager.ReportPartyProgress(metricKey: string, amount: number)   Function	Has an actor	AdvancesReportProgress	Yes (e.g. junk collection)	Bumps the actor's own Lifetime metric, advances the actor's Personal quests, and fans the same amount out to every online player's Party quests for that metric ReportPartyProgress	No (e.g. enemy died, train distance)	Advances every online player's Party quests and bumps each player's Lifetime metric total  Either path calls ensureCurrent first (rolls any elapsed period before applying progress) and only replicates (QuestStateSync) to players whose progress actually changed.

searchDocs.title: Claim and auto-grant sweep​
searchDocs.content: function QuestManager.ClaimQuest(player: Player, questId: string): (boolean, number, number, number)   Manual claim is wired to Packets.ReqClaimQuest and invokes ClaimQuest, which validates in order — profile loaded, quest exists, quest is in the currently active set for its scope, progress ≥ target, not already claimed — and returns (ok, reasonCode, coinsGranted, expGranted). The claimed flag is set before the reward is granted, so a re-entrant or duplicate call cannot double-pay: the second call fails fast with ALREADY_CLAIMED.  The auto-grant sweep runs inside ensureCurrent (called on join, before every progress report/claim, and on the periodic rollover tick). When a scope's stored period index differs from the current index, it walks the old set (selectQuests(scope, oldPeriodIndex)) and grants any quest that was completed but never claimed, before resetting that scope's Progress/Claimed maps. A player who finishes a quest right before rotation and never opens the claim UI is still paid.  Both paths share one grantReward function, which pays coins/exp then fires Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted(player, quest.Reward). BattlePassManager connects to this signal and reads reward.BPExp off the payload regardless of whether the grant came from a manual claim or an auto-grant sweep — see Battle Pass — EXP earning.

searchDocs.title: Sources​
searchDocs.content: QuestSourcesLoader (gameplay-only — safe to run in the lobby place, where these events simply never fire) wires the three QuestConfig.Metrics to their gameplay triggers:  Metric	Category	TriggerEnemyKills	Party	Humanoid.Died on any CollectionService-tagged ENEMY_TAG ("EnemyNPC") model — one Janitor per tracked enemy DistanceTravelled	Party	A recurring task.wait(DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS) loop credits DISTANCE_PER_TICK while Signals.SetTrainState reports the train running JunkCollected	Personal	Signals.OnJunkCollected — fired by JunkService once per successful finalized junk grab (collector, junkId)  Adding a quest that reuses one of these Metric keys needs no source code change — only a new entry in QuestConfig.Quests. Wiring a brand-new metric needs one new source hookup in QuestSourcesLoader (see Tune Quests).

searchDocs.title: Perk seam​
searchDocs.content: profile.Data.Lifetime is a { [key]: number } table that is never reset by rollover — distinct from the per-period Progress maps. advancePlayer bumps Lifetime["QuestsCompleted"] by 1 on every below-target → at-target transition, and both report functions bump Lifetime["metric:"..metricKey] by the raw reported amount.  function QuestManager.GetLifetimeStat(player: Player, key: string): number   This is a deliberate seam for a future PerkConfig unlock criterion (e.g. "unlock this perk after QuestsCompleted >= 25") — not wired to any perk this cycle.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: QuestClient is a GUI-agnostic read-model, the same shape as PerkClient. It caches the authoritative QuestStateSync snapshot, recomputes the active set client-side with the same QuestState.selectQuests the server uses (so client and server never disagree), and exposes a QuestView descriptor:  export type QuestView = { Id: string, Scope: "Daily" | "Weekly" | "Season", Category: "Personal" | "Party", DisplayName: string, Description: string, Icon: string?, Metric: string, Target: number, Progress: number, IsComplete: boolean, IsClaimed: boolean, IsClaimable: boolean, RewardCoins: number, RewardExp: number, ExpiresAt: number, }   Queries: GetQuests/GetActiveQuests/GetCompletedQuests/GetQuest, plus GetLifetimeStat and a fire-and-forget Claim(questId) command. A Changed signal fires on every snapshot update. No GUI ships this cycle — a future screen requires QuestClient and subscribes to Changed, exactly like PerkClient.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved quest data QuestConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerQuests") is the ProfileStore key for progress, claimed flags, and the never-reset Lifetime table. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile — all prior quest progress and lifetime stats are orphaned (not deleted, just unreachable). It must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places for the cross-place session handoff to share the same record.  Personal progress from ReportProgress also advances Party quests ReportProgress(actor, metricKey, amount) is not Personal-only — it fans the same amount out to every online player's Party quests for that metric, then additionally advances the actor's Personal quests. A quest author reusing a Personal-sourced metric (JunkCollected) for a new Party quest gets it "for free" — no new source wiring needed.  The active set query needs the correct period index QuestState.selectQuests takes a periodIndex, not a timestamp. Always derive it via QuestState.dayIndex/weekIndex(os.time()) (server) or read it from the cached QuestStateSync snapshot (client, via QuestClient) — never hardcode or guess an index.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Extra daily quests (DailyExtra, no source yet): selectQuests(scope, period, extraPersonal) picks Counts.Personal + extraPersonal Personal ids from the same seeded shuffle, so the normal set stays and the extra is the next id in that day's rotation. The daily rollover resets DailyExtra to 0. Every server selectQuests call passes extraFor(profile, scope) (Daily only), and QuestStateSync carries dailyExtra so QuestClient shows the same set. The Quest Hunter perk that raised it is gone (perk review part 3); a Robux product will (part 4B). A Studio self-check in QuestState asserts the extra pick keeps the normal set.Contract Bonus (QuestRewardBonus, 0.25; id QuestTracker): QuestManager.grantReward pays floor(Coins × (1 + bonus)) coins and floor(Exp × (1 + bonus)) XP, and ClaimQuest returns those amounts. Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted still carries the base reward, so Battle Pass EXP is not multiplied (Season Surge owns BP EXP). The rollover auto-grant uses the same path, so the bonus applies when the perk is live at grant time.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Source as QuestSourcesLoader participant Manager as QuestManager (server) participant Client as QuestClient (owning client) Note over Source,Manager: REPORT Source->>Manager: ReportProgress(actor, metric, amt) / ReportPartyProgress(metric, amt) Manager->>Manager: ensureCurrent() — roll elapsed periods first Manager->>Manager: advancePlayer() bumps Progress[questId] (clamped to Target) alt progress changed Manager->>Client: QuestStateSync(periods, expiry, progress, claimed, lifetime) end Note over Manager: COMPLETE (progress[questId] >= Target) Manager->>Manager: bumpLifetime("QuestsCompleted", 1) on the below→at-target transition Client->>Client: QuestView.IsClaimable becomes true (IsComplete and not IsClaimed) Note over Client,Manager: CLAIM Client->>Manager: ReqClaimQuest(questId) Manager->>Manager: validate (active set, progress >= Target, not claimed) Manager->>Manager: claimed[questId] = true (BEFORE grant — idempotent guard) Manager->>Manager: CoinManager.AddCoins(.., "Quest:"..questId); XPManager.AddXP(..); Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Fire(player, reward) Manager-->>Client: (ok, reasonCode, coinsGranted, expGranted) Manager->>Client: QuestStateSync (reconciled snapshot)

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: QuestConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/QuestConfig.luauPlaybook: Tune Quests  Field	EffectSTORE_NAME	ProfileStore key — change this only if you intentionally want to wipe all saved quest progress/claims/lifetime data. DailyResetOffset / WeeklyResetOffset	Shift where the daily/weekly period boundary falls (seconds). Derived from ResetTimezoneOffset. ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS	How often the live server tick re-checks online players for a period rollover. DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS / DISTANCE_PER_TICK	Cadence and per-tick amount for the DistanceTravelled source while the train runs. searchDocs.title: Threat model​
searchDocs.content: A reserved server (created by the lobby via TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync) already blocks the normal server-list join and rejects follow-a-friend joins. Two vectors remain: launching the gameplay placeId directly and landing in a non-reserved public server (game.PrivateServerId == ""), or a non-roster user reaching a reserved server with a stale access code or expired session.  JoinGuard closes both by validating every joiner against an authoritative roster keyed off the engine-set game.PrivateServerId, which cannot be spoofed from the client — so authorization can never be forged.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place contract​
searchDocs.content: Coordination between the lobby and gameplay places goes through two MemoryStore hash maps (fast, TTL-native, built for ephemeral cross-server state — unlike DataStore, which is slower, rate-limited, and has no native expiry). SessionStore is the only module that touches them.  Roster — keyed by privateServerId:  { partyId, authorizedUserIds: {number}, leaderUserId, createdAt }   The lobby writes this immediately before TeleportAsync, so it exists by the time the gameplay server boots. SessionStore.GetRoster reads it on boot with a short retry loop (GET_RETRIES × GET_RETRY_WAIT) to cover the boot/write race. SessionCoordinator mutates it via RemoveFromRoster when a grace window expires, and clears it entirely via ClearRoster on run end.  Session pointer — keyed by userId:  { placeId, accessCode, privateServerId, jobId, status, heartbeatAt }   This lets the lobby route a rejoiner back to the exact live server. The lobby seeds placeId/accessCode/privateServerId at teleport time, obtaining accessCode + privateServerId from the server-only TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync(gameplayPlaceId). Gameplay fills jobId and heartbeats the entry via SessionStore.RefreshPointer(userId, jobId), which uses UpdateAsync to stamp only jobId/status/heartbeatAt onto the already-seeded entry — it returns without creating a pointer if the lobby never seeded one, since gameplay never learns the raw accessCode and must not fabricate it.  jobId is informational/liveness only — it is not used to route the rejoin. On the lobby side, rejoin must set opts.ReservedServerAccessCode = accessCode alone; the engine API forbids combining ReservedServerAccessCode with ServerInstanceId or ShouldReserveServer on the same TeleportOptions. The access code alone resolves to the one reserved server it was issued for. TeleportData may additionally carry { partyId, rosterVersion } for diagnostics/logging — never trusted for authorization.

searchDocs.title: Components​
searchDocs.content: JoinGuard — IsReservedServer() is true only for a non-empty PrivateServerId with PrivateServerOwnerId == 0 (rejects both a directly-launched public server and a VIP server). IsAuthorized(roster, userId) checks roster.authorizedUserIds. BounceToLobby(player) retry-teleports to DisruptionConfig.LOBBY_PLACE_ID, reusing that config and its TELEPORT_RETRIES count from the Disruption system.SessionCoordinator.IsAuthorized(player) — whether the player may play this run: false when every player is bounced (not a reserved server, or no roster), otherwise the Studio bypass or the roster check. It yields until Initialize has read the roster. PerkSystemLoader passes it to PerkInventoryManager.Initialize, so a bounced player never uses a shop perk consumable (see Perk Inventory).SessionState — RegisterProvider(name, capture, restore) lets other managers plug into the grace/restore flow (see below). Capture(player) must run synchronously from PlayerRemoving, before any deferred teardown clears state. HoldForGrace/HasGrace/TakeBundle/Discard manage the grace window via a Janitor per held entry.SessionSystemLoader — registers AmmoManager.Snapshot/RestorePool and HealthManager.GetHealth/SetHealth as SessionState providers (under the keys "ammo" and "health"), then calls SessionCoordinator.Initialize().

searchDocs.title: Grace and restore flow​
searchDocs.content: On an unexpected PlayerRemoving (no prior ReqLeaveToLobby), SessionCoordinator.handleLeave synchronously calls SessionState.Capture(player) — which clones every Tool from the player's Backpack and Character into a per-user folder under ServerStorage.SessionToolCache, then runs every registered provider's capture (ammo pool snapshot, current health) — and holds the bundle via SessionState.HoldForGrace(userId, bundle, SessionConfig.GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS, onExpire). The player stays on the roster while held.  Scenario	What happensRejoin within the grace window	JoinGuard re-admits the player (still authorized). SessionCoordinator.handleJoin sees SessionState.HasGrace(userId) and calls scheduleRestore, which waits for CharacterAdded (or applies immediately if a character already exists) and, deferred one frame so HealthManager's full-health CharacterAdded reset runs first, calls SessionState.Restore(player, bundle) — reattaching cached Tools to the fresh Backpack and running every provider's restore. The player respawns at the normal train/party spawn; character position is never captured or restored. Grace window expires without a rejoin	The task.delay in HoldForGrace fires onExpire, which clears the session pointer and removes the user from the roster so they can no longer rejoin; the bundle's Janitor destroys the cached Tools folder. Clean leave (ReqLeaveToLobby)	SessionCoordinator marks the userId in cleanLeaving before bouncing, so the ensuing PlayerRemoving calls SessionState.Discard (no grace hold) and clears the pointer + roster entry immediately. Run end	When PlayerRemoving leaves the server empty (#Players:GetPlayers() <= 1, checked before removal completes) or on game:BindToClose, runEnded clears the roster and every remaining pointer for this privateServerId. No live-server rejoin is possible once the run has ended — a later rejoin attempt lands in the normal lobby flow.  SessionState's tools-folder cleanup uses an explicit Janitor index (Janitor:Add(toolsFolder, "Destroy", TOOLS_JANITOR_INDEX)), not the implicit form, specifically so TakeBundle can detach the folder without destroying it: it calls Janitor:RemoveNoClean(TOOLS_JANITOR_INDEX) (clears the index with no side effect) rather than Janitor:Remove (which would run the cleanup method immediately and destroy the very folder the caller is about to restore Tools from).  A SESSION_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS loop in SessionCoordinator periodically refreshes the roster TTL (SessionStore.RefreshRosterTTL) and every present, authorized player's pointer TTL (SessionStore.RefreshPointer), so a live run never expires while a dead run (crashed process, no clean shutdown) self-expires after ENTRY_TTL_SECONDS.

searchDocs.title: Non-goals​
searchDocs.content: Live-server rejoin only — rejoin works only while the reserved server stays alive (≥ 1 member keeps it running). If the server empties, the run ends and rejoiners return to the lobby fresh; there is no shared-world snapshot or run resurrection.No character-position restore — a rejoining player always respawns at the normal train/party spawn.No DataStore for ephemeral state — health/ammo/Tools grace-window state lives only in server memory (SessionState) and is lost if the server itself dies during the grace window; this is a deliberate scope cut, not an oversight.The lobby implementation (reserve, roster write, rejoin UI) is a separate project; only the cross-place contract above is specified here.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: BYPASS_GUARD_IN_STUDIO still exercises grace/restore In Studio, SessionConfig.BYPASS_GUARD_IN_STUDIO (default true) makes SessionCoordinator authorize everyone unconditionally, since no reserved server or lobby exists locally. It does not disable the grace/restore code paths — a Studio playtest still exercises Capture/HoldForGrace/Restore normally.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Player participant Coordinator as SessionCoordinator participant State as SessionState participant Guard as JoinGuard participant Store as SessionStore (MemoryStore) Note over Player,Coordinator: UNEXPECTED DROP Player--xCoordinator: PlayerRemoving (no prior ReqLeaveToLobby) Coordinator->>State: Capture(player) — Tools + ammo + health Coordinator->>State: HoldForGrace(userId, bundle, GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS, onExpire) alt Rejoin within GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS Player->>Coordinator: PlayerAdded (still on roster) Coordinator->>Guard: IsAuthorized(roster, userId) Guard-->>Coordinator: true Coordinator->>State: HasGrace(userId) == true Coordinator->>State: scheduleRestore -> TakeBundle + Restore (on CharacterAdded) State-->>Player: Tools reattached; ammo + health restored at train spawn else Grace window expires State->>State: onExpire fires Coordinator->>Store: ClearPointer(userId); RemoveFromRoster(privateServerId, userId) Note over Player: A later join is now unauthorized -> Guard.BounceToLobby ejects them end

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: SessionConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SessionConfig.luau  Its names and GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID/map-name values are the contract with the lobby. The lobby lives in this repo and requires the same module (see Multiple Places).  Field	EffectGRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS	How long (120s) a dropped player's slot + cached health/ammo/Tools are held for a live-server rejoin before being discarded. SESSION_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS	How often (30s) the live gameplay server refreshes the roster + session-pointer TTLs in MemoryStore. ENTRY_TTL_SECONDS	TTL (90s, 3x heartbeat) written on both MemoryStore structures; refreshed every heartbeat, so a server that dies unobserved self-expires roughly this many seconds later. GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID	This place's PlaceId. Used by the lobby to reserve + teleport in. Set to 107438402196338; 0 = unset. ROSTER_MAP_NAME	MemoryStore hash-map name for the roster ("EJ_SessionRoster"), shared with the lobby project. SESSION_MAP_NAME	MemoryStore hash-map name for the session pointer ("EJ_SessionPointers"), shared with the lobby project. BYPASS_GUARD_IN_STUDIO	When true (default), authorizes everyone in Studio so local playtests work without a reserved server, while still exercising grace/restore logic.
