Resolves each node's GuiPath to its card, paints the five node states, writes labels/costs/timers from config, wires card clicks + the detail panel + queue slots + fuel gauge Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ResearchService.luau	ModuleScript; authoritative owner of ResearchState.State, wires packet handlers + tick loop, gates ReqResearchEnqueue on gamepass ownership Server	src/ServerScriptService/ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau	One-line boot script: require(ResearchService) then ResearchService.Initialize() Server	src/ServerScriptService/ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau	Connects Signals.OnResearchLevelUp, republishes ResearchBuffs / ResearchUnlocked from every node's Effects list Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ResearchState.luau	Pure, stateless rules module: enqueue, cancel, advance, refuel, serialize, isEligible (loops Prereqs, AND semantics) Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ResearchResultCodes.luau	Frozen result-code enum shared by client and server, including GAMEPASS_REQUIRED Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ResearchConfig.luau	Bench tag/interaction distances, queue/fuel/refund constants, NodeStateColors palette, BIOME_SELECTOR_GAMEPASS_ID, and the 31-node Nodes table  Packets: ReqResearchSnapshot, ReqResearchEnqueue (can now return GAMEPASS_REQUIRED), ReqResearchCancel, ReqResearchRefuel, ResearchStateUpdate — see Networking MapSignals: OnResearchLevelUp, OnResearchStateChanged — see Signals Map  This is a data + binding system: no new packets or signals were added to grow the catalog from 3 placeholder nodes to 38 (31 after the melee branch was removed) — the queue/fuel/cancel/broadcast machinery is unchanged.

searchDocs.title: Core loop​
searchDocs.content: Enqueue — player spends materials immediately (pay-on-enqueue, not pay-on-complete) to queue an eligible node. If nothing is active, the job just enqueued starts immediately. The server also checks the node's Gamepass (if any) before accepting — see Gamepass gating.Advance — a server tick burns bench fuel and advances the active job's elapsed time. Progress pauses whenever fuel hits 0; it resumes the instant fuel is added back.Complete — when elapsed >= duration, the node's level is recorded, Signals.OnResearchLevelUp fires, and the next queued job (if any) becomes active.Refuel — a player clicks the Refuel button in the tech tree GUI (QueueFuelContainer.ActionContainer); TechTreeGuiController fires ReqResearchRefuel with no target. The server spends pool Energy via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo. There is no refuel ProximityPrompt — see Studio setup.Cancel — a player cancels a node's job (queued or active); see Cascade-cancel.  Because there is one shared queue and one shared fuel pool for the whole server, this is explicitly a co-op system: any player at the bench can enqueue, cancel, or refuel, and progress benefits everyone.

searchDocs.title: Buff nodes vs. unlock-flag nodes​
searchDocs.content: Every entry in ResearchConfig.Nodes is a Node with MaxLevel = 1 and a single Levels[1] entry (Cost, Duration). The levelling machinery (MaxLevel, Levels keyed by number) is still generic — it costs nothing to keep and a future node could ship with MaxLevel > 1 — but every node shipped today researches once. Two shapes exist:  Buff nodes declare an Effects list (not a single Effect) — e.g. { { Type = "StatBuff", Key = "MaxHP", PerLevel = 50 } }. A list is required because two nodes need more than one key at once: Shield_Efficiency/Shield_EfficiencyPlus each grant ShieldEfficiency and ShieldStrength, and Shield_Delta grants MaxHP and ShieldAutoRegen. ResearchEffectsDispatcher sums every entry across every researched node sharing a Key into ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs (see Buff/unlock folders).Unlock-flag nodes have Effects = nil. Completing them writes only a ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> BoolValue; there is no buff to compute. This is every node outside the Train Shield branch — Ranged/Armor weapon and armor nodes gate Workbench recipes, and Train Weapon/Train Utility/Special nodes gate systems that do not exist yet (see Honest status of Effects). The one recipe gate actually wired in WorkbenchConfig — CraftSMG's RequiresNode = "Ranged_SMG" — points at a Ranged branch node, confirming any node id can gate a recipe. See Workbench Crafting for the consumer side.

searchDocs.title: Prerequisites are AND-lists​
searchDocs.content: Prereqs: { string }? is a list, not a single id — every listed prereq must be at level ≥ 1 (ResearchState.isEligible loops the list) — there is no OR, and no separate minimum-level field now that every node is MaxLevel = 1. Three nodes actually need more than one prerequisite, which is the reason the field is a list at all:  Ranged_EnergyFirearms — Ranged_SniperRifle and Ranged_ExplosivesShield_Delta — Shield_Gamma and Shield_EfficiencyPlusTrainWep_Sturmlanze — TrainWep_MissileLauncher and TrainWep_BurstCannon  ResearchConfig.validate() walks every Prereqs edge at Studio-boot time and warns on an unknown prereq id or a prereq cycle — see Verification.

searchDocs.title: Cascade-cancel​
searchDocs.content: Cancelling is keyed by (nodeId, fromLevel). ResearchState.cancel removes every queued job of the same node with targetLevel >= fromLevel (full refund), and if the active job belongs to the same node and active.targetLevel >= fromLevel, cancels it too at ResearchConfig.ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION (0.5) — the same mechanism the old multi-level Tech Tree used.  With every node now MaxLevel = 1, a node can only ever have one job outstanding at a time (queued or active, never both, and never two queued levels stacked behind each other) — ResearchState.validateEnqueue rejects a second enqueue for the same node with AT_MAX_LEVEL. So in practice cascade-cancel today always resolves to cancelling that single job: fromLevel is always 1, and there is nothing behind it to cascade into. The generic multi-level mechanism is kept as-is (smaller diff than removing it) in case a future node ships with MaxLevel > 1.  If neither the queue nor the active job matches, ReqResearchCancel returns NOTHING_QUEUED and nothing is refunded. Refunds are credited to the server-wide Material Pool with the bench's TrajectoryPoints as the effect origin (pivot fallback); every client animates them into the Materials HUD.

searchDocs.title: Fuel and pause behavior​
searchDocs.content: Fuel is a single server-wide reserve, capped at ResearchConfig.FUEL_CAP (100).While a job is active, fuel burns at ResearchConfig.FUEL_BURN_RATE (1.0/sec) — an idle bench (no active job) never burns fuel.ResearchState.advance clamps effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel / burnRate) so a job's elapsed only ever grows in step with fuel actually spent — the moment fuel reaches 0, elapsed stops advancing (the job pauses, it does not fail or lose progress). Refueling resumes it on the next tick.Refueling spends shared pool Energy: ReqResearchRefuel calls MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", FUEL_CAP − fuel, FUEL_PER_POINT) — the same path the Train Fuel, Train Shield, Jump Drive and Energy armor use — so it spends only the points needed to fill. A full bench returns FUEL_FULL (nothing spent); an empty pool returns NO_FUEL_ITEM. The trigger is now the GUI's Refuel button rather than a second ProximityPrompt — see Studio setup.  Fuel and queue are shared, not per-player There is exactly one fuel value and one queue for the entire server. Any player at the bench can enqueue against the shared queue, refuel the shared reserve, or cancel any job — including jobs another player paid for. This is intentional (co-op resource pooling) but means griefing-by-cancel is possible; there is no per-player ownership check.

searchDocs.title: Buff/unlock folders​
searchDocs.content: ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau is the sole writer of two ReplicatedStorage folders, both recomputed from scratch (not delta-accumulated) on every Signals.OnResearchLevelUp, iterating every node's Effects list:  Folder	Shape	Written by	Read byReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs	Attributes on the folder itself: one numeric attribute per StatBuff.Key (summed PerLevel * level across all nodes with that key), plus FuelEfficiency (product of DrainPerLevel ^ level across all FuelEfficiency-effect nodes; 1 = no effect)	ResearchEffectsDispatcher	TrainShieldManager (MaxHP), TrainFuelManager (FuelEfficiency), TrainShieldGuiController readout (ShieldStrength/ShieldEfficiency/ShieldAutoRegen — display only, see below) ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked	One BoolValue (named by nodeId, Value = true) per node at level ≥ 1	ResearchEffectsDispatcher	WorkbenchService (server gate), WorkbenchGuiController (client greying)  Recompute-from-levels means totals are always correct with no drift risk, at the cost of iterating every node in ResearchConfig.Nodes on every level-up (cheap — 31 nodes). ResearchEffectsDispatcher also seeds both folders once at server boot (before any player joins) so WaitForChild consumers never race an empty folder.  Honest status of Effects​  Only two of the five buff keys published by the Train Shield branch feed real gameplay math today — the other three are read by the shield monitor's readout and rendered, but nothing changes behavior based on them. Every other branch's nodes are unlock-flag-only; the systems they gate (energy weapons, collectors, recycler, shared storage, train weapons) do not exist yet.  Buff key	Consumer	Real effect day one?MaxHP	TrainShieldManager.computeMax	Yes FuelEfficiency	TrainFuelManager drain	Yes ShieldStrength	TrainShieldGuiController readout only	No — display only ShieldEfficiency	TrainShieldGuiController readout only	No — display only ShieldAutoRegen	TrainShieldManager regen loop (Shield δ)	Yes — 0.5% of max every 10 s; the Shield Capacitor perk doubles it  Util_EngineBooster (Train Utility branch) deliberately ships with no Effects at all: it is "+speed, burns more fuel", FuelEfficiency exists and works, but there is no train speed buff key yet — publishing only the fuel-cost half would make researching it a strict downgrade. It stays unlock-flag-only until a speed key exists.

searchDocs.title: Card states & palette​
searchDocs.content: TechTreeGuiController paints every card into one of five states, sourced from ResearchConfig.NodeStateColors — the single source of truth for the palette (Background, Stroke, NameText, StatusText, StatusIcon, Line):  State	MeaningLocked	Prereqs not yet met Available	Eligible, not queued/active/researched (this is also the authored card's default look) Queued	Waiting behind the active job InProgress	The active job — also pulses its stroke colour via MotionMaster (never TweenService) Unlocked	Researched — spends the tree's one saturated accent, cyan #33CCFF, reused from TrainConfig.SHIELD_ICON_HEALTHY_COLOR  There is no Unaffordable state. A node you can reach but cannot pay for still renders Available — only the cost numbers in the detail panel's UnlockCostContainer turn red and the action button disables. One less state to build and to learn, and the affordance sits where the player is already looking when deciding to buy.  ConnectionLines on a card is an outgoing list — a card names the Line* frames that run from it to its children, so a line takes the state of the card that declares it, not either endpoint. Only Locked and Unlocked change a line's colour; a queued or in-progress node has not actually opened its path yet, so its outgoing lines stay Available mauve until it completes. Unlocked lines render at ResearchConfig.UNLOCKED_LINE_TRANSPARENCY (0.35) so lit paths glow without dominating the panel.

searchDocs.title: Gamepass gating​
searchDocs.content: ResearchState stays pure and knows only about Prereqs — ownership is a separate gate layered on top by ResearchService:  Server checks MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync at enqueue time (ReqResearchEnqueue), caching the result per (player, passId); a PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished hook clears a cached denial so a mid-session purchase is picked up immediately. A gated node the player doesn't own is rejected with the new GAMEPASS_REQUIRED (11) result code.Client (TechTreeGuiController) does not pre-check ownership for greying — an ungated attempt simply surfaces the "Requires a game pass." toast on rejection.Owning the pass makes a node eligible; it is still queued with materials and duration like any other node.  Today exactly one node uses this: Special_BiomeSelector (SpecialTech.SpecialTech1), gated on ResearchConfig.BIOME_SELECTOR_GAMEPASS_ID = 1982397425. Note that passesGamepassGate treats only a missing Gamepass field as "no gate" — a node carrying Gamepass = 0 is refused with GAMEPASS_REQUIRED, because 0 is not a pass anyone can own. So blanking the id locks the node rather than freeing it.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared responsibilities​
searchDocs.content: Shared — ResearchState.luau is a pure, stateless module with no Roblox service calls: newState, levelOf, pendingLevel, isEligible (loops Prereqs, AND semantics), validateEnqueue, enqueue, cancel (cascade logic), advance (tick), refuel, serialize. Both the server (authority) and the client GUI (asState() cast over the cached snapshot, for greying/afford checks) call the same pure helpers, so the rules can never drift between sides. validateEnqueue deliberately does not check materials or gamepass ownership — those checks are server-only and layered on top by ResearchService.  Server — ResearchService.luau is the authoritative owner of ResearchState.State. It is a ModuleScript, not a .server.luau Script — see ModuleScript + loader split below. Initialize() (idempotent, guarded by a boot flag) wires all four packet handlers plus the RunService.Heartbeat tick loop, the gamepass ownership cache, and its PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished/PlayerRemoving hooks. GetLevels() exposes the live levels table for ResearchEffectsDispatcher to read.  Server — ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau is a one-line boot script: require(...ResearchService) then ResearchService.Initialize(). Mirrors PerkManager.luau / PerkSystemLoader.server.luau.  Server — ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau connects Signals.OnResearchLevelUp and republishes both buff/unlock folders from scratch, looping every node's Effects list. See Buff/unlock folders.  Client — TechTreeGuiController.client.luau binds the Studio-authored StarterGui.TechTreeGui; it never generates GUI. It opens the tree from the bench's TechPromptPart ProximityPrompt, resolves every node's ResearchConfig.GuiPath to a card ("<BranchFrame>.<CardFrame>", relative to TechScrollingFrame), and asserts the card ↔ node bijection while binding (see Verification). Cards are plain Frames with Active = true and an InputBegan handler — no injected TextButtons. Selecting a card feeds the detail panel (InfoActionContainer); the queue panel (InProgressContainer + QueueButton1..3) and a three-segment fuel gauge (FuelBar1/2/3, one continuous 0–100 reading split in thirds) are driven by MotionMaster springs, never TweenService. The panel closes three ways: TopContainer.CloseButton (bound once for the script's lifetime), re-triggering the bench prompt, or the bench losing its tag. Move/Stash wiring is one call — PlaceableActions.bind(benchModel, gui.benchInteraction) — but see Move/Stash is inert today. Uses one Janitor for the open/close lifecycle (springs + the per-frame RenderStepped connection are recreated on open, destroyed on close). Between ResearchStateUpdate broadcasts, interpolated() fast-forwards the active job's elapsed time and the fuel gauge locally using the known burn rate and the synced server clock — ported, not reinvented, from the controller this one replaced.

searchDocs.title: ModuleScript + loader split (caution)​
searchDocs.content: ResearchService is a ModuleScript, booted by a separate loader ResearchService.luau lives under ServerStorage/SharedModules/ as a ModuleScript, not ServerScriptService/ResearchService.server.luau. This is deliberate: Roblox's require() only accepts ModuleScript instances — a *.server.luau file compiles to a plain Script, which can never be required by another script. Because ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau needs to call ResearchService.GetLevels(), ResearchService has to be a ModuleScript. The split mirrors the existing PerkManager.luau (ModuleScript, state + Initialize()) / PerkSystemLoader.server.luau (thin boot Script) pattern: ResearchService.luau defines state + an idempotent Initialize() that wires packets and the tick loop, but does nothing until Initialize() is called.ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau is the only script that calls ResearchService.Initialize(), exactly once per server. If you ever see require() fail on a *.server.luau/*.client.luau path in this codebase, this is the fix: split the requirable state into a ModuleScript and add a thin loader Script that calls its Initialize().

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Manual, one-time Studio work — none of this is created automatically by code:  Bench Model. The ResearchBench tag on ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems.ResearchBench, with PrimaryPart set; placed clones live under workspace.PlacedObjects and inherit the tag. Lookup is by tag, never by name — see The bench is a placeable.Refund-arc trajectory. A child Model named TrajectoryPoints (tagged PlacementIgnore, per the Placement "tag the CollisionBox only" rule) holding two BasePart children: SpawnPoint (arc start, the bench's output mouth) and LandingPoint (arc end, the floor drop zone). If missing, MaterialPool.ArcPoints falls back to the bench pivot; the refund is still credited.Research prompt. A child BasePart named TechPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt — opens the GUI. MaxActivationDistance is set to ResearchConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE by the client controller at runtime.No refuel prompt. Refueling is a button inside the opened GUI (QueueFuelContainer.ActionContainer) firing ReqResearchRefuel, see Core loop. There is no second ProximityPrompt and no REFUEL_PROMPT_PART_NAME constant.Material templates. ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials holds Wood and Metal Tool templates whose Handle the clients clone for the cosmetic refund effect — shared with the Shredder, no duplication needed.StarterGui.TechTreeGui. The authored tree itself — 7 branch frames positioned inside one TechScrollingFrame, each node a card Frame (TechText, StatusContainer.{StatusIcon,StatusText}, UIStroke, UICorner, UIPadding, plus an outgoing ConnectionLines attribute). Every node's GuiPath in ResearchConfig must resolve to one of these cards; TechTreeGuiController asserts the bijection on bind (a node with a bad path warns and is skipped; an unclaimed card warns too) — see Known GUI authoring gaps for the intentionally-left issues.  Known GUI authoring gaps​  These are attribute edits that live in Studio only — not fixed here, recorded as open items for you to address (or not) in the editor:  SpecialTech1 declares ConnectionLines = "Line1,Line2" but the SpecialTech branch has no Line children — stale copy-paste from a duplicated card. TechTreeGuiController warns once per missing line and skips it; this is the only expected warning pair at boot.RangeWeapon4 (Explosives) owns Line5,Line6,Line7 but has only two children, while RangeWeapon3B (Sniper Rifle) owns none despite feeding Ranged_EnergyFirearms. The Sniper Rifle → Energy Firearms connector is parked on Explosives, so it lights when Explosives completes rather than when Sniper Rifle does. Cosmetic; the fix is moving one line name between the two cards' attributes.QueueButton2/QueueButton3 lack the ExampleItem child that QueueButton1 has. TechTreeGuiController guards this (FindFirstChild, nil-safe) so nothing errors, but those two slots will never show a filled-slot icon when occupied — only AddIcon visibility toggles correctly.  The bench is a placeable​  The bench is authored the same way as the Workbench: the ResearchBench tag lives on the template at ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems.ResearchBench, so every clone PlacementServer places inherits it. ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools.ResearchBench is the matching Tool (attribute PlaceableName = "ResearchBench", with a Handle).  The tag is not identity CollectionService:GetTagged(BENCH_TAG) matches three different things, in no guaranteed order: the placed bench, the ReplicatedStorage template, and other players' build-mode ghosts — PlacementSystem strips tags from the local ghost but not from the other-player ghosts it parents under workspace.GhostModels, prompts included. This is the trap CannonConfig documents when it says placed cannons are found by attribute and "NOT a CollectionService tag — that would also match client build-mode ghosts." Both lookups (ResearchService.findBench, the client's isLiveBench) therefore require Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects, the same condition PlaceableActionsServer enforces. A workspace-descendant check is not enough: ghosts live in workspace too, and an unfiltered lookup either measures isNearBench against a template in ReplicatedStorage — failing every enqueue with TOO_FAR — or hands out a working tech tree prompt on someone else's floating preview.  BenchInteractionContainer's MoveButton/StashButton go through PlaceableActions.bind, but PlaceableActionsServer.handleAction additionally requires a non-empty PlaceableName attribute on the placed Model. That attribute is never authored in Studio — PlacementServer stamps it at runtime on the line after it parents the clone (PlacementServer.server.luau, both the place and restore paths), which is why the PlaceableItems templates have no such attribute while the PlaceableTools Tools do (theirs is hand-authored and read at place-time). A bench dragged into workspace.PlacedObjects by hand therefore lacks it. open() checks it into stashable and hides the container when it fails, so the buttons are never visible-but-dead.  The ResearchBench Tool has no source today: it is not in StarterPack and CraftWorkbench is the only Kind = "Placeable" recipe. Stashing the world bench is currently the only way to hold it, so a player who stashes and then loses the Tool loses the bench. Add a Workbench recipe with Output = { Kind = "Placeable", PlaceableName = "ResearchBench" } if that matters.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every request The client's ProximityPrompt distance is never trusted. ReqResearchEnqueue, ReqResearchCancel, and ReqResearchRefuel all re-run isNearBench on the server using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE. A player invoking from range receives TOO_FAR.  Validate-then-consume ordering on enqueue ReqResearchEnqueue pays with one atomic MaterialPool.Spend(cost): it checks every cost entry against the server-wide pool before subtracting any. If the pool is short on any single material, nothing is consumed — there is no partial-payment state. The gamepass check runs after prereq/queue validation but before the materials check.  Cost is paid on enqueue, not on completion Materials are deducted the instant a level is successfully enqueued — the queue holds already-paid-for jobs. Cancelling is therefore the only way to get materials back, and only at the refund fractions described in Cascade-cancel.  Gamepass ownership is cached per (player, passId), including denials UserOwnsGamePassAsync is a yielding web call. ResearchService caches both grants and denials so it isn't re-queried on every enqueue attempt; a purchase completing mid-session clears the cached denial via PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished. A failed web call denies without caching, so the next attempt retries rather than sticking a player with a false negative.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as TechTreeGuiController participant S as ResearchService participant D as ResearchEffectsDispatcher P->>C: Walk within INTERACT_DISTANCE, trigger TechPromptPart C->>S: ReqResearchSnapshot() S->>C: { levels, active, queue, fuel } C->>C: cache populated; cards/detail/queue/fuel repainted P->>C: Click a card, then RESEARCH in the detail panel C->>S: ReqResearchEnqueue(nodeId) S->>S: re-check bench + proximity S->>S: ResearchState.validateEnqueue (unknown/prereq/max level/queue full) S->>S: passesGamepassGate(player, nodeId) - GAMEPASS_REQUIRED if ungated node not owned S->>S: MaterialPool.Spend(cost) - NOT_ENOUGH_MATERIALS if the pool is short S->>S: ResearchState.enqueue(...) - starts immediately if idle S->>C: (success, reasonCode) S->>C: ResearchStateUpdate(state, serverTime) loop every TICK_INTERVAL S->>S: ResearchState.advance(state, dt, FUEL_BURN_RATE) Note over S: effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel/burnRate) - progress pauses at fuel==0 alt elapsed >= duration S->>D: Signals.OnResearchLevelUp(nodeId, level) S->>S: startNext() - pop next queued job end S->>C: broadcast() on completion, or at most every HEARTBEAT_BROADCAST_INTERVAL end C->>C: interpolate elapsed/fuel locally between broadcasts (synced server clock) C->>C: repaint() - card/line states + detail panel + queue slots D->>D: republish(): recompute ResearchBuffs from every node's Effects list D->>D: publish ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> if level >= 1 P->>C: Click a queue slot or the in-progress panel C->>S: ReqResearchCancel(nodeId, fromLevel) S->>S: ResearchState.cancel -> (activeRefund?, queuedRefund) S->>S: eject queuedRefund @ 1.0, activeRefund @ ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION S->>C: (success, reasonCode) + broadcast() P->>C: Click Refuel in the queue panel C->>S: ReqResearchRefuel() S->>S: MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", FUEL_CAP − fuel, FUEL_PER_POINT) S->>S: ResearchState.refuel(state, value, FUEL_CAP) S->>C: (success, reasonCode) + broadcast()

searchDocs.content: Config module: ResearchConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ResearchConfig.luauPlaybook: Tune Research BenchPerks: ResearchFullRefund (Lab Insurance, Party shop) — while it is > 0, cancelling the active job refunds 1.0 of its cost instead of ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION. ResearchSpeedBonus (Lab Rats, Party) — ResearchService sets state.speed = 1 + b each tick; ResearchState.advance adds fueled seconds × speed progress (fuel still burns per real second). speed is serialized, so the Tech Tree timer and bar agree. See Perks. searchDocs.title: The catalog​
searchDocs.content: 31 nodes across 6 branches, each GuiPath relative to TechScrollingFrame. Costs/durations follow a fixed tier curve (Metal 25/60/120/200/320, Wood —/10/25/40/60, Duration 30/60/120/180/240s) but every node's numbers are written out explicitly in config so each is independently tunable.  Branch	Nodes	Effects?Ranged Weapons (7)	Ranged_Handgun → Ranged_SMG → Ranged_AssaultRifle/Ranged_SniperRifle → Ranged_Explosives → Ranged_AntiVehicle, and Ranged_EnergyFirearms (needs SniperRifle + Explosives)	Unlock-flag only Armour (5)	Armor_Light → Armor_MedBallistic/Armor_MedEnergy → Armor_HeavyBallistic/Armor_HeavyEnergy	Unlock-flag only Train Shield (6)	Shield_Alpha → Shield_Beta/Shield_Efficiency → Shield_Gamma/Shield_EfficiencyPlus → Shield_Delta (needs Gamma + EfficiencyPlus)	Yes — see Honest status of Effects Train Weapons (6)	TrainWep_Cannon → TrainWep_AutoCannon/TrainWep_EnergyCannon → TrainWep_MissileLauncher/TrainWep_BurstCannon → TrainWep_Sturmlanze (needs Missile + Burst)	Unlock-flag only Train Utility (6)	Util_Recycler → Util_Storage/Util_EngineBooster → Util_CollectorAlpha/Util_WeaponOptimizer → Util_CollectorBeta	Unlock-flag only (Util_EngineBooster deliberately ships no Effects — see Honest status of Effects) Special (1)	Special_BiomeSelector	Unlock-flag only; gated on BIOME_SELECTOR_GAMEPASS_ID — see Gamepass gating  Every gameplay system behind an unlock-flag node — energy weapons, collectors, the recycler, shared storage, train weapons — publishes only its ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> flag today; the system itself has not been built. See ResearchConfig.Nodes for the exact per-node GuiPath/Prereqs/Cost/Duration/Effects.

searchDocs.title: Verification​
searchDocs.content: Two checks, split by what each can actually see at runtime — there is no automated test suite for this project.  ResearchConfig.validate() — pure data, no DataModel access, runs under RunService:IsStudio() at the bottom of the module so it warns on every Studio session. Asserts every Prereqs entry names a real node, the prereq graph is acyclic, every node has Levels[1] and a non-empty GuiPath, every Effects entry has a handler in the dispatcher (StatBuff/FuelEfficiency), and NodeStateColors defines all six fields for all five states.  Controller bind pass — GuiPath resolution can only be checked where the GUI exists, so the card ↔ node bijection is asserted in TechTreeGuiController as it binds: every node's GuiPath must resolve to a real card, and every card under TechScrollingFrame must be claimed by exactly one node. Mismatches warn with the offending name rather than erroring, so a half-authored tree still opens. The SpecialTech1 gap (see Two known GUI authoring gaps) is the one expected warning pair.  Everything else is Studio verification, per project convention.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SettingsClient.luau	Get/Set/GetAll/GetDefinition/GetByCategory, value cache, debounced save, join-sync apply Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SettingsAppliers.luau	Client-only key -> applier registry (volumes → Groups.SetVolume) Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/SettingsManager.luau	ProfileStore session lifecycle, legacy Volumes migration, SyncSettings on join, SaveSetting listener Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SettingsSchema.luau	Validate(key, value), Sanitize(map) — the one validator both sides call Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SettingsConfig.luau	Definitions registry, VolumeBusByKey, GetDefaults(), STORE_NAME  Packets: SyncSettings, SaveSetting — see Networking MapSignals: OnSettingChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Config & schema​
searchDocs.content: SettingsConfig is pure data with no client dependencies, so the server can require it directly. SettingsConfig.Definitions is the single registry — one entry per setting key, typed as:  export type Definition = { type: "number" | "boolean" | "enum", default: any, category: string, label: string, order: number, min: number?, max: number?, step: number?, options: { string }?, }   SettingsConfig.GetDefaults() returns a fresh { [string]: any } map of every key to its default — this seeds both a brand-new ProfileStore profile and profile:Reconcile() for existing ones. SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey maps the four volume setting keys to their SoundConfig/Groups bus name (Master, BGM, SFX, Ambience) — the one place that mapping is declared, reused by both the migration step and SettingsAppliers. SettingsConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerSettings") is the ProfileStore name and must not change without a migration plan, since it is also where the legacy Volumes table is read from.  SettingsSchema is the single validator, called identically by server and client so the two sides can never disagree on what's valid. SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value): (boolean, any) looks key up in Definitions (unknown key is rejected, acting as an allowlist); for "number" it rejects non-numbers/NaN then clamps to [min, max]; for "boolean" it requires an exact boolean; for "enum" it requires membership in options. SettingsSchema.Sanitize(map) builds a complete settings map from GetDefaults() overlaid with every entry in map that passes Validate — anything invalid or no longer in the registry is silently dropped.

searchDocs.title: Server authority​
searchDocs.content: SettingsManager owns one ProfileStore session per player (PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync(tostring(player.UserId), ...)), following the same lifecycle pattern as CoinManager/XPManager: it kicks the player if the session fails to start, ends the session and re-kicks on OnSessionEnd, and ends the session on PlayerRemoving.  On join, before profile:Reconcile() runs, migrateLegacyVolumes(profile) does a one-time, idempotent copy: for every key in VolumeBusByKey, if Settings[key] is unset and the legacy profile.Data.Volumes[bus] is a valid number, it's validated and copied into Settings[key]. Once a key exists in Settings it is never overwritten from Volumes again, so this is safe to leave running indefinitely. The legacy Volumes table itself is left in place (not cleared) after migration.  SettingsManager.Initialize() — called once per server by SettingsSystemLoader.server.luau — wires Packets.SaveSetting.OnServerEvent: it looks up the player's profile (drops the message if none), checks key is a string, re-validates (key, value) through SettingsSchema.Validate, and on success writes profile.Data.Settings[key] = coerced. There is no explicit save call — ProfileStore autosaves the profile. Any invalid or unknown-key message is silently dropped.

searchDocs.title: Client API​
searchDocs.content: SettingsClient — initialized once via SettingsController.client.luau calling SettingsClient.Init() at startup — is the only module the settings GUI talks to. It holds a local cache of every setting's current value and exposes Get(key), Set(key, value): boolean, GetAll(), GetDefinition(key), and GetByCategory() (every definition grouped by category and sorted by order; today: "Audio" with 4 entries, "Controls" with 1, CameraSensitivity).  Internally, applyAndNotify(key, value) is the shared path for both the join-sync handler and Set: it writes the cache, calls SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, value), then fires Signals.OnSettingChanged:Fire(key, value). The join-sync path calls only applyAndNotify (never scheduleSave), which is what prevents applying the server's own synced values from looping back into another save. scheduleSave(key, value) debounces persistence per key: the latest value is stashed in a pending table, and a single task.delay(0.25, ...) per key sends the trailing value via Packets.SaveSetting:Fire(key, value) — rapid changes (e.g. dragging a volume slider) collapse into one network send 0.25s after the drag settles.

searchDocs.title: Client appliers​
searchDocs.content: SettingsAppliers is a client-only key -> (value) -> () registry, kept deliberately separate from SettingsConfig so the shared config module stays free of client-only dependencies (Groups, UserSettings()) that the server must never require. The four volume keys are wired generically by iterating VolumeBusByKey and calling Groups.SetVolume(bus, value) — see Sound for the underlying SoundManager.SetVolume/GetVolume primitives; persistence lives here, not in SoundManager. Apply(key, value) looks up and calls the applier for key, or no-ops silently if the key has no client-side effect — CameraSensitivity is a deliberate example of the no-entry-needed case: it has no applier because CameraController reads it directly via SettingsClient.Get("CameraSensitivity") at startup and stays live via Signals.OnSettingChanged (see Camera).

searchDocs.title: Adding a new setting​
searchDocs.content: Two steps, at most:  Add one entry to SettingsConfig.Definitions — a unique key, a type ("number" | "boolean" | "enum"), a default, a category + label for the GUI, an order within that category, and the relevant bounds (min/max/step for "number", options for "enum"). That's enough for the setting to round-trip end to end: it seeds into new profiles, syncs on join, validates, and persists.If the setting has a direct client-side effect, add a matching entry to SettingsAppliers's appliers table — a one-argument function that applies value. Skip this step for settings with no client effect.  No packet, schema, or ProfileStore change is needed for a new setting — SettingsSchema.Validate and SettingsManager are fully generic over the Definitions table.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never call SettingsAppliers or SettingsManager's internals directly GUI code should only ever call SettingsClient.Get/Set/GetAll/GetDefinition/GetByCategory and listen to Signals.OnSettingChanged. Calling SettingsAppliers.Apply directly skips validation, caching, and persistence — the value will apply visually but never save and will be wiped out by the next join-sync. SettingsManager is server-only and cannot be called from client code; firing Packets.SaveSetting directly skips client-side validation and the cache, desyncing SettingsClient.Get from what the server actually has.  The join-sync path never re-saves. SettingsClient.Init()'s SyncSettings handler calls applyAndNotify directly, not Set — applying the server's own synced values must never re-fire a save back to the server in a feedback loop.SettingsManager.Initialize() re-validates every SaveSetting message. A modified or out-of-date client can fire any (key, value) pair; the server drops anything that fails SettingsSchema.Validate rather than trusting the client's own clamping.Legacy Volumes data is migrated, not deleted. migrateLegacyVolumes copies old per-bus volumes into the generic Settings map once, but the old Volumes table is left on the profile afterward. Don't write new code that reads profile.Data.Volumes.Removing a Definitions entry doesn't delete saved data, but does stop syncing it. SettingsSchema.Sanitize drops any key no longer present in Definitions, so a removed setting simply disappears from SyncSettings/GetAll going forward — it does not actively scrub the old key from the ProfileStore document.CameraSensitivity scales GetMouseDelta(), not an engine property. UserGameSettings.MouseSensitivity is gated behind the RobloxScript capability (CoreScript-only) and throws if a game LocalScript writes it. UserInputService.MouseDeltaSensitivity is settable but only scales GetMouseDelta() consumers — it would have had no effect on the old default Roblox camera, which didn't consume GetMouseDelta() for look/rotation at all. That constraint is why CameraController is a fully script-owned Scriptable camera that reads raw GetMouseDelta() and scales it by CameraConfig.MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity itself. See Camera.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ShredderClient.client.luau	Prompt registration, nonce-guarded two-step handshake, junk-count-reactive HoldDuration updates Server	src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau	Session management, anti-exploit validation, junk consumption, yield credited to MaterialPool Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderMath.luau	Shared ComputeHoldDuration helper (linear interpolation) Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderResultCodes.luau	Frozen result-code enum (9 codes) shared between client and server Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShredderConfig.luau	All tunable constants for interaction, hold duration, anti-exploit, client arc animation, and asset names  Packets: ReqShredderStart, ReqShredderComplete, ShredderHoldEnded — see Networking MapSignals: none — the shredder is a self-contained two-step RemoteFunction handshake

searchDocs.title: Client: prompt and handshake​
searchDocs.content: ShredderClient watches CollectionService for Workbench-tagged models. On each workbench it finds a ProximityPrompts/ShredPromptPart/ProximityPrompt, sets ActionText, HoldDuration, and MaxActivationDistance from config, and wires three connections: PromptButtonHoldBegan (fires ReqShredderStart), PromptButtonHoldEnded (fires ShredderHoldEnded and bumps the nonce to cancel), and Triggered (fires ReqShredderComplete only when the nonce matches the armed value). A Backpack and Character Janitor pair keeps HoldDuration in sync whenever junk is added or removed. If the player holds the prompt with zero Wood/Metal junk, an "info" notification fires and the prompt is briefly disabled.

searchDocs.title: Server: two-step session​
searchDocs.content: ReqShredderStart validates the workbench tag, proximity (INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE), per-player cooldown, and junk availability. It stores a session record (workbench, start time, computed duration, junk snapshot). ReqShredderComplete re-checks all constraints plus timing (elapsed >= duration - HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE), re-validates junk still belongs to the player from the snapshot, computes the Wood/Metal yield, and destroys all junk Tools.

searchDocs.title: Processing animation​
searchDocs.content: Each placed workbench plays ShredderConfig.PROCESS_ANIMATION_ID (looped) on its AnimationController.Animator while any hold is on. The server plays it, so it replicates to every client. Holds: a player from a successful ReqShredderStart until ReqShredderComplete, ShredderHoldEnded, a new start, leaving, or a safety timeout (duration + HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE + 1 s); and each Salvage Drone junk for ShopPerkConfig.DRONE_PROCESS_SECONDS. ShredderHoldEnded only releases the animation hold; it never ends the session, because it can arrive after ReqShredderComplete. A bench with no Animator warns once and processes without the animation. The game creator must own the animation asset.

searchDocs.title: Output​
searchDocs.content: On a valid completion the server calls MaterialPool.Add({ Wood, Metal }, MaterialPool.ArcPoints(bench)). The pool is server-wide — no material Tools are created, nothing lands on the floor, and the workbench is never locked (WORKBENCH_BUSY is no longer returned). Every client animates the gain locally: Handle clones arc out of TrajectoryPoints and fly into the Materials HUD. See Material Pool.

searchDocs.title: Shared math and result codes​
searchDocs.content: ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration linearly interpolates hold time between MIN_HOLD_DURATION (1 item) and MAX_HOLD_DURATION (MAX_JUNK_COUNT items). Both client and server call it so the prompt ring and the server timing check always agree. ShredderResultCodes is a frozen enum used by both sides for unambiguous rejection reasons.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit thresholds are sensitive INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE, and PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN are the primary barriers against timing exploits and teleport-shredding. Increasing tolerances too far removes protection; tightening them too far breaks legit high-latency players.  Studio asset requirements:  Each workbench Model must be tagged "Workbench" with a PrimaryPart set.Each workbench should contain a child Model named "TrajectoryPoints" (tag it PlacementIgnore) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: "SpawnPoint" (at the shredder output mouth) and "LandingPoint" (floor landing target). If it is missing, the pool is still credited and the effect starts at the workbench pivot.In ReplicatedStorage, a Folder named "CraftingMaterials" should contain Tool templates named "Wood" and "Metal", each with a BasePart child named "Handle". Clients clone the Handle for the cosmetic arc; without it the effect skips straight to the 2D fly.  Nonce guard. The client uses a per-workbench nonce pair (holdNonce, armedNonce) to drop stale ReqShredderComplete calls when the player releases early or changes workbenches mid-hold. Modifying the hold flow must preserve this guard or the server's NO_SESSION rejection will fire spuriously.  Junk snapshot. The server snapshots junk at ReqShredderStart time. ReqShredderComplete re-filters that snapshot to tools still in the player's possession — it does not re-scan the Backpack. This prevents inflation from picking up new junk during the hold.  Wood/Metal only. Only Metal and Wood junk types are consumed and yield output: KNOWN_JUNK_TYPES on both sides lists just those two. Energy junk never becomes a Tool — it is credited to the Material Pool on grab.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Energy Recycler (PartyPerkBuffs.ShredEnergyPerJunk): each shredded junk also credits that much Energy in the same MaterialPool.Add.Overclock Core (PartyPerkBuffs.OverclockBonus): one server-wide counter counts each Wood/Metal junk processed at a workbench (player shred or drone) while the perk is live. Every ShopPerkConfig.OVERCLOCK_EVERYth junk yields ×(1 + bonus) (computeYield per junk).Salvage Drone delivery (Signals.DroneJunkDelivered(bench, type, tier) from JunkService): Wood/Metal is processed like one shredded junk (Overclock, Efficient Shredding, Energy Recycler); Energy credits its Yield × (1 + EnergyYieldBonus). The pool gain arcs from the bench TrajectoryPoints, and the bench animates.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant C as ShredderClient participant S as ShredderServer C->>C: PromptButtonHoldBegan - countJunks() > 0 C->>S: ReqShredderStart(bench) S->>S: validate tag, proximity, cooldown, junk count S->>S: ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration() S->>S: record session + StartTime S->>C: (isValid, duration, code) C->>C: prompt.HoldDuration = duration C->>C: PromptButtonHoldEnded -> nonce bump (cancels armed session) C->>C: Prompt.Triggered (hold complete), armedNonce check passes C->>S: ReqShredderComplete(bench) S->>S: re-validate session, workbench match, elapsed >= duration - TOLERANCE S->>S: re-verify junk still owned, computeYield(junks) S->>S: destroy junk Tools, record cooldown S->>S: MaterialPool.Add({Wood, Metal}, ArcPoints(bench)) Note over S: MaterialPoolUpdate to all clients<br/>(each plays arc + fly-to-HUD) S->>C: (success, woodCount, metalCount, code)

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SprintController.client.luau	Input binding, WalkSpeed/FOV prediction, intent signalling, sync consumption Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/StaminaManager.luau	Drain/regen simulation, buff application, sync dispatch Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SprintValidation.luau	Shared sprint gate conditions (humanoid state checks) Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau	Speed, FOV, drain/regen, validation thresholds, buff presets  Packets: StaminaSprintIntent, StaminaStateSync, StaminaBuffSync — see Networking MapSignals: OnStaminaValueChanged, OnStaminaBuffsChanged, OnSprintToggled, MobileSprintToggled, OnServerStaminaBuffStateChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Client prediction​
searchDocs.content: SprintController binds sprint to LeftShift and ButtonB (gamepad) via ContextActionService; a separate MobileSprintToggled signal handles the mobile toggle button. On each RenderStepped tick it calls canSprintNow() (wraps SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint) and calls setSprinting accordingly, which sets humanoid.WalkSpeed, tweens FieldOfView via TweenPlus, and fires Signals.OnSprintToggled. Sprint intent resets on CharacterRemoving and on WindowFocusReleased.  On StaminaStateSync the client clamps the received stamina, forces sprint off if the server says so, and fires Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged for the HUD. On StaminaBuffSync it forwards buff state to Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged for UI and icon updates.

searchDocs.title: Server authority​
searchDocs.content: StaminaManager maintains a StaminaRecord per player (Stamina, IsSprinting, SprintIntent, LastSprintTime, LastSyncTime). On the StaminaSprintIntent packet it immediately updates sprint state and calls syncPlayer. Its Heartbeat loop clamps dt to MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s to prevent large delta spikes, drains stamina at StaminaDrain * dt * UsageMultiplier while sprinting, and regenerates at StaminaRegen * dt * RegenMultiplier after RegenDelay seconds of not sprinting.  It syncs to the client when sprint state changes, stamina hits 0 (forced stop), stamina refills to max, or the periodic sync interval (STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s) elapses while stamina is changing. It consults StaminaBuffManager each tick for buff multipliers and resyncs immediately on Signals.OnServerStaminaBuffStateChanged. StaminaManager.RestoreStamina(player, amount) is available for pickup items but has no caller yet. StaminaManager.Initialize() must be called exactly once — it is called by StaminaSystemLoader.server.luau.

searchDocs.title: Shared validation gate​
searchDocs.content: SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint(humanoid, rules) returns false if health is 0, MoveDirection magnitude is below MinMoveDirection, the character is moving backward beyond MaxBackwardComponent, or horizontal speed is below MinHorizontalSpeed. It is called identically on the client (canSprintNow) and the server (canPlayerSprint) so the gate condition can never desync between the two sides.

searchDocs.title: Buffs​
searchDocs.content: Buff presets (StaminaRegenBuff, StaminaUsageBuff, InfiniteStaminaBuff) define strength and duration for collectible buffs; BuffIcons holds asset ids for the HUD. Buff state is authoritative on the server — StaminaBuffSync pushes the current multipliers to the client for display only, and the client never applies buffs directly to the drain/regen calculation.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Sprint logic must be mirrored on both sides SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint is the shared gate. If you add a new sprint-blocking condition (e.g. stun), add it to SprintValidation and verify it is called by both SprintController (client) and StaminaManager (server). A condition added only to one side will cause desyncs.  WalkSpeed is client-only. The server does not validate movement speed (see audit note S3 in SprintController's source); a cheating client can move at any speed. If movement integrity becomes necessary, add a server-side speed sanity check.STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s (10 Hz). The server only sends a sync when stamina is actively changing — if stamina is full and the player is standing still, no sync is sent, which is intentional.MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s clamp. The server caps the Heartbeat delta so a lag spike cannot drain or regen an unrealistic amount of stamina in one tick. Do not remove this clamp.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Quick Breath (StaminaRegenBonus): StaminaManager regen × (1 + bonus); server only (the client shows the synced value).Sprint Boots (MoveSpeedBonus): SprintController scales walk and sprint speed, and re-applies it on cannon dismount, respawn and buff change. There is no server speed cap.Free Runner (FreeSprint): StaminaManager skips sprint drain while the replicated workspace attribute PirateAttackActive is not true (set by PirateAttackEvent). The client needs no change: it shows the server's synced stamina.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as SprintController participant S as StaminaManager P->>C: Hold Shift / mobile toggle C->>S: Packets.StaminaSprintIntent(true) S->>S: record.SprintIntent = true loop Heartbeat (dt clamped to 0.1s) S->>S: drain or regen stamina by UsageMultiplier / RegenMultiplier end S->>C: Packets.StaminaStateSync(stamina, isSprinting) C->>C: currentStamina = stamina; force stop if !isSprinting C-->>C: Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged(stamina) -> HUD bar Note over C: RenderStepped, every frame C->>C: setSprinting(intent AND canSprintNow()) C->>C: humanoid.WalkSpeed, FOV tween C-->>C: Signals.OnSprintToggled(isSprinting) -> HUD S-->>C: Packets.StaminaBuffSync(infinite, regenMult, usageMult) C-->>C: Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged(...) -> HUD / buff icons

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/init.luau	Public facade (PlaySFX/PlaySFXAt/PlayLooped/PlayMusic/SetAmbience/SetVolume); the only module other scripts should require Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Groups.luau	Creates/manages the Master → SFX / BGM / Ambience SoundGroup hierarchy under SoundService Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Pool.luau	Per-asset pool of BasePart + Sound pairs used by PlaySFXAt Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/SFX.luau	Play (2D), PlayAt (positional pooled), PlayLooped, and the replication receiver Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Music.luau	Context playlist manager: shuffle, fade, gapped or continuous crossfade Client	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Ambience.luau	Global 2D ambience bed management with MotionMaster fade Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SoundController.client.luau	Thin bootstrap; calls SoundManager.Init() once Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/MusicDirector.client.luau	Resolves the active BGM context (Jump > Combat > Pursuit > LowFuel > Normal) and drives SoundManager.PlayMusic Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/MusicService.luau	Stateless API (SetContext) for gameplay code to switch a player's combat music context Server	src/ServerScriptService/ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau	Validated relay for positional sound replication: rate limit + allowlist Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau	Asset IDs, volumes, pitch, pool sizes, bus volumes, playlists, ambience beds  Packets: ReplicateSoundAtLocation, SetMusicContext — see Networking MapSignals: OnTrainStateChanged (consumed, from TrainClient — toggles LowFuel locally) — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Facade and playback​
searchDocs.content: SoundController.client.luau calls SoundManager.Init() once at startup. Init creates the SoundGroup bus hierarchy (Groups.Ensure), warms the positional sound pool (Pool.Ensure plus per-asset pre-warm), connects the replication receiver (SFX.ConnectReplication), and autostarts any ambience beds listed in SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart. Asset preloading happens earlier, in ReplicatedFirst/LoadingScreen.client.luau: it preloads every rbxassetid:// string in the Configs modules plus every Sound in the replicated services through PreloadLib.  After Init, any client script or tool may require(SharedModules.SoundManager) and call the facade (PlaySFX, PlaySFXAt, PlayLooped, PlayMusic, SetAmbience, SetVolume). The submodules (Groups, Pool, SFX, Music, Ambience) are internal and should not be required directly. The bus hierarchy is fixed:  SoundService └─ Master SoundGroup ├─ SFX SoundGroup ├─ BGM SoundGroup └─ Ambience SoundGroup

searchDocs.title: Positional replication​
searchDocs.content: The server does not play audio itself — ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau acts only as a validated relay for Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation:  Per-player rate limit (MIN_INTERVAL = 0.05s) rejects bursts.Payload shape is validated (data.SoundConfig.Id must be a string).The sound ID must be in ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS, built at startup from SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() — any SFX entry with Replicate = true is included automatically.The original payload is passed to every other connected player via FireClient.  The receiving client's SFX.ConnectReplication handler acquires a pooled part at the given position and plays it, the same path PlaySFXAt uses locally.

searchDocs.title: BGM contexts​
searchDocs.content: SoundConfig.Music.Playlists defines five named playlists — one per BGM context (Normal, Combat, LowFuel, Jump, Pursuit). There is no generic/default playlist; Music.Play falls back to "Normal" only when called with no argument.  Context	Trigger	Gap behaviorNormal	Default; nothing else active	Gapped — random silence between tracks Combat	Server calls MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat")	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence LowFuel	Automatic, client-derived from fuel level	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence Jump	Automatic, from Packets.JumpStateSync while JumpDriveConfig.IsJumpActive(phase)	Continuous; Shuffle = false Pursuit	Automatic: train stalled (Signals.OnTrainStateChanged), or the Threat Timer phase is Imminent/Arrived (Packets.ThreatStateSync)	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence  Priority when more than one condition is true: Jump > Combat > Pursuit > LowFuel > Normal. MusicDirector.client.luau holds five local inputs — jumpActive (from JumpStateSync), combatContext (set by the server), stalledActive and lowFuelActive (both derived locally from Signals.OnTrainStateChanged), and threatPhase (from ThreatStateSync) — and recomputes the resolved context on every change to any of them, calling SoundManager.PlayMusic(context) only when the resolved context actually changes. A low-fuel state during combat is suppressed without losing track position when combat ends.  Driving combat from server gameplay code (an event or outpost zone):  local MusicService = require(game.ServerStorage.SharedModules.MusicService) MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") -- on event/outpost enter MusicService.SetContext(player, "Normal") -- on event/outpost leave   MusicService.SetContext is stateless — it only fires Packets.SetMusicContext to the targeted player. Passing "Normal" clears the combat override; the client then falls back to LowFuel or Normal based on its own fuel state. Low fuel itself needs no gameplay code: MusicDirector watches Signals.OnTrainStateChanged and activates LowFuel whenever fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL drops below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct (default 0.25).

searchDocs.title: Volume persistence​
searchDocs.content: The four buses (Master, SFX, BGM, Ambience) persist across sessions as part of the generic Settings system, not inside SoundManager itself. SoundManager.SetVolume(group, volume) / GetVolume(group) remain the immediate-apply primitives — they read/write the Groups bus hierarchy directly and do nothing else.  UI code that needs the change saved calls SettingsClient.Set("MasterVolume" | "MusicVolume" | "SFXVolume" | "AmbienceVolume", value) instead. SettingsClient.Set validates via SettingsSchema, applies it (SettingsAppliers maps the key to a bus via SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey and calls Groups.SetVolume), fires Signals.OnSettingChanged(key, value), and schedules a debounced save (Packets.SaveSetting) that coalesces rapid changes (e.g. a slider drag) into one trailing send. On join, SettingsManager delivers the saved settings map via Packets.SyncSettings; SettingsClient applies each entry the same way but never re-saves a synced value, so no feedback loop results. See Settings for the full validate/apply/persist flow.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never create ad-hoc Sound instances All Sound creation must go through SoundManager. Creating Sound instances by hand bypasses the bus groups (volume controls have no effect), skips the positional pool (memory churn), and may leak sounds that persist across character reloads.  SoundManager.Init() must be called before any Play* call. It is called once by SoundController.client.luau; do not call it again elsewhere.PlaySFXAt parents a pooled BasePart at the given Vector3 in the workspace; the pool releases it after sound.TimeLength + 0.05 seconds. Do not hold references to the part or sound after the call.PlayLooped returns a LoopHandle. The caller must call handle:Stop() or handle:Destroy() when done — an abandoned handle leaks a live Sound under SoundService.A sound entry with Replicate = true and an empty Id ("") is excluded from the allowlist automatically by GetReplicatedIds(); the pool warm step also skips empty IDs.The BGM and Ambience buses default below 1.0. An SFX entry authored at Volume = 0.5 will be audibly louder than music at the same numeric volume because the bus multipliers differ.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant ClientA as Playing client participant Relay as ReplicatedSoundService (server) participant ClientB as Other clients participant MusicSvc as MusicService (server) participant Director as MusicDirector (owning client) Note over ClientA,ClientB: POSITIONAL SFX REPLICATION ClientA->>ClientA: SoundManager.PlaySFXAt(name, position) — local pooled playback ClientA->>Relay: ReplicateSoundAtLocation(location, soundConfig) Relay->>Relay: rate-limit (MIN_INTERVAL) + payload + ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS check Relay->>ClientB: FireClient to all other players ClientB->>ClientB: SFX.ConnectReplication — Pool.Acquire(position) positional playback Note over MusicSvc,Director: BGM CONTEXT SWITCH MusicSvc->>Director: SetMusicContext(context) (e.g. "Combat") Director->>Director: resolve priority Jump > Combat > Pursuit > LowFuel > Normal alt resolved context changed Director->>Director: SoundManager.PlayMusic(context) — crossfade or gap per playlist end Note over Director: Signals.OnTrainStateChanged (fuel) toggles LowFuel locally — no server round-trip

searchDocs.content: Config module: SoundConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luauPlaybook: Add a Sound  Bus volumes (SoundConfig.GroupVolumes):  Bus	DefaultMaster	1.0 SFX	1.0 BGM	0.6 Ambience	0.5  Per-SFX definition fields (SoundConfig.Sfx):  Field	DescriptionId	Roblox asset ID string; empty string disables the entry Volume	Default playback volume (0–1) Pitch	Fixed pitch multiplier PitchRange	Two-element array {min, max}; randomizes pitch per play Group	Bus name ("SFX", "BGM", "Ambience"); defaults to "SFX" Replicate	true to include the entry in the server relay allowlist Debounce	Minimum seconds between plays of this entry (anti-spam) PoolInitial	Pre-allocated pool slots warmed at Init (positional only) PoolMax	Hard cap on the per-asset pool size (positional only)  Adding a new replicable SFX needs only Replicate = true on the SoundConfig.Sfx entry — GetReplicatedIds() and ReplicatedSoundService pick it up automatically on next server start. searchDocs.title: Phases​
searchDocs.content: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Counting Counting --> Imminent: remaining reaches 0 Imminent --> Arrived: SPAWN_DELAY elapsed (OnThreatArrived fires) Counting --> Counting: jump arrival (reset to ARRIVAL_SECONDS) Imminent --> Counting: jump arrival Arrived --> Counting: jump arrival   Phase	MeaningCounting	The countdown runs from ARRIVAL_SECONDS (900 s) Imminent	The countdown hit 0. The omen toast shows, and SPAWN_DELAY (30 s) runs in real time Arrived	Signals.OnThreatArrived fired once. Holds until the next jump arrival

searchDocs.title: Speed​
searchDocs.content: The countdown speed is a pure function of the current state (speedFor):  Condition (first match wins)	SpeedTrain not started yet, a jump is active, game over, or phase Arrived	0 (paused) Phase Imminent	1 Train stalled (OnTrainFuelStateChanged stalled = true)	STALLED_SPEED (4) × Bait Buoy Otherwise	1 × Bait Buoy  Imminent ignores fuel on purpose: the 30 s is the party's last warning, and refuelling during it neither shortens nor lengthens it. An Emergency Generator coast does not speed up the countdown — the signal reports a coast as empty = true, stalled = false, and the timer reads only stalled. The client shows a "running on fumes" toast instead (see Client).  Bait Buoy (party shop perk, PartyPerkBuffs.ThreatSlowdown 0.10): the Counting speed is PerkBuffRead.Reduce(speed, ThreatSlowdown) (× 0.9, never below 10%). Imminent stays real time. A change of the attribute calls commit, so remaining is snapshot under the old speed. Clients read the replicated speed from ThreatStateSync, so the clocks need no change.  Braking does not pause the countdown. A braked train burns no fuel (Train Fuel); the Leviathan clock is the cost of waiting.

searchDocs.title: Algebraic model​
searchDocs.content: Like TrainFuelManager, there is no per-frame loop. Every input (train start, fuel state, jump phase, game over) calls commit(), which:  snapshots remaining -= speed * (now - lastEventTime) under the old speed,picks the new speed with speedFor,bumps a nonce and, if the speed is above 0, schedules task.delay(remaining / speed) to advance the phase — a stale callback whose nonce no longer matches does nothing,broadcasts ThreatStateSync(phase, remaining, speed, serverTime).  Entering a new phase (enterPhase) moves lastEventTime to now before committing, so the new phase's budget is not reduced by time spent in the old one. Time lost while stalled stays lost: refuelling only returns the speed to 1.  Clients compute the live countdown as max(0, remaining - speed * (GetServerTimeNow() - serverTime)), the same extrapolation TrainStateSync uses.

searchDocs.title: Jump reset​
searchDocs.content: OnJumpPhaseChanged pauses the countdown while JumpDriveConfig.IsJumpActive(phase) is true. On the arrival edge (active → inactive) it resets to a full Counting, whatever the phase was. If the train is still stalled on arrival, the new cycle starts at STALLED_SPEED.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: TrainClient shows two fuel toasts from TrainStateSync edges: FUMES_MESSAGE (warn) when coastEndsAt goes from 0 to a value above 0, and FUEL_OUT_MESSAGE (alert) when isStalled goes from false to true. They follow the stall flag, not the countdown speed, so the fuel-out toast also shows during Imminent.ThreatController shows OMEN_MESSAGE (alert) once when the phase becomes Imminent.MusicDirector plays Pursuit while the train is stalled or the phase is past Counting (priority Jump > Combat > Pursuit > LowFuel > Normal). The Pursuit playlist has no tracks until asset ids are added to SoundConfig.  A player who joins while one of these states is already active gets that toast once, from the join snapshot. This is intentional: they need to know.

searchDocs.title: Seams​
searchDocs.content: Leviathan boss. Signals.OnThreatArrived is where the future boss spec spawns the boss. The boss must leave on the OnJumpPhaseChanged arrival edge, matching the reset above. It hits the train with TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(amount, ThreatConfig.BOSS_DAMAGE_SOURCE); see Train Shield — Hull.Game-over cutscene. Reads the TrainGameOverReason from Signals.OnTrainGameOver.

searchDocs.title: Config surface​
searchDocs.content: ThreatConfig timer fields: ARRIVAL_SECONDS (900), STALLED_SPEED (4), SPAWN_DELAY (30), Phase. Toasts: NOTIF_TYPE, FUMES_NOTIF_TYPE, NOTIF_DURATION, FUMES_MESSAGE, FUEL_OUT_MESSAGE, OMEN_MESSAGE. Hull fields are documented under Train Shield — Hull.

searchDocs.title: Algebraic fuel model​
searchDocs.content: getFuel() is computed as fuelAtLastEvent - currentRate * elapsed rather than ticked every frame. commitEvent snapshots fuel under the old rate before switching to the new one, so every transition (brake, refuel, stall) is seamless. A scheduleNonce guards task.delay callbacks: any subsequent commitEvent increments the nonce, and a stale callback no-ops if its captured nonce no longer matches. Do not call reschedule directly — always go through commitEvent.  While hasStarted = false (before the first brake release), the drain rate is forced to 0 and no task.delay stall timer is scheduled — fuel is frozen pre-game.

searchDocs.title: Brake toggle​
searchDocs.content: Triggering a TrainBrakeLever-tagged prompt sends ReqToggleBrake(lever). The server flips isBraked; on the first-ever un-brake it also sets hasStarted = true and fires Signals.SetTrainStarted(true). Either way it calls commitEvent(), which reschedules the stall task.delay under the new rate and broadcasts TrainStateSync. The client updates the lever's ActionText ("Stop Train" / "Resume Train") from the returned isBraked. A braked train has rate 0, so no stall is scheduled (the same path as the pre-start and jump freezes).

searchDocs.title: Lever animation​
searchDocs.content: Purely cosmetic and entirely client-side — the server never knows the lever's physical pose. TrainClient swings the pivot by BRAKE_LEVER_SWING_DEG about the pivot's own Z axis between the two brake states, using MotionMaster (never TweenService), and plays BRAKE_LEVER_ANIM_ID once on the model's Animator as a button-press flourish plus the TrainBrakeLever SFX.  Which end means "braked" is a property of how the model was posed, not of the brake logic, so it lives in config: BRAKE_LEVER_REST_IS_BRAKED says whether the authored pose is the braked one. If the lever reads backwards in-game, flip that boolean — don't negate BRAKE_LEVER_SWING_DEG, which only changes which way it rotates.  Three rules keep it honest:  Only a flip animates. TrainStateSync also arrives on refuel and stall events, so the handler compares isBraked against the previous value — otherwise the lever would re-swing every time someone tops up the tank.Joining snaps. The first snapshot after joining, and any lever that registers late (tag added at runtime, streaming), poses instantly with no swing.Reversal is continuous. The in-flight tween lives in the lever's Janitor under the "leverTween" index; adding a new one there destroys the old, which pauses it in place rather than resetting it, so a mid-swing toggle starts from wherever the lever actually is.  Every client animates from the same replicated isBraked, so no extra network traffic is needed to keep the levers agreeing.

searchDocs.title: Refuel​
searchDocs.content: Triggering a TrainEngine-tagged prompt sends ReqRefuelTrain(engine). The server validates the tag, proximity, and that the tank isn't already full, spends pool Energy via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", maxFuel − fuel, FUEL_PER_POINT) (only the points needed; 0 spent → NO_ENERGY), clears a stall if fuel becomes > 0, then calls commitEvent(newFuel). A boolean isRefueling mutex serializes concurrent requests — it is not a queue, so a second request while one is in flight returns NO_ENERGY even if the pool has Energy; the player can retry immediately after.  The engine is the PowerCore model, which is also the Jump Drive bench (it carries both tags). Its refuel prompt has a 1.5 s HoldDuration so the refuel animation has time to read.  Refuel animation​  Cosmetic, and every player sees it. Roblox replicates ProximityPrompt.PromptButtonHoldBegan/Ended to the server, but it runs no distance check on them, so TrainFuelManager validates each hold (proximity, pool Energy > 0, fuel < max). Then it writes the holder's UserId to the engine attribute TrainConfig.REFUEL_ATTR ("RefuelingBy", 0 = nobody). A watchdog drops a hold after HoldDuration + REFUEL_HOLD_GRACE if its end event never arrives. PlayerRemoving also drops it. With two holders, the attribute shows one of them until both release. No packet is involved: the attribute replicates, and late joiners see it at once.  TrainRefuelFxController animates off the attribute. While it is non-zero, the controller sends an Energy_Tier1 clone from the holder's chest to ChuteAttachment every REFUEL_FX.CellInterval (MotionMaster.SplineMove + shrink). The model does a squash-and-stretch about its bottom center: it stretches up, leans left, leans right, and settles. Each lean hinges on a bottom edge, so the base stays grounded. When the bounce blends out, every part is written back to its exact rest CFrame/Size from a snapshot, so drift cannot accumulate. Tuning is in TrainConfig.REFUEL_FX. The attribute never gates the refuel itself.

searchDocs.title: Fuel out​
searchDocs.content: Running out of fuel no longer ends the round. A stall lasts until fuel is added: the drain rate is 0, the brake cannot be toggled, and nothing is scheduled. While the train is stalled, the Threat Timer runs at ThreatConfig.STALLED_SPEED, so the Leviathan arrives sooner. Round endings now come from the train hull (see Train Shield — Hull).  Every commitEvent compares two flags against the last values it sent — empty (fuelAtLastEvent <= 0) and isStalled — and fires Signals.OnTrainFuelStateChanged(empty, stalled) when either flips. Fuel can only reach 0 at a commit (onEmpty, onStall, ApplyFuelDamage), so the edge is exact. An Emergency Generator coast is empty = true, stalled = false: the hull counts hits, but the threat timer does not speed up. ThreatTimerManager reads stalled; TrainShieldManager reads empty.  TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount: number, source: any?): boolean is the combat fuel-damage sink. amount is fuel units already converted by TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR — the only caller today is TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage, once the shield is at 0. It returns true when fuel absorbed the hit and false when fuel was already 0 (stalled or coasting), in which case the caller counts a hull hit. Before the round is live, during a jump, after game over, or for an amount that is not > 0 (or is NaN), it is a no-op that returns true. A hit that leaves fuel above 0 commits the lower level. A hit that drives fuel to 0 sets isStalled before commitEvent(0), so the train stalls at once — there is no Emergency Generator coast on this path, and the round does not end.  TrainFuelManager.AddFuel(amount: number) is the perk fuel source (Fuel Line, from JunkService on each Energy grab). It caps at max fuel, clears a stall or a coast like a refuel (any gain), and is a no-op after game over, on a full tank, or for an amount that is not a positive finite number.

searchDocs.title: Client HUD prediction​
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelGuiController reads the authored StarterGui.TrainFuelGui (never creates UI). It holds no snapshot of its own — every RenderStepped frame it asks TrainStateCache.PredictedFuel() for the extrapolated fuel level (fuel - rate * (now - serverTime), clamped to [0, maxFuel]) and smooths displayedFuel toward it with frame-rate-independent exponential smoothing (k = 8). It sets FuelBar.Size (fuel ÷ the snapshot's maxFuel) and FuelText.Text, and colors the bar green (running) / amber (braked) / red (stalled) from the cached snapshot's isBraked/isStalled. While an Emergency Generator coast runs, the text is COAST 23s (counts down to coastEndsAt) and the bar is orange.  Before the server has sent a snapshot, PredictedFuel() returns nil — the controller never invents a starting value (it used to seed one from TrainConfig.INITIAL_FUEL/MAX_FUEL plus a client-read workspace:GetServerTimeNow(), which is what produced the reported 0% flash; see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake). While nil, the HUD renders a placeholder ("—", a neutral grey, zero-width bar) instead. The first non-nil value is applied directly rather than eased into, so there is no visible sweep from a guessed number.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Each TrainEngine-tagged and TrainBrakeLever-tagged root (a Model or BasePart) must contain a BasePart named TrainConfig.PROMPT_PART_NAME ("ProxPromptPart") with a child ProximityPrompt. Both client and server resolve the prompt part recursively via PromptResolver, so it may be nested at any depth. The prompt's MaxActivationDistance and the engine's ActionText are authored in Studio; only the lever's ActionText is set by script.  The engine model (PowerCore) also needs ModelStreamingMode = Atomic (Workspace streams, and the refuel animation snapshots every part on stream-in) and an Attachment named TrainConfig.CHUTE_ATTACHMENT_NAME ("ChuteAttachment") at any depth, where the Energy cells fly to. Without the attachment, refuel still works and the animation is skipped with a warning.  A brake lever model additionally needs, for the animation:  A PrimaryPart acting as the pivot, anchored, with all moving geometry WeldConstrainted (or Motor6Ded) to it. An assembly containing an anchored part is rigid, so writing PrimaryPart.CFrame carries the whole lever on every client with no physics ownership involved. Without a PrimaryPart the prompt still works and the animation is skipped with a warning.The lever saved in a known pose, with TrainConfig.BRAKE_LEVER_REST_IS_BRAKED set to say which state that pose represents. The current rig follows the usual convention — lever pulled toward the player means braked — and is authored that way, hence BRAKE_LEVER_REST_IS_BRAKED = true.Optionally an AnimationController/Animator for the button press. No Animator simply means no press flourish.  Do not leave a Script inside the model driving the lever itself — the pose is owned by TrainClient and a second writer will fight it.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: A stall never ends the round on its own There is no grace timer any more. A stalled train only speeds up the Threat Timer; the round ends through the hull in TrainShieldManager, whose TrainGameOver.Trigger is still a placeholder (log + Signals.OnTrainGameOver, no cutscene or round reset yet).  Algebraic drift note: commitEvent captures now() once and uses it for both lastEventTime and the serverTime field broadcast in TrainStateSync. Any task.wait or async work inserted between the snapshot and the broadcast would drift the client's extrapolation baseline — keep commitEvent synchronous.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Spare Tank (PartyPerkBuffs.MaxFuelBonus, 20): max fuel = MAX_FUEL + MaxFuelBonus. maxFuel() replaces every MAX_FUEL read in the manager and travels in TrainStateSync, so the HUD and music use the real cap. A change of the attribute commits (clamps fuel when the perk ends); it is skipped while stalled (fuel is 0, so there is nothing to re-clamp).Emergency Generator (permanent party perk, LastGaspSeconds 15/level): when drain empties the tank, onEmpty starts a coast instead of a stall: coastEndsAt = now + LastGaspSeconds, rate 0, fuel 0, and the train still counts as running (junk keeps moving). reschedule arms the coast end → onStall. Any fuel gain ends the coast (commitEvent clears coastEndsAt when fuel > 0 or stalled). Fuel damage to 0 skips the coast and stalls at once. A coast does not speed up the Threat Timer; the client shows a "running on fumes" toast. The coast clock does not pause for a jump.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Sv as TrainFuelManager participant Cl as TrainClient participant Cache as TrainStateCache participant Gui as TrainFuelGuiController Note over Sv,Cl: JOIN - via JoinSync on ClientReady, not PlayerAdded Sv->>Cl: TrainStateSync(fuel, rate, isBraked, isStalled, serverTime, maxFuel, coastEndsAt) Cl->>Cache: SetFuel(snapshot) Cl->>Cl: Signals.OnTrainStateChanged(snap) - MusicDirector, lever ActionText Note over Cl,Sv: BRAKE TOGGLE Cl->>Sv: ReqToggleBrake(lever) Sv->>Sv: validate lever tag + proximity, flip isBraked (first un-brake: hasStarted=true) Sv->>Sv: commitEvent() - snapshot fuel, switch rate, scheduleNonce++, reschedule() Sv-->>Cl: (success, isBraked, code) Sv->>Cl: TrainStateSync(...) Note over Cl,Sv: REFUEL Cl->>Sv: ReqRefuelTrain(engine) Sv->>Sv: validate proximity + not full, spend pool Energy (SpendUpTo) Sv->>Sv: commitEvent(newFuel) Sv-->>Cl: (success, fuelAdded, code) Note over Sv: NATURAL STALL Sv->>Sv: task.delay(timeToEmpty) fires -> onStall(): isStalled=true, commitEvent(0) Sv->>Sv: commitEvent fires OnTrainFuelStateChanged(empty, stalled) - ThreatTimerManager speeds up Note over Sv: COMBAT FUEL HIT Sv->>Sv: TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage while shield==0 -> ApplyFuelDamage(amount*FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR) Sv->>Sv: newFuel<=0: isStalled=true, commitEvent(0) - returns true (absorbed) Sv->>Sv: fuel already 0: returns false - TrainShieldManager counts a hull hit Note over Gui: CLIENT HUD LOOP (RenderStepped) Gui->>Cache: PredictedFuel() - nil until first snapshot -> render placeholder Gui->>Gui: predicted = snap.fuel - snap.rate*(now-snap.serverTime); smooth k=8 Gui->>Gui: FuelBar.Size + color (green/amber/red)
