searchDocs.title: How it works​
searchDocs.content: Order: at boot the server numbers every Model under Workspace.TrainPlatforms: FrontPlatform (FRONT_PLATFORM_NAME) is 1, the rest by distance from it. It writes the number to a PlatformIndex attribute. No Studio setup is needed; adding or removing a platform Model in Studio changes the count (add a Costs entry for each new locked index).Starting count: STARTING_PLATFORMS platforms start built. The server raises any value below 2 to 2 (with a warn); a value above the platform count means all start built.Boot: platforms above the starting count move to ServerStorage/LockedPlatforms. A copy with every CollectionService tag removed goes to ReplicatedStorage/PlatformGhosts/<index> (tags must go: GetTagged also returns ReplicatedStorage instances, so a tagged copy would count as a BuildArea). Each locked platform gets Seam and SeamAxis attributes.State: attributes on TrainPlatforms — BuiltCount, DepositedWood, DepositedMetal (progress of platform BuiltCount + 1). Attributes replicate to late joiners, so there is no JoinSync sender.Deposit: the handler moves min(cost − deposited, pool) of each material via MaterialPool.Spend, with no yield between reading and writing. A second request in the same frame sees the new totals; a request for an already-finished platform returns STALE. Material is never spent past the cost.Build: when both materials are full, the locked platform is parented back into TrainPlatforms. Placement and drop code find its BuildArea / DroppableSurface tags at run time — no placement change.Client: the ghost and billboard show only while the prompt is shown (PromptShown / PromptHidden). The prompt is disabled in build mode, where F toggles grid mode.Reveal: on ChildAdded of a platform not present at load, the client hides the real platform (LocalTransparencyModifier) in the same callback, extrudes a visual copy behind a neon wall (SWEEP_DURATION), then shows the real one. Collision is live the whole time.  sequenceDiagram participant P as PlatformExtendController participant S as PlatformExtendService participant MP as MaterialPool participant TP as TrainPlatforms (attributes) P->>S: ReqPlatformDeposit(index) S->>MP: Spend({ Wood, Metal }) S->>TP: DepositedWood / DepositedMetal alt both full S->>TP: parent platform, BuiltCount += 1 TP-->>P: ChildAdded → hide, sweep, show end S-->>P: (code, woodAdded, metalAdded)

searchDocs.title: Dev command​
searchDocs.content: /expand (alias /platform) in chat builds the next platform at once, free, and plays the normal reveal. It sends ReqDevExpandPlatform; DevCommandsService gates it on place owner / group rank 250+ and calls PlatformExtendService.DevBuildNext(). Any Wood/Metal already deposited toward that platform is cleared (it was spent from the pool).  Fallback reveal If the scan sweep is rejected after playtesting, replace only the body of playReveal with a dust-cloud burst that shows the platform while it is hidden.

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: All values are in PlatformConfig: STARTING_PLATFORMS (minimum 2), Costs (3 → W50/M30, 4 → W90/M55, 5 → W155/M90, 6 → W270/M160; ×1.75 per platform), HOLD_DURATION, PROMPT_DISTANCE, SERVER_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, DEPOSIT_COOLDOWN, ghost colour/transparency, and SWEEP_*. Sound ids: SoundConfig keys PlatformDeposit, PlatformBuilt.  Perks: BuildCostReduction (Thrifty Builder, Party) — each platform cost goes through PerkBuffRead.ReduceCost (×max(0.1, 1−b), rounded up) in both PlatformExtendService (charged) and PlatformExtendController (shown). See Perks.

searchDocs.title: Not included​
searchDocs.content: No persistence (platforms reset with the server, like the pool), no out-of-order building, no refunds or demolition.

searchDocs.title: Client: controller and handlers​
searchDocs.content: WeaponController.client.luau is the bootstrap that watches the local character for Tool equip/unequip events. It looks up WeaponConfig[tool.Name].Category and dispatches to the matching category handler (GunHandler or ThrowableHandler). It creates one Janitor per equipped Tool (and one per character) so all connections clean up correctly on unequip, death, or weapon switch. It fires Signals.WeaponEquipped/Signals.WeaponUnequipped for the HUD, and Signals.RequestShootingCamera on equip/unequip to toggle the aim camera mode. It binds R to OnReload and G to OnDetonate for handlers that declare those callbacks.  GunHandler — hitscan + rocket cosmetic + ammo prediction. On activate, it gates on a client-local fire-rate check and predicted magazine count (via AmmoApi), then fires ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir, renderTime). It draws the shooter's own tracer (hitscan only; rocket has no local projectile) and supports semi and automatic fire. OnReload fires ReqReloadWeapon and predicts the ammo transition after the server-confirmed reload window. Authoritative ammo is reconciled via WeaponMagSync → Signals.WeaponMagChanged and AmmoPoolSync → Signals.AmmoPoolChanged.  ThrowableHandler — grenade and C4. On activate, it gates on the throw cooldown, plays throw sound, and fires ReqThrowProjectile(origin, dir). There is no local projectile cosmetic — the server-spawned instance replicates to all clients. For C4 (Detonation == "Manual"), OnDetonate fires ReqDetonate. Grenade ignores G.  TrajectoryPreview — a client-local green-neon ballistic arc shown while any throwable is equipped, using a fixed pool of reused BasePart segments updated every RenderStepped. Origin offset (SPAWN_OFFSET = 2.5) and upward aim bias match ServerProjectile/ThrowableHandler exactly so the preview arc matches the real projectile path. Purely cosmetic — no packets sent.  WeaponEffectsController — consumes replicated combat FX packets. WeaponFired is ignored for the local shooter (who already drew its own tracer) and renders tracer + impact spark for other players' shots. ExplosionAt renders an expanding neon sphere + sound for rocket, grenade, and C4 detonations, for everyone including the shooter.

searchDocs.title: Shared validation (WeaponValidation)​
searchDocs.content: Pure math run on both client (prediction) and server (authority):  canFire(lastFireTime, cooldown, now) — fire-rate gate.resolveHumanoidModel(part) — resolves a hit part to its Humanoid-bearing Model.applySpread(direction, spreadDegrees) — applies a random spread cone to an aim direction (cosmetic on client; server does its own authoritative ray).isWithinRange(origin, hitPos, maxDistance) — range cap check.ammoAfterShot(mag) / ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magazineSize) — pure ammo transitions. ammoReloadFromPool returns (newMag, taken) where taken is the pool amount consumed.aoeFalloff(center, hitPos, radius, maxDamage) — linear AOE falloff.queryAOEModels(center, radius, ignore) — sphere overlap returning { model, humanoid, distance } for AOE application.

searchDocs.title: Server: packet handling​
searchDocs.content: WeaponServer.server.luau receives all weapon packets and runs per-category validation (fire-rate, ammo, origin tolerance, direction validity) before any damage or projectile spawn. It manages gun ammo initialisation on equip via WeaponState.EnsureAmmo + WeaponMagSync. On reload, it waits ReloadTime, calls ammoReloadFromPool, consumes the drawn ammo from AmmoManager, then fires WeaponMagSync + AmmoPoolSync (the latter emitted by AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo). On a successful throwable throw, the server destroys the player's matching Tool (onThrowProjectile — 1 Tool = 1 throw). It drives the FastCast2 rocket caster (rocketServerCaster) — its LengthChanged callback steps the cosmetic part, its Hit callback calls CombatService.ApplyAOE and broadcasts ExplosionAt. It also handles throwable throw (onThrowProjectile) and detonate (onDetonate).

searchDocs.title: Lag compensation​
searchDocs.content: Hitscan hits on NPCs are rewound to what the shooter saw. The client sends Chrono.EnemyRenderTime() with ReqFireWeapon; the server clamps it with LagCompensation.ResolveRewindTime (in the past, at most min(1, ping×2 + 0.6) s; bad values → no rewind, the request is never dropped) and runs LagCompensation.Raycast. Each live NPC's snapshot at that time gives delta = current * past:Inverse(); the ray is shifted by delta and tested against that NPC alone, while world geometry and dead NPCs are tested unrewound. The shooter's own position is never rewound. Rockets and throwables have travel time and are not compensated. See Chrono Replication.

searchDocs.title: Server: damage routing (CombatService)​
searchDocs.content: CombatService is the single damage router with two primary entry points:  ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — applies damage to a resolved Model. Players route through HealthManager.ApplyDamage (keeping the HUD-tracked record correct — see Health); faction-tagged NPCs ("EnemyNPC"/"FriendlyNPC") take direct humanoid:TakeDamage. Anything without a recognized faction is ignored. Friendly-fire is enforced via Factions.canDamage: only Player↔Enemy damage lands; players never hurt players or friendly NPCs. A nil attacker is treated as environmental and bypasses the faction gate. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt.ApplyAOE(center, radius, maxDamage, attackType, attacker, ignore) — calls queryAOEModels, applies aoeFalloff to each target, and routes through ApplyToModel with aoeVariant = "Explosion".  Also available: ApplyToPart(part, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — resolves a hit part to its Humanoid-bearing Model then calls ApplyToModel. EnemyWeapon calls the same entry points for enemy fire — see Enemy Combat.  ApplyToModel and ApplyToPart return (routed: boolean, dealt: number): dealt is the NPC health actually removed (an overkill hit counts only what was left; 0 for a player target or a miss). Vampire Rounds lifesteal runs here on dealt, so every player weapon gets it — see Combat perks.

searchDocs.title: Combat perks (Perk Rework part 5)​
searchDocs.content: Vampire Rounds (Lifesteal 0.03, shop): after a player's hit removes NPC health, CombatService heals the attacker by dealt × Lifesteal through HealthManager.HealPlayer, capped at ShopPerkConfig.LIFESTEAL_MAX_PER_SECOND (2 HP/s, 100-HP scale) by a per-player bucket (CombatPerkMath.lifestealTake). Any weapon counts: guns, explosives, cannons.Weak Spot (WeakSpotBonus 0.15, shop): when the owner's hitscan bullet removes enemy health and the enemy survives (a killing hit does not mark, so no glow stays on the body), WeaponServer calls CombatService.Mark(model, WEAK_SPOT_SECONDS, bonus) and fires EnemyMarked. ApplyToModel multiplies any player damage to a marked enemy by 1 + bonus (guns, AOE, cannons — the whole party; enemy fire and the environment do not get it). A re-hit refreshes the mark; it never stacks. Clients show a red AlwaysOnTop Highlight (WeaponEffectsController).Finishing Touch (FinisherBonus 0.25, shop): at the hitscan hit site, CombatPerkMath.finisherExtra passes the bonus as scaledDamage's extra when the enemy is below ShopPerkConfig.FINISHER_HEALTH_FRACTION (25%) of its max health. Guns only; rockets, throwables and cannons do not get it.Ricochet (RicochetChance 5%/level, permanent): after a hitscan hit removes enemy health, a server roll bounces PerkConfig.RICOCHET_DAMAGE_FRACTION (35%) of the shot's full damage (before overkill, so a kill shot bounces as hard as any hit) to the nearest other live EnemyNPC within RICOCHET_RADIUS (12 studs) that the hit point can see. It runs once per hit and never for the bounce, so it cannot chain. The tracer is a WeaponFired with the first enemy as shooter, so every client (the shooter too) draws it. Rockets and throwables never ricochet.Last Stand (LastStandBonus 0.20, shop): scaledDamage adds the bonus while the attacker's HealthManager.GetHealth / GetMaxHealth is below ShopPerkConfig.LAST_STAND_HEALTH_FRACTION (0.25). Every weapon that uses scaledDamage gets it, explosives too.Rally Banner (RallyDamageBonus 0.05 + RallyRegenBonus 0.20, party): PerkBuffRead.Rally(player, key, RALLY_RADIUS) returns the party value while another live player is within ShopPerkConfig.RALLY_RADIUS (20 studs), else 0. scaledDamage adds the damage part; HealthManager regen adds the regen part. No tick or flag: each reader checks distance when it asks. RallyAuraController (client) checks the same rule once a second and fades a thin gold CylinderHandleAdornment ring in at the local character's feet.

searchDocs.title: Server: per-player state (WeaponState)​
searchDocs.content: Per-player authoritative state. Fields per player record:  lastFire: { [weaponName]: number } — os.clock() of last shot/throw per weapon; gates fire-rate.ammo: { [weaponName]: { mag, reloadEndsAt } } — magazine count and reload window (reloadEndsAt is the os.clock() timestamp when a reload finishes; 0 means not reloading). Reserve is no longer stored here — pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager.active: { ActiveCharge } — active manual throwables (C4) awaiting detonation.  Key functions: EnsureAmmo (seeds magazine from config), GetMag/SetMag, GetLastFire/SetLastFire, IsReloading, SetReloadEnd, GetActiveCount, AddActive, TakeAllActive. Clear destroys all active charges and removes the player's record on PlayerRemoving.

searchDocs.title: Server: projectiles (ServerProjectile)​
searchDocs.content: Spawns and owns server-authoritative, replicated projectile instances cloned from ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets into workspace/ServerProjectiles. Two spawn paths:  spawnRocket(templateName, cframe) — anchored, non-collidable cosmetic part; the caller (WeaponServer) steps its CFrame along the FastCast2 cast.spawnThrowable(templateName, origin, direction, speed, rest, ignore) — server-owned physics rigid body. prepareAssembly un-anchors all parts, sets the WeaponProjectile collision group (passes through characters), and applies per-mode elasticity: "Stick" (C4) elasticity = 0 (lands dead); "Bounce" (Grenade) elasticity = 0.15 (one small hop). installSettle polls until the charge has contacted a world surface and come to rest, then anchors it flat. Network ownership is kept server-side via root:SetNetworkOwner(nil).

searchDocs.title: HUD integration contract​
searchDocs.content: This system ships no UI. A HUD widget that wants to display ammo or combat feedback must consume:  Packets (server → owning client, handled by AmmoApi): WeaponMagSync(weaponName, mag) — authoritative magazine count sent on equip, after each shot, and after reload completion.AmmoPoolSync(ammoType, amount) — authoritative pool count for a given ammo type sent whenever the pool changes (shot, reload, craft). AmmoApi read surface (preferred over raw packets): AmmoApi.GetMag(weaponName) → (mag, magSize) — current magazine and max size.AmmoApi.GetPool(ammoType) → (amount, capacity) — current pool and capacity cap.AmmoApi.GetEquippedAmmo() → (mag, magSize, pool, cap)? — combined ammo for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns.AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount(toolName) → count — counts matching Tools in the Backpack + equipped slot. Signals (client-side): WeaponEquipped(toolName, category) — fired on equip.WeaponUnequipped(toolName) — fired on unequip.WeaponMagChanged(weaponName, mag) — fired by AmmoApi on predicted mag update and on WeaponMagSync reconciliation.AmmoPoolChanged(ammoType, amount) — fired by AmmoApi on AmmoPoolSync or local prediction.ThrowableCountChanged(toolName, count) — fired by AmmoApi when the backpack throwable count changes.WeaponReloadStarted(weaponName, reloadTime) — fired when a reload request is sent.WeaponReloadComplete(weaponName) — fired when the reload window elapses or reload is rejected.WeaponLocalHit(model) — fired on a predicted hitscan hit for hitmarker display.  Ammo HUD. AmmoHudController (client) drives the authored AmmoGui (bottom-right ScreenGui). The count is split across two labels either side of a divider — MainContainer.AmmoCount and MainContainer.ReserveAmmoCount — laid out horizontally by a UIListLayout. For guns that is the loaded magazine beside the reserve pool; for throwables the carried count goes in AmmoCount and ReserveAmmoCount shows an em-dash, so the widget keeps its shape across weapon swaps. The GUI has no weapon-name label, so the equipped weapon's DisplayName is not shown. It is hidden when nothing is equipped. All data comes from AmmoApi + the weapon/ammo Signals; the HUD never talks to the server.  The label names are load-bearing AmmoHudController resolves AmmoCount and ReserveAmmoCount by name with an untimed WaitForChild. Renaming either in Studio stalls the controller at load (Roblox's "Infinite yield possible" warning names the missing instance). Divider is layout-only and is never touched by code.

searchDocs.title: Ammo economy​
searchDocs.content: Pool and magazine model​  Ammo is split into two distinct layers:  Magazine (WeaponState, server) — per-gun in-memory count representing what is currently loaded. The magazine is seeded to MagazineSize rounds on the gun's first equip (EnsureAmmo) and then persists across deaths within the session (it is not refilled on every equip or on respawn). On each shot the magazine decrements by one. On reload, the magazine refills from the pool. The magazine is the only ammo state WeaponState owns; there is no longer a reserve field per gun.Pool (AmmoManager, server) — per-player, per-type in-memory count of unloaded ammo. Entirely session-only — nothing is persisted to a DataStore. The pool is seeded to each type's Starting value on the player's first spawn only; it then persists across deaths for the rest of the session (dying never refills reserve ammo). Every type's Starting is 0: players are never given free reserve ammo — all reserve ammo is crafted (see Crafting ammo). AmmoManager.EnsureStarting re-syncs the current pool to the owning client on each respawn so the HUD shows the correct value after the character and Backpack rebuild. The pool is shared across all guns of the same ammo type.  A freshly crafted weapon still spawns with one full magazine (the magazine is seeded to MagazineSize on first equip), so it can fire immediately. But once that magazine is emptied the gun cannot be reloaded until the player crafts ammo into the reserve pool.  Ammo types (AmmoConfig)​  Ammo type	Display name	Capacity	Starting (first spawn)Light	Light Rounds	300	0 Heavy	Heavy Rounds	60	0 Rocket	Rockets	12	0  Gun → ammo type mapping:  Gun	Ammo typePistol, SMG, AR	Light SR	Heavy RocketLauncher	Rocket  Reload flow​  Client fires ReqReloadWeapon.Server checks mag < magSize and pool > 0; rejects otherwise (returns 0 reload time).Server waits ReloadTime, then calls ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magSize) (in WeaponValidation), which returns (newMag, taken).AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo(player, ammoType, taken) is called atomically; it clamps, deducts, and fires AmmoPoolSync to the owning client.Server sets the new magazine via WeaponState.SetMag and fires WeaponMagSync to the owning client.  Throwables​  Throwables are physical Roblox Tools in the player's Backpack. Each throw consumes exactly one Tool: WeaponServer.onThrowProjectile destroys the equipped throwable Tool server-side on a successful throw. There is no numeric reserve or CarryCount in WeaponState — count is inferred by AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount by scanning the Backpack and equipped slot.  C4 detonation is intentionally decoupled from holding the Tool: ThrowableDetonateController.client.luau listens for the global G keybind and fires ReqDetonate regardless of what is currently equipped. The server no-ops if the player has no active charges. This design handles the edge case where the last C4 was thrown (destroying its Tool) but live charges are still stuck to surfaces awaiting detonation.  Crafting ammo​  See Workbench Crafting for the full crafting flow; the recipe values below are illustrative — WorkbenchConfig.Recipes is canonical.  Ammo can be replenished at a Workbench. Crafting recipes in the "ammo" category call AmmoManager.AddAmmo (which clamps to Capacity). Available ammo recipes:  Recipe	OutputCraftLightAmmo	+60 Light Rounds CraftHeavyAmmo	+12 Heavy Rounds CraftRocketAmmo	+2 Rockets CraftGrenade	3 Grenade Tools CraftC4	1 C4 Tool  Weapon Tool recipes clone the template from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates directly into the player's Backpack.  Client read surface (AmmoApi)​  AmmoApi is the single client-side cache and read surface for all ammo data. HUD widgets and handlers should call AmmoApi rather than listening to raw packets.  Method	Returns	NotesGetMag(weaponName)	(mag, magSize)	Current magazine count and magazine capacity. GetPool(ammoType)	(amount, capacity)	Current pool count and pool capacity cap. GetEquippedAmmo()	(mag, magSize, pool, cap)?	Combined view for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns or unarmed. GetThrowableCount(toolName)	count	Counts matching Tool instances in Backpack + equipped slot.  AmmoApi listens to WeaponMagSync and AmmoPoolSync packets, updates its cache, and fires the corresponding Signals. It also watches the player's Backpack for tool additions/removals (rebinding per-character via Janitor) to keep GetThrowableCount accurate. Bootstrapped once by AmmoController.client.luau.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Fire-rate enforcement Guns enforce 60/RPM intervals and throwables enforce CooldownTime via WeaponState.GetLastFire. Requests that arrive too early are silently dropped.  Server-authoritative ammo and reload Magazine counts and reload timing are owned by WeaponState on the server; pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager. Firing at an empty magazine is rejected. Firing while a reload window is active (reloadEndsAt > now) is rejected. Reloading with an empty pool is rejected. Neither the magazine count, pool count, nor the reload timer is read from the client.  Origin, spread, and distance validation The claimed muzzle origin for guns and throw origin for throwables must be within 14 studs of the server-side HumanoidRootPart position and must be a finite (non-NaN) vector. Claimed directions with zero or non-finite magnitude are rejected before normalization. The server caps hitscan range at MaxDistance on its authoritative ray; applySpread is applied client-side for feel only — the server recasts from the validated origin and does not verify the spread angle.  Friendly-fire prevention Enforced in CombatService.ApplyToModel via Factions.canDamage. Only Player↔Enemy damage lands. Players never damage other players or friendly NPCs; enemies never damage other enemies or friendly NPCs. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt — the self-check bypasses the faction gate so a player's own rocket can still hurt them if they walk into the blast.  NPC pass-through via CollectionService tag: the "EnemyNPC"/"FriendlyNPC" CollectionService tag is the dual-purpose NPC marker. It gates damage routing in CombatService (only tagged NPCs with a Humanoid take weapon damage) and, via NpcCollisionService, places NPC parts in the Character collision group so thrown charges physically pass through them (see Enemy Spawner → Collision and combat wiring). A Model without a recognized faction tag receives no damage and does not block thrown projectiles — tag it or it is invisible to the weapon system.  HealthManager routing via CombatService: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage (via CombatService) will leave the HUD showing a stale record value. Never write to humanoid.Health directly for player damage. See Health.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Extended Mags (MagazineBonus): magazine size via WeaponValidation.magazineSize (rounds down, min 1) on the server (WeaponServer equip + reload) and the client (AmmoApi.GetMag).Battle Rations (PartyDamageBonus): adds to DamageBonus inside scaledDamage.Lucky Shot (CritChance): server roll on hitscan hits; a crit doubles the hit.Blast Kit (ExplosiveDamageBonus): adds to grenade, rocket and C4 damage.Grenadier (BlastRadiusBonus): scales the blast radius for both ApplyAOE and the ExplosionAt visual.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant C as Client (handler) participant S as Server (WeaponServer) Note over C,S: HITSCAN GUN C->>C: canFire gate + local ammo predict; muzzle flash + local tracer C->>S: ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir, renderTime) S->>S: canFire, IsReloading, mag>0, origin tolerance (<=14 studs) S->>S: LagCompensation.Raycast (NPCs rewound to renderTime, capped MaxDistance); headshot x Multiplier on "Head" S->>S: CombatService.ApplyToModel (Bullet) S->>C: WeaponFired(shooter, name, origin, endpoint, isHit) S->>C: WeaponMagSync(name, mag) / AmmoPoolSync(ammoType, amount) -> owner C->>C: WeaponEffectsController tracer for non-shooters; WeaponMagChanged for HUD Note over C,S: ROCKET (Gun / Projectile) C->>S: ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir, renderTime) S->>S: same gates as hitscan; ServerProjectile.spawnRocket (anchored cosmetic, FastCast2-stepped) S->>S: FastCast2 Hit -> CombatService.ApplyAOE (AOE) S->>C: ExplosionAt(center, radius, name) C->>C: spawnExplosion + sound Note over C,S: GRENADE (Throwable / Fuse) C->>S: ReqThrowProjectile(origin, dir) S->>S: cooldown gate + origin tolerance; ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable (Rest="Bounce") S->>S: task.delay(FuseTime) -> CombatService.ApplyAOE (AOE) S->>C: ExplosionAt(center, radius, name) Note over C,S: C4 (Throwable / Manual) C->>S: ReqThrowProjectile(origin, dir) S->>S: MaxActive check; spawnThrowable (Rest="Stick"); WeaponState.AddActive(player, part) C->>S: ReqDetonate() S->>S: WeaponState.TakeAllActive; per charge: CombatService.ApplyAOE, part:Destroy() S->>C: ExplosionAt per charge

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: WeaponConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/WeaponConfig.luau. Edit stats here — never in handler or server code.Config module: AmmoConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/AmmoConfig.luau.Perks: SpreadReduction (GunHandler spread ×max(0.1, 1−b), client only — the server trusts the fire direction), ReloadSpeedBonus (WeaponServer reload timer ÷(1+b); GunHandler predicts the same value), HeadshotBonus (WeaponServer headshot multiplier ×(1+b)), DamageBonus (scaledDamage). See Perks.  Common fields (all weapons): Category ("Gun"|"Throwable"), DisplayName, ToolName (must match the in-game Tool's Name exactly), Damage (base per-bullet; 0 for throwables, AOE only), DamageType ("Bullet"|"AOE"), HeadshotMultiplier? (gun only, applied on a ray hit against a part named "Head").  Gun fields: FireMode ("Hitscan"|"Projectile"), RPM (fire interval = 60/RPM), Automatic (hold-to-fire vs. semi), MagazineSize (reserve pool lives in AmmoManager, keyed by AmmoType), AmmoType ("Light"|"Heavy"|"Rocket"), ReloadTime, Spread (max cone half-angle, degrees), MaxDistance, FireSound/ReloadSound/DrySound/ImpactSound. Projectile-only additions: ProjectileSpeed, Gravity (Vector3), AOERadius, AOEDamage (center damage, linear falloff to 0 at radius), CosmeticTemplate (name in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets).  Throwable fields: Detonation ("Fuse" auto after FuseTime | "Manual" all charges on ReqDetonate), Rest ("Bounce"|"Stick"), ThrowSpeed, FuseTime (Fuse only), MaxActive (Manual only, max simultaneous charges per player), AOERadius/AOEDamage, CooldownTime, CosmeticTemplate, ThrowSound/ExplodeSound.  Note: CarryCount has been removed. How many throwables a player carries is determined by how many matching Tool instances are in their Backpack (crafted or spawned); AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount reads this count at runtime.

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TrainShieldController.client.luau	Energy-recharge prompt registration, ReqRechargeShield calls; on TrainShieldSync writes TrainStateCache then fires Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TrainShieldGuiController.client.luau	Every copy of the shield readout — the diegetic SurfaceGui per TrainShieldMonitor-tagged part and the full-screen zoom ScreenGui — plus the zoom prompt. searchDocs.title: Recharge​
searchDocs.content: Triggering a ShieldConsole-tagged prompt sends ReqRechargeShield(console). The server validates the tag and proximity, and spends pool Energy via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", maxShield − currentShield, SHIELD_PER_POINT) (only the points needed, never over-filled). An isRecharging boolean mutex serializes concurrent requests — like the fuel system's isRefueling, it is not a queue: a second request in flight returns SHIELD_FULL or NO_ENERGY rather than a queued success. On success the client plays SoundManager.PlaySFX("ShieldRecharge").

searchDocs.title: Damage / fuel bleed-through​
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(amount, source?) is the single damage entry point for the train — all incoming attack/hazard damage, whether it lands on the shield or bleeds through to fuel, routes through this call. No system calls it yet; it is designed for a future combat/hazard system. Guards (all must pass or the call is a no-op): hasStarted must be true, TrainGameOver.HasFired() must be false, amount must be > 0 and not NaN.  Shield > 0 (absorbs): currentShield = max(0, currentShield - amount); broadcast() -- a hit that drives it exactly to 0 discards its excess; this does NOT end the round Shield == 0, fuel > 0: TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount * TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR, source) -- a hit that zeroes fuel stalls the train; it does NOT end the round Shield == 0, fuel == 0: ApplyFuelDamage returns false -> hull hit (see Hull)   This replaced the old behavior where the shield reaching 0 called TrainGameOver.Trigger directly — shield depletion by itself no longer ends the round, it just removes the train's damage buffer. TrainConfig.CORE_TAG ("TrainCore") marks the train's structural model; Shield Nova centers its burst on it (falling back to the engine).

searchDocs.title: Hull​
searchDocs.content: With the shield at 0 and fuel at 0, the train has a hull of ThreatConfig.HULL_HITS (3) hits. ApplyDamage learns that fuel is empty when TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage returns false, and then calls hitHull(source):  A hit whose source is ThreatConfig.BOSS_DAMAGE_SOURCE ("Leviathan") ends the round at once: TrainGameOver.Trigger(LEVIATHAN_STRIKE).Any other hit adds 1 to hullHits. The HULL_HITS-th hit ends the round: TrainGameOver.Trigger(HULL_BREACHED).  An Emergency Generator coast counts as empty fuel, so hull hits count during a coast too (the train keeps coasting; a hit does not stall it).  Restore. The hull returns to full only after the train is safe — shield above 0 or fuel above 0 — for ThreatConfig.HULL_RESTORE_DELAY (60 s) without a break. updateHull() runs from broadcast() (every shield change) and from Signals.OnTrainFuelStateChanged (every fuel-empty edge), and acts only on the safe/unsafe edge: the safe edge starts the delay, the unsafe edge cancels it with a nonce. Topping up while safe never restarts the delay. This stops players from resetting the hull by feeding 1 Energy and letting it drop back to 0.  Nothing calls ApplyDamage yet (no enemy fires at the train), so the hull only matters once enemy-to-train attacks and the Leviathan boss are wired. Both are separate future work; see Threat Timer.

searchDocs.title: Max formula (buffs)​
searchDocs.content: maxShield = (BASE_SHIELD + ResearchBuffs.MaxHP) * (1 + PartyPerkBuffs.TrainShieldBonus)   Research Bench additive: each completed Train Shield node accumulates onto ResearchBuffs.MaxHP — Shield_Alpha +50, Shield_Beta +100, Shield_Gamma +150, Shield_Delta +200 (each MaxLevel = 1, up to +500 total) — added before the perk multiplier. See Research Bench.Party perk multiplicative: TrainShieldBonus = 0.05 * maxLevel across all players (server-max resolution), applied on top of the base + Research sum.Ratio-preserving recompute: when either buff changes, recomputeMax preserves the current fill ratio (currentShield / oldMax) and rounds to the nearest integer — a player at 60% shield stays at ~60% after an upgrade.  subscribeBuffs attaches GetAttributeChangedSignal listeners to both buff folders via WaitForChild, then calls recomputeMax once after attach to catch any missed signals during the wait. See Research Bench and Perks for the upstream buff systems.

searchDocs.title: Shield monitor​
searchDocs.content: The shield HUD is diegetic first: TrainShieldGuiController clones the ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui SurfaceGui template onto every BasePart tagged TrainConfig.SHIELD_MONITOR_TAG ("TrainShieldMonitor"), discovered via CollectionService:GetTagged plus live add/remove signals. The clone is created client-side, so each player drives their own independent copy on the same shared surface — no server/replication involvement in the GUI itself. Each registered monitor owns a Janitor that destroys the clone when the tag is removed.  A second ProximityPrompt on the console opens PlayerGui.TrainShieldGui, a full-screen copy of the same layout, for players who want to read the console without standing at the right angle to the glass. Both assets share one element tree under MainContainer.SafeContainer, so one resolveView and one render path serve both — see The zoom view below.  Readouts​  All five readouts are wired to real sources today. SHIELD HEALTH and SHIELD CAPACITY also drive real gameplay math (current/max shield). STRENGTH RATING, SHIELD EFFICIENCY, and AUTO-REGENERATION read the Shield_Efficiency/Shield_EfficiencyPlus/Shield_Delta buff keys and display them accurately — but nothing in the codebase changes damage or refuel math based on those three yet, so researching them changes the readout, not the shield's actual behavior. See Research Bench — Honest status of Effects.  Readout	Source	BehaviourShield % / ONLINE-CRITICAL / SHIELD HEALTH	TrainStateCache.ShieldFraction()	Eased per frame, then banded (below) SHIELD CAPACITY	TrainStateCache.ShieldMax() ÷ BASE_SHIELD	100% at stock; rises as ResearchBuffs.MaxHP and the party perk raise max STRENGTH RATING	ResearchBuffs[SHIELD_STRENGTH_BUFF_KEY]	B → A → S per ShieldStrengthRatings; B when unset SHIELD EFFICIENCY	ResearchBuffs[SHIELD_EFFICIENCY_BUFF_KEY]	Percentage added to an Energy insert; 0 % when unset AUTO-REGENERATION	ResearchBuffs[SHIELD_AUTOREGEN_BUFF_KEY]	FUNCTIONAL (green) once > 0, else BROKEN (red)  The shield fraction is bucketed into one of TrainConfig.ShieldBands, healthiest first:  Band	Shield	ColourHEALTHY	above 60%	#33ffad WARNING	30–60%	#ffcc33 DANGER	30% or below	#e6372e  The SHIELD HEALTH line always takes the band colour. The shield icon's big number, ONLINE/CRITICAL status and TRAIN SHIELD title hold their authored CRT cyan (SHIELD_ICON_HEALTHY_COLOR, #33ccff) through HEALTHY and adopt the band colour from WARNING down — so a full shield reads cyan on the icon and green on the stat line, which is deliberate, while anything worth warning about colours both in step. DANGER is also where the Shield ImageLabel swaps to its cracked asset and the status flips to CRITICAL. Moving up a band costs an extra SHIELD_BAND_HYSTERESIS (0.03), so a value resting on a boundary can't strobe between two colours every frame.  The percentage is always out of the current max, so a capacity upgrade raises what 100% is worth without the number ever reading above 100 — SHIELD CAPACITY is where a 2000-point shield shows up as 200%, not the shield readout.  What updates when​  Only the eased shield number needs RenderStepped; one global loop drives every view. The other four stats change rarely, so they run event-driven off Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged (capacity moves only when the server recomputes max, which is the same event that carries a snapshot) and ResearchBuffs.AttributeChanged. ResearchBuffs is a plain attribute folder in ReplicatedStorage, so the Tech Tree's totals replicate to the client for free — no packet, no server change. The controller waits up to 30s for the folder, since a server script creates it, then reconciles once after attaching.  TrainStateCache.ShieldFraction() returns nil until the server has actually sent a snapshot. The monitor does not invent a starting value — it used to seed displayedShieldPct = 1, asserting "Online 100%" before the server had spoken at all; see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake. While nil it renders a placeholder ("—", neutral grey) and snaps directly to the first real value with no eased sweep.  TrainShieldController writes TrainStateCache before firing Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged, so the monitor sees the same snapshot whether it reads the cache at init or the signal fires while it's already running.  The zoom view​  StarterGui.TrainShieldGui is a ScreenGui with ResetOnSpawn = false, so the PlayerGui copy survives respawns and is resolved exactly once at startup. The controller forces Enabled = false at init regardless of how the asset was saved.  The TrainConfig.SHIELD_ZOOM_PROMPT_PART_NAME prompt on each ShieldConsole opens it; its MainContainer.CloseButton closes it. While the panel is up every zoom prompt is disabled, so the Close button is the only exit and a held key can't retrigger the prompt sitting underneath the panel. The render loop skips the zoom view entirely while it is hidden, and stats are re-applied on open so a panel opened after a buff change is never stale.  Opening fires Signals.RequestMouseIcon(true) on PC (UserInputService.MouseEnabled and KeyboardEnabled), which is what makes the Close button clickable — the third-person camera otherwise holds MouseBehavior = LockCenter with the icon hidden. CameraController is the sole owner of those properties; this controller never writes them directly, so shift-lock and aim mode stay the single arbiter and aim mode still outranks the request. See Camera — Modes and the Signals Map.  The panel is modal, so setHudHidden clears the rest of the HUD under it. That takes three switches, because no single one covers everything:  Switch	HidesStarterGui:SetCore("TopbarEnabled", false)	Roblox's topbar and every CoreGui it owns — chat, leaderboard, menu button Satchel:SetBackpackEnabled(false)	The hotbar and inventory TopbarPlus.setTopbarEnabled(false)	Satchel's inventory icon  The middle one is the easy mistake: SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.Backpack, false) does nothing here, because Satchel already called it at boot and draws its own hotbar. Satchel re-applies its own flag every Heartbeat, so the hotbar cannot flip back on while the panel is up. Disabling it also unbinds the number-key hotbar actions, so tools can't be swapped through the panel. The third is needed because TopbarPlus icons live in developer ScreenGuis that TopbarEnabled never reaches.  Satchel and TopbarPlus are required inside the zoom setup task after the Close button is wired, not at the top of the file — requiring Satchel boots the entire backpack UI and can yield, and neither the diegetic monitor nor the panel's exit should wait on that. SetCore is pcall'd because it errors if the CoreGui has not registered the callback yet.  One caveat from the engine: with TopbarEnabled false, the strip the topbar occupied still captures mouse events, so a button placed in the top 36 px of the panel will not respond to clicks. Keep interactive elements clear of it.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Each ShieldConsole-tagged root (Model or BasePart) carries two prompt parts, each a BasePart with a child ProximityPrompt, resolved recursively via PromptResolver:  Config field	Part name	Prompt doesSHIELD_PROMPT_PART_NAME	InsertFuelPromptPart	Spend pool Energy to recharge (TrainShieldController → ReqRechargeShield) SHIELD_ZOOM_PROMPT_PART_NAME	OpenMonitorGuiPart	Open the full-screen readout (TrainShieldGuiController)  Give the two prompts distinct ActionText — both shipped as Interact / Shield Generator, which is indistinguishable in game. Multiple consoles are supported, each registered independently.  Tag every BasePart that should display a monitor with TrainConfig.SHIELD_MONITOR_TAG. Element names in both assets — ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui (the SurfaceGui template) and StarterGui.TrainShieldGui (the zoom ScreenGui) — are load-bearing and must match each other: TrainShieldGuiController resolves one shared path set with WaitForChild and will hang on startup if either asset renames or re-nests anything under MainContainer.SafeContainer. Tag the train's structural model with TrainConfig.CORE_TAG ("TrainCore") — Shield Nova's burst center; until it exists the TrainEngine model is used.  Never tag a MeshPart as the monitor. A SurfaceGui adorns its part's bounding box face, not the mesh geometry, and its orientation is the part's CFrame — so a screen that is inset, curved, or tilted inside its bounding box will have the GUI floating in front of it at the wrong angle, with no way to correct it short of rotating the visible mesh. Instead add an invisible flat Part (Transparency = 1, CanCollide/CanQuery/CanTouch off, ~0.05 thick) aligned to the real glass plane and nudged ~0.02 studs out to avoid z-fighting, then tag that. Workspace.Monitor is the reference case: Monitor_Screen's glass is a flat slab leaning back ~31.6°, so the tag lives on a sibling ScreenSurface part instead — 7.5877 × 4.8854 studs, aspect ~1.553 (canvas 3885 × 2501 at PixelsPerStud 512), sat exactly 0.02 studs proud of the glass along its own normal to avoid z-fighting.  That height is not the glass's bounding-box height. The glass leans back ~31.6°, so its extent along its own plane is 4.1067 / cos(31.6°) ≈ 4.82 studs — a surface matched to the bounding box would cover only 85% of the visible glass. The current size covers the full slab. Note it deliberately covers more than the unoccluded aperture: raycasting a grid at the glass with every opaque part of the model as a target shows the bezel opening is rounded, not rectangular, so the extreme corners of this rectangle sit over the CRT bulge. Keep GUI content inside the middle ~90% rather than shrinking the surface — a strictly inscribed rectangle covers only 44% of the glass and reads as far too small.  Because every element is Scale-sized, changing the surface ratio silently stretches all of them rather than letterboxing. Re-check the layout after any resize, and keep the zoom ScreenGui's UIAspectRatioConstraint in step with it so the two copies don't drift apart.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Font width drives text sharpness, not just PixelsPerStud Every label on the monitor is TextScaled inside a Scale-sized box, so the font's width per character sets the rendered type size — a wider face is scaled further down to fit the same box. Michroma measures ~31.6px/char against ~21 for a normal sans (measured via TextService:GetTextBoundsAsync at size 48), so it rasterised the small readouts at roughly 20px, where its uniform hairline stems alias into the "no anti-aliasing" look. The fix was two levers that multiply: PixelsPerStud raised 256 → 512 (canvas 3885×2501 at the current surface size; safe because the layout is entirely Scale-based, so nothing reflows), and the small readouts — ShieldStatus and the ShieldStatsContainer labels — moved to Sarpanch Bold. Michroma is kept for the large display text (ShieldValue, Title), which is big enough to carry it. Apply the same rule to any label added later: if it renders small, it is not a Michroma label. Michroma is a single-face family — GetTextBoundsAsync returns identical metrics for Regular, Medium, Bold and Heavy — so a FontWeight.Bold on a Michroma label does nothing. Those were reset to Regular. Sarpanch does ship a real Bold, which is why the small labels use it. And do not reach for AlwaysOnTop to sharpen text (the API docs suggest it helps on high-DPI displays): it renders over 3D geometry, so the GUI would draw straight through the monitor bezel.  LightInfluence must stay at 0 The monitor has to stay readable across every biome, including night and interior ones. SurfaceGui.LightInfluence is 0 on the template, meaning environmental lighting has no effect and the CRT renders its authored colours everywhere. Any value above 0 tints the screen toward ambient and makes it dim exactly where visibility matters most. Brightness (emissive scaling, only active while LightInfluence is 0) is left at 1; raising it blows out the thin strokes on the display text. This applies only to the SurfaceGui — the zoom ScreenGui is drawn in screen space and is unaffected by world lighting either way.  The template's Adornee is cleared on every clone A SurfaceGui with a non-nil Adornee renders on that instance and ignores its parent, so an Adornee saved into GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui propagates to every clone and the monitor renders nowhere — silently, with no error. This bit the project once already, when the template kept a reference to the deleted placeholder generator. TrainShieldGuiController now sets gui.Adornee = nil after cloning, so the asset can be re-authored on any part without breaking the monitor.  Two upgrade stats are displayed but not yet enforced STRENGTH RATING and SHIELD EFFICIENCY render from ResearchBuffs attributes the Tech Tree writes, but the server does not read them: ApplyDamage applies full damage and handleRecharge adds a flat SHIELD_PER_POINT per point. AUTO-REGENERATION is enforced: see Passive regen and perks. Wiring one up is therefore two edits, and both are required or the monitor will advertise a buff the server never applies: A ResearchConfig node with Effect = { Type = "StatBuff", Key = <the matching TrainConfig key>, PerLevel = … } — ResearchEffectsDispatcher accumulates any StatBuff key, so no dispatcher change is needed. This alone moves the readout.The corresponding read in TrainShieldManager — scale the hit in ApplyDamage, scale value in handleRecharge, or implement the regen loop. The controller and TrainConfig need no change either way; that is the point of routing the display through named buff keys instead of hardcoding the stock strings.  Recharge mutex is not a queue isRecharging is a boolean, not a queue. A second recharge request while one is in-flight returns SHIELD_FULL or NO_ENERGY — not a queued success. The player can try again immediately after.  Pre-game freeze hasStarted is false until Signals.SetTrainStarted fires (the first brake release on the fuel side). ApplyDamage is a no-op until then.

searchDocs.title: Passive regen and perks​
searchDocs.content: Passive regen (research Shield δ, ResearchBuffs.ShieldAutoRegen > 0): every SHIELD_AUTOREGEN_INTERVAL (10 s) a loop in TrainShieldManager adds max × SHIELD_AUTOREGEN_PCT (0.5%, at least 1) while the round is live, the game is not over and the shield is below max. A broken (0) shield regens too.Shield Capacitor (party shop perk, ShieldRegenBonus 1): the regen is × (1 + ShieldRegenBonus). It does nothing without the research.Shield Nova (permanent party perk, ShieldNovaDamage 40/level): the ApplyDamage hit that takes the shield to 0 calls tryNova. If the 180 s cooldown (SHIELD_NOVA_COOLDOWN) is ready, it deals CombatService.ApplyAOE damage in SHIELD_NOVA_RADIUS (30) around the first TrainCore-tagged instance (else the TrainEngine model), pushes enemies away with one server impulse (SHIELD_NOVA_KNOCKBACK), and fires ExplosionAt(center, radius, "ShieldNova"). Every player character is in the ignore list, because an AOE with no attacker would hit players. Nothing calls ApplyDamage yet (no enemy fires at the train), so test it from the command bar.  Shield depletion is no longer a game over The shield can sit at 0 indefinitely, and so can fuel (a stall only speeds up the Threat Timer). Only the hull ends the round.  typeof guard on OnServerInvoke ReqRechargeShield.OnServerInvoke receives (player, console) where console is client-supplied. A typeof(console) == "Instance" guard runs before acquiring the isRecharging lock, so a malformed invocation (nil or non-Instance) is rejected cleanly without erroring.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Hardened Shield (PartyPerkBuffs.ShieldDamageReduction): ApplyDamage reduces hits the shield absorbs; the fuel bleed after the shield is down is unchanged.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Sv as TrainShieldManager participant Cl as TrainShieldController participant Cache as TrainStateCache participant Gui as TrainShieldGuiController Note over Sv,Cl: JOIN - via JoinSync on ClientReady, not PlayerAdded Sv->>Cl: TrainShieldSync(currentShield, maxShield) Cl->>Cache: SetShield(current, max) Cl->>Cl: Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged(current, max) Gui->>Cache: ShieldFraction() every RenderStepped; ShieldMax() on the signal Note over Cl,Sv: RECHARGE Cl->>Sv: ReqRechargeShield(console) Sv->>Sv: isRecharging mutex, validate tag + proximity Sv->>Sv: MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", missing, SHIELD_PER_POINT) Sv-->>Cl: (success, shieldAdded, code) Sv->>Cl: TrainShieldSync(...) Note over Sv: DAMAGE (future combat/hazard caller) Sv->>Sv: ApplyDamage(amount, source) - guard hasStarted, not HasFired, amount>0 alt currentShield > 0 Sv->>Sv: currentShield = max(0, currentShield - amount); broadcast() else currentShield == 0 Sv->>Sv: TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount * FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR, source) end Note over Sv: BUFF CHANGE Sv->>Sv: ResearchBuffs.MaxHP or PartyPerkBuffs.TrainShieldBonus changes Sv->>Sv: recomputeMax() - ratio-preserving rescale, broadcast() Note over Gui: SHIELD READOUT (RenderStepped, every view) Gui->>Cache: ShieldFraction() - nil until first snapshot -> placeholder Gui->>Gui: displayedShieldPct eased; pickBand() -> colour, HEALTHY/WARNING/DANGER, image swap Note over Gui: UPGRADE STATS (event driven, not per frame) Gui->>Cache: ShieldMax() / BASE_SHIELD -> SHIELD CAPACITY Gui->>Gui: ResearchBuffs.AttributeChanged -> strength / efficiency / auto-regen

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: TrainConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/TrainConfig.luau (shield fields below; for fuel knobs see Train Fuel)Perks: TrainShieldBonus (max shield ×(1+b)), ShieldPerEnergyBonus (recharge shield per Energy point = SHIELD_PER_POINT ×(1+b)). Both are Party keys read through PerkBuffRead.Party. See Perks.  Field	Default	EffectBASE_SHIELD	1000	Base shield capacity before Research Bench / perk buffs SHIELD_AUTOREGEN_PCT	0.005	Share of max shield regenerated per interval once Shield δ is researched SHIELD_AUTOREGEN_INTERVAL	10	Seconds between regen ticks SHIELD_NOVA_RADIUS	30	Shield Nova burst radius SHIELD_NOVA_COOLDOWN	180	Seconds between Shield Nova bursts SHIELD_NOVA_KNOCKBACK	60	Shield Nova push speed (studs/s) CORE_TAG	"TrainCore"	CollectionService tag on the train's structural model (Shield Nova center; engine fallback) SHIELD_CONSOLE_TAG	"ShieldConsole"	CollectionService tag on shield console models SHIELD_PROMPT_PART_NAME	"InsertFuelPromptPart"	Child BasePart holding the Energy-recharge ProximityPrompt SHIELD_ZOOM_PROMPT_PART_NAME	"OpenMonitorGuiPart"	Child BasePart holding the open-full-screen-readout ProximityPrompt SHIELD_MONITOR_TAG	"TrainShieldMonitor"	Tagged BasePart the diegetic monitor SurfaceGui clones onto ShieldBands	HEALTHY ≥0.6 / WARNING ≥0.3 / DANGER	Health band text + colour, healthiest first; also gates the cracked icon SHIELD_BAND_HYSTERESIS	0.03	Extra fraction needed to climb up a band, so boundaries don't strobe SHIELD_ICON_HEALTHY_COLOR	#33ccff	Icon number/status/title colour while in the healthiest band; below it they follow ShieldBands SHIELD_STRENGTH_BUFF_KEY	"ShieldStrength"	ResearchBuffs key for damage reduction (unwritten — see gotcha) SHIELD_EFFICIENCY_BUFF_KEY	"ShieldEfficiency"	ResearchBuffs key for recharge bonus (unwritten) SHIELD_AUTOREGEN_BUFF_KEY	"ShieldAutoRegen"	ResearchBuffs key for passive regen (Shield δ); read by the regen loop ShieldStrengthRatings	S ≥0.25 / A ≥0.1 / B	Rating ladder, best first; B is stock SHIELD_PER_POINT	5	Shield added per Energy point (full 1000 = 200 pts) FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR	0.05	Bleed-through conversion: fuel lost = attackDamage * FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR (e.g. 100 attack damage → 5 fuel)  Hull values live in ThreatConfig: HULL_HITS (3), HULL_RESTORE_DELAY (60 s), BOSS_DAMAGE_SOURCE ("Leviathan").

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/WorkbenchGuiController.client.luau	Recipe grid, ProximityPrompt wiring, ReqCraft fire, OnItemCrafted signal Server	src/ServerScriptService/WorkbenchService.server.luau	Authoritative ReqCraft handler: proximity, validation, consume, dispatch Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/CraftOutputDispatcher.luau	Output grant for Weapon / Armor / Placeable; feasibility check runs here Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/WorkbenchValidation.luau	Stateless pure validator: recipe lookup, gate check, material sufficiency Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/WorkbenchResultCodes.luau	Frozen result-code enum shared by client and server Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/WorkbenchConfig.luau	All tuning: interaction constants, template folders, category lists, sounds, and the Recipes table  Packets: ReqCraft — see Networking MapSignals: OnItemCrafted, RequestWorkbenchCategory — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Opening the bench​
searchDocs.content: The GUI has two pages under MainContainer.SecondaryContainer.Bottom's UIPageLayout: WorkbenchContainer (recipe crafting) and ArmoryContainer (the armor tab). The Top.CategoryContainer buttons Personal and Recharge jump between them; a touch swipe also flips pages, and the active tab (BackgroundTransparency = 0) follows UIPageLayout.CurrentPage either way. Each page repeats its own StashButton/MoveButton; PlaceableActions.bind wires every match.  Hovering a MoveButton / StashButton swaps each button's Icon image and eases its ButtonIconContainer.BackgroundColor3 to the dark accent Color3.fromRGB(19, 15, 24) via MotionMaster, restoring the originally-authored icon and color on mouse leave. This is purely cosmetic, wired in WorkbenchGuiController.client.luau (not PlaceableActions), and only on devices with a mouse — a tap fires MouseEnter without MouseLeave, which would leave the hover look stuck.  Mobile scaling. The GUI is authored at 1920×1080 (reference mobile screen: 780×360). Scale-sized frames shrink on their own, but pixel values do not, so the controller binds the reusable SharedModules/Gui/ResponsiveScale module to MainContainer with a reference height of 1080 * 0.8. It scales every UITextSizeConstraint.MinTextSize/MaxTextSize and ScrollingFrame.ScrollBarThickness by MainContainer.AbsoluteSize.Y / reference (capped at 1, never upscales), live on resize and for descendants added later. The authored value is kept once in an Authored<Property> attribute, so rescales never compound and runtime clones carry it. Offset-sized frames are not scaled — author new layout in Scale.  On the first open of a session, the detail pane auto-selects the first recipe in the grid's sort order (Category, then DisplayName — the same order shown under the "All" filter) so it never shows the unselected Studio placeholder. This is a one-time default: once any recipe is selected (by this default or by a player click), the selection persists across closes/reopens like any manual pick.

searchDocs.title: Client — recipe grid and gating​
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchGuiController opens via the bench CraftPromptPart ProximityPrompt. It builds the recipe grid from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes and greys any recipe whose RequiresNode is not present in ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked. Fires ReqCraft on the Craft button and fires Signals.OnItemCrafted on a confirmed success. The CloseButton closes the GUI. The DropdownButton is driven by the reusable Dropdown widget, which fires Signals.RequestWorkbenchCategory on selection to re-filter the grid. Uses a Janitor per GUI open/close lifecycle.

searchDocs.title: Server — authoritative craft handler​
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchService is the sole owner of the authoritative ReqCraft handler. On ReqCraft(bench, recipeId) it validates, in order:  Look up the recipe in WorkbenchConfig (else UNKNOWN_RECIPE).Verify the bench is a tagged Workbench Model (else INVALID_TARGET).Re-check proximity, INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE (else TOO_FAR).CRAFT_COOLDOWN gate, per-player timestamp (else COOLDOWN).Check the RequiresNode gate in ResearchUnlocked (else LOCKED).CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(player, recipe.Output) — verify the output slot is usable before consuming any materials (else OUTPUT_FAILED).Atomically spend the cost from the server-wide Material Pool with MaterialPool.Spend(cost) (false → INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS, nothing consumed).  On pass: call CraftOutputDispatcher.grant(player, recipe.Output) and record the cooldown timestamp. The handler returns (success: Boolean8, code: NumberU8).

searchDocs.title: Output dispatch​
searchDocs.content: CraftOutputDispatcher handles the four output kinds:  Kind == "Weapon" — clones the named Tool from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates into the player's Backpack.Kind == "Armor" — calls ArmorManager.Grant(player, output.ArmorKind), which awards the kind at full pool or refills it if already owned, and auto-equips if nothing is worn. See Armor — Crafting.Kind == "Placeable" — grants the named Tool from ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> into the player's Backpack.Kind == "Ammo" — adds to the player's session-only ammo pool via AmmoManager.AddAmmo.  isFeasible(player, output) verifies the target output slot is usable (e.g. the template exists, the armor kind is known and not already at full pool) before materials are consumed. A misconfigured recipe never costs the player materials.

searchDocs.title: Recipe schema​
searchDocs.content: Recipes are declared in WorkbenchConfig.Recipes as a { [string]: Recipe } table keyed by a string recipe ID:  export type Output = { Kind: "Weapon", ToolName: string, Count: number? } | { Kind: "Armor", ArmorKind: string } | { Kind: "Placeable", PlaceableName: string } | { Kind: "Ammo", AmmoType: string, Amount: number } export type Recipe = { Category: string, -- one of RecipeCategories ("weapons"|"ammo"|"armor"|"workstation") DisplayName: string, Description: string, Tier: number, -- 1..5 flavor/quality badge only; NOT a prerequisite ladder Icon: string, -- rbxassetid:// string for the grid tile and detail panel Cost: { Wood: number?, Metal: number? }, RequiresNode: string?, -- Research Bench nodeId gate or nil = always available Output: Output, }   Tier is a purely cosmetic quality badge displayed as a star rating in the GUI. It has no prerequisite chain and imposes no unlock order — any recipe with RequiresNode = nil is available to craft at any time regardless of Tier. The only unlock gate is RequiresNode. The Cost table is limited to Wood and Metal because the GUI renders exactly two material rows; adding a third material requires a GUI layout change and a matching config key.  The Recipes table is the live catalog. The shipped placeholder entries:  Recipe ID	Category	Cost	RequiresNode	OutputCraftPistol	weapons	Metal 10	nil	Weapon "Pistol" CraftArmorLight	armor	Metal 15	"Armor_Light"	Armor "Light" CraftWorkbench	workstation	Wood 5	nil	Placeable "Workbench" CraftSMG	weapons	Metal 25	"Ranged_SMG"	Weapon "SMG"  The other four armor recipes (CraftArmorMedBallistic, CraftArmorMedEnergy, CraftArmorHeavyBallistic, CraftArmorHeavyEnergy) follow the same shape, one per ArmorConfig.Kinds entry — see Armor — The catalog for the full table.  The workstation category currently contains only CraftWorkbench — it exists as its own dropdown filter rather than folding the Workbench into weapons or armor because future placeable stations (e.g. a second crafting structure) are expected to land in the same category.

searchDocs.title: Research gate seam​
searchDocs.content: ResearchEffectsDispatcher publishes leveled-up node IDs into a ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked folder (a BoolValue per node at level ≥ 1, named by nodeId) in parallel to the ResearchBuffs folder. This folder is written by the server whenever a node reaches level 1 and is read by:  WorkbenchService (server): authoritative gate check. A craft request whose recipe has a non-nil RequiresNode is rejected with LOCKED if the corresponding BoolValue is absent or false. Because the folder is written by the server, clients cannot forge an unlock.WorkbenchGuiController (client): greying. Recipes with a locked RequiresNode are rendered as unavailable in the grid so players know they need to research the gating node first. The client reads this folder but never writes it.  Unlike the old Tech Tree (where a node auto-unlocked the instant its pooled material cost was met), a gating Research Bench node now also costs time: the player pays materials on enqueue, then the node's level advances in real time (gated by bench fuel) before ResearchUnlocked is written. Recipes behind a RequiresNode are therefore no longer available the moment materials are gathered — see Research Bench for the full enqueue/advance/complete flow and the ResearchBuffs/ResearchUnlocked folder contract.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Tag the Workbench Model. In ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/Workbench, tag the root Model with the CollectionService tag Workbench (the same tag the Shredder scans for — one Model serves as both crafting station and shredder). Give it a BasePart named CraftPromptPart (anywhere under the Model — PromptResolver finds it recursively) containing a ProximityPrompt. Set the Model's PrimaryPart. The shredder half uses a sibling ShredPromptPart.Create ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates. Add a folder named WeaponTemplates inside ServerStorage. Place craftable weapon Tools here (e.g. clones of Pistol and SMG from StarterPack). These are separate from the StarterPack copies — the Workbench clones from here into the player's Backpack, so stat changes or visual differences can live here independently.Ensure craftable placeables exist. Each recipe with Output.Kind == "Placeable" needs a Tool at ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<PlaceableName>. The Workbench itself already follows this convention as a grid-placeable item.Material templates are shared. ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials already holds Wood and Metal Tool templates (shared with the Shredder and Research Bench systems). No duplication is needed.Wire ResearchUnlocked. ResearchEffectsDispatcher creates and writes this folder automatically at runtime. No manual Studio setup is required for the gate to function. If testing in isolation (without a running ResearchService/ResearchEffectsDispatcher), create a Folder named ResearchUnlocked in ReplicatedStorage and add BoolValue children named after whichever node IDs you want to treat as unlocked.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every craft The client proximity prompt is never trusted. WorkbenchService re-runs the distance check using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE on every ReqCraft call. A player exploiting from range receives TOO_FAR.  Feasibility is checked before materials are consumed CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(player, recipe.Output) runs (and must succeed) before any material is spent from the pool. A recipe that references a missing weapon template or an unknown/already-full armor kind therefore fails without costing the player anything. Misconfigured recipes are safe to ship; they only result in a visible craft failure.  Research gate is read from server-written state The ResearchUnlocked folder is written exclusively by ResearchEffectsDispatcher on the server. A client cannot create or modify entries in that folder. The server re-reads the folder on every ReqCraft call, so a client that somehow fakes the UI greying cannot bypass the gate.  Cost is limited to Wood and Metal The GUI renders exactly two material rows. Cost may only specify Wood and/or Metal. Adding a third material type (e.g. Energy) requires a GUI layout change alongside the config key — otherwise the cost is silently unchecked on the client (though the server will still validate it).  Tier is a flavor badge, not a prerequisite ladder Tier (1–5) drives the star-rating display only. There is no inter-recipe prerequisite chain derived from Tier values. The sole unlock gate is RequiresNode. Do not attempt to use Tier as a crafting order enforcer — it will not work without code changes.  Known edge case: respawn mid-craft (v1) If a player's Backpack disappears between the feasibility check passing and CraftOutputDispatcher.grant executing (e.g. the player respawns during that narrow window), materials may be spent from the pool but the grant returns OUTPUT_FAILED. The client receives a failure response and the pool loses the materials. This is an accepted v1 limitation — the window is sub-frame in practice. A future refund path or a pre-grant Backpack re-check is the recommended fix.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Ammunition Specialist (PartyPerkBuffs.CraftedAmmoBonus, 0.2): CraftOutputDispatcher adds floor(Amount × (1 + bonus)) rounds for an Ammo output (still capped by AmmoConfig Capacity). Ammo types in ShopPerkConfig.CRAFTED_AMMO_EXCLUDED (Rocket) get no bonus. Grenades and C4 craft as weapons, so the perk never touches them.Scrap Recycler (PartyPerkBuffs.CraftRefund): after a successful craft, WorkbenchService gives back floor(spent × refund) Wood and Metal through MaterialPool.Add (arcs from the bench).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as WorkbenchGuiController participant S as WorkbenchService P->>C: Walk within INTERACT_DISTANCE C->>C: ProximityPrompt fires (CraftPromptPart) C->>C: GUI opens; grid from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes C->>C: Grey recipes whose RequiresNode is not in ResearchUnlocked P->>C: Click a recipe tile C->>C: Show DisplayName, Description, Tier badge, Cost rows, RequiresNode note P->>C: Click Craft button C->>S: ReqCraft(bench, recipeId) S->>S: look up recipe (else UNKNOWN_RECIPE) S->>S: verify tagged Workbench Model (else INVALID_TARGET) S->>S: re-check proximity (else TOO_FAR) S->>S: CRAFT_COOLDOWN gate (else COOLDOWN) S->>S: check RequiresNode in ResearchUnlocked (else LOCKED) S->>S: CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(Output) (else OUTPUT_FAILED) S->>S: verify materials held (else INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS) S->>S: consume materials, CraftOutputDispatcher.grant(...) S->>S: record cooldown timestamp S->>C: (success, code) alt success C->>C: Signals.OnItemCrafted:Fire(recipeId) C->>C: success FX / SoundManager.PlaySFX(CraftSuccess) else failure C->>C: failure toast / SoundManager.PlaySFX(CraftFail) end

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: WorkbenchConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/WorkbenchConfig.luau  Perks: BuildCostReduction (Thrifty Builder, Party) — WorkbenchValidation.costOf(recipe, reduction) lowers each material by ×max(0.1, 1−b), rounded up. The caller reads the value (WorkbenchService charges it, WorkbenchGuiController shows it), so the validator stays pure. See Perks.  Field	Default	EffectSTATION_TAG	"Workbench"	CollectionService tag on the placed Workbench Model (shared with the Shredder — the same Model is both stations) INTERACT_DISTANCE	12	Studs within which the GUI opens and crafts are accepted INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE	5	Server-side slack added to the distance check PROMPT_PART_NAME	"CraftPromptPart"	BasePart (anywhere under the Model) holding the open-GUI ProximityPrompt; resolved recursively by PromptResolver CRAFT_COOLDOWN	0.5	Per-player seconds between accepted crafts MATERIALS_FOLDER	"CraftingMaterials"	ReplicatedStorage folder of Wood/Metal Tool templates (shared with Shredder and Research Bench) WEAPON_TEMPLATES_FOLDER	"WeaponTemplates"	ServerStorage folder of craftable weapon Tools DEFAULT_CATEGORY	"all"	Initial dropdown selection (meta filter, not a valid recipe Category) Categories	{"all","weapons","ammo","armor","workstation"}	Dropdown filter options in display order RecipeCategories	{"weapons","ammo","armor","workstation"}	Valid values for a recipe's Category field CategoryLabels	{all="All", weapons="Weapon", ammo="Ammo", armor="Armor", workstation="Workstation"}	Human-readable labels keyed by category value, shown in the dropdown Sounds.CraftSuccess	""	SoundConfig key played on successful craft (empty = silent) Sounds.CraftFail	""	SoundConfig key played on rejected craft
